name: Standing / seated isometric heel-raise hold
chineseName: 站姿/坐姿等長提踵靜態維持 (比目魚肌/腓腸肌活化)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Heavy sustained isometric contractions provide immediate cortical motor disinhibition and exercise-induced hypoalgesia for reactive Achilles tendinopathy while respecting the anatomical compression zone of insertional subtypes.

jointActions: Closed chain; heavy isometric; Stage 1 tendon analgesia & motor activation

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg (or both legs if single-leg is >4/10 painful) with fingertips on a wall for balance
execution.description: Heavy sustained isometric contractions provide immediate cortical motor disinhibition and exercise-induced hypoalgesia for reactive Achilles tendinopathy while respecting the anatomical compression zone of insertional subtypes.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg (or both legs if single-leg is >4/10 painful) with fingertips on a wall for balance

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Subtype Angle Rule: For Mid-Portion Achilles Tendinopathy, hold at mid-range (heel 1-2 inches off the floor); for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy or Early Post-Rupture (Week 6-8), rise higher into 20°–30° of plantarflexion so the calcaneus is completely decompressed away from the deep tendon

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold completely static for 45 seconds at ~70% MVIC (adding a backpack or seated thigh weight once bodyweight feels easy)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes and complete 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Rise halfway up onto the ball of your foot and freeze your heel in mid-air for 45 seconds" (external).
commonErrors: Holding the isometric stretch at the bottom of a step in full dorsiflexion when the patient has Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy (pinches the retrocalcaneal bursa and deep tendon fibers against the calcaneus, flaring pain!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral standing isometric hold (shifting 60%–70% weight to the affected side); seated isometric calf hold.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform unilaterally with external dumbbell/backpack load; perform both straight-knee (gastrocnemius) and 90° bent-knee seated (soleus) isometric holds.

precautions: Holding the isometric stretch at the bottom of a step in full dorsiflexion when the patient has Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy (pinches the retrocalcaneal bursa and deep tendon fibers against the calcaneus, flaring pain!). Cues: "Rise halfway up onto the ball of your foot and freeze your heel in mid-air for 45 seconds" (external).
clinicalNotes: Heavy sustained isometric contractions provide immediate cortical motor disinhibition and exercise-induced hypoalgesia for reactive Achilles tendinopathy while respecting the anatomical compression zone of insertional subtypes.

name: Flat-ground heel raise
chineseName: 平地雙腳提踵 (踮腳尖肌力基礎)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Jonsson et al. demonstrated that when the traditional Alfredson step-edge eccentric protocol was modified to stop at flat ground (0°) for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy, clinical success jumped from 32% to 67%! Stopping at 0° applies high tensile mechanotransduction to remodel the tendon without wrapping the distal insertion over the superior calcaneal prominence.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; non-compressive insertional loading

execution.startingPosition: Stand on a completely flat floor (or lowering down onto a 0.5-inch book/heel lift under the heel in very irritable early cases) with feet hip-width apart
execution.description: Jonsson et al. demonstrated that when the traditional Alfredson step-edge eccentric protocol was modified to stop at flat ground (0°) for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy, clinical success jumped from 32% to 67%! Stopping at 0° applies high tensile mechanotransduction to remodel the tendon without wrapping the distal insertion over the superior calcaneal prominence.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a completely flat floor (or lowering down onto a 0.5-inch book/heel lift under the heel in very irritable early cases) with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press up through the first and second metatarsal heads over 3 seconds to maximal plantarflexion

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly over 3 seconds until the heel gently touches the flat floor (0° neutral ankle angle)—never dropping below floor level!

coachingCues: "Rise high onto your big-toe ball and lower for a slow 3-count until your heel kisses the flat floor" (external).
commonErrors: Dropping the heel off a step edge into dorsiflexion during Weeks 1-6 of Insertional Achilles rehab or Weeks 1-12 of Post-Achilles Rupture rehab.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Place a 1-cm book or heel wedge on the floor so the heel stops in 5°–10° plantarflexion before reaching flat ground.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress from bilateral to single-leg flat-ground heel raises; add backpack/dumbbell weight; only introduce step-edge dorsiflexion in late Stage 2/3 once insertional tenderness is zero.

precautions: Dropping the heel off a step edge into dorsiflexion during Weeks 1-6 of Insertional Achilles rehab or Weeks 1-12 of Post-Achilles Rupture rehab. Cues: "Rise high onto your big-toe ball and lower for a slow 3-count until your heel kisses the flat floor" (external).
clinicalNotes: Jonsson et al. demonstrated that when the traditional Alfredson step-edge eccentric protocol was modified to stop at flat ground (0°) for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy, clinical success jumped from 32% to 67%! Stopping at 0° applies high tensile mechanotransduction to remodel the tendon without wrapping the distal insertion over the superior calcaneal prominence.

name: Seated bent-knee calf raise HSR
chineseName: 坐姿屈膝比目魚肌高負荷肌腱訓練 (HSR)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: The soleus contributes the largest physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA) to the Achilles tendon, and due to Achilles tendon torsion, the soleus fibers form the deep and medial portion of the mid-substance and insertion (the exact region most commonly degenerated in runners!). Bending the knee to 90° slackens the bi-articular gastrocnemius and forces the soleus to carry the entire load, which is essential because endurance runners incur peak soleus loads of 6–8x body weight on every stride.

jointActions: Closed chain / seated; Heavy Slow Resistance; soleus & medial Achilles loading

execution.startingPosition: Sit on a seated calf raise machine (or on a bench with a heavy weight across the distal thigh) with knees bent at 90°
execution.description: The soleus contributes the largest physiological cross-sectional area (PCSA) to the Achilles tendon, and due to Achilles tendon torsion, the soleus fibers form the deep and medial portion of the mid-substance and insertion (the exact region most commonly degenerated in runners!). Bending the knee to 90° slackens the bi-articular gastrocnemius and forces the soleus to carry the entire load, which is essential because endurance runners incur peak soleus loads of 6–8x body weight on every stride.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit on a seated calf raise machine (or on a bench with a heavy weight across the distal thigh) with knees bent at 90°

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: For Mid-Portion Tendinopathy, place forefeet on a step to use full range; for Insertional Tendinopathy or Post-Rupture, keep the foot on a flat platform (stopping at 0° neutral)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press up over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Move slowly for 3 seconds up and 3 seconds down, driving strictly through your big-toe joint" (external).
commonErrors: Using trivial 2-5 kg weights for the soleus (the soleus is a massive postural/locomotor muscle that requires heavy slow loading to stimulate tendon adaptation); bouncing at the bottom.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral seated calf raises with moderate weight.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progressively load up to 1.0–1.5x body weight on single-leg seated calf press.

precautions: Using trivial 2-5 kg weights for the soleus (the soleus is a massive postural/locomotor muscle that requires heavy slow loading to stimulate tendon adaptation); bouncing at the bottom. Cues: "Move slowly for 3 seconds up and 3 seconds down, driving strictly through your big-toe joint" (external).

chineseName: 台階邊緣離心下沉與高負荷肌腱修復 (Alfredson)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Level A gold-standard intervention in the 2018/2024 JOSPT Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy CPG. Loading through full dorsiflexion below step level maximizes longitudinal tensile strain across the mid-substance (2–6 cm above calcaneus), stimulating tenocyte collagen synthesis, glycosaminoglycan normalization, and neovascular ingrowth reduction.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric / HSR through full dorsiflexion; Stage 2 matrix remodeling

execution.startingPosition: Stand with the balls of both feet on the edge of a step
execution.description: Level A gold-standard intervention in the 2018/2024 JOSPT Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy CPG. Loading through full dorsiflexion below step level maximizes longitudinal tensile strain across the mid-substance (2–6 cm above calcaneus), stimulating tenocyte collagen synthesis, glycosaminoglycan normalization, and neovascular ingrowth reduction.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with the balls of both feet on the edge of a step

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: For Heavy Slow Resistance (Beyer/Kongsgaard protocol): rise on the affected leg over 3 seconds to full plantarflexion and lower slowly over 3 seconds below step level into full dorsiflexion

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: For Alfredson Eccentric-Only Protocol: rise up using both legs, shift 100% weight to the affected leg, lower slowly over 3-4 seconds below step level, and use the uninjured leg to return to the top

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Perform both with the knee straight (gastrocnemius) and with the knee bent at 30°–45° (soleus).

coachingCues: "Lower your heel slowly over a full 3-count below the step, keeping your ankle straight without rolling outward" (external).
commonErrors: Applying this below-step exercise to an Insertional Achilles patient or an early Post-Rupture patient (strictly contraindicated for those two groups!); rushing the lowering phase.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Flat-ground heel raises if below-step dorsiflexion causes pain >5/10 on the Silbernagel Pain Monitoring Scale.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add external weight in a backpack or hold dumbbells (5-30 kg).

precautions: Applying this below-step exercise to an Insertional Achilles patient or an early Post-Rupture patient (strictly contraindicated for those two groups!); rushing the lowering phase. Cues: "Lower your heel slowly over a full 3-count below the step, keeping your ankle straight without rolling outward" (external).
clinicalNotes: Level A gold-standard intervention in the 2018/2024 JOSPT Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy CPG. name: Inner-range plantarflexion heel-block raise
chineseName: 內側角度蹠屈墊木提踵 (足底深層穩定)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: After an Achilles tendon rupture (and in chronic tendinopathy with calf weakness), patients exhibit a severe deficit in end-range plantarflexion torque (the final 15°–20° of heel-rise height). By resting the heel on a raised block and holding for 5 seconds at peak tiptoe height, this exercise selectively recruits the gastrocnemius-soleus in its shortened inner range while protecting a healing ruptured tendon from being stretched past neutral!

jointActions: Closed chain; concentric/isometric in 15°–30° plantarflexion; end-range torque

execution.startingPosition: Place a 1-to-1.5-inch book or heel wedge on the floor
execution.description: After an Achilles tendon rupture (and in chronic tendinopathy with calf weakness), patients exhibit a severe deficit in end-range plantarflexion torque (the final 15°–20° of heel-rise height). By resting the heel on a raised block and holding for 5 seconds at peak tiptoe height, this exercise selectively recruits the gastrocnemius-soleus in its shortened inner range while protecting a healing ruptured tendon from being stretched past neutral!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place a 1-to-1.5-inch book or heel wedge on the floor

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand with the balls of the feet on the floor and the heels resting on the raised book (putting the ankle in ~15°–20° of baseline plantarflexion)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Rise from the book up to maximal end-range tiptoe plantarflexion over 2 seconds, hold hard at the very top for 5 seconds, and lower back onto the raised book over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Compare both ankles in a mirror—drive all the way to your highest tiptoe peak and hold at the top for 5 full seconds" (external).
commonErrors: Stopping halfway up (only rising to mid-range plantarflexion instead of reaching full maximal tiptoe height matching the uninjured ankle).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated heel raises with a wedge under the heel; bilateral standing with countertop support.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform single-leg inner-range raises; gradually reduce the book thickness to flat ground after Week 10-12 post-rupture while maintaining peak heel-rise height symmetry.

precautions: Stopping halfway up (only rising to mid-range plantarflexion instead of reaching full maximal tiptoe height matching the uninjured ankle). Cues: "Compare both ankles in a mirror—drive all the way to your highest tiptoe peak and hold at the top for 5 full seconds" (external).
clinicalNotes: After an Achilles tendon rupture (and in chronic tendinopathy with calf weakness), patients exhibit a severe deficit in end-range plantarflexion torque (the final 15°–20° of heel-rise height). name: Single-leg weighted Smith-machine / dumbbell calf press
chineseName: 單腳負重史密斯機/啞鈴小腿推蹬
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Before an athlete is cleared for Stage 3 plyometrics or running (where the Achilles experiences 6–8x body weight), bodyweight heel raises are completely insufficient! High-load single-leg HSR (building toward 0.3–0.5x body weight added external load for 6-8 reps, and >= 25 single-leg heel-rise endurance reps) restores tendon cross-sectional stiffness and elastic recoil capacity.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral HSR (3s up / 3s down); maximal tensile stiffness

execution.startingPosition: Stand on one leg under a Smith machine bar (or holding a heavy dumbbell on the ipsilateral side while using two fingertips of the opposite hand on a rack for balance)
execution.description: Before an athlete is cleared for Stage 3 plyometrics or running (where the Achilles experiences 6–8x body weight), bodyweight heel raises are completely insufficient! High-load single-leg HSR (building toward 0.3–0.5x body weight added external load for 6-8 reps, and >= 25 single-leg heel-rise endurance reps) restores tendon cross-sectional stiffness and elastic recoil capacity.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on one leg under a Smith machine bar (or holding a heavy dumbbell on the ipsilateral side while using two fingertips of the opposite hand on a rack for balance)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press up through the ball of the big toe over 3 seconds to full plantarflexion height

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 1 second at the top, then lower over a strict 3-to-4-second count (to flat ground for insertional/rupture, or step edge for mid-portion).

coachingCues: "Keep your knee locked tall and hit the exact same top height marker on every single repetition" (external).
commonErrors: Bending the knee during a straight-leg gastrocnemius press to cheat the weight up with the quads; cutting the top range short as the weight gets heavy.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral weighted heel raises with single-leg eccentric lowering.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase external load progressively; test Single-Leg Heel-Rise Endurance (Silbernagel test: max reps to a metronome at 30 reps/min, targeting >= 90% LSI).

precautions: Bending the knee during a straight-leg gastrocnemius press to cheat the weight up with the quads; cutting the top range short as the weight gets heavy. Cues: "Keep your knee locked tall and hit the exact same top height marker on every single repetition" (external).
clinicalNotes: Before an athlete is cleared for Stage 3 plyometrics or running (where the Achilles experiences 6–8x body weight), bodyweight heel raises are completely insufficient! High-load single-leg HSR (building toward 0.3–0.5x body weight added external load for 6-8 reps, and >= 25 single-leg heel-rise endurance reps) restores tendon cross-sectional stiffness and elastic recoil capacity.

name: Bilateral-to-unilateral pogo hops
chineseName: 雙腳轉單腳連續踝彈跳 (Pogo Hops 增強式)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Heavy Slow Resistance builds muscle and tendon strength, but does NOT restore the rapid elastic energy storage-and-release ("spring") behavior of the Achilles tendon required for running. Stage 3 pogo hops retrain short-contact-time ankle stiffness via the stretch-shortening cycle.

jointActions: Plyometric; reactive ankle stiffness; fast stretch-shortening cycle (SSC)

execution.startingPosition: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees nearly straight (soft 10° unlock)
execution.description: Heavy Slow Resistance builds muscle and tendon strength, but does NOT restore the rapid elastic energy storage-and-release ("spring") behavior of the Achilles tendon required for running. Stage 3 pogo hops retrain short-contact-time ankle stiffness via the stretch-shortening cycle.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees nearly straight (soft 10° unlock)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Bounce rhythmically on the balls of the feet like a jump-rope hop (120–140 beats per minute), keeping ground contact times short and crisp (<200 ms) and preventing the heels from slamming into the floor

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Perform 3 sets of 20 bilateral pogo hops; once 24-hour morning stiffness remains zero, progress to alternating-foot hops (skipping/boxer shuffle) and then 10-15 single-leg pogo hops.

coachingCues: "Imagine the floor is hot lava—bounce off the balls of your feet with stiff, springy ankles" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the heel collapse to the floor with a long, mushy contact time (increases deep dorsiflexion strain instead of training stiff elastic recoil); doing plyometrics on consecutive days.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Fast bilateral heel-rises on flat ground without leaving the floor ("rebound heel pulses").

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Double-leg pogo hops (50% weight) -> Boxer-shuffle alternating hops -> Single-leg pogo hops in place -> Forward/lateral line pogo hops.

precautions: Letting the heel collapse to the floor with a long, mushy contact time (increases deep dorsiflexion strain instead of training stiff elastic recoil); doing plyometrics on consecutive days. Cues: "Imagine the floor is hot lava—bounce off the balls of your feet with stiff, springy ankles" (external).
clinicalNotes: Heavy Slow Resistance builds muscle and tendon strength, but does NOT restore the rapid elastic energy storage-and-release ("spring") behavior of the Achilles tendon required for running. Stage 3 pogo hops retrain short-contact-time ankle stiffness via the stretch-shortening cycle.

Forward horizontal hopping and sprint acceleration place peak tensile forces (8–12x body weight) on the Achilles tendon. Passing the Single-Leg Hop for Distance and Triple Hop tests (>= 90% LSI) with zero 24-hour pain flare confirms readiness for full team sport competition.

jointActions: Plyometric / high-velocity propulsion; peak Achilles tensile load tolerance

execution.startingPosition: 1) Exercise A (Single-Leg Forward Hop Series): Hop forward continuously on the affected leg across 3-5 cones spaced 1 meter apart, rebounding smoothly off the forefoot without heel collapse
execution.description: Represents Stage 4 of the Silbernagel and Malliaras return-to-sport continuum. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Single-Leg Forward Hop Series): Hop forward continuously on the affected leg across 3-5 cones spaced 1 meter apart, rebounding smoothly off the forefoot without heel collapse

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (Incline to Flat Sprint Acceleration): Perform 4-6 x 20-meter submaximal-to-maximal accelerations starting up a slight 5% incline (incline accelerations emphasize concentric push-off while reducing eccentric braking impact) before progressing to flat-ground sprinting and cutting.

coachingCues: "Drive the ground away behind you through the ball of your foot with crisp, powerful push-offs" (external).
commonErrors: Sprinting in flat/negative-drop track spikes immediately upon returning to the field (suddenly increases Achilles dorsiflexion strain—transition footwear gradually!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Return to Stage 3 bilateral/single-leg vertical pogo hops if next-morning stiffness increases by >2 points on the 0-10 scale.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase sprint velocity from 70% -> 85% -> 100%; progress from incline accelerations to flat-ground sprinting and change-of-direction cuts.

precautions: Sprinting in flat/negative-drop track spikes immediately upon returning to the field (suddenly increases Achilles dorsiflexion strain—transition footwear gradually!). Cues: "Drive the ground away behind you through the ball of your foot with crisp, powerful push-offs" (external).
clinicalNotes: Represents Stage 4 of the Silbernagel and Malliaras return-to-sport continuum. Forward horizontal hopping and sprint acceleration place peak tensile forces (8–12x body weight) on the Achilles tendon. Passing the Single-Leg Hop for Distance and Triple Hop tests (>= 90% LSI) with zero 24-hour pain flare confirms readiness for full team sport competition.

name: Post-cast unloaded active ROM, scar glide & stationary bike (Ankle Fracture Wk 2–6)
chineseName: 拆石膏早期無負重主動活動度、疤痕滑動與飛輪訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Six weeks of immobilization causes severe intra-articular synovial fluid stasis, capsular contracture, and subcutaneous scar adherence to the fibular plate and medial malleolar screws. Early unloaded cyclic motion and scar mobilization restore skin and capsular extensibility before full weight-bearing begins.

jointActions: Active mobility / cyclic; open/closed chain; synovial nutrition & adhesion prevention

execution.startingPosition: 1) As soon as the surgeon allows the CAM boot to be removed for seated ROM (often Week 2–3 after stable ORIF, or Week 6 after cast removal), perform 20 slow dorsiflexion-plantarflexion pumps, 15 inversion-eversion wiper glides (if syndesmosis is stable), and 2 ankle alphabets, 3 times daily
execution.description: Six weeks of immobilization causes severe intra-articular synovial fluid stasis, capsular contracture, and subcutaneous scar adherence to the fibular plate and medial malleolar screws. Early unloaded cyclic motion and scar mobilization restore skin and capsular extensibility before full weight-bearing begins.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: As soon as the surgeon allows the CAM boot to be removed for seated ROM (often Week 2–3 after stable ORIF, or Week 6 after cast removal), perform 20 slow dorsiflexion-plantarflexion pumps, 15 inversion-eversion wiper glides (if syndesmosis is stable), and 2 ankle alphabets, 3 times daily

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Gently mobilize the healed surgical scars over the lateral and medial malleoli (only once sutures/staples are removed and incisions are 100% closed!) in vertical, horizontal, and circular directions for 3 minutes so skin/fascia does not tether to the underlying plate/screws

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Spin on a stationary bike with low resistance for 10-15 minutes daily.

coachingCues: "Gently coax a millimeter more motion out of your ankle every day, and keep the healed skin gliding freely over the ankle bones" (external).
commonErrors: Mobilizing an incision before scabs/sutures have completely healed; forcing aggressive inversion/external rotation if a syndesmotic screw is still in place.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Warm-water whirlpool or bath-assisted active ankle ROM to use hydrotherapy buoyancy and warmth to ease post-cast stiffness.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase stationary bike resistance and lower saddle height to increase ankle dorsiflexion excursion at the top of the pedal stroke.

precautions: Mobilizing an incision before scabs/sutures have completely healed; forcing aggressive inversion/external rotation if a syndesmotic screw is still in place.Cues: "Gently coax a millimeter more motion out of your ankle every day, and keep the healed skin gliding freely over the ankle bones" (external).
clinicalNotes: Six weeks of immobilization causes severe intra-articular synovial fluid stasis, capsular contracture, and subcutaneous scar adherence to the fibular plate and medial malleolar screws. name: Plantar fascia myofascial release & "Pronation-Unlocking" Wedge Lunge (Pes Cavus)

description: In Pes Cavus, a chronically plantarflexed first ray ("forefoot valgus") hits the ground early and forces the subtalar joint to tip outward into rigid varus/supination ("the tripod kickstand effect"). By elevating the 2nd–5th metatarsal heads and lateral heel on a wedge so the 1st metatarsal head can drop freely, and driving the knee over the big toe, we biomechanically unlock the subtalar and midtarsal joints into healthy, shock-absorbing pronation!

jointActions: Myofascial / subtalar mobilization; closed chain; restoring mid-stance shock absorption

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Indications: Perform specifically for Pes Cavus (Rigid High Arch / Supinated Foot) to teach the foot to unlock and absorb shock

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step A (Plantar Fascia & Abductor Hallucis Release — 2 min): Sit and roll the rigid, contracted medial arch slowly over a firm massage ball for 2 minutes while gently extending the toes to reduce resting plantar aponeurosis stiffness

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step B (Lateral Heel Wedge + 1st-Ray Cutout "Pronation Lunge"): Place a small 0.5-cm wedge under the outer (lateral) half of your heel AND place a pad under the outer 2nd–5th metatarsal heads while leaving the 1st metatarsal head (big-toe ball) unsupported in a cutout drop zone. Gently lunge your knee forward and slightly medially over your big toe for 12-15 slow oscillations (3s hold), feeling the calcaneus gently evert and the high medial arch soften and flatten toward the floor to absorb load!

coachingCues: "Let your high arch melt and soften toward the floor like a shock-absorbing spring as your knee glides forward over your big toe" (external).
commonErrors: Teaching a Pes Cavus patient to "dome their arch higher" with Short-Foot exercises (worsens their rigid supination deformity and lateral column stress fractures!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Manual clinician subtalar eversion (calcaneal valgus) joint mobilization + plantar fascia stretching.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Remove the wedges and practice active "Soft-Arch / Knee-Over-Big-Toe" lunges on flat ground.

precautions: Teaching a Pes Cavus patient to "dome their arch higher" with Short-Foot exercises (worsens their rigid supination deformity and lateral column stress fractures!).Cues: "Let your high arch melt and soften toward the floor like a shock-absorbing spring as your knee glides forward over your big toe" (external).

description: After 6 weeks of non-weight-bearing after an Ankle Fracture, patients experience intense kinesiophobia (fear of loading the healed fracture) and walk with an externally rotated, stiff-ankle "peg-leg" gait. Visual biofeedback on a bathroom scale proves to the patient's brain that the bone and hardware are safe while applying controlled axial compression (Wolff's Law) to mineralize the fracture callus.

jointActions: Graduated axial loading; closed chain; Wolff's Law callus remodeling & gait symmetry

execution.startingPosition: Place two identical bathroom scales side by side near a countertop or parallel bars

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place two identical bathroom scales side by side near a countertop or parallel bars

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step onto one scale with your uninjured foot and the other scale with your fractured foot (in the boot during Weeks 4–6 PWB, then in supportive athletic shoes during Weeks 6–8 WBAT)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Practice shifting your body weight smoothly side to side and forward-backward (heel-to-toe) to hit your exact weekly weight-bearing target (e.g. 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% full body weight), holding each weight shift for 10 seconds x 15 reps

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Practice slow "Heel-to-Big-Toe Roll-Through Steps" between parallel bars to eliminate the stiff-legged "peg-leg" post-boot limp!

coachingCues: "Watch the scale dial to trust your healed bone, and roll smoothly from heel to big toe on every step" (external).
commonErrors: Ditching crutches too early while walking with a severe antalgic limp and externally rotated foot (creates chronic hip/knee pain and anterior ankle impingement—always keep 1 crutch on the opposite hand until the gait pattern is 100% symmetrical!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform in the CAM walking boot with 2 crutches at 25%–50% body weight.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Wean from 2 crutches -> 1 crutch (held on the uninjured side!) -> cane -> unassisted walking in supportive shoes once a limp-free heel-to-toe roll is achieved.

precautions: Ditching crutches too early while walking with a severe antalgic limp and externally rotated foot (creates chronic hip/knee pain and anterior ankle impingement—always keep 1 crutch on the opposite hand until the gait pattern is 100% symmetrical!).Cues: "Watch the scale dial to trust your healed bone, and roll smoothly from heel to big toe on every step" (external).

name: Banded Knee-to-Wall dorsiflexion & Low-Load Long-Duration calf stretch
chineseName: 彈力帶屈膝觸牆背屈活動度與低負荷長時間小腿伸展

description: Post-ankle fracture stiffness is the most stubborn impairment in orthopedic rehab because both the posterior joint capsule and the gastrocnemius-soleus muscle-tendon unit are shortened. Dense capsular scar tissue requires Low-Load Long-Duration (LLLD) total end-range time (TERT) to induce plastic collagen creep, combined with banded posterior talar glides to prevent anterior talocrural pinching. (Also critical for Pes Cavus, which frequently has concurrent gastroc-soleus equinus!).

jointActions: Arthrokinematic / flexibility; closed chain; posterior talar glide & capsule creep

execution.startingPosition: 1) Step A (Banded Knee-to-Wall Mobilization): Loop a heavy band low across the anterior talar neck (below the malleoli) pulling backward; drive the knee forward over the second toe toward the wall (3 sets x 15 oscillations with 5s holds)
execution.description: Post-ankle fracture stiffness is the most stubborn impairment in orthopedic rehab because both the posterior joint capsule and the gastrocnemius-soleus muscle-tendon unit are shortened. Dense capsular scar tissue requires Low-Load Long-Duration (LLLD) total end-range time (TERT) to induce plastic collagen creep, combined with banded posterior talar glides to prevent anterior talocrural pinching. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Step A (Banded Knee-to-Wall Mobilization): Loop a heavy band low across the anterior talar neck (below the malleoli) pulling backward; drive the knee forward over the second toe toward the wall (3 sets x 15 oscillations with 5s holds)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step B (Low-Load Long-Duration [LLLD] Wedge Stretch for Post-Fracture Stiffness): Stand with the forefoot elevated on a 15^\circ–20^\circ slant board or step edge and maintain a gentle, tolerable (3/10) continuous dorsiflexion stretch for 3 bouts of 2–3 minutes daily.

coachingCues: "Keep your heel glued down and let the gentle 2-minute hold slowly melt the stiffness at the back of your ankle" (external).
commonErrors: Forcing a sharp bony pinch at the front of the ankle (if pinching occurs at the front instead of a stretch at the back, increase the downward-posterior band pull on the talus!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated towel dorsiflexion stretch if standing prolonged stretch causes malleolar swelling.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Elevate the foot on a chair and lean upper body weight over the knee during the banded mobilization.

precautions: Forcing a sharp bony pinch at the front of the ankle (if pinching occurs at the front instead of a stretch at the back, increase the downward-posterior band pull on the talus!).Cues: "Keep your heel glued down and let the gentle 2-minute hold slowly melt the stiffness at the back of your ankle" (external).

Strengthening eversion + dorsiflexion rebalances the frontal-plane force couple across the subtalar joint and pulls the foot out of supination.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; correcting hindfoot varus supination

execution.description: In Pes Cavus (and after lateral malleolar Weber A/B fractures), the hindfoot is pulled into varus/inversion by an overactive tibialis posterior and tibialis anterior, while the antagonistic peroneus brevis and peroneus tertius are weak and lengthened. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the leg extended and loop a resistance band around the lateral forefoot, anchored medially

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Push the outer pinky-toe border of the foot outward and upward (combined eversion + dorsiflexion to recruit the peroneus brevis, peroneus tertius, and lateral EDL!) over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at full eversion

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Slowly control the inward return over 4 seconds—for Pes Cavus, stop at neutral so the foot does not rest in its habitual inverted/supinated posture!

coachingCues: "Keep your kneecap pointed at the ceiling and lift your pinky toe up and out toward the side wall" (external).
commonErrors: Rotating the whole leg externally at the hip/knee instead of isolating the ankle evertors.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Isometric eversion holds against a wall (Weeks 4–6 post-ORIF once cleared).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress band resistance; standing isometric/isotonic lateral band pulls.

precautions: Rotating the whole leg externally at the hip/knee instead of isolating the ankle evertors.Cues: "Keep your kneecap pointed at the ceiling and lift your pinky toe up and out toward the side wall" (external).

Pressing through the 1st ray during heavy slow calf raises restores tricep surae muscle mass while keeping the subtalar joint centered out of varus!

steps.instruction: Perform 3-4 sets x 10-12 Seated Bent-Knee Calf Raises (soleus) and Standing Straight-Knee Calf Raises (gastrocnemius) over a 3s up / 2s hold / 3s down tempo

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Crucial Alignment Cue for Both Post-ORIF and Pes Cavus: Trap a flat resistance band under the first metatarsal head (big-toe knuckle) pulled laterally—press hard through the big-toe ball as you rise so the ankle NEVER rolls outward into varus/supination at the top of the heel raise!

precautions: Letting the ankle roll onto the outer pinky-toe border as the calf fatigues.Cues: "Crush the floor under your big-toe knuckle all the way to the top of your tiptoes" (external).

For Pes Cavus athletes, allowing controlled subtalar pronation during weight acceptance combined with deep knee/hip flexion replaces their rigid "bony impact" gait with muscular shock attenuation.

For Pes Cavus athletes, allowing controlled subtalar pronation during weight acceptance combined with deep knee/hip flexion replaces their rigid "bony impact" gait with muscular shock attenuation.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a 4-to-6-inch step (for Forward Step-Downs) or in a Split-Squat stance with the affected leg forward

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Specific Rule for Pes Cavus: Instead of doming the arch stiffly and pushing the knee out toward the pinky toe, keep the first metatarsal head planted and guide the kneecap forward over the space between the first and second toes, allowing the rigid high arch to gently unlock and pronate 2–3 mm to absorb weight! steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower over 3-4 seconds and drive smoothly back up.

coachingCues: "Keep your whole foot relaxed and flat on the step, press your big-toe ball down, and let your ankle and knee bend deeply together" (external).
commonErrors: In Post-ORIF fractures, compensating for restricted ankle dorsiflexion by lifting the heel early or collapsing into severe valgus; in Pes Cavus, gripping/clawing the toes and rolling onto the lateral border of the shoe.

regressions.name: 退階方案

name: Banded talocrural distraction & posterior talar glide (Anterior Impingement)
chineseName: 彈力帶距骨小腿關節牽引與向後滑動鬆動術 (前夾擠)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: In Anterior Ankle Impingement (soft-tissue anterolateral gutter scar or mild tibiotalar osteophytes) and Ankle OA, the talus fails to glide posteriorly during dorsiflexion, causing the anterior tibial lip to slam into the talar neck. Applying a strong downward-and-posterior band traction over the talus opens the anterior joint space and restores normal roll-and-glide arthrokinematics.

jointActions: Arthrokinematic mobilization; closed chain; anterior joint-space decompression

execution.startingPosition: Anchor a heavy monster band low behind you and place your affected foot up on a 6-to-12-inch box
execution.description: In Anterior Ankle Impingement (soft-tissue anterolateral gutter scar or mild tibiotalar osteophytes) and Ankle OA, the talus fails to glide posteriorly during dorsiflexion, causing the anterior tibial lip to slam into the talar neck. Applying a strong downward-and-posterior band traction over the talus opens the anterior joint space and restores normal roll-and-glide arthrokinematics.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Anchor a heavy monster band low behind you and place your affected foot up on a 6-to-12-inch box

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Position the band strictly across the anterior neck of the talus (below the medial and lateral malleoli) and angle the band so it pulls backward and downward at a 30°–45° angle

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step forward until the band pulls very firmly on the talus (creating joint distraction and a posterior talar glide)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Slowly rock your knee forward over your second toe only up to the point just before any anterior pinch is felt (0/10 pinch!), hold 3 seconds while actively contracting the tibialis anterior (pulling the shin forward), and rock back for 12-15 reps.

coachingCues: "Let the heavy band pull the front of your ankle bone down and back, and stop your forward knee rock a hair before any front pinch" (external).
commonErrors: Pushing aggressively into the sharp anterior pinch (crushes the inflamed anterior synovium and worsens swelling!); placing the band too high above the ankle bones on the tibia.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Long-axis supine talocrural joint distraction (looping a figure-8 strap around the midfoot/ankle and gently tractioning the joint inline without bending into dorsiflexion).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Combine with a 1-cm heel lift under the rearfoot during daily walking/squatting to reduce repetitive anterior impingement while tissues calm down.

precautions: Pushing aggressively into the sharp anterior pinch (crushes the inflamed anterior synovium and worsens swelling!); placing the band too high above the ankle bones on the tibia.Cues: "Let the heavy band pull the front of your ankle bone down and back, and stop your forward knee rock a hair before any front pinch" (external).
clinicalNotes: In Anterior Ankle Impingement (soft-tissue anterolateral gutter scar or mild tibiotalar osteophytes) and Ankle OA, the talus fails to glide posteriorly during dorsiflexion, causing the anterior tibial lip to slam into the talar neck. Applying a strong downward-and-posterior band traction over the talus opens the anterior joint space and restores normal roll-and-glide arthrokinematics.

name: Seated FHL tendon gliding & isolated big-toe isometric press (Posterior / FHL)

description: In Posterior Ankle Impingement and FHL Stenosing Tenosynovitis ("Dancer's Tendinitis"), the FHL muscle belly sits low in the calf and gets wedged into the narrow fibro-osseous tunnel between the medial and lateral posterior talar tubercles ("the cork in the bottle sign"). Gliding and loading the FHL with the ankle at 0° neutral rehabilitates the tendon while keeping the posterior talar space completely open and decompressed!

jointActions: Tendon glide + isometric; open/closed chain; posterior talar tunnel decompression

execution.startingPosition: Part A (FHL Tendon Glides in Neutral Ankle): Sit with the ankle held at 0° neutral (NOT pointed down into plantarflexion, which pinches the posterior tunnel!). Slowly flex the big toe down and extend it up 15 times to glide the FHL tendon smoothly through the fibro-osseous tunnel behind the medial malleolus without bony posterior compression
execution.description: In Posterior Ankle Impingement and FHL Stenosing Tenosynovitis ("Dancer's Tendinitis"), the FHL muscle belly sits low in the calf and gets wedged into the narrow fibro-osseous tunnel between the medial and lateral posterior talar tubercles ("the cork in the bottle sign"). Gliding and loading the FHL with the ankle at 0° neutral rehabilitates the tendon while keeping the posterior talar space completely open and decompressed!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Part A (FHL Tendon Glides in Neutral Ankle): Sit with the ankle held at 0° neutral (NOT pointed down into plantarflexion, which pinches the posterior tunnel!). Slowly flex the big toe down and extend it up 15 times to glide the FHL tendon smoothly through the fibro-osseous tunnel behind the medial malleolus without bony posterior compression

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Part B (Flat-Toe Isometric FHL Press): Stand or sit with the foot flat on the floor (or with the big toe hanging over the edge of a book) and press the pad of the big toe straight down into the floor (keeping the IP joint flat—no toe curling!) for 5 x 30-second holds at 60% effort.

coachingCues: "Keep your ankle at a 90-degree L-shape so the back of your ankle stays wide open, and press the flat pad of your big toe straight down without clawing the tip" (external).
commonErrors: Performing big-toe curls while the ankle is pointed in maximal plantarflexion (maximally pinches the FHL tendon and os trigonum in the posterior ankle!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Passive big-toe mobilization and gentle calf myofascial release if active FHL gliding clicks or catches painfully.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Resisted eccentric-concentric big-toe flexion with a resistance band while keeping the ankle at 0° neutral.

precautions: Performing big-toe curls while the ankle is pointed in maximal plantarflexion (maximally pinches the FHL tendon and os trigonum in the posterior ankle!).Cues: "Keep your ankle at a 90-degree L-shape so the back of your ankle stays wide open, and press the flat pad of your big toe straight down without clawing the tip" (external).

name: Flat-ground heel raise with relaxed toes (stopping shy of posterior pinch)
chineseName: 放鬆腳趾平地提踵 (止於後側夾擠角度前)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化

description: Dancers, gymnasts, and soccer players with Posterior Ankle Impingement / FHL Tendinopathy almost universally have weak gastrocnemius-soleus muscles and compensate by over-recruiting the FHL (clawing the big toe) to push off the ground. Training heel raises in the pain-free mid-range while keeping the toes relaxed teaches the gastroc-soleus to do its job and immediately unloads the posterior talar tunnel.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; gastroc-soleus vs. FHL dissociation

execution.startingPosition: Stand barefoot on a flat floor facing a wall
execution.description: Dancers, gymnasts, and soccer players with Posterior Ankle Impingement / FHL Tendinopathy almost universally have weak gastrocnemius-soleus muscles and compensate by over-recruiting the FHL (clawing the big toe) to push off the ground. Training heel raises in the pain-free mid-range while keeping the toes relaxed teaches the gastroc-soleus to do its job and immediately unloads the posterior talar tunnel.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand barefoot on a flat floor facing a wall

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Rise onto the balls of the feet over 3 seconds, stopping 5°–10° below the end-range height where posterior ankle pinching occurs (for Posterior Impingement) or starting from flat ground without dropping below step level (for Anterior Impingement)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Crucial Motor Control Check: At the top of the heel raise, tap or wiggle all five toes lightly to prove that your toes are completely relaxed and flat—not clawing into the floor

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Stop an inch below the pinch at the back of your ankle, and keep your toes long and relaxed like piano keys on the floor" (external).
commonErrors: Forcing the heel raise all the way into the painful posterior bony block ("pushing through the pinch" crushes the os trigonum/posterior capsule and perpetuates inflammation!); gripping the floor with the big toe.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated calf raises or bilateral heel raises to 50% height.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg heel raises stopping just shy of the posterior pinch ceiling; gradually expand top height as posterior synovitis resolves.

precautions: Forcing the heel raise all the way into the painful posterior bony block ("pushing through the pinch" crushes the os trigonum/posterior capsule and perpetuates inflammation!); gripping the floor with the big toe.Cues: "Stop an inch below the pinch at the back of your ankle, and keep your toes long and relaxed like piano keys on the floor" (external).
clinicalNotes: Dancers, gymnasts, and soccer players with Posterior Ankle Impingement / FHL Tendinopathy almost universally have weak gastrocnemius-soleus muscles and compensate by over-recruiting the FHL (clawing the big toe) to push off the ground. Training heel raises in the pain-free mid-range while keeping the toes relaxed teaches the gastroc-soleus to do its job and immediately unloads the posterior talar tunnel.

name: Resisted FHL band flexion & Toe-Off towel press (FHL Stage 2 HSR)
chineseName: 彈力帶屈拇長肌抗阻彎曲與蹬地毛巾下壓 (FHL二期HSR)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Rebuilds high tensile capacity in the Flexor Hallucis Longus tendon and muscle belly so it can tolerate the extreme propulsion demands of jumping, sprinting, and ballet relevé without developing tendinosis or triggering tenosynovitis.

jointActions: Open/closed chain; slow eccentric/concentric; isolated FHL tendon remodeling

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the leg extended and the ankle held at 0° neutral
execution.description: Rebuilds high tensile capacity in the Flexor Hallucis Longus tendon and muscle belly so it can tolerate the extreme propulsion demands of jumping, sprinting, and ballet relevé without developing tendinosis or triggering tenosynovitis.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the leg extended and the ankle held at 0° neutral

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a flat resistance band around the plantar pad of the big toe (first phalanx), holding the band taut with your hands

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep the interphalangeal (IP) joint of the big toe straight (no curling the tip) and press the whole big toe downward at the MTP joint over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and let the band pull the big toe back up into extension over a slow 4-second eccentric count.

coachingCues: "Keep your big toe straight like a popsicle stick and press it down from the main knuckle, then fight the band for 4 slow seconds on the way back" (external).
commonErrors: Flexing the distal tip of the big toe (hammer-clawing) instead of flexing from the first MTP knuckle; letting the ankle drop into full plantarflexion during early FHL loading.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Isometric big-toe presses at neutral MTP angle.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing "Vele's Forward Lean" (leaning the whole body forward from the ankles while pressing the flat big toes into the floor to prevent falling forward); single-leg heel raise off a step with a small pad under the big toe once posterior impingement is resolved.

precautions: Flexing the distal tip of the big toe (hammer-clawing) instead of flexing from the first MTP knuckle; letting the ankle drop into full plantarflexion during early FHL loading.Cues: "Keep your big toe straight like a popsicle stick and press it down from the main knuckle, then fight the band for 4 slow seconds on the way back" (external).
clinicalNotes: Rebuilds high tensile capacity in the Flexor Hallucis Longus tendon and muscle belly so it can tolerate the extreme propulsion demands of jumping, sprinting, and ballet relevé without developing tendinosis or triggering tenosynovitis.

name: Heel-elevated box squat & vertical-shin RDL (Anterior Impingement offloading)
chineseName: 羅馬尼亞硬舉 (RDL 膕旁肌與臀肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化

description: Athletes with Anterior Ankle Impingement (e.g., from bony osteophytes/spurs) or Talocrural OA often lose quadriceps and gluteal strength because standard flat-foot squats provoke sharp anterior ankle pain at >10° dorsiflexion. Using a heel wedge and vertical-shin hip hinges allows heavy lower-limb strength training with zero anterior tibiotalar contact stress.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic eccentric/concentric; lower-limb strength without DF pinch

execution.startingPosition: For Squats: Place a 0.5-to-1-inch heel wedge or weight plates under both heels and squat down to a box (60°–80° knee flexion)—elevating the heels places the talocrural joint in 10°–15° of relative plantarflexion, allowing deep knee flexion for quadriceps hypertrophy without the tibia impinging against the anterior talus
execution.description: Athletes with Anterior Ankle Impingement (e.g., from bony osteophytes/spurs) or Talocrural OA often lose quadriceps and gluteal strength because standard flat-foot squats provoke sharp anterior ankle pain at >10° dorsiflexion. Using a heel wedge and vertical-shin hip hinges allows heavy lower-limb strength training with zero anterior tibiotalar contact stress.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: For Squats: Place a 0.5-to-1-inch heel wedge or weight plates under both heels and squat down to a box (60°–80° knee flexion)—elevating the heels places the talocrural joint in 10°–15° of relative plantarflexion, allowing deep knee flexion for quadriceps hypertrophy without the tibia impinging against the anterior talus

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: For Posterior Chain: Perform Single-Leg or Bilateral Romanian Deadlifts (RDLs) with a vertical shin (0° ankle dorsiflexion).

coachingCues: "Rest your heels on the wedge so the front of your ankle stays completely pinch-free while your thighs and glutes work hard" (external).
commonErrors: Forcing flat-foot deep squats into an anterior bony block; letting knees collapse medially into valgus.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Higher box height; bodyweight-only squats with heel wedge.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually reduce heel-wedge height as banded posterior talar glides restore pain-free dorsiflexion range; increase dumbbell/barbell load.

precautions: Forcing flat-foot deep squats into an anterior bony block; letting knees collapse medially into valgus.Cues: "Rest your heels on the wedge so the front of your ankle stays completely pinch-free while your thighs and glutes work hard" (external).
clinicalNotes: Athletes with Anterior Ankle Impingement (e.g., from bony osteophytes/spurs) or Talocrural OA often lose quadriceps and gluteal strength because standard flat-foot squats provoke sharp anterior ankle pain at >10° dorsiflexion. Using a heel wedge and vertical-shin hip hinges allows heavy lower-limb strength training with zero anterior tibiotalar contact stress.

name: Seated bent-knee soleus HSR (non-impinging mid-range 0°–25° PF arc)
chineseName: Seated bent-knee soleus HSR (non-impinging mid-range 0°–25° PF arc)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: By operating inside the "Goldilocks mid-range arc" (0° neutral to 25° plantarflexion), both Anterior Impingement patients and Posterior Impingement patients can build massive soleus strength without impinging either the anterior osteophyte or the posterior os trigonum! A strong soleus eccentrically brakes forward tibial progression in Anterior Impingement and provides push-off torque in Posterior Impingement.

jointActions: Closed chain / seated; Heavy Slow Resistance; talocrural shock-absorber capacity

execution.startingPosition: Sit on a seated calf raise machine with knees at 90° and feet on a flat platform
execution.description: By operating inside the "Goldilocks mid-range arc" (0° neutral to 25° plantarflexion), both Anterior Impingement patients and Posterior Impingement patients can build massive soleus strength without impinging either the anterior osteophyte or the posterior os trigonum! A strong soleus eccentrically brakes forward tibial progression in Anterior Impingement and provides push-off torque in Posterior Impingement.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit on a seated calf raise machine with knees at 90° and feet on a flat platform

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press up over 3 seconds into a strong mid-range plantarflexion (stopping 5°–10° before any posterior pinch in Posterior Impingement) and lower over 3 seconds back to flat neutral (stopping before any anterior pinch in Anterior Impingement).

coachingCues: "Work heavily inside your pain-free middle window—stop before the front pinch at the bottom and before the back pinch at the top" (external).
commonErrors: Dropping the heel deep below a step (pinches Anterior Impingement) or forcing violent end-range tiptoe lockout (pinches Posterior Impingement).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral seated calf raises with moderate weight.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg heavy seated calf press.

precautions: Dropping the heel deep below a step (pinches Anterior Impingement) or forcing violent end-range tiptoe lockout (pinches Posterior Impingement).Cues: "Work heavily inside your pain-free middle window—stop before the front pinch at the bottom and before the back pinch at the top" (external).
clinicalNotes: By operating inside the "Goldilocks mid-range arc" (0° neutral to 25° plantarflexion), both Anterior Impingement patients and Posterior Impingement patients can build massive soleus strength without impinging either the anterior osteophyte or the posterior os trigonum! name: Single-leg balance on demi-pointe / tripod foot with hip external rotation
chineseName: 單腳站立本體感覺平衡

description: In dancers and kicking athletes, "forcing turnout" from the feet or "sickling" (allowing the ankle to roll into inversion while on demi-pointe) narrows the posterior talar tunnel and pinches the os trigonum and FHL tendon. Training proximal hip external rotation coupled with strict first-and-second-ray alignment keeps the talus centered during weight-bearing plantarflexion.

jointActions: Closed chain; neuromuscular; turnout & subtalar-midtarsal alignment control

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg with a resistance band looped above the knees (anchored medially to pull the knee inward)
execution.description: In dancers and kicking athletes, "forcing turnout" from the feet or "sickling" (allowing the ankle to roll into inversion while on demi-pointe) narrows the posterior talar tunnel and pinches the os trigonum and FHL tendon. Training proximal hip external rotation coupled with strict first-and-second-ray alignment keeps the talus centered during weight-bearing plantarflexion.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with a resistance band looped above the knees (anchored medially to pull the knee inward)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Externally rotate the stance hip from the glutes to align the kneecap strictly over the second toe and establish a tripod foot (or rise to a pain-free 50%–75% demi-pointe for dancers/athletes with Posterior Impingement)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold alignment for 30 seconds while keeping weight centered between the first and second metatarsal heads (never "sickling" outward into inversion or rolling inward into pronation!).

coachingCues: "Turn out from your top hip pockets, press down through your big and second toes, and keep your ankle bone stacked straight over your forefoot" (external).
commonErrors: Sickling the ankle outward toward the pinky toe on demi-pointe; locking the knee into hyperextension.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Flat-foot tripod balance on the floor with banded hip external rotation cue.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add upper-body port de bras / medicine ball reaches or partner perturbations while holding demi-pointe alignment.

precautions: Sickling the ankle outward toward the pinky toe on demi-pointe; locking the knee into hyperextension.Cues: "Turn out from your top hip pockets, press down through your big and second toes, and keep your ankle bone stacked straight over your forefoot" (external).
clinicalNotes: In dancers and kicking athletes, "forcing turnout" from the feet or "sickling" (allowing the ankle to roll into inversion while on demi-pointe) narrows the posterior talar tunnel and pinches the os trigonum and FHL tendon. Training proximal hip external rotation coupled with strict first-and-second-ray alignment keeps the talus centered during weight-bearing plantarflexion.

name: Controlled forefoot pogo hops & kick/relevé deceleration (Late RTS)

description: In soccer players ("Footballer's Ankle"), Posterior Impingement occurs when kicking the ball on the laces forces the ankle into violent end-range plantarflexion, while Anterior Impingement occurs during deep deceleration cuts. Training stiff mid-range pogo hops and active dorsiflexor checkrein control during kicking prevents end-range bony collision upon return to sport.

jointActions: Plyometric / sport-specific; elastic spring without end-range bony block

execution.startingPosition: 1) Exercise A (Mid-Range Forefoot Pogo Hops): Perform 3 sets of 15-20 springy double-to-single-leg pogo hops on the balls of the feet, maintaining ankle stiffness so the heel neither slams into deep dorsiflexion (protecting Anterior Impingement) nor whips into extreme plantarflexion (protecting Posterior Impingement)
execution.description: In soccer players ("Footballer's Ankle"), Posterior Impingement occurs when kicking the ball on the laces forces the ankle into violent end-range plantarflexion, while Anterior Impingement occurs during deep deceleration cuts. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Mid-Range Forefoot Pogo Hops): Perform 3 sets of 15-20 springy double-to-single-leg pogo hops on the balls of the feet, maintaining ankle stiffness so the heel neither slams into deep dorsiflexion (protecting Anterior Impingement) nor whips into extreme plantarflexion (protecting Posterior Impingement)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (Soccer Kick / Instep Band Checkrein for Posterior Impingement): Loop a light resistance band over the dorsum (top) of the forefoot anchored behind you; practice a controlled kicking swing while the tibialis anterior contracts eccentrically at ball-contact simulation to prevent the foot from whipping uncontrollably into bony posterior plantarflexion block!

coachingCues: "Keep your ankle firm and active like a locked boot when striking the ball—never let your foot whip loosely to the end of the joint" (external).
commonErrors: Kicking a heavy wet soccer ball at 100% power with a limp, relaxed ankle on the first day back on the pitch.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Submaximal bilateral rebound heel pulses on flat ground.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Graduated return to ball striking (starting with inside-of-foot passes before laces drives) or full allegro jump combinations in dance; rigid dorsal/posterior athletic taping during initial games to block the final 5° of impingement.

precautions: Kicking a heavy wet soccer ball at 100% power with a limp, relaxed ankle on the first day back on the pitch.Cues: "Keep your ankle firm and active like a locked boot when striking the ball—never let your foot whip loosely to the end of the joint" (external).

name: Inner-to-mid-range isometric calf hold (straight-knee & bent-knee)
chineseName: Inner-to-mid-range isometric calf hold (straight-knee & bent-knee)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: According to Järvinen et al.'s muscle-healing histology and the Green & Pizzari (2022 BJSM) consensus, early gentle isometric contractions in a shortened-to-mid-range position align regenerating myotubes parallel to the lines of stress, promote capillary ingrowth, and prevent muscle atrophy without pulling apart the immature granulation tissue at the myotendinous junction.

jointActions: Closed chain; submaximal isometric; early myofiber alignment & analgesia

execution.startingPosition: Begin in Days 3–7 as soon as standing in shoes is tolerable
execution.description: According to Järvinen et al.'s muscle-healing histology and the Green & Pizzari (2022 BJSM) consensus, early gentle isometric contractions in a shortened-to-mid-range position align regenerating myotubes parallel to the lines of stress, promote capillary ingrowth, and prevent muscle atrophy without pulling apart the immature granulation tissue at the myotendinous junction.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Begin in Days 3–7 as soon as standing in shoes is tolerable

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Position A (Seated Bent-Knee Isometric for Soleus): Sit with knees at 90°, rise halfway up onto the balls of the feet, rest your hands or a light weight on your knees, and hold static for 30–45 seconds at a pain-free intensity (<= 2/10)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Position B (Standing Straight-Knee Isometric for Gastrocnemius): Stand facing a wall, rise into ~20°–30° of plantarflexion (where the torn gastrocnemius fibers are gently approximated, NOT stretched!), shift weight gradually onto the injured leg, and hold static for 30–45 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Complete 5 holds in each position daily.

coachingCues: "Rise halfway up onto the balls of your feet where the calf is shortened and comfortable, and hold rock-steady with zero sharp pain."

regressions.rationale: Seated unloaded isometric plantarflexion against a very light resistance band (starting in 20° plantarflexion).

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Holding the isometric in ankle dorsiflexion (below step level) during the first 10 days—dorsiflexion stretches the acute tear gap and causes re-bleeding!External Cue: "Rise halfway up onto the balls of your feet where the calf is shortened and comfortable, and hold rock-steady with zero sharp pain."
clinicalNotes: According to Järvinen et al.'s muscle-healing histology and the Green & Pizzari (2022 BJSM) consensus, early gentle isometric contractions in a shortened-to-mid-range position align regenerating myotubes parallel to the lines of stress, promote capillary ingrowth, and prevent muscle atrophy without pulling apart the immature granulation tissue at the myotendinous junction.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a flat floor (place a 0.5-inch book under the heels for the first 3–5 days if descending to flat ground still produces a stretch twinge)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Rise smoothly onto the balls of both feet over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower over 3 seconds until the heels kiss the floor

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Perform 3 sets with the knees straight (gastrocnemius) and 3 sets with the knees bent at 30°–45° (soleus).

coachingCues: "Press straight through your big-toe knuckle to make sure the inner half of your calf works evenly."
commonErrors: Rolling onto the lateral pinky toes to avoid loading the medial head of the gastrocnemius (the medial head is injured in >80% of "Tennis Leg" tears, so patients instinctively supinate onto the lateral foot to offload the medial gastrocnemius—always cue pressing through the first metatarsal head / big-toe ball!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Support 20%–30% of body weight with hands on a countertop or parallel bars.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress from Bilateral (50/50) -> 2-Up / 1-Down (eccentric lowering on the injured leg to flat ground) -> Pure Single-Leg Flat-Ground Heel Raises.

precautions: Rolling onto the lateral pinky toes to avoid loading the medial head of the gastrocnemius (the medial head is injured in >80% of "Tennis Leg" tears, so patients instinctively supinate onto the lateral foot to offload the medial gastrocnemius—always cue pressing through the first metatarsal head / big-toe ball!).External Cue: "Press straight through your big-toe knuckle to make sure the inner half of your calf works evenly."
clinicalNotes: Safely transitions from static isometrics to dynamic concentric-eccentric excursion while using the flat floor as a physical safety stop so the healing myotendinous junction cannot accidentally drop into over-lengthened dorsiflexion.

name: Step-edge eccentric long-length heel drop (sarcomerogenesis protocol)

description: After a muscle strain heals, the scar shortens the adjacent muscle fascicles, shifting the muscle's optimal length-tension curve to a shorter angle and leaving it vulnerable to re-tearing when stretched during sprinting or lunging. Slow eccentric loading into outer-range dorsiflexion stimulates longitudinal sarcomerogenesis (adding new sarcomeres in series), restoring fascicle length and outer-range strength!

primaryMuscles: Gastrocnemius (straight knee) and soleus (bent knee) at long muscle lengths
jointActions: Closed chain; slow eccentric through full dorsiflexion; fascicle lengthening

execution.startingPosition: 1) Clearance Gate: Begin only once flat-ground single-leg heel raises are pain-free and walking produces 0/10 pain (typically Week 3–4+)
execution.description: After a muscle strain heals, the scar shortens the adjacent muscle fascicles, shifting the muscle's optimal length-tension curve to a shorter angle and leaving it vulnerable to re-tearing when stretched during sprinting or lunging. Slow eccentric loading into outer-range dorsiflexion stimulates longitudinal sarcomerogenesis (adding new sarcomeres in series), restoring fascicle length and outer-range strength!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Clearance Gate: Begin only once flat-ground single-leg heel raises are pain-free and walking produces 0/10 pain (typically Week 3–4+)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand with the balls of the feet on a step edge

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Rise up using both legs (or the injured leg), then lower the injured heel slowly over a strict 4-second eccentric count below the level of the step into comfortable outer-range dorsiflexion stretch

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Perform 3 sets with the knee locked straight (lengthening the bi-articular gastrocnemius across both knee and ankle!) and 3 sets with the knee bent 35° (lengthening the soleus).

coachingCues: "Lower slowly for 4 seconds into a gentle, controlled stretch below the step, then drive smoothly back up."
commonErrors: Introducing below-step eccentric drops too early in Week 1 (causes scar elongation or re-tear); bouncing at the bottom of the step.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Limit the drop below the step to half-depth (5° dorsiflexion) before progressing to full dorsiflexion.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add external dumbbell or backpack weight; perform both eccentric and concentric phases unilaterally off the step.

precautions: Introducing below-step eccentric drops too early in Week 1 (causes scar elongation or re-tear); bouncing at the bottom of the step.External Cue: "Lower slowly for 4 seconds into a gentle, controlled stretch below the step, then drive smoothly back up."

description: Highlighted in the 2022 BJSM Calf Consensus: athletes rarely tear their calf standing straight up vertically—they tear it in a split-stance lunge or acceleration lean! Training the Front-Leg Bent-Knee Lunge Heel Raise builds deep soleus braking/propulsion, while the Rear-Leg Straight-Knee Lean Heel Raise trains the medial gastrocnemius in the exact bi-articular posture of "Tennis Leg"!

jointActions: Closed chain; functional isometric/isotonic; horizontal push-off angle specificity

execution.startingPosition: Position A (Front-Foot Lunge Heel Raise — Soleus Acceleration Bias): Drop into a split-squat lunge with the injured leg in front (front knee bent at 60°–80°, torso inclined slightly forward). Hold the lunge depth completely still while raising and lowering the front heel 12–15 times (or holding a 30s isometric with dumbbells!)
execution.description: Highlighted in the 2022 BJSM Calf Consensus: athletes rarely tear their calf standing straight up vertically—they tear it in a split-stance lunge or acceleration lean! steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Position A (Front-Foot Lunge Heel Raise — Soleus Acceleration Bias): Drop into a split-squat lunge with the injured leg in front (front knee bent at 60°–80°, torso inclined slightly forward). Hold the lunge depth completely still while raising and lowering the front heel 12–15 times (or holding a 30s isometric with dumbbells!)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Position B (Rear-Foot Lunge Push-Off — Gastrocnemius "Tennis Leg" Bias): Place the injured leg in back in a long split stance with the back knee nearly straight and torso leaning forward at 45° (the exact sprint acceleration / tennis lunge posture!), and drive through the back forefoot for 12–15 slow heel raises.

coachingCues: "Freeze your hips and knees at one constant height, and move purely through your ankle and big-toe ball."
commonErrors: Letting the hips rise and fall with the quads instead of isolating the movement strictly to the ankle while the knee angle stays frozen.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Unweighted split-stance isometric heel-raise holds for 30 seconds.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold heavy dumbbells in both hands or a barbell across the shoulders; progress to explosive split-squat switches.

precautions: Letting the hips rise and fall with the quads instead of isolating the movement strictly to the ankle while the knee angle stays frozen.External Cue: "Freeze your hips and knees at one constant height, and move purely through your ankle and big-toe ball."

Athletes must master vertical hops first, then horizontal hops, before high-speed sprinting.

jointActions: Plyometric; fast stretch-shortening cycle; vertical -> horizontal vector transition

execution.startingPosition: Step 1 (Vertical Pogo Hops — Lower Calf Strain): Perform 3 sets of 20 crisp double-leg -> alternating -> single-leg vertical pogo hops in place

steps.instruction: Step 2 (Horizontal Forward & Diagonal Hops — Higher Gastrocnemius/Soleus Strain): Once vertical hops are 100% pain-free the next morning, progress to single-leg forward pogo hops over mini-cones and forward-backward line hops (horizontal propulsion requires the ankle to dorsiflex further and the knee to extend simultaneously, testing the exact "Tennis Leg" stretch-shortening mechanism!).

Drive one knee up to 90° hip flexion with the ankle dorsiflexed, then punch the foot rapidly down and back into the floor (simultaneous hip extension, knee extension, and ankle plantarflexion—the exact bi-articular Gastrocnemius action!) for 3 sets of 8–10 switches

name: Peroneal myofascial decompression & Cuboid self-mobilization (Cuboid Stage 1)
chineseName: Peroneal myofascial decompression & Cuboid self-mobilization (Cuboid Stage 1)

description: In Cuboid Syndrome, a hypertonic peroneus longus pulls the plantar aspect of the cuboid medially and downward during pronation, locking the calcaneocuboid joint. Releasing the proximal peroneus longus muscle belly reduces the bowstring tension on the cuboid groove, while the felt cuboid pad holds the plantar cuboid elevated in its anatomical mortise during weight-bearing.

jointActions: Arthrokinematic / myofascial; open chain; calcaneocuboid pulley decompression

execution.startingPosition: 1) Indications: Perform for Cuboid Syndrome (do NOT perform over a 5th Metatarsal Fracture!)
execution.description: In Cuboid Syndrome, a hypertonic peroneus longus pulls the plantar aspect of the cuboid medially and downward during pronation, locking the calcaneocuboid joint. Releasing the proximal peroneus longus muscle belly reduces the bowstring tension on the cuboid groove, while the felt cuboid pad holds the plantar cuboid elevated in its anatomical mortise during weight-bearing.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Indications: Perform for Cuboid Syndrome (do NOT perform over a 5th Metatarsal Fracture!)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step A (Peroneus Longus Muscle-Belly Release — 90s): Sit and place a foam roller or massage ball under the upper-outer calf (proximal fibular shaft—well away from the ankle and foot!) to gently relax hypertonic trigger points in the peroneus longus muscle belly that are pulling on the cuboid pulley

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step B (Dorsal-Plantar Cuboid Glide & Pad Support): Following clinician Cuboid Whip/Squeeze reduction (Jennings & Davies, JOSPT), sit and grasp the cuboid bone (just behind the 4th and 5th metatarsal bases, in front of the calcaneus) between your thumbs and index fingers, gently gliding it dorsally while flexing/extending the 4th and 5th toes for 10-15 oscillations, then secure a felt Cuboid Pad under the plantar cuboid held with low-Dye antipronation tape.

coachingCues: "Relax the tight outer calf muscle first, and keep the felt pad tucked right under the cuboid bone behind the outer bump of your foot" (external).
commonErrors: Placing the felt cuboid pad too far forward under the base of the 5th metatarsal (blocks 5th ray flexion and actually pushes the cuboid downward out of place—the pad must stop behind the 5th metatarsal tuberosity directly under the cuboid body!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Clinician manual Cuboid Squeeze / Cuboid Whip manipulation prior to self-care.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Transition to intrinsic Short-Foot and Tibialis Posterior arch-locking exercises so the midfoot stays elevated without needing the felt pad.

precautions: Placing the felt cuboid pad too far forward under the base of the 5th metatarsal (blocks 5th ray flexion and actually pushes the cuboid downward out of place—the pad must stop behind the 5th metatarsal tuberosity directly under the cuboid body!). Cues: "Relax the tight outer calf muscle first, and keep the felt pad tucked right under the cuboid bone behind the outer bump of your foot" (external).
clinicalNotes: In Cuboid Syndrome, a hypertonic peroneus longus pulls the plantar aspect of the cuboid medially and downward during pronation, locking the calcaneocuboid joint. Releasing the proximal peroneus longus muscle belly reduces the bowstring tension on the cuboid groove, while the felt cuboid pad holds the plantar cuboid elevated in its anatomical mortise during weight-bearing.

name: Non-weight-bearing sagittal ankle pumps & 4-way hip/quad series (5th Met Stage 1)
chineseName: Non-weight-bearing sagittal ankle pumps & 4-way hip/quad series (5th Met Stage 1)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Why must inversion and eversion be avoided in early 5th Metatarsal Base Fractures? Inversion passively pulls the peroneus brevis tendon and lateral plantar aponeurosis taut, distracting the fracture gap; active eversion contracts the peroneus brevis, pulling directly on the 5th metatarsal styloid! Pure gentle sagittal ankle motion prevents talocrural stiffness and DVT without stressing the 5th metatarsal base, while 4-way hip work prevents proximal gluteal atrophy.

steps.instruction: Step 1 (Sagittal Pogo Hops): Perform 3 sets of 15-20 bilateral -> single-leg forefoot pogo hops, landing evenly across the 1st-through-5th metatarsal heads

steps.instruction: Step 2 (Lateral Deceleration & 45° Cuts — Peak Lateral Column Test): Because lateral cutting and stopping on the outside foot place maximum bending and shear stress directly on the 5th metatarsal shaft (the primary mechanism of Jones Fractures in basketball and soccer players!), progress gradually from 50% speed lateral side-steps -> lateral bounds to stick -> 100% reactive 45° cuts (wearing a custom orthotic with a slight lateral forefoot post or carbon plate if prescribed for Jones fracture protection).

progressions.name: 進階方案
