name: Kim's "Toe-Spread-Out" (TSO) exercise (Hallux Valgus correction)
chineseName: 防膝外翻臀肌與動態對齊控制
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Landmark EMG and ultrasound research by Kim et al. (2013 & 2016, JOSPT) demonstrated that the Toe-Spread-Out (TSO) exercise achieves significantly higher selective activation of the abductor hallucis (relative to the adductor hallucis) and greater increase in abductor hallucis cross-sectional area than the traditional Short-Foot exercise, reducing the Hallux Valgus Angle over an 8-week program!

jointActions: Intrinsic motor control; closed chain; selective abductor hallucis hypertrophy

execution.startingPosition: Sit in a chair with your hip and knee at 90° and your bare foot flat on the floor
execution.description: Landmark EMG and ultrasound research by Kim et al. (2013 & 2016, JOSPT) demonstrated that the Toe-Spread-Out (TSO) exercise achieves significantly higher selective activation of the abductor hallucis (relative to the adductor hallucis) and greater increase in abductor hallucis cross-sectional area than the traditional Short-Foot exercise, reducing the Hallux Valgus Angle over an 8-week program!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit in a chair with your hip and knee at 90° and your bare foot flat on the floor

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step 1: Keep your heel and the balls of your foot (metatarsal heads) planted on the floor and lift all five toes slightly upward

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step 2: Push your pinky toe (5th toe) downward and outward to the lateral floor while keeping the other toes up

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Step 3: Pull your big toe (hallux) medially (inward away from the second toe) and downward onto the floor, holding that wide spread for 5 full seconds

steps.title: 步驟 5
steps.instruction: Relax and repeat for 12-15 repetitions.

coachingCues: "Lift all five toes, drop your pinky toe out wide, then reach your big toe inward toward your other foot to open a wide gap between your first and second toes" (external).
commonErrors: Curling/clawing the big toe downward without spreading it medially away from the second toe; rolling the ankle outward into supination to fake toe abduction.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Use your fingers to gently assist the big toe into medial abduction for the first 5 reps until the brain reconnects with the abductor hallucis motor units.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform Toe-Spread-Out in standing bilateral stance -> single-leg stance -> use a light mini-band around the two big toes pulling them laterally while you actively abduct both big toes medially against the band.

precautions: Curling/clawing the big toe downward without spreading it medially away from the second toe; rolling the ankle outward into supination to fake toe abduction. Cues: "Lift all five toes, drop your pinky toe out wide, then reach your big toe inward toward your other foot to open a wide gap between your first and second toes" (external).
clinicalNotes: Landmark EMG and ultrasound research by Kim et al. (2013 & 2016, JOSPT) demonstrated that the Toe-Spread-Out (TSO) exercise achieves significantly higher selective activation of the abductor hallucis (relative to the adductor hallucis) and greater increase in abductor hallucis cross-sectional area than the traditional Short-Foot exercise, reducing the Hallux Valgus Angle over an 8-week program!

name: Flat-toe isometric hallux plantarflexion press (Turf Toe / Sesamoid Stage 1)

description: In Grade I–III Turf Toe, the plantar plate and sesamoid-phalangeal ligaments on the bottom of the 1st MTP joint are torn by hyperextension. Because the two tendons of the Flexor Hallucis Brevis (FHB) encapsulate the sesamoids and blend directly into the plantar plate, isometric plantarflexion at 0° neutral strengthens the FHB and FHL to act as a dynamic muscular shield over the plantar plate without stretching the tear into dorsiflexion!

jointActions: Isometric at 0° MTP angle; closed/open chain; plantar plate & sesamoid shield

execution.startingPosition: Sit with your bare foot resting flat on a firm book or board so the 1st MTP joint is at 0° neutral extension (completely flat—never bent upward!). For Sesamoiditis, place a felt Dancer's pad under the forefoot so the tender sesamoids sit in a cutout relief window
execution.description: In Grade I–III Turf Toe, the plantar plate and sesamoid-phalangeal ligaments on the bottom of the 1st MTP joint are torn by hyperextension. Because the two tendons of the Flexor Hallucis Brevis (FHB) encapsulate the sesamoids and blend directly into the plantar plate, isometric plantarflexion at 0° neutral strengthens the FHB and FHL to act as a dynamic muscular shield over the plantar plate without stretching the tear into dorsiflexion!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with your bare foot resting flat on a firm book or board so the 1st MTP joint is at 0° neutral extension (completely flat—never bent upward!). For Sesamoiditis, place a felt Dancer's pad under the forefoot so the tender sesamoids sit in a cutout relief window

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Place a popsicle stick, credit card, or folded resistance band underneath the full length of the big toe

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the big toe completely straight (no curling at the tip joint!), press the entire pad of the big toe downward into the floor/stick at 50%–70% pain-free effort for 30-45 seconds so the therapist cannot slide the card out from under the toe

steps.title: 步驟 4

commonErrors: Extending (bending upward) the big toe during early Turf Toe or Sesamoiditis rehab (re-tears the healing plantar plate and pulls the sesamoids apart!); curling the distal tip of the toe instead of pressing flat from the MTP joint.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Gentle 30% effort presses with the ankle slightly plantarflexed to slacken the FHL.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Pull on the resistance band under the big toe to increase isometric demand; progress to Vele's Forward Lean in standing.

precautions: Extending (bending upward) the big toe during early Turf Toe or Sesamoiditis rehab (re-tears the healing plantar plate and pulls the sesamoids apart!); curling the distal tip of the toe instead of pressing flat from the MTP joint. clinicalNotes: In Grade I–III Turf Toe, the plantar plate and sesamoid-phalangeal ligaments on the bottom of the 1st MTP joint are torn by hyperextension. execution.startingPosition: 1) Indications: Perform for Hallux Limitus / Early Hallux Rigidus and Hallux Valgus (do NOT perform dorsiflexion stretches in acute Turf Toe!)

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Indications: Perform for Hallux Limitus / Early Hallux Rigidus and Hallux Valgus (do NOT perform dorsiflexion stretches in acute Turf Toe!)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sit and cross the affected foot over the opposite knee. Stabilize the head of the first metatarsal firmly between the thumb and index finger of one hand

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: With the other hand, grasp the base of the big toe (proximal phalanx) close to the joint line

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Pull the big toe longitudinally away from the foot (long-axis distraction to separate the joint surfaces) and glide the base of the big toe downward toward the sole of the foot (plantar glide) for 10-15 slow oscillations (5s hold each) before gently testing pain-free extension.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Pure long-axis joint distraction holds (5 x 15 seconds) if dorsal osteophytes are inflamed (cheileitis).

progressions.name: 進階方案

Because the heel never lifts off the floor, the big toe never bends into hyperextension, making it the ultimate high-load strengthening exercise for Turf Toe, Sesamoiditis, and Hallux Rigidus.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand barefoot (or with a Dancer's pad for Sesamoiditis) about 6-10 inches facing a wall for safety, with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep your ankles, knees, hips, and spine aligned in one straight plank—and keep your heels and entire feet completely flat on the floor (0° MTP bend!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lean your entire straight body forward from the ankles toward the wall until you feel your toes and arches pressing with maximal force into the floor to stop you from falling forward

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold that peak forward lean for 5-10 seconds (keep toes flat—no clawing!), then use your toe flexors and calves to push your body back to vertical.

coachingCues: "Lean your whole straight body forward from the ankles like a ski jumper while pressing your flat big toes hard into the floor to brake yourself" (external).
commonErrors: Bending at the hips (sticking the buttocks back) instead of leaning forward like a straight falling tree from the ankles; lifting the heels off the floor (which bends the MTP joint!); clawing the tips of the toes.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Decrease the forward lean angle; keep two fingertips lightly touching the wall in front of you.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Shift 70%–100% of weight onto the single affected leg during the forward lean; hold a weight plate at the chest.

precautions: Bending at the hips (sticking the buttocks back) instead of leaning forward like a straight falling tree from the ankles; lifting the heels off the floor (which bends the MTP joint!); clawing the tips of the toes. Pressing the first ray down activates the peroneus longus to plantarflex the first metatarsal head, instantly clearing dorsal joint space at the 1st MTP!

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; first-ray hypermobility control

steps.title: 步驟 2

regressions.rationale: Straight-plane dorsiflexion to neutral only (omitting rotational letters if inversion is painful).

progressions.rationale: Add seated isometric eversion holds (pressing the outer edge of the foot against a wall or couch leg for 5 x 30s).

precautions: Aggressively stretching the ankle downward and inward (plantarflexion + inversion) in the first 3-4 weeks to "stretch out stiffness"—this re-ruptures the delicate Type III collagen bridging the ATFL! Cues: "Pull your toes straight up toward your shin to lock the ankle securely, and avoid rolling the sole of your foot inward" (external).

Early dorsiflexion pumping clears joint effusion without stretching the torn lateral ligaments.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the heel glued flat to the floor, drive the knee forward over the second toe to touch the wall (hold 3 seconds, return, and repeat for 15 reps)

steps.title: 步驟 4

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 2 Eccentric-Biased Band Eversion (Weeks 2-6+): Sit with legs extended and loop a resistance band around the forefoot anchored medially. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand barefoot near a wall on the affected foot and place a flat resistance band (anchored laterally, pulling taut) or a coin directly underneath the first metatarsal head (the ball of the big toe)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press the ball of the big toe firmly down to trap the band/coin against the floor (activating the peroneus longus)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Rise straight up onto the ball of the foot over 2 seconds while keeping weight centered over the first and second toes—never letting the ankle roll out onto the pinky-toe edge

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top and lower over 3 seconds without losing tension on the band under the big toe.

commonErrors: Letting the ankle roll outward onto the fourth and fifth toes at the top of the calf raise so the band slips out from under the big-toe knuckle.

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Letting the ankle roll outward onto the fourth and fifth toes at the top of the calf raise so the band slips out from under the big-toe knuckle. Cues: "Pin that band under your big-toe knuckle—if your ankle rolls outward even a millimeter, the band will snap away!" (external).

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; lateral sway reduction

execution.startingPosition: Loop a resistance band around both ankles and stand on the injured leg with the first ray anchored firmly on the floor and a soft 10° knee bend

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a resistance band around both ankles and stand on the injured leg with the first ray anchored firmly on the floor and a soft 10° knee bend

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain a level pelvis and push the uninjured leg outward against the band for 12-15 repetitions over a 2s out / 3s return tempo (forcing the injured stance ankle evertors and ipsilateral gluteus medius to stabilize against lateral sway)

steps.title: 步驟 3

According to the 2021 JOSPT Ankle CPG (Level A evidence), progressive single-leg balance and perturbation training cuts recurrent ankle sprain risk by ~40%–50% by restoring feed-forward peroneal pre-activation.

jointActions: Proprioceptive; neuromuscular; mechanoreceptor & reflex latency recalibration

execution.startingPosition: Stand barefoot on the injured leg (forming an active "tripod foot" between the heel, big-toe ball, and pinky-toe ball) on a firm floor, progressing to a foam pad or wobble disc

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand barefoot on the injured leg (forming an active "tripod foot" between the heel, big-toe ball, and pinky-toe ball) on a firm floor, progressing to a foam pad or wobble disc

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain a soft 15° knee bend and level hips for 30-45 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Add external perturbations: toss and catch a medicine ball or tennis ball off a rebounder/wall at varying heights and lateral angles while preventing the ankle from rolling into inversion.

commonErrors: Clawing the toes or rolling onto the lateral border of the foot to "hang" on passive lateral ligaments instead of keeping the first metatarsal head down.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Single-leg balance on firm floor with eyes open; tandem stance (heel-to-toe) if single-leg stance is unsteady.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Eyes closed on firm floor -> eyes open on foam pad/wobble board -> eyes closed on foam pad -> reactive partner band taps around the pelvis/shoulders.

precautions: Clawing the toes or rolling onto the lateral border of the foot to "hang" on passive lateral ligaments instead of keeping the first metatarsal head down. name: Multi-planar single-leg hop-to-stabilization (CAI return-to-sport)

description: Lateral hops place high frontal-plane inversion moments on the ankle at ground contact. Because the human spinal stretch reflex takes ~60–80 milliseconds—whereas an inversion ankle sprain happens in <40 milliseconds—the brain must learn to pre-activate the peroneus longus 100 milliseconds before the foot hits the floor! Multi-planar hop-to-stabilization rewires this central feed-forward landing program.

jointActions: Plyometric; reactive dynamic stabilization; inversion-moment feed-forward control

execution.startingPosition: Place 4 tape marks on the floor in a cross pattern (forward, backward, medial, lateral) 1.5 to 2.5 feet apart (or use the Side Hop Test lines spaced 30 cm apart)
execution.description: Lateral hops place high frontal-plane inversion moments on the ankle at ground contact. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place 4 tape marks on the floor in a cross pattern (forward, backward, medial, lateral) 1.5 to 2.5 feet apart (or use the Side Hop Test lines spaced 30 cm apart)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand on the injured leg, hop forward onto the target mark, and stick the landing on the ball-to-midfoot with a soft 45° knee bend and flat tripod foot, holding completely motionless for 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Repeat hopping laterally (side-to-side across the ankle's inversion/eversion axis) and diagonally, sticking every landing for 3 seconds before progressing to rapid continuous side hops.

coachingCues: "Pre-set your foot wide and flat in the air before you land—stick the floor through your big-toe ball and freeze for 3 seconds" (external).
commonErrors: Landing with the forefoot inverted ("supinated catch") or with a stiff knee; taking extra corrective hops.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Double-leg multi-planar hops (pogo hops across a line); low-amplitude forward step-and-hop.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a 90° or 180° rotational hop-and-stick; hop onto a Bosu/foam pad; transition to reactive cutting drills.

precautions: Landing with the forefoot inverted ("supinated catch") or with a stiff knee; taking extra corrective hops. Cues: "Pre-set your foot wide and flat in the air before you land—stick the floor through your big-toe ball and freeze for 3 seconds" (external).

name: "Intrinsic Plus" Lumbrical tabletop press & paper-grip exercise

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化

description: The lumbricals and interossei perform a unique biomechanical action called the "Intrinsic Plus" movement: they flex the MTP joints while simultaneously extending (straightening) the PIP and DIP toe joints! When the lumbricals are weak, the extrinsic toe extensors (EDL) pull the MTP joints into hyperextension (clawing the toes), which drags the protective plantar fat pad forward off the metatarsal heads and exposes the bones and interdigital nerves to direct floor impact! The flat-toe paper-grip exercise selectively restores lumbrical function, pulling the proximal phalanges and plantar fat pad back underneath the metatarsal heads.

steps.instruction: Keeping all five toes completely straight and flat at the middle and tip joints (zero curling/clawing!), press the straight toes downward from the main knuckles (MTP joints) into the paper for 6 seconds so someone pulling the paper cannot slide it out

name: Peroneus Longus + Tibialis Posterior "Midfoot Stirrup" band series (Lisfranc)

description: Anatomical cadaver studies prove that the Peroneus Longus and Tibialis Posterior tendons cross each other on the plantar aspect of the tarsometatarsal joints to form an anatomical "Dynamic Midfoot Stirrup." Specifically, the Peroneus Longus inserts onto the lateral aspect of the medial cuneiform and base of the 1st metatarsal—when it contracts, it pulls the 1st ray laterally and plantarward tightly against the base of the 2nd metatarsal, directly compressing and stabilizing the Lisfranc joint!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the ankle in neutral-to-slight plantarflexion (never forcing midfoot twisting)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Peroneus Longus First-Ray Depression & Eversion): Loop a resistance band around the first metatarsal head/forefoot anchored medially; press the first metatarsal downward and outward over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and return to neutral over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Exercise B (Tibialis Posterior Inversion): Anchor the band laterally and sweep the midfoot gently inward in slight plantarflexion over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and return to neutral over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Use slow, smooth tension to tighten the muscular stirrup underneath your midfoot arch" (external).
commonErrors: Applying the band around the distal toes and twisting the forefoot aggressively (places rotary torque across the healing Lisfranc ligament—place the band slightly higher across the metatarsal shafts/heads and move smoothly!).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing first-ray band press (trapping a laterally pulled band under the big-toe knuckle while maintaining a Short-Foot arch dome).

precautions: Applying the band around the distal toes and twisting the forefoot aggressively (places rotary torque across the healing Lisfranc ligament—place the band slightly higher across the metatarsal shafts/heads and move smoothly!). steps.instruction: Wear supportive athletic shoes with your custom arch orthotic / carbon plate (for Lisfranc) or metatarsal dome pad (for Metatarsalgia / Morton's Neuroma)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand facing a wall with the affected foot in back, toes pointed 5° inward to lock the subtalar/midtarsal joints

description: Biomechanical bone-strain gauge studies prove that the soleus is the single most important muscle for preventing and curing MTSS and Tibial Stress Fractures. During running mid-stance, the soleus must absorb 6–8x body weight while pulling upward and posteriorly to counteract anterior-medial tibial bending. Bending the knee to 90° disengages the gastrocnemius and forces the soleus (and deep posterior FDL/tibialis posterior) to adapt to heavy loads without any running impact shock!

Bending the knee to 90° disengages the gastrocnemius and forces the soleus (and deep posterior FDL/tibialis posterior) to adapt to heavy loads without any running impact shock!

steps.instruction: Stage 2 HSR: Press up to full plantarflexion over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower slowly over 3 seconds for 3-4 sets of 8-12 heavy reps.

commonErrors: Performing only standing straight-knee calf raises (which bias the gastrocnemius and leave the deep soleus under-loaded!); bouncing at the bottom of the rep.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated bilateral calf raises or seated resistance-band plantarflexion during early non-weight-bearing tibial BSI weeks.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progressively load single-leg seated calf raises toward 1.0–1.5x body weight; pair with standing bent-knee (45° knee bend) Smith-machine calf raises.

precautions: Performing only standing straight-knee calf raises (which bias the gastrocnemius and leave the deep soleus under-loaded!); bouncing at the bottom of the rep.Cues: "Keep your knee bent at 90 degrees, load it heavy, and take 3 full seconds up and 3 full seconds down" (external).
clinicalNotes: Biomechanical bone-strain gauge studies prove that the soleus is the single most important muscle for preventing and curing MTSS and Tibial Stress Fractures. During running mid-stance, the soleus must absorb 6–8x body weight while pulling upward and posteriorly to counteract anterior-medial tibial bending. Bending the knee to 90° disengages the gastrocnemius and forces the soleus (and deep posterior FDL/tibialis posterior) to adapt to heavy loads without any running impact shock!

description: Excessive navicular drop (>10 mm) and prolonged subtalar pronation during mid-stance are Level A risk factors for MTSS in systematic reviews (Newman et al.; Hamstra-Wright et al.) because pronation forces obligatory internal tibial torsion, adding torsional shear to sagittal tibial bending! jointActions: Closed chain; intrinsic foot strengthening; reducing internal tibial twist

execution.startingPosition: Sit, then stand barefoot with weight on the tripod foot

steps.title: 步驟 1

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Without curling the toes, draw the ball of the big toe backward toward the heel to raise the navicular and medial longitudinal arch; hold for 6 seconds and repeat for 12-15 reps.

description: Simultaneously loads the gastrocnemius, soleus, and tibialis posterior in weight-bearing while the tennis ball locks the calcaneus in inversion, training the exact muscular synergy that stiffens the ankle-tibia complex during the propulsive phase of running.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic HSR; weight-bearing posteromedial muscular corset

execution.startingPosition: Stand on flat ground (progressing to a step edge once posteromedial shin tenderness is <= 1/10) with a tennis ball squeezed between your inner heels just below the medial malleoli
execution.description: Simultaneously loads the gastrocnemius, soleus, and tibialis posterior in weight-bearing while the tennis ball locks the calcaneus in inversion, training the exact muscular synergy that stiffens the ankle-tibia complex during the propulsive phase of running.

steps.instruction: Rise slowly onto the balls of the feet over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top while keeping the ball pinched, and lower over 3-4 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3

name: Metronome cadence (+5%–10%) & midfoot-strike retraining (Diebal CECS / MTSS)
chineseName: Metronome cadence (+5%–10%) & midfoot-strike retraining (Diebal CECS / MTSS)

description: For MTSS and Tibial Stress Fractures, increasing cadence by 5%–10% and widening step width reduces peak tibial vertical loading rate and medial bending moments by 15%–20% on every step! For Anterior CECS, Diebal et al.'s landmark AJSM military studies proved that switching from a rearfoot overstride to a higher-cadence forefoot/midfoot kiss eliminates eccentric tibialis anterior overload, dropping anterior compartment pressures from pathological (>60 mmHg) to normal and resolving CECS without surgery!

jointActions: Neuromuscular gait retraining; closed chain; tibial load & compartment decompression

execution.startingPosition: 1) Measure your natural running cadence (steps per minute) and set a metronome app 5% to 10% higher (typically targeting ~172–180 spm) while keeping running speed slow and easy
execution.description: For MTSS and Tibial Stress Fractures, increasing cadence by 5%–10% and widening step width reduces peak tibial vertical loading rate and medial bending moments by 15%–20% on every step! For Anterior CECS, Diebal et al.'s landmark AJSM military studies proved that switching from a rearfoot overstride to a higher-cadence forefoot/midfoot kiss eliminates eccentric tibialis anterior overload, dropping anterior compartment pressures from pathological (>60 mmHg) to normal and resolving CECS without surgery!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Measure your natural running cadence (steps per minute) and set a metronome app 5% to 10% higher (typically targeting ~172–180 spm) while keeping running speed slow and easy

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Focus on landing with your foot underneath your hips (eliminating overstriding) with a quiet, flat midfoot or soft forefoot kiss rather than a high-angle dorsiflexed heel-slam (essential for Anterior CECS!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep a 2-inch "window" between your knees/ankles to prevent crossover gait

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Follow a strict every-other-day Walk-Run Progression (e.g. Level 1: 6 x [1 min run / 2 min walk] -> Level 2: 6 x [2 min run / 1 min walk] -> Level 3: 4 x [4 min run / 1 min walk] -> 20 min continuous run), advancing only if pain is 0/10 during and 24 hours after!

coachingCues: "Run like a quiet ninja on hot coals—quick, short steps landing softly right underneath your hips" (external).
commonErrors: Running on consecutive days during return from a Tibial Stress Fracture or MTSS (bone remodeling requires 24–48h between impact bouts!); in CECS, aggressively stretching onto the tiptoes with an exaggerated calf-raise stride instead of simply landing quietly underneath the center of mass.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Uphill treadmill walk-jog intervals (4%–5% grade reduces impact shock) or anti-gravity treadmill / deep-water running.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase total running time by no more than 10%–15% per week while fading the metronome cues over 6 weeks.

precautions: Running on consecutive days during return from a Tibial Stress Fracture or MTSS (bone remodeling requires 24–48h between impact bouts!); in CECS, aggressively stretching onto the tiptoes with an exaggerated calf-raise stride instead of simply landing quietly underneath the center of mass.Cues: "Run like a quiet ninja on hot coals—quick, short steps landing softly right underneath your hips" (external).

name: Seated plantar fascia-specific Windlass stretch (DiGiovanni protocol)

description: Overnight during sleep, the ankle rests in plantarflexion and the plantar fascia contracts in a shortened state; stepping out of bed barefoot suddenly rips micro-adhesions at the medial calcaneal tubercle ("first-step pain"). DiGiovanni et al.'s landmark RCT proved that performing this seated Windlass stretch before weight-bearing produces significantly superior pain relief compared to standing Achilles stretching alone.

jointActions: Flexibility; tissue-specific passive stretch; pre-step morning pain prevention

execution.startingPosition: Perform this in bed before taking your very first step in the morning (and before standing up after sitting >30 minutes)
execution.description: Overnight during sleep, the ankle rests in plantarflexion and the plantar fascia contracts in a shortened state; stepping out of bed barefoot suddenly rips micro-adhesions at the medial calcaneal tubercle ("first-step pain"). steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Perform this in bed before taking your very first step in the morning (and before standing up after sitting >30 minutes)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sit and cross the affected foot over the opposite knee

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Use the hand on the affected side to grasp the base of all five toes (focusing on the big toe) and pull the toes upward toward the shin (maximal MTP dorsiflexion) until you feel a firm stretch in the arch of the foot

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Use your other thumb to palpate and gently massage along the taut plantar fascia band to confirm tension

steps.title: 步驟 5
steps.instruction: Hold for 10 seconds and repeat 10 times.

coachingCues: "Pull your big toe back toward your shin until the cord in your arch feels tight like a guitar string under your thumb—do 10 holds before your foot touches the bedroom floor" (external).
commonErrors: Standing up out of bed barefoot first to walk to the bathroom before doing the stretch (defeats the entire purpose of preventing the morning micro-tear!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Pull the big toe back more gently if sharp insertional heel pain is felt during the stretch.

progressions.name: 進階方案

execution.description: The abductor hallucis and intrinsic plantar muscles act as the immediate local partners to the extrinsic tibialis posterior tendon. steps.title: 步驟 1

description: In healthy biomechanics, rising onto the toes requires the tibialis posterior to fire first to invert the calcaneus and lock the transverse tarsal joint; in PTTD, the calcaneus stays stuck in valgus (eversion) and the patient pushes off an unlocked, collapsed midfoot. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand facing a wall for fingertip support with your feet parallel and place a tennis ball (or small lacrosse/massage ball) snugly between your inner heels, just below the medial ankle bones (medial malleoli)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Gently squeeze the tennis ball between your heels—this automatically brings both calcanei out of valgus and into slight hindfoot inversion

steps.title: 步驟 3

name: Standing gastroc-soleus stretch with 5° toe-in
chineseName: Standing gastroc-soleus stretch with 5° toe-in
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Gastrocnemius-soleus tightness (ankle equinus) is a major driver of PTTD: when the ankle cannot dorsiflex past 5°–10° at the talocrural joint during mid-stance, the body compensates by unlocking the midtarsal joint and collapsing into severe subtalar pronation ("midtarsal break"), which places destructive strain on the tibialis posterior tendon. Stretching the calf with a 5°–10° toe-in locks the midfoot so the stretch goes strictly to the gastroc-soleus rather than collapsing the arch!

name: Seated isometric eversion in neutral/slight plantarflexion
chineseName: 坐姿 踝關節抗阻外翻訓練 (腓骨肌群) (等長維持)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化

description: In Peroneal Tendinopathy (or superior peroneal retinaculum injury), combining dorsiflexion + eversion forces the peroneal tendons forward out of the retromalleolar groove and compresses them violently against the lateral malleolus. Similarly, in a High Ankle Sprain, dorsiflexion + external rotation spreads the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis apart. Performing isometric eversion in neutral or slight plantarflexion delivers analgesic tendon loading to the peroneus longus and brevis while keeping the tendons safely seated in their groove and the mortise narrow!

jointActions: Open chain; heavy isometric; lateral analgesia without mortise wedging or subluxation

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the affected leg extended or supported on a chair and position the ankle in neutral (0°) or slight 10° plantarflexion (strictly avoiding dorsiflexion!)

Performing isometric eversion in neutral or slight plantarflexion delivers analgesic tendon loading to the peroneus longus and brevis while keeping the tendons safely seated in their groove and the mortise narrow!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the affected leg extended or supported on a chair and position the ankle in neutral (0°) or slight 10° plantarflexion (strictly avoiding dorsiflexion!)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a wide resistance band around the lateral forefoot (or press the outer border of the forefoot against a stationary couch leg/wall)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Push the outer edge of the foot outward (pure eversion without externally rotating the leg or dorsiflexing the ankle) at 50%–70% pain-free effort for 45 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rest 1-2 minutes and complete 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Keep your ankle relaxed at neutral or slightly pointed down, hold your shin bone still, and press the pinky-toe edge of your foot gently into the band" (external).
commonErrors: Pulling the toes up into dorsiflexion while pushing outward (triggers peroneal subluxation clicking or anterior syndesmotic pain at the AITFL!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce contraction intensity to 30%–40% effort if lateral retromalleolar pain exceeds 2-3/10.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase isometric hold force to 70%–80% MVIC; transition to slow isotonic band eversion in the neutral-to-eversion outer arc.

precautions: Pulling the toes up into dorsiflexion while pushing outward (triggers peroneal subluxation clicking or anterior syndesmotic pain at the AITFL!). steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in supportive athletic shoes (with a 0.5-cm silicone heel cup inserted for Sever's Disease) facing a wall for balance, feet pointed strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Rise halfway up onto the balls of both feet (into ~15°–20° plantarflexion)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Shift 60%–100% of weight onto the affected foot (keeping pain <= 2/10 at the heel growth plate or anterior syndesmosis) and hold completely static for 30-45 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower smoothly back to the flat floor and rest 1 minute for 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Wear your cushioned shoes, point your feet dead straight at 12 o'clock, and rise halfway up to hold steady" (external).
commonErrors: Performing this barefoot on a hard floor or dropping the heel off a step edge in Sever's Disease or early High Ankle Sprain (both provoke severe flare-ups!).

steps.title: 步驟 2

steps.instruction: Push the outer border of the foot outward into full eversion over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and slowly resist the band back to neutral alignment only over a 4-second eccentric count (do NOT let the band pull the foot into full inversion stretch early, as end-range inversion wraps and compresses the peroneus brevis tendon against the lateral malleolus pulley!).

commonErrors: Letting the band pull the foot all the way into full inversion at the bottom of every rep during acute/subacute Peroneal Tendinopathy (compresses the split-tear zone of peroneus brevis against the fibula!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Isometric eversion holds at mid-range.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress band resistance to heavy blue/black/gold bands; gradually allow eccentric return past neutral into mild inversion in late Stage 2 once retromalleolar tenderness is zero.

precautions: Letting the band pull the foot all the way into full inversion at the bottom of every rep during acute/subacute Peroneal Tendinopathy (compresses the split-tear zone of peroneus brevis against the fibula!). Cues: "Push out for 3 seconds, hold for 2, and stop right at the midline on the way back—don't let your foot roll inward past neutral" (external).
clinicalNotes: Applies the tendon compression-protection principle (Cook & Purdam) to the lateral ankle: just as insertional Achilles tendinopathy avoids end-range dorsiflexion and gluteal tendinopathy avoids hip adduction across midline, Peroneal Tendinopathy must avoid end-range inversion early so the tendon is loaded purely in tension without retromalleolar pulley compression.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a flat floor (with shoes + heel cups for Sever's, or barefoot/shoes with a resistance band trapped under the big-toe knuckle for Peroneal Tendinopathy & High Ankle Sprain)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Align both feet strictly parallel at 12 o'clock (zero external foot turnout, protecting the syndesmosis against external talar torque)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press firmly through the ball of the big toe and rise over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower over 3 seconds back to the flat floor (never dropping below step level!).

progressions.name: 進階方案

name: Neutral-plane squat & step-up
chineseName: 上階梯登階肌力訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: In a High Ankle Sprain, dynamic knee valgus is the #1 enemy during weight-bearing exercises: when the femur and tibia drop medially over a fixed foot, the talus is forced into relative external rotation and pronation inside the mortise, tearing the healing AITFL! Training squats and step-ups with strict 12 o'clock alignment and knee-over-second-toe tracking gradually restores functional dorsiflexion without rotational diastasis.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic eccentric/concentric; graduated sagittal weight-bearing

execution.startingPosition: Stand in front of a 4-to-6-inch step (or perform a box squat) with the affected foot pointed strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock
execution.description: In a High Ankle Sprain, dynamic knee valgus is the #1 enemy during weight-bearing exercises: when the femur and tibia drop medially over a fixed foot, the talus is forced into relative external rotation and pronation inside the mortise, tearing the healing AITFL! steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in front of a 4-to-6-inch step (or perform a box squat) with the affected foot pointed strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly bend the knee forward over the second toe only to a pain-free dorsiflexion angle (keeping zero pinch at the front/outer syndesmosis and zero pull at the calcaneus in Sever's)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Prevent the knee from collapsing inward into valgus (when the knee collapses inward while the foot is planted, it creates a destructive external rotation + dorsiflexion torque across the ankle mortise!)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Press through the heel and midfoot to stand tall.

coachingCues: "Keep your foot pointed at 12 o'clock and your kneecap tracking over your middle toes—never let your knee dip inward" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the knee cave medially inside the big toe (imparts an immediate external rotation stress test to the syndesmosis!); forcing aggressive Knee-to-Wall stretches during the first 6 weeks of a High Ankle Sprain or active Sever's flare.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Vertical-shin box squats (where the shin remains nearly vertical at 0°–5° dorsiflexion, placing zero wedge force on the ankle mortise and zero traction on the Sever's calcaneus!).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually increase forward knee translation (dorsiflexion angle) across Weeks 5-10 as the syndesmosis or calcaneal apophysis heals; add forward step-downs.

precautions: Letting the knee cave medially inside the big toe (imparts an immediate external rotation stress test to the syndesmosis!); forcing aggressive Knee-to-Wall stretches during the first 6 weeks of a High Ankle Sprain or active Sever's flare. Cues: "Keep your foot pointed at 12 o'clock and your kneecap tracking over your middle toes—never let your knee dip inward" (external).

steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg at the center of a Y-grid with the foot pointed at 12 o'clock and the first metatarsal head (big-toe ball) pressed firmly down

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Reach the free foot anteriorly (only as far as pain-free dorsiflexion allows), posteromedially, and posterolaterally

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Critical Rule for High Ankle Sprain: During the posteromedial reach (reaching behind and across your standing leg), actively fire your standing hip external rotators so your standing knee and shin do NOT twist inward over your planted foot!

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Static single-leg balance on a firm floor holding a tripod foot for 30-45 seconds.

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Allowing the standing knee to twist medially while reaching behind the body (recreates the external rotation injury mechanism of a High Ankle Sprain). name: Subtalar-neutral isometric co-contraction (Sinus Tarsi decompression)

description: The sinus tarsi is the "eye of the subtalar joint," packed with free nerve endings and Pacinian/Ruffini mechanoreceptors. When the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament (ITCL) is sprained, the calcaneus shifts into valgus/pronation and crushes the inflamed sinus tarsi tissues. Isometric co-contraction in subtalar neutral teaches the tibialis posterior and peroneals to form a muscular splint that holds the sinus tarsi open and decompressed.

jointActions: Isometric; open/closed chain; Stage 1 ITCL & sinus tarsi stabilization

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the foot resting lightly on the floor and palpate the talar neck with your thumb and index finger to find Subtalar Neutral (where the medial and lateral curves of the talar head feel equally prominent, and the lateral sinus tarsi hollow feels completely open and pain-free)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hold the foot in that exact neutral posture while applying gentle 40%–60% alternating manual or band isometric pressures against the inner forefoot (inversion hold, 15s) and outer forefoot (eversion hold, 15s) without allowing the subtalar joint to move a single millimeter!

coachingCues: "Freeze your heel and arch in the exact middle comfort zone—don't let the band budge your foot inward or outward" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the foot collapse into pronation/eversion (immediately pinches the lateral sinus tarsi) or roll into full inversion (stretches the cervical ligament).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Gentle 30% effort isometric holds in unloaded sitting.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform standing rhythmic stabilization (clinician or partner taps the ankle/leg from different directions while the patient holds subtalar neutral).

precautions: Letting the foot collapse into pronation/eversion (immediately pinches the lateral sinus tarsi) or roll into full inversion (stretches the cervical ligament). Cues: "Freeze your heel and arch in the exact middle comfort zone—don't let the band budge your foot inward or outward" (external).

name: Seated / supine Tibial Nerve Neurodynamic Slider ("Nerve Flossing")
chineseName: Seated / supine Tibial Nerve Neurodynamic Slider ("Nerve Flossing")
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: A Neurodynamic Slider moves the tibial nerve up to 5–10 mm longitudinally through the tarsal tunnel while keeping net intraneural strain near zero. This "milking" motion disperses inflammatory cytokines and intraneural venous congestion (restoring vasa nervorum blood flow) and prevents fibrotic tethering between the tibial nerve and the neighboring FDL/FHL tendons.

primaryMuscles: Tibial nerve tract (sciatic -> tibial -> medial/lateral plantar nerves)
jointActions: Neurodynamic slider; open chain; intraneural oedema clearance without tension

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on the edge of a plinth or chair (or lie supine with the hip flexed to 90° and hands supporting behind the thigh)
execution.description: A Neurodynamic Slider moves the tibial nerve up to 5–10 mm longitudinally through the tarsal tunnel while keeping net intraneural strain near zero. This "milking" motion disperses inflammatory cytokines and intraneural venous congestion (restoring vasa nervorum blood flow) and prevents fibrotic tethering between the tibial nerve and the neighboring FDL/FHL tendons.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on the edge of a plinth or chair (or lie supine with the hip flexed to 90° and hands supporting behind the thigh)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Position 1 (Proximal Glide / Distal Slack): Point the foot downward and slightly inward (plantarflexion + inversion, which slackens the tibial nerve at the ankle) while slowly straightening the knee and extending the neck (looking up)—this pulls the nerve gently upward toward the thigh without stretching it at the ankle

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Position 2 (Distal Glide / Proximal Slack): Simultaneously bend the knee back down (which slackens the sciatic nerve at the thigh) while gently pulling the foot and toes up to neutral dorsiflexion—this glides the nerve gently downward through the tarsal tunnel without pulling from above

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Oscillate smoothly between Position 1 and Position 2 for 10-12 completely pain-free repetitions.

coachingCues: "Think of pulling a silk ribbon smoothly back and forth through a ring—when the knee straightens, the foot points down; when the knee bends, the foot comes up. Never feel a zing or burn!" (external).
commonErrors: Holding the foot pulled hard into dorsiflexion + eversion while kicking the knee straight and slumping the neck forward (this is an aggressive Tensioner that stretches the nerve from both ends simultaneously and triggers severe neuropathic flare-ups!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform in supine with the hip at only 45° flexion and move only the knee while keeping the ankle comfortably plantarflexed/inverted ("one-ended proximal slider").

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: In the late stage (Weeks 6-8+ once Tinel's sign and resting burning are zero), transition gradually to gentle Tensioners (extending the knee while maintaining neutral-to-mild dorsiflexion).

precautions: Holding the foot pulled hard into dorsiflexion + eversion while kicking the knee straight and slumping the neck forward (this is an aggressive Tensioner that stretches the nerve from both ends simultaneously and triggers severe neuropathic flare-ups!).Cues: "Think of pulling a silk ribbon smoothly back and forth through a ring—when the knee straightens, the foot points down; when the knee bends, the foot comes up. Never feel a zing or burn!" (external).
clinicalNotes: A Neurodynamic Slider moves the tibial nerve up to 5–10 mm longitudinally through the tarsal tunnel while keeping net intraneural strain near zero. This "milking" motion disperses inflammatory cytokines and intraneural venous congestion (restoring vasa nervorum blood flow) and prevents fibrotic tethering between the tibial nerve and the neighboring FDL/FHL tendons.

description: Inside the tight tarsal tunnel, the tibial nerve is sandwiched directly between the Flexor Digitorum Longus (anteriorly) and Flexor Hallucis Longus (posteriorly). Tenosynovitis or swelling of these flexor tendons frequently creates perineural adhesions that trap the tibial nerve. Differential tendon gliding with a slackened nerve frees the mechanical interface between the tendons and nerve sheath.

jointActions: Tendon-nerve differential glide; open chain; tarsal tunnel interface mobility

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the knee bent at 90° (slacking the proximal sciatic-tibial nerve) and the ankle resting in slight plantarflexion and inversion (opening the tarsal tunnel roof)
execution.description: Inside the tight tarsal tunnel, the tibial nerve is sandwiched directly between the Flexor Digitorum Longus (anteriorly) and Flexor Hallucis Longus (posteriorly). Tenosynovitis or swelling of these flexor tendons frequently creates perineural adhesions that trap the tibial nerve. Differential tendon gliding with a slackened nerve frees the mechanical interface between the tendons and nerve sheath.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the knee bent at 90° (slacking the proximal sciatic-tibial nerve) and the ankle resting in slight plantarflexion and inversion (opening the tarsal tunnel roof)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly curl and straighten only the big toe 10 times (gliding the FHL tendon past the tibial nerve)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly curl and straighten the four lesser toes 10 times (gliding the FDL tendon past the nerve)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Gently sweep the foot into inversion and back to neutral 10 times (gliding the tibialis posterior tendon).

coachingCues: "Keep your ankle relaxed and slightly tilted inward so the tunnel stays wide open while each tendon glides smoothly one by one" (external).
commonErrors: Performing toe curls with the ankle pulled into dorsiflexion and eversion (narrows the tunnel and rubs the tendons tightly against the compressed nerve).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Passive big-toe and lesser-toe mobilization with the ankle held in plantarflexion-inversion.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add light resistance band toe flexion once gliding is completely smooth and symptom-free.

precautions: Performing toe curls with the ankle pulled into dorsiflexion and eversion (narrows the tunnel and rubs the tendons tightly against the compressed nerve).Cues: "Keep your ankle relaxed and slightly tilted inward so the tunnel stays wide open while each tendon glides smoothly one by one" (external).

primaryMuscles: Tibialis posterior (preventing calcaneal valgus traction on the tibial nerve)

execution.description: Pes planus / hindfoot valgus is the #1 biomechanical cause of idiopathic Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome because every degree of calcaneal eversion stretches the tibial nerve around the medial malleolus pulley. Strengthening the tibialis posterior in its inner-to-mid range prevents valgus collapse during walking.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the ankle in slight plantarflexion and loop a resistance band around the forefoot anchored laterally

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Clamp the shin still with your hands and sweep the forefoot inward into full inversion over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and return slowly over 4 seconds—stopping strictly at neutral alignment (never allowing the band to pull the foot into eversion/pronation where the flexor retinaculum tightens over the tibial nerve!).

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

name: Seated isometric dorsiflexion & mild inversion hold (Stage 1 analgesia)

description: Because the Tibialis Anterior is both an ankle dorsiflexor and a subtalar inverter, holding an isometric contraction in slight dorsiflexion + inversion maximally recruits the tibialis anterior motor units and induces Stage 1 tendon analgesia without sliding the inflamed paratenon repeatedly under the tight extensor retinaculum.

jointActions: Open chain; heavy isometric; extensor retinaculum analgesia & motor activation

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the affected leg supported on a plinth or chair and position the ankle in 0° neutral to 10° dorsiflexion and slight inversion (in this position, the tibialis anterior tendon is slightly lifted away from the underlying talar neck, avoiding plantarflexion wrap-around compression)
execution.description: Because the Tibialis Anterior is both an ankle dorsiflexor and a subtalar inverter, holding an isometric contraction in slight dorsiflexion + inversion maximally recruits the tibialis anterior motor units and induces Stage 1 tendon analgesia without sliding the inflamed paratenon repeatedly under the tight extensor retinaculum.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the affected leg supported on a plinth or chair and position the ankle in 0° neutral to 10° dorsiflexion and slight inversion (in this position, the tibialis anterior tendon is slightly lifted away from the underlying talar neck, avoiding plantarflexion wrap-around compression)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a wide flat resistance band over the medial dorsum of the foot (placing the band over the distal metatarsal heads—NOT over the tender anterior ankle crease!) or cross the unaffected heel over the forefoot

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pull the foot upward and slightly inward against the resistance at 50%–70% pain-free effort for 45 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rest 1-2 minutes and complete 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Place the band down near your toe knuckles, pull your foot up into a solid 90-degree lock, and hold steady for 45 seconds" (external).
commonErrors: Placing the resistance band directly across the inflamed anterior ankle joint line (crushes the extensor retinaculum like a tight shoelace!); stretching the foot into full plantarflexion between sets (stretching wraps the tendon tightly over the anterior tibia and worsens insertional and retinacular pain!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce effort to 30%–40% if tenosynovitis crepitus or sharp anterior pain is present; relace shoes using the "window/ladder lacing" technique to skip the eyelets directly over the inflamed extensor retinaculum!

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase isometric hold force to 75% MVIC; transition to slow eccentric band dorsiflexion.

precautions: Placing the resistance band directly across the inflamed anterior ankle joint line (crushes the extensor retinaculum like a tight shoelace!); stretching the foot into full plantarflexion between sets (stretching wraps the tendon tightly over the anterior tibia and worsens insertional and retinacular pain!).Cues: "Place the band down near your toe knuckles, pull your foot up into a solid 90-degree lock, and hold steady for 45 seconds" (external).
clinicalNotes: Because the Tibialis Anterior is both an ankle dorsiflexor and a subtalar inverter, holding an isometric contraction in slight dorsiflexion + inversion maximally recruits the tibialis anterior motor units and induces Stage 1 tendon analgesia without sliding the inflamed paratenon repeatedly under the tight extensor retinaculum.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Indications: Perform for Foot Drop / Peroneal Nerve Neuropraxia or severe post-cast anterior weakness

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sit with the leg extended and loop a rigid strap around the forefoot (or apply dual-channel Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation [NMES] over the proximal motor point of the tibialis anterior just lateral to the tibial crest)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Actively fire the tibialis anterior (watching the tendon pop up at the front of the ankle) while using the strap to gently assist the foot to full dorsiflexion; then remove strap assistance at the top, try to hold the foot up actively for 5 seconds, and lower as slowly as possible over 4 seconds.

coachingCues: "Pull your toes and foot up with the strap, then let go of the strap and fight gravity with your shin muscle on the way down" (external).
commonErrors: Over-fatiguing a recovering neuropathic muscle within a single set (if the foot begins to slap down uncontrollably on rep 8, stop the set and rest 2 minutes—neuropathic muscles fatigue rapidly!).

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gravity-resisted active dorsiflexion without strap -> seated toe taps to a metronome -> band-resisted dorsiflexion.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the leg extended, heel resting off the edge of a foam roller or plinth, and anchor a resistance band in front of you looped over the forefoot

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Pull the foot up into full dorsiflexion (with slight supination/inversion to target the tibialis anterior insertion on the medial cuneiform) over 2 seconds; use the other foot or your hand to assist the concentric lift if heavy

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at peak dorsiflexion

steps.title: 步驟 4

progressions.name: 進階方案

description: The closed-chain standing Tibialis Raise places body-weight leverage across the anterior ankle compartment in the exact posture of heel-strike loading response. By stepping the feet further away from the wall, the moment arm on the tibialis anterior increases progressively without needing gym machines.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; loading-response shock absorption

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your back, shoulders, and glutes leaning flat against a wall and walk both feet 12 to 18 inches forward in front of the wall (knees straight but unlocked)
execution.description: The closed-chain standing Tibialis Raise places body-weight leverage across the anterior ankle compartment in the exact posture of heel-strike loading response. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with your back, shoulders, and glutes leaning flat against a wall and walk both feet 12 to 18 inches forward in front of the wall (knees straight but unlocked)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping your heels planted on the floor, pull both forefeet and toes as high up toward your shins as possible over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold the peak contraction for 2 seconds at the top

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower the forefeet slowly back down to the floor over a strict 3-to-4-second eccentric count without letting the soles slap the ground!

coachingCues: "Keep your glutes glued to the wall, pull your toes to the sky, and lower your forefeet over 4 silent seconds so they kiss the floor without a sound" (external).

name: Step-down heel-strike deceleration drill (controlling "Foot Slap")
chineseName: 下台階離心控制訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Bridges isolated open-chain tibialis anterior strength directly into the gait cycle! In both Tibialis Anterior Tendinopathy and recovering Foot Drop, the patient's forefoot slaps loudly onto the ground within 50 milliseconds of heel contact. Practicing slow-motion heel-to-forefoot step-downs retrains high-velocity eccentric braking at Loading Response.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric neuromuscular; loading-response braking re-education

execution.startingPosition: Stand on a low 4-to-6-inch step on the uninjured leg
execution.description: Bridges isolated open-chain tibialis anterior strength directly into the gait cycle! In both Tibialis Anterior Tendinopathy and recovering Foot Drop, the patient's forefoot slaps loudly onto the ground within 50 milliseconds of heel contact. Practicing slow-motion heel-to-forefoot step-downs retrains high-velocity eccentric braking at Loading Response.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a low 4-to-6-inch step on the uninjured leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step forward off the box with the injured leg, landing deliberately on the heel with the forefoot pulled high (dorsiflexed)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: From the moment your heel touches the floor, use your tibialis anterior to lower the forefoot to the floor as slowly and quietly as humanly possible over a 2-to-3-second count ("rolling through the foot in slow motion") while your knee bends softly to absorb weight

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Step back up and repeat for 10-12 reps.

coachingCues: "Strike on your heel and unroll your foot onto the floor like a slow-motion carpet—make zero sound when your toes touch down" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the forefoot slap down with an audible "thwack" upon heel contact; locking the knee straight on heel strike.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated or standing in-place heel-strike-to-flat-foot slow roll-downs on level ground.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform walking down a gentle decline ramp focusing on silent, controlled heel-to-toe roll-through; increase walking speed.

precautions: Letting the forefoot slap down with an audible "thwack" upon heel contact; locking the knee straight on heel strike.Cues: "Strike on your heel and unroll your foot onto the floor like a slow-motion carpet—make zero sound when your toes touch down" (external).

name: Metronome running cadence (+5%–10%) & uphill-to-flat gait progression (RTS)
chineseName: 步態與觸地生物力學重塑
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化

description: Biomechanical running studies prove that overstriding (landing with the heel far in front of the center of mass with the ankle steeply dorsiflexed) and downhill running generate the highest eccentric tibialis anterior braking forces and anterior compartment pressures. Increasing running cadence by 5%–10% immediately cuts peak tibialis anterior eccentric demand by 25%–35%!

jointActions: Neuromuscular gait retraining; closed chain; overstriding elimination

execution.startingPosition: Phase 1 (Uphill Treadmill Walk/Jog — Weeks 4-6): Begin return-to-running on a 4%–6% uphill treadmill incline—running uphill places the ankle in slight dorsiflexion at initial contact and eliminates the long plantarflexion braking arc that overloads the tibialis anterior
execution.description: Biomechanical running studies prove that overstriding (landing with the heel far in front of the center of mass with the ankle steeply dorsiflexed) and downhill running generate the highest eccentric tibialis anterior braking forces and anterior compartment pressures. Increasing running cadence by 5%–10% immediately cuts peak tibialis anterior eccentric demand by 25%–35%!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Uphill Treadmill Walk/Jog — Weeks 4-6): Begin return-to-running on a 4%–6% uphill treadmill incline—running uphill places the ankle in slight dorsiflexion at initial contact and eliminates the long plantarflexion braking arc that overloads the tibialis anterior

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Flat Running with +5%–10% Metronome Cadence — Weeks 6-10): Transition to flat running with a metronome set 5%–10% higher than baseline step rate (e.g., 162 -> 174 spm) so the foot lands closer underneath the center of mass with a softer midfoot/shallow-heel contact rather than an overstriding high-angle heel strike

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Phase 3 (Graduated Downhill Running — Week 8-10+): Re-introduce downhill running last!

coachingCues: "Take quick, quiet steps that land right underneath your hips rather than reaching your heel out in front of you" (external).
commonErrors: Running downhill early in rehab (downhill running is the #1 trigger of Tibialis Anterior Tendinopathy relapse!); lacing running shoes tightly across the top two eyelets without using a heel-lock or skip-lace pattern.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Stay on a 4%–5% uphill treadmill incline if flat running reproduces any anterior shin tightness.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Fade metronome audio cues over 4-6 weeks; progress to continuous flat runs, then gentle rolling hills.

precautions: Running downhill early in rehab (downhill running is the #1 trigger of Tibialis Anterior Tendinopathy relapse!); lacing running shoes tightly across the top two eyelets without using a heel-lock or skip-lace pattern.Cues: "Take quick, quiet steps that land right underneath your hips rather than reaching your heel out in front of you" (external).
clinicalNotes: Biomechanical running studies prove that overstriding (landing with the heel far in front of the center of mass with the ankle steeply dorsiflexed) and downhill running generate the highest eccentric tibialis anterior braking forces and anterior compartment pressures. Increasing running cadence by 5%–10% immediately cuts peak tibialis anterior eccentric demand by 25%–35%!

description: Reverses Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) driven by post-operative joint effusion and altered mechanoreceptor afferents. Restores active terminal knee extension (0°) and drives superior patellar mobility, preventing infrapatellar contracture without straining the healing ACL graft.

jointActions: Isometric; open chain; terminal knee extension; AMI resolution

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting with the operated leg extended and a small rolled towel directly under the knee joint
execution.description: Reverses Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) driven by post-operative joint effusion and altered mechanoreceptor afferents. Restores active terminal knee extension (0°) and drives superior patellar mobility, preventing infrapatellar contracture without straining the healing ACL graft.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting with the operated leg extended and a small rolled towel directly under the knee joint

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Dorsiflex the ankle slightly to neutral

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Contract the quadriceps to push the back of the knee down and flatten the towel roll firmly into the plinth

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold the maximal contraction for 5-10 seconds while confirming superior patellar glide, then relax for 2 seconds.

coachingCues: "Crush the towel flat into the bed with the back of your knee" (external); "Pull your kneecap up into your hip and lock your front thigh solid" (internal).
commonErrors: Posterior pelvic tilt or hip hiking to substitute for quad firing; digging the heel into the bed to recruit hamstrings and calf plantarflexors.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Larger towel roll under the knee; clinician tactile cueing on VMO; bilateral simultaneous quad sets to utilize cross-education.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform flat on the plinth without towel roll; progress to straight leg raises (SLR) once zero extension lag is achieved; standing terminal knee extension (TKE) with resistance band.

precautions: Posterior pelvic tilt or hip hiking to substitute for quad firing; digging the heel into the bed to recruit hamstrings and calf plantarflexors. Cues: "Crush the towel flat into the bed with the back of your knee" (external); "Pull your kneecap up into your hip and lock your front thigh solid" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Reverses Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) driven by post-operative joint effusion and altered mechanoreceptor afferents. Restores active terminal knee extension (0°) and drives superior patellar mobility, preventing infrapatellar contracture without straining the healing ACL graft.

description: Delivers isolated quadriceps overload to reverse post-ACLR atrophy, preventing the hip and ankle compensations common in closed-chain movements. Restricting range to the 90°–45° arc maintains broad patellofemoral contact area and minimizes anterior tibial shear strain on the remodeling ACL graft (peak graft strain occurs between 30° and 0°).

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; isolated strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on a leg extension machine with knees at 90° and the shin pad positioned just proximal to the malleoli
execution.description: Delivers isolated quadriceps overload to reverse post-ACLR atrophy, preventing the hip and ankle compensations common in closed-chain movements. Restricting range to the 90°–45° arc maintains broad patellofemoral contact area and minimizes anterior tibial shear strain on the remodeling ACL graft (peak graft strain occurs between 30° and 0°).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on a leg extension machine with knees at 90° and the shin pad positioned just proximal to the malleoli

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Extend the knee smoothly from 90° up to 45° of flexion over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 1 second at 45°

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly back to 90° over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Keep your back glued to the pad and stop your shin at the 45-degree marker" (external); "Focus the tension purely in the center of your front thigh" (internal).
commonErrors: Kicking past 45° into terminal extension prematurely; leaning the torso back to swing the weight with momentum; internal/external hip rotation.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Isometric holds at 90° and 60° flexion; light ankle cuff weights; gravity-only active extension within 90°–45°.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase external load; expand arc to 90°–30° after weeks 8-12 per graft maturation; full range (90°–0°) in mid-to-late phase.

precautions: Kicking past 45° into terminal extension prematurely; leaning the torso back to swing the weight with momentum; internal/external hip rotation. Cues: "Keep your back glued to the pad and stop your shin at the 45-degree marker" (external); "Focus the tension purely in the center of your front thigh" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Delivers isolated quadriceps overload to reverse post-ACLR atrophy, preventing the hip and ankle compensations common in closed-chain movements. Restricting range to the 90°–45° arc maintains broad patellofemoral contact area and minimizes anterior tibial shear strain on the remodeling ACL graft (peak graft strain occurs between 30° and 0°).

description: Resolves "Quadriceps Avoidance Gait" where ACLR patients flex the trunk forward to offload the knee onto the hip extensors. Anchoring the proximal tibias posteriorly allows an upright torso, maximizing the knee flexion moment arm on the quadriceps while reducing patellofemoral compression and anterior tibial translation.

jointActions: Closed chain; high-load isometric / slow eccentric; strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Loop a thick, non-elastic strap around a sturdy rack at knee height and step both legs inside so the strap sits just below the knee joint lines behind the proximal tibias
execution.description: Resolves "Quadriceps Avoidance Gait" where ACLR patients flex the trunk forward to offload the knee onto the hip extensors. Anchoring the proximal tibias posteriorly allows an upright torso, maximizing the knee flexion moment arm on the quadriceps while reducing patellofemoral compression and anterior tibial translation.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a thick, non-elastic strap around a sturdy rack at knee height and step both legs inside so the strap sits just below the knee joint lines behind the proximal tibias

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step back to pull the strap taut with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the trunk completely vertical, sit back and down into 70°–90° knee flexion

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold isometrically or drive up smoothly through the midfoot/heels.

coachingCues: "Sit straight down as if sliding your back down a vertical wall" (external); "Push your shins forward into the strap and keep your chest tall" (internal).
commonErrors: Leaning the torso forward (hip hinging); medial knee valgus collapse; heels lifting off the floor.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Decrease squat depth to 45°–60°; shorten isometric hold to 20-30s; use upper limb support.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a goblet dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest; perform single-leg biased Spanish squats; increase depth to 90°.

precautions: Leaning the torso forward (hip hinging); medial knee valgus collapse; heels lifting off the floor. Cues: "Sit straight down as if sliding your back down a vertical wall" (external); "Push your shins forward into the strap and keep your chest tall" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Resolves "Quadriceps Avoidance Gait" where ACLR patients flex the trunk forward to offload the knee onto the hip extensors. name: Lateral Poliquin step-down (ACLR)
chineseName: 下台階離心控制訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Builds unilateral eccentric quadriceps control through functional knee flexion (0°–60°) while exposing and correcting dynamic knee valgus, hip internal rotation and contralateral pelvic drop (Trendelenburg). Prepares the knee for stair descent and deceleration ground contacts.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric; unilateral functional strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Stand on a 2-to-6-inch box with the stance foot near the lateral edge and the contralateral foot suspended off the side with the ankle dorsiflexed
execution.description: Builds unilateral eccentric quadriceps control through functional knee flexion (0°–60°) while exposing and correcting dynamic knee valgus, hip internal rotation and contralateral pelvic drop (Trendelenburg). Prepares the knee for stair descent and deceleration ground contacts.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a 2-to-6-inch box with the stance foot near the lateral edge and the contralateral foot suspended off the side with the ankle dorsiflexed

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lower the body slowly over 3 seconds by bending the stance knee forward over the toes while keeping the pelvis level

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lightly tap the floating heel on the floor without transferring weight

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive through the stance foot to return to standing.

coachingCues: "Brush the floor with your heel as softly as touching an eggshell" (external); "Track your kneecap straight over your second toe while keeping your belt line flat" (internal).
commonErrors: Dynamic knee valgus (knee collapsing medially past the big toe); contralateral pelvic drop; bouncing off the bottom heel; lateral trunk lean over the stance hip.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Lower box height (2 inches); fingertip support on a wall; forward step-down.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase box height (up to 6-8 inches); perform on a 15°–25° decline slant board; hold dumbbells at the sides.

precautions: Dynamic knee valgus (knee collapsing medially past the big toe); contralateral pelvic drop; bouncing off the bottom heel; lateral trunk lean over the stance hip. Cues: "Brush the floor with your heel as softly as touching an eggshell" (external); "Track your kneecap straight over your second toe while keeping your belt line flat" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Builds unilateral eccentric quadriceps control through functional knee flexion (0°–60°) while exposing and correcting dynamic knee valgus, hip internal rotation and contralateral pelvic drop (Trendelenburg). Prepares the knee for stair descent and deceleration ground contacts.

rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷

description: The hamstrings are the primary dynamic synergists to the ACL, applying a posterior drawer force on the tibia to counteract anterior tibial translation and rotatory instability. Eccentric overload stimulates longitudinal sarcomerogenesis, lengthens muscle fascicles and restores knee flexor torque (vital after hamstring autograft harvest).

jointActions: Closed chain / fixed anchor; supramaximal eccentric; ACL synergist

execution.startingPosition: Kneel tall on a padded mat with ankles secured firmly under an anchor or held by a clinician
execution.description: The hamstrings are the primary dynamic synergists to the ACL, applying a posterior drawer force on the tibia to counteract anterior tibial translation and rotatory instability. Eccentric overload stimulates longitudinal sarcomerogenesis, lengthens muscle fascicles and restores knee flexor torque (vital after hamstring autograft harvest).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Kneel tall on a padded mat with ankles secured firmly under an anchor or held by a clinician

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep knees, hips and shoulders aligned in a straight line (0° hip extension)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lean forward from the knees over 3-5 seconds, resisting gravity with the hamstrings as long as possible

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Catch yourself on your hands in a push-up position and push lightly back to the start.

coachingCues: "Keep a rigid steel rod from your shoulders through your hips to your knees" (external); "Squeeze your glutes tight and brake the fall with the back of your thighs" (internal).
commonErrors: Bending at the hips (sticking the buttocks backward) to reduce the lever arm; lumbar hyperextension; asymmetrical loading toward the uninjured leg.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Use a resistance band anchored behind the body under the chest for assistance; supine eccentric hamstring sliders on a towel or Swiss ball.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Extend eccentric tempo to >5 seconds; lower all the way to the floor without breaking at the hips; perform unassisted concentric return.

precautions: Bending at the hips (sticking the buttocks backward) to reduce the lever arm; lumbar hyperextension; asymmetrical loading toward the uninjured leg. Cues: "Keep a rigid steel rod from your shoulders through your hips to your knees" (external); "Squeeze your glutes tight and brake the fall with the back of your thighs" (internal).
clinicalNotes: The hamstrings are the primary dynamic synergists to the ACL, applying a posterior drawer force on the tibia to counteract anterior tibial translation and rotatory instability. Eccentric overload stimulates longitudinal sarcomerogenesis, lengthens muscle fascicles and restores knee flexor torque (vital after hamstring autograft harvest).
