description: Streamlined clinical adaptation of the SEBT focusing on the 3 most sensitive vectors for lower-limb injury prediction. An anterior reach asymmetry >4 cm identifies residual quadriceps eccentric weakness or ankle dorsiflexion restriction and correlates strongly with non-contact secondary ACL injury risk.

jointActions: Closed chain; neuromuscular; tri-planar dynamic stability

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the involved leg at the apex of a 3-line Y-grid (anterior, posteromedial at 135°, posterolateral at 135°) with hands on hips
execution.description: Streamlined clinical adaptation of the SEBT focusing on the 3 most sensitive vectors for lower-limb injury prediction. An anterior reach asymmetry >4 cm identifies residual quadriceps eccentric weakness or ankle dorsiflexion restriction and correlates strongly with non-contact secondary ACL injury risk.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the involved leg at the apex of a 3-line Y-grid (anterior, posteromedial at 135°, posterolateral at 135°) with hands on hips

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Flex the stance knee and reach the free foot as far anteriorly as possible to lightly tap the line, then return to single-leg balance

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Repeat along the posteromedial and posterolateral lines without putting weight on the reaching toe.

coachingCues: "Reach out and touch the tape like a feather without making a sound" (external); "Screw your stance foot into the floor and keep your knee pointing straight forward" (internal).
commonErrors: Transferring body weight onto the reach foot; medial knee collapse (valgus pinch) during posteromedial reach; heel lifting off the stance foot.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add partner perturbations or medicine ball passes at peak reach; perform on a foam balance pad; add reactive visual light cues.

precautions: Transferring body weight onto the reach foot; medial knee collapse (valgus pinch) during posteromedial reach; heel lifting off the stance foot. Cues: "Reach out and touch the tape like a feather without making a sound" (external); "Screw your stance foot into the floor and keep your knee pointing straight forward" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Streamlined clinical adaptation of the SEBT focusing on the 3 most sensitive vectors for lower-limb injury prediction. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the edge of a 12-to-18-inch plyometric box on the surgical leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step forward off the box without jumping upward

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Land on the surgical foot rolling smoothly from forefoot to heel while flexing deeply through the hip, knee (45°–60° flexion) and ankle

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Stick and hold the landing motionless for 3 full seconds.

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase box height (20-24 inches); drop into immediate vertical jump or broad jump; add mid-air ball catch or reactive directional cue.

precautions: Stiff, erect landing with minimal knee flexion; loud flat-footed slap impact; dynamic knee valgus collapse; extra stutter hops on landing. description: High-velocity deceleration is a primary non-contact ACL tear mechanism. Training the penultimate step lowers the centre of gravity and distributes braking impulse across multiple foot contacts, preventing catastrophic single-step shear overload on an extended lead knee.

jointActions: High-velocity deceleration; closed chain; eccentric braking

execution.startingPosition: Place cones to mark a 10-metre acceleration lane leading into a 3-to-5-metre braking box
execution.description: High-velocity deceleration is a primary non-contact ACL tear mechanism. Training the penultimate step lowers the centre of gravity and distributes braking impulse across multiple foot contacts, preventing catastrophic single-step shear overload on an extended lead knee.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place cones to mark a 10-metre acceleration lane leading into a 3-to-5-metre braking box

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sprint forward at 70%–100% velocity into the braking zone

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower the centre of mass by sinking the hips on the penultimate (second-to-last) step with a slight backward trunk lean

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Plant the lead foot in active knee flexion, coming to a complete stop within 3 steps, and hold balance for 2 seconds.

coachingCues: "Drop your hips low to the grass on your second-to-last step and chop to a halt in 3 steps" (external); "Load your back leg first to sink your hips, then absorb the brake through your thighs" (internal).
commonErrors: Slamming onto a stiff, extended lead leg; pitching the chest forward over the knees; skipping the penultimate braking step.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Submaximal jog (50% speed) to stop; lengthen braking zone to 5-7 metres; 3-step walk-in braking drill.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase approach speed to 100% sprint; shorten braking zone to 2-3 metres; add immediate backpedal or reactive 45° cut upon stopping.

precautions: Slamming onto a stiff, extended lead leg; pitching the chest forward over the knees; skipping the penultimate braking step. Cues: "Drop your hips low to the grass on your second-to-last step and chop to a halt in 3 steps" (external); "Load your back leg first to sink your hips, then absorb the brake through your thighs" (internal).
clinicalNotes: High-velocity deceleration is a primary non-contact ACL tear mechanism. Training the penultimate step lowers the centre of gravity and distributes braking impulse across multiple foot contacts, preventing catastrophic single-step shear overload on an extended lead knee.

description: Trains frontal- and transverse-plane ground reaction force attenuation during lateral propulsion and landing, replicating side-step cutting where valgus and internal rotation moments peak. Restores rate of force development (RFD) and multi-planar neuromuscular control.

jointActions: Plyometric; reactive multi-planar stability; frontal plane deceleration

execution.startingPosition: Stand on one leg in an athletic quarter-squat
execution.description: Trains frontal- and transverse-plane ground reaction force attenuation during lateral propulsion and landing, replicating side-step cutting where valgus and internal rotation moments peak. Restores rate of force development (RFD) and multi-planar neuromuscular control.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on one leg in an athletic quarter-squat

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Push off explosively sideways across a 1-to-1.5-metre distance

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Land on the opposite (surgical) foot, absorbing lateral momentum through deep triple flexion (hip, knee 45°–60°, ankle)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Stick and hold the single-leg landing completely still for 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Land on a single railroad track with your foot, knee, hip and shoulder aligned straight ahead" (external); "Catch the force deep in your outer hip and freeze" (internal).
commonErrors: Dynamic knee valgus collapse on landing; lateral trunk lean over the landing leg; stiff-knee impact; secondary balance hops.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce lateral bound distance to 0.5 metres; allow contralateral toe-touch on landing for balance; lateral step-and-hop.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Continuous lateral skater bounds without pausing; lateral bound into 90° rotational bound; add partner shoulder perturbation on landing.

precautions: Dynamic knee valgus collapse on landing; lateral trunk lean over the landing leg; stiff-knee impact; secondary balance hops. Cues: "Land on a single railroad track with your foot, knee, hip and shoulder aligned straight ahead" (external); "Catch the force deep in your outer hip and freeze" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Trains frontal- and transverse-plane ground reaction force attenuation during lateral propulsion and landing, replicating side-step cutting where valgus and internal rotation moments peak. Restores rate of force development (RFD) and multi-planar neuromuscular control.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with the affected leg elevated on 1-2 pillows (supporting the calf and thigh so the popliteal fossa behind the knee is not crushed against a hard edge) and the knee resting at a comfortable 15°–20° soft bend

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Pump the ankle smoothly up into full dorsiflexion and down into full plantarflexion for 20-30 rhythmic repetitions

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Follow with 10 gentle heel slides between 15° and 90° of knee flexion—stopping before the back of the knee feels tight or pinched.

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Set resistance to zero or Level 1

steps.title: 步驟 3

description: The semimembranosus tendon forms the medial wall of a Baker's cyst and is also a frequent site of distal medial hamstring tendinopathy. Performing isometric contractions at 30°–45° flexion provides analgesic tendon loading and resolves arthrogenic muscle inhibition without pulling the tendons taut across the posterior capsule (which happens at 0° extension).

jointActions: Isometric; closed/open chain; AMI resolution & distal hamstring analgesia

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with a soft bolster or pillow supporting the knee at a comfortable 30°–45° bend (in this position, the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa is completely slack and decompressed)

Performing isometric contractions at 30°–45° flexion provides analgesic tendon loading and resolves arthrogenic muscle inhibition without pulling the tendons taut across the posterior capsule (which happens at 0° extension).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with a soft bolster or pillow supporting the knee at a comfortable 30°–45° bend (in this position, the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa is completely slack and decompressed)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step A (Isometric Heel-Dig): Gently press the heel downward into the bed for 30 seconds at 40%–60% effort to isometrically load the distal semimembranosus and biceps femoris tendons without joint motion

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step B (Mid-Range Quad Set): Push the back of the knee gently into the bolster while tightening the front thigh for 10 seconds to combat quadriceps AMI.

coachingCues: "Keep your knee comfortably supported on the small bolster at 30 degrees and gently press your heel down to wake up the back of your thigh" (external).
commonErrors: Performing aggressive 0° hyperextension towel crushes when a Baker's cyst or proximal gastrocnemius tendon is acutely inflamed (Foucher's sign demonstrates that 0° hyperextension maximally compresses the cyst between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Submaximal 30% effort holds if distal hamstring insertions are acutely tender.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase isometric intensity to 70% MVIC; gradually reduce bolster height toward 5°–10° flexion as posterior tightness resolves.

precautions: Performing aggressive 0° hyperextension towel crushes when a Baker's cyst or proximal gastrocnemius tendon is acutely inflamed (Foucher's sign demonstrates that 0° hyperextension maximally compresses the cyst between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus!).Cues: "Keep your knee comfortably supported on the small bolster at 30 degrees and gently press your heel down to wake up the back of your thigh" (external).

description: Treating a Baker's cyst permanently requires strengthening the quadriceps so the tibiofemoral joint is shielded from impulsive mechanical stress during walking—when the underlying Knee OA or meniscal lesion is offloaded by a strong quadriceps muscle, synovial irritation ceases and the Baker's cyst naturally resorbs.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on a leg extension machine (or sturdy chair with an ankle weight/band) with knees at 85°–90°

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Smoothly extend the knee over 2 seconds, stopping at 10° short of full lockout (preventing posterior capsule tension at 0° in early weeks, then progressing to 0° once comfortable)

steps.title: 步驟 3

regressions.rationale: Isometric holds at 60° and 45° flexion.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase resistance load progressively; expand range to full 90°–0° extension once terminal extension no longer creates posterior pulling.

precautions: Snapping the leg into hyperextension at the top or letting the weight stack pull the knee past 100° flexion at the bottom.Cues: "Extend smoothly to just shy of lockout, squeeze your front thigh for 2 seconds, and lower under control" (external).

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; gastrocnemius origin remodeling

execution.description: The medial and lateral heads of the gastrocnemius originate on the posterior femoral condyles directly overlying the posterior knee capsule and Baker's cyst. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on flat ground (avoiding hanging the heel below a step edge initially, as aggressive ankle dorsiflexion + knee extension overstretches the proximal gastrocnemius origin and compresses a Baker's cyst)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain a tiny 5°–10° soft unlock in the knees (do NOT lock the knees backward into hyperextension)

steps.instruction: Rise smoothly onto the balls of the feet over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower to the flat floor over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Follow with 3 sets of 12 seated bent-knee calf raises for the soleus.

coachingCues: "Keep a tiny soft cushion in your knees and rise straight up from the flat floor without locking your knees back" (external).

regressions.rationale: Seated bent-knee calf raises (which completely slacken the proximal gastrocnemius origin across the knee while loading the soleus!).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg flat-ground calf raises with dumbbell load; progress to step-edge heel drops and straight-knee calf raises only in the late stage once posterior tenderness is zero.

precautions: Performing aggressive straight-knee calf stretches off a step edge during an acute Baker's cyst or proximal gastrocnemius tendinopathy flare (tightens the medial gastrocnemius tendon directly across the cyst and enthesis, worsening posterior pain!).Cues: "Keep a tiny soft cushion in your knees and rise straight up from the flat floor without locking your knees back" (external).

steps.title: 步驟 1

steps.title: 步驟 2

description: As the knee extends from 30° to 0° in an open kinetic chain, the patella translates superiorly while its inferior pole tilts posteriorly, squeezing the edematous infrapatellar fat pad into the intercondylar notch and anterior tibia (the basis of a positive Hoffa's Test). Training in the 90°–30° arc builds isolated quadriceps and VMO strength to improve patellar tracking without provoking terminal impingement.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; isolated quad loading without terminal pinch

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on a leg extension machine with knees at 90° flexion
execution.description: As the knee extends from 30° to 0° in an open kinetic chain, the patella translates superiorly while its inferior pole tilts posteriorly, squeezing the edematous infrapatellar fat pad into the intercondylar notch and anterior tibia (the basis of a positive Hoffa's Test). Training in the 90°–30° arc builds isolated quadriceps and VMO strength to improve patellar tracking without provoking terminal impingement.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on a leg extension machine with knees at 90° flexion

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Extend the knee smoothly over 2 seconds, stopping strictly at 30° of knee flexion (do NOT extend into the final 30°–0° terminal range)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold an isometric pause at the 30° mark for 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly back to 90° over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Kick up until your shin is 30 degrees below horizontal—treat the final 30 degrees as a no-fly zone" (external).
commonErrors: Kicking all the way to 0° full extension (triggers sharp inferior-medial or inferior-lateral fat-pad pain on every repetition).

regressions.rationale: Isometric holds at 60° and 45° flexion with light-to-moderate resistance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase weight resistance in the 90°–30° arc; in the late stage (Weeks 6-8+), gradually encroach into 20° and 10° as fat-pad swelling resolves.

description: Many patients with chronic Hoffa's Fat Pad Syndrome exhibit postural genu recurvatum (hanging passively on the posterior capsule and crushing the anterior fat pad during single-leg stance). jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; frontal-plane pelvic & sagittal knee control

execution.startingPosition: Stand sideways on a 2-to-4-inch step on the affected leg
execution.description: Many patients with chronic Hoffa's Fat Pad Syndrome exhibit postural genu recurvatum (hanging passively on the posterior capsule and crushing the anterior fat pad during single-leg stance). steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand sideways on a 2-to-4-inch step on the affected leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Unlock the stance knee to a soft 10°–15° bend—actively prevent the knee from snapping backward into genu recurvatum

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Holding that 10°–15° soft knee angle completely fixed, slowly drop the free side of the pelvis 1-2 inches over 3 seconds, then hike the pelvis back to level over 2 seconds using the outer stance hip.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Practice standing "soft-knee unlocking" in front of a side-view mirror on flat ground for 30-second holds before adding the step pelvic drop.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a dumbbell in the contralateral hand; remove fingertip balance support.

precautions: Locking the stance knee backward into hyperextension as soon as attention shifts to the pelvis (immediately pinches the fat pad); bending and straightening the knee instead of moving the pelvis.Cues: "Keep a 10-degree cushion in your standing knee while your hip bone does the lifting" (external).

steps.instruction: Stand in front of a mid-height box or bench (set to ~60°–75° knee flexion) with feet shoulder-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sit the hips back and lower over 3 seconds until your glutes lightly touch the box

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand parallel to a wall with your unaffected leg closest to the wall and your affected (ITBS) leg on the outside as the standing stance leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep the affected stance knee at a comfortable 5°–10° soft unlock (staying well above the provocative 20°–30° ITB impingement angle)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Flex the inside (unaffected) hip and knee to 90° and press the lateral aspect of that bent knee firmly into the wall

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold a strong isometric push for 30-45 seconds—this forces the outside (affected) stance hip abductors to fire maximally to prevent your pelvis from shifting away from the wall.

coachingCues: "Stand tall on your outside leg with the knee nearly straight, and drive your inside knee into the wall until your outside back pocket burns" (external).
commonErrors: Bending the outside (affected) stance knee to 25°–30° while holding (which places the ITB directly into its compressive impingement zone during an acute flare); leaning the shoulders into the wall instead of driving purely from the pelvis.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Side-lying isometric hip abduction hold against a resistance band; reduce push intensity to 50% effort.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Place a foam roller or ball between the inside knee and the wall; progress to dynamic single-leg wall-press squats once the 20°–30° flexion zone is no longer painful.

precautions: Bending the outside (affected) stance knee to 25°–30° while holding (which places the ITB directly into its compressive impingement zone during an acute flare); leaning the shoulders into the wall instead of driving purely from the pelvis. Cues: "Stand tall on your outside leg with the knee nearly straight, and drive your inside knee into the wall until your outside back pocket burns" (external).
clinicalNotes: Delivers high closed-chain isometric recruitment of the affected stance-limb gluteus medius and maximus in a single-leg weight-bearing posture while keeping the affected knee at ~5°–10° flexion (completely decompressing the highly innervated fat pad between the distal ITB and lateral femoral epicondyle that gets pinched at 20°–30° flexion).

name: Side-lying straight-leg hip abduction (wall-slide anti-TFL)
chineseName: 側臥 髖關節外展肌力強化 (臀中肌/臀小肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: A critical error in ITBS rehab is allowing the patient to perform hip abduction with the hip flexed—this selectively recruits the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL), which inserts directly into the anterior border of the ITB and increases ITB tension! Performing abduction against a wall in slight hip extension biases the posterior gluteus medius and minimus while inhibiting TFL dominance.

primaryMuscles: gluteus minimus (tensor fasciae latae inhibited via slight hip extension)
jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; isolated gluteus medius hypertrophy

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your uninjured side with your back, glutes and top heel resting flat against a wall behind you
execution.description: A critical error in ITBS rehab is allowing the patient to perform hip abduction with the hip flexed—this selectively recruits the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL), which inserts directly into the anterior border of the ITB and increases ITB tension! Performing abduction against a wall in slight hip extension biases the posterior gluteus medius and minimus while inhibiting TFL dominance.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your uninjured side with your back, glutes and top heel resting flat against a wall behind you

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep the top (affected) leg straight in 5°–10° of hip extension with the toes angled slightly downward toward the floor

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slide the top heel straight up the wall to 35° abduction over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top and lower slowly over 3 seconds while maintaining heel contact with the wall.

coachingCues: "Keep your heel lightly painting a vertical line up the wall behind you with your toes turned slightly down" (external); "Feel the burn in your upper back pocket, never in the front crease of your hip" (internal).
commonErrors: Letting the top foot leave the wall and drift forward into hip flexion (TFL substitution); rotating the leg externally (toes pointing up at the ceiling); hiking the pelvis with the quadratus lumborum.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce abduction height; perform 20-second isometric holds at mid-range.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a 1-3 kg ankle cuff weight or resistance band around the ankles; progress to side-plank with top-leg hip abduction.

precautions: Letting the top foot leave the wall and drift forward into hip flexion (TFL substitution); rotating the leg externally (toes pointing up at the ceiling); hiking the pelvis with the quadratus lumborum. Cues: "Keep your heel lightly painting a vertical line up the wall behind you with your toes turned slightly down" (external); "Feel the burn in your upper back pocket, never in the front crease of your hip" (internal).
clinicalNotes: A critical error in ITBS rehab is allowing the patient to perform hip abduction with the hip flexed—this selectively recruits the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL), which inserts directly into the anterior border of the ITB and increases ITB tension! Performing abduction against a wall in slight hip extension biases the posterior gluteus medius and minimus while inhibiting TFL dominance.

name: Lateral band walk (forefoot / ankle band placement)

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Biomechanical EMG research by Cambridge & McGill demonstrates that placing the resistance band around the forefeet (rather than the knees) adds an external internal-rotation torque in addition to adduction, significantly increasing gluteus medius and gluteus maximus activation while reducing relative TFL recruitment.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; weight-bearing anti-adduction

execution.startingPosition: 1) Loop a flat resistance band around the forefeet (across the metatarsal heads) or just above the ankles
execution.description: Biomechanical EMG research by Cambridge & McGill demonstrates that placing the resistance band around the forefeet (rather than the knees) adds an external internal-rotation torque in addition to adduction, significantly increasing gluteus medius and gluteus maximus activation while reducing relative TFL recruitment.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a flat resistance band around the forefeet (across the metatarsal heads) or just above the ankles

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand with knees unlocked at ~15° flexion (staying above the 25°–30° impingement zone in early weeks, or at 30°–40° in intermediate weeks once pain-free) and feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step sideways 6-8 inches while keeping toes pointed straight ahead, then eccentrically control the trailing leg back to hip-width

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Complete 12-15 steps in each direction.

coachingCues: "Keep your feet parallel like skis and push the band outward from your back pockets" (external).
commonErrors: Turning the toes outward like a duck during the lateral step (recruits TFL and hip flexors); rocking the trunk side-to-side; letting the feet snap together.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Move band placement to the ankles or just above the knees; perform in a taller 10° knee-bend stance if 30° flexion irritates the lateral knee.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer band resistance; monster walks (diagonal forward/backward steps); add upper-body dumbbell carries.

precautions: Turning the toes outward like a duck during the lateral step (recruits TFL and hip flexors); rocking the trunk side-to-side; letting the feet snap together. Cues: "Keep your feet parallel like skis and push the band outward from your back pockets" (external).
clinicalNotes: Biomechanical EMG research by Cambridge & McGill demonstrates that placing the resistance band around the forefeet (rather than the knees) adds an external internal-rotation torque in addition to adduction, significantly increasing gluteus medius and gluteus maximus activation while reducing relative TFL recruitment.

name: Standing eccentric pelvic drop (hip hike on step)
chineseName: Standing eccentric pelvic drop (hip hike on step)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷

description: During running mid-stance, contralateral pelvic drop increases the tension across the upper gluteus maximus and TFL aponeurosis into the ITB, pulling the distal band tightly against the lateral femoral epicondyle. High-volume eccentric pelvic drops build the local muscular endurance of the stance gluteus medius needed to keep the pelvis level across thousands of running strides.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric/concentric; frontal-plane Trendelenburg control

execution.startingPosition: Stand sideways on a 3-to-4-inch step on the affected leg with the stance knee held straight (5° soft unlock) and the unaffected leg hanging off the edge
execution.description: During running mid-stance, contralateral pelvic drop increases the tension across the upper gluteus maximus and TFL aponeurosis into the ITB, pulling the distal band tightly against the lateral femoral epicondyle. High-volume eccentric pelvic drops build the local muscular endurance of the stance gluteus medius needed to keep the pelvis level across thousands of running strides.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand sideways on a 3-to-4-inch step on the affected leg with the stance knee held straight (5° soft unlock) and the unaffected leg hanging off the edge

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly allow the unsupported side of the pelvis to drop downward 2 inches over a strict 4-second eccentric count

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Contract the affected stance hip abductors to pull the pelvis back up to level over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and repeat.

coachingCues: "Keep both knees straight and let your opposite hip sink slowly over 4 seconds before hiking your belt line flat" (external).
commonErrors: Bending the stance knee to 25°–30° while dropping the hip (triggers lateral knee impingement pain); tilting the shoulders sideways.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce eccentric drop range; use fingertip support on a wall.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a heavy dumbbell in the hand on the hanging-leg side; perform on a foam pad; increase reps to 20 for running endurance.

precautions: Bending the stance knee to 25°–30° while dropping the hip (triggers lateral knee impingement pain); tilting the shoulders sideways. Cues: "Keep both knees straight and let your opposite hip sink slowly over 4 seconds before hiking your belt line flat" (external).
clinicalNotes: During running mid-stance, contralateral pelvic drop increases the tension across the upper gluteus maximus and TFL aponeurosis into the ITB, pulling the distal band tightly against the lateral femoral epicondyle. High-volume eccentric pelvic drops build the local muscular endurance of the stance gluteus medius needed to keep the pelvis level across thousands of running strides.

Heavy slow split squats build high-load gluteus maximus and quadriceps strength so the runner does not fatigue in the final miles of a run.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR); kinetic-chain load capacity

execution.startingPosition: Stand in a split stance with the rear foot elevated on a bench and the affected leg forward
execution.description: The gluteus maximus inserts heavily (approx. 70%–80% of its superficial fibers) into the posterior border of the ITB and acts as a powerful hip external rotator and abductor that controls femoral internal rotation. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a split stance with the rear foot elevated on a bench and the affected leg forward

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Incline the torso slightly forward (15°–20° hip flexion bias increases gluteus maximus recruitment while reducing TFL activity)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower smoothly over 3 seconds down to 75°–90° knee flexion (moving smoothly past the 20°–30° impingement zone without pausing in that window)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive through the front heel over 3 seconds to return to ~10° flexion.

coachingCues: "Lean your chest slightly over your front thigh, keep your knee stacked over your middle toes, and move smoothly all the way down" (external).
commonErrors: Pausing repeatedly right at 25°–30° of knee flexion (the peak ITB compression angle); allowing the front knee to collapse inward or the pelvis to drop on the rear-leg side.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Split squat with both feet on the floor; restrict range if passing through 25°–30° flexion is still tender.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase dumbbell or barbell load progressively toward 8RM.

precautions: Pausing repeatedly right at 25°–30° of knee flexion (the peak ITB compression angle); allowing the front knee to collapse inward or the pelvis to drop on the rear-leg side. Cues: "Lean your chest slightly over your front thigh, keep your knee stacked over your middle toes, and move smoothly all the way down" (external).
clinicalNotes: The gluteus maximus inserts heavily (approx. 70%–80% of its superficial fibers) into the posterior border of the ITB and acts as a powerful hip external rotator and abductor that controls femoral internal rotation. Heavy slow split squats build high-load gluteus maximus and quadriceps strength so the runner does not fatigue in the final miles of a run.

patellar-tendinopathy-jumper-s-knee.description: Bridges isolated machine HSR to free-standing unilateral closed-chain strength. Simultaneously builds quadriceps and gluteus maximus capacity while challenging frontal-plane pelvic and knee stability under heavy unilateral loads.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral HSR; Stage 2 functional knee-hip extensor integration

execution.startingPosition: Stand about 2 feet in front of a rear-foot bench or roller pad, resting the top of the back foot on the pad and keeping 85%–90% of weight on the front (affected) leg
execution.description: Bridges isolated machine HSR to free-standing unilateral closed-chain strength. Simultaneously builds quadriceps and gluteus maximus capacity while challenging frontal-plane pelvic and knee stability under heavy unilateral loads.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand about 2 feet in front of a rear-foot bench or roller pad, resting the top of the back foot on the pad and keeping 85%–90% of weight on the front (affected) leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain an upright-to-slightly-inclined torso and lower slowly over 3 seconds until the back knee hovers 1-2 inches above the floor (front knee at ~80°–90° flexion)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 1 second at the bottom

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive up through the front midfoot/heel over 3 seconds without locking out completely at the top.

coachingCues: "Lower your back knee straight toward the floor for a slow 3-count while keeping your front knee over your middle toes" (external); "Keep 90% of your weight heavy through your front foot" (internal).
commonErrors: Pushing off heavily with the rear elevated leg; allowing the front knee to collapse medially into valgus; bouncing rapidly at the bottom of the rep.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Standard split squat with both feet on the floor; reduce knee flexion depth to 60°; bodyweight-only tempo split squat.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold heavy dumbbells in both hands or a barbell on the back; elevate the front foot on a 2-inch plate to increase knee flexion excursion.

precautions: Pushing off heavily with the rear elevated leg; allowing the front knee to collapse medially into valgus; bouncing rapidly at the bottom of the rep.Cues: "Lower your back knee straight toward the floor for a slow 3-count while keeping your front knee over your middle toes" (external); "Keep 90% of your weight heavy through your front foot" (internal).

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift with contralateral load
chineseName: 單腳 羅馬尼亞硬舉 (RDL 膕旁肌與臀肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷

description: Holding the load in the contralateral hand creates an external rotary and adduction torque across the stance hip, forcing the gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, and deep external rotators to work synergistically to keep the femur externally rotated and aligned over the foot—all while keeping the knee at a safe 15° angle outside the 25°–30° ITB compression zone.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric/concentric; anti-adduction & anti-internal rotation

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg with a fixed 15° knee bend and hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in the opposite (contralateral) hand
execution.description: Holding the load in the contralateral hand creates an external rotary and adduction torque across the stance hip, forcing the gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, and deep external rotators to work synergistically to keep the femur externally rotated and aligned over the foot—all while keeping the knee at a safe 15° angle outside the 25°–30° ITB compression zone.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with a fixed 15° knee bend and hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in the opposite (contralateral) hand

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge backward at the hips over 3 seconds, lowering the weight toward the mid-shin while extending the free leg straight behind you

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Resist the weight's tendency to pull your torso and femur into internal rotation and adduction

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive the stance hip forward over 2 seconds to stand tall.

coachingCues: "Keep your belt line and shoulders level with the horizon—don't let the weight twist your knee inward" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the contralateral shoulder and hip dip toward the floor; letting the stance knee drift medially; flexing the knee to 30° during the hinge.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Kickstand (B-stance) RDL with contralateral dumbbell; fingertip balance support with the ipsilateral hand.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase contralateral dumbbell weight; add a single-leg knee drive at the top of the rep; perform barefoot to challenge intrinsic foot arch stability.

precautions: Letting the contralateral shoulder and hip dip toward the floor; letting the stance knee drift medially; flexing the knee to 30° during the hinge. Cues: "Keep your belt line and shoulders level with the horizon—don't let the weight twist your knee inward" (external).
clinicalNotes: Holding the load in the contralateral hand creates an external rotary and adduction torque across the stance hip, forcing the gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, and deep external rotators to work synergistically to keep the femur externally rotated and aligned over the foot—all while keeping the knee at a safe 15° angle outside the 25°–30° ITB compression zone.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg with the opposite foot suspended off the side

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a light resistance band around the stance knee pulling medially to cue lateral glute engagement

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lower the floating heel to the floor over 3 seconds, passing smoothly and pain-free through the 20°–30° knee flexion zone up to 50°–60° flexion while keeping the patella aligned over the second toe

name: Metronome running cadence (+5%–10%) & step-width retraining
chineseName: Metronome running cadence (+5%–10%) & step-width retraining
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
Phase 4: 增強式與重返運動
description: Strengthening the hip muscles alone does not automatically change faulty running kinematics (Willy & Davis). Two biomechanical modifications immediately reduce ITB strain rate and lateral femoral epicondyle compression during running: (1) increasing step rate by 5%–10% shortens stride length, brings initial foot contact closer to the body's centre of mass, decreases braking impulse, and reduces peak hip adduction angle; (2) widening step width by 2-3 cm eliminates "crossover gait" (where both feet land on the midline), which directly reduces peak ITB strain.

jointActions: Neuromuscular gait retraining; closed chain; running kinematics modification

execution.description: Strengthening the hip muscles alone does not automatically change faulty running kinematics (Willy & Davis). Two biomechanical modifications immediately reduce ITB strain rate and lateral femoral epicondyle compression during running: (1) increasing step rate by 5%–10% shortens stride length, brings initial foot contact closer to the body's centre of mass, decreases braking impulse, and reduces peak hip adduction angle; (2) widening step width by 2-3 cm eliminates "crossover gait" (where both feet land on the midline), which directly reduces peak ITB strain.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Measure your baseline preferred running step rate (cadence, steps per minute [spm]) on a flat treadmill or track at your normal easy pace (e.g. 164 spm)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Set an audible metronome app or running watch beat 5% to 10% higher (e.g. 172 to 180 spm) while keeping treadmill/running speed exactly the same

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Run on flat terrain matching every footstrike to the metronome beat while imagining running with your feet on either side of a painted line (eliminating "crossover gait")

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Follow a walk-run interval progression (e.g. 6-8 x 2 min run / 1 min walk), fading the metronome cues over 4-6 weeks.

coachingCues: "Run quiet and quick on the beat, keeping your feet on two separate sides of a narrow line on the road" (external).
commonErrors: Running faster when the metronome speeds up instead of taking shorter, quicker steps at the same pace; crossing the feet over the midline; resuming downhill running too early (downhill running decreases knee flexion at initial contact into the 20°–30° impingement zone and maximizes eccentric braking).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: In-place metronome pogo marches and A-skips at 175-180 spm; uphill treadmill walking/jogging at 5%–6% grade (uphill running increases knee flexion >35° at footstrike, keeping the knee out of the 20°–30° impingement zone!).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually fade metronome audio feedback (faded-feedback schedule over 8 sessions) to internalize the motor pattern; increase continuous running duration by 10%–15% per week; re-introduce gentle hills and downhill running last.

precautions: Running faster when the metronome speeds up instead of taking shorter, quicker steps at the same pace; crossing the feet over the midline; resuming downhill running too early (downhill running decreases knee flexion at initial contact into the 20°–30° impingement zone and maximizes eccentric braking). Cues: "Run quiet and quick on the beat, keeping your feet on two separate sides of a narrow line on the road" (external).
clinicalNotes: Strengthening the hip muscles alone does not automatically change faulty running kinematics (Willy & Davis). Two biomechanical modifications immediately reduce ITB strain rate and lateral femoral epicondyle compression during running: (1) increasing step rate by 5%–10% shortens stride length, brings initial foot contact closer to the body's centre of mass, decreases braking impulse, and reduces peak hip adduction angle; (2) widening step width by 2-3 cm eliminates "crossover gait" (where both feet land on the midline), which directly reduces peak ITB strain.

steps.instruction: Heel Slides (Early Post-TKA or Stiff OA): Lie supine or sit upright, loop a towel or strap around the foot, and slide the heel slowly toward the buttocks until a firm, tolerable stretch is felt across the anterior knee; hold 10-15 seconds and slide out straight

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stationary Bike: Adjust the saddle height so the knee bends comfortably at the top of the stroke, set low resistance, and pedal smoothly for 10-20 minutes (rocking back and forth as a pendulum first if full revolution is not yet achieved post-TKA).

coachingCues: "Keep your hips level on the seat and let the pedal circle smoothly loosen your knee" (external).
commonErrors: Hiking the hip or tilting the pelvis laterally on the bike saddle to avoid bending the stiff knee; forcing aggressive passive bouncing at end-range flexion.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Pendulum pedal rocking (4 o'clock to 8 o'clock arc) on the stationary bike; supine heel slides on a slick slide-board or plastic bag to reduce friction.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Lower the bike saddle by 1-2 cm per week to increase peak knee flexion; add moderate aerobic resistance to build cardiovascular and muscular endurance.

precautions: Hiking the hip or tilting the pelvis laterally on the bike saddle to avoid bending the stiff knee; forcing aggressive passive bouncing at end-range flexion. Cues: "Keep your hips level on the seat and let the pedal circle smoothly loosen your knee" (external).
clinicalNotes: Articular cartilage lacks blood vessels and depends on cyclic compression and decompression to pump nutrient-rich synovial fluid into chondrocytes while clearing inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, TNF-alpha) from the joint space. Post-TKA, early daily heel slides and cycling prevent intra-articular adhesions and restore the >= 110°–120° flexion needed for stairs and getting out of chairs.

name: Heel-propped passive extension & maximal quad set (post-TKA 0° extension)
chineseName: 股四頭肌等長收縮 (Quad Set)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Loss of terminal knee extension (a flexion contracture of even 5°–10°) after TKA or in severe Knee OA forces the quadriceps to work continuously during standing, increases patellofemoral contact stress, and causes a limp. According to the 2020 APTA TKA Clinical Practice Guideline, early restoration of 0° extension paired with high-intensity quadriceps activation (and NMES) is the #1 predictor of long-term functional walking speed.

jointActions: Passive low-load long-duration stretch + isometric; AMI resolution

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting and place a firm rolled towel or bolster directly under the heel and Achilles tendon so the calf and knee hang completely unsupported in the air
execution.description: Loss of terminal knee extension (a flexion contracture of even 5°–10°) after TKA or in severe Knee OA forces the quadriceps to work continuously during standing, increases patellofemoral contact stress, and causes a limp. According to the 2020 APTA TKA Clinical Practice Guideline, early restoration of 0° extension paired with high-intensity quadriceps activation (and NMES) is the #1 predictor of long-term functional walking speed.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting and place a firm rolled towel or bolster directly under the heel and Achilles tendon so the calf and knee hang completely unsupported in the air

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Allow gravity to gently stretch the posterior knee capsule into full 0° extension for 5-10 minutes (Low-Load Long-Duration [LLLD] stretch)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Every 30-60 seconds during or after the prop, perform a maximal 5-second quad set by pushing the back of the knee down toward the bed.

coachingCues: "Keep the pillow strictly under your heel so your knee hangs free in the air and gravity straightens it out" (external).
commonErrors: Leaving a pillow propped under the bent knee while sleeping or watching TV (creates a permanent fixed flexion contracture after TKA!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Shorten heel-prop bouts to 2-3 minutes if posterior capsule stretch discomfort exceeds 4/10; place a small towel under the knee for quad sets only, then remove it immediately after the exercise.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Place a 1-2 kg cuff weight or light sandbag across the proximal tibia/distal thigh during the heel prop to increase passive extension torque; progress to straight-leg raises once 0° extension is achieved.

precautions: Leaving a pillow propped under the bent knee while sleeping or watching TV (creates a permanent fixed flexion contracture after TKA!). Cues: "Keep the pillow strictly under your heel so your knee hangs free in the air and gravity straightens it out" (external).
clinicalNotes: Loss of terminal knee extension (a flexion contracture of even 5°–10°) after TKA or in severe Knee OA forces the quadriceps to work continuously during standing, increases patellofemoral contact stress, and causes a limp. According to the 2020 APTA TKA Clinical Practice Guideline, early restoration of 0° extension paired with high-intensity quadriceps activation (and NMES) is the #1 predictor of long-term functional walking speed.

name: Seated open-chain knee extension (progressive resistance)

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Quadriceps weakness is both a primary risk factor for Knee OA progression and the most severe impairment after TKA (where quadriceps torque drops by 50%–60% in the first month post-op). Because patients with Knee OA or TKA instinctively shift weight onto the uninvolved leg during bilateral squats, isolated open-chain knee extensions are essential to ensure the affected quadriceps receives true progressive overload.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; isolated quadriceps hypertrophy

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on a leg extension machine (or sturdy chair with an ankle weight/resistance band anchored to the chair leg) with knees at 90°
execution.description: Quadriceps weakness is both a primary risk factor for Knee OA progression and the most severe impairment after TKA (where quadriceps torque drops by 50%–60% in the first month post-op). Because patients with Knee OA or TKA instinctively shift weight onto the uninvolved leg during bilateral squats, isolated open-chain knee extensions are essential to ensure the affected quadriceps receives true progressive overload.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on a leg extension machine (or sturdy chair with an ankle weight/resistance band anchored to the chair leg) with knees at 90°

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Extend the knee smoothly to full comfortable extension over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top, squeezing the front thigh

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly over 3 seconds back to 90°.

coachingCues: "Lift smoothly for 2 seconds, hold at the top for 2 seconds, and lower for 3 seconds" (external).
commonErrors: Swinging the leg rapidly with trunk momentum; avoiding resistance loading due to benign, painless crepitus (educate the patient that painless joint noises are safe and normal during OA strengthening).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Restrict range to pain-free arcs (e.g. 90°–30° if terminal patellofemoral crepitus is painful in PFJ OA); isometric holds at 60° and 45°.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase weight load progressively every 1-2 weeks; perform eccentric-emphasis lowering (2 legs lift up, affected leg lowers over 4 seconds).

precautions: Swinging the leg rapidly with trunk momentum; avoiding resistance loading due to benign, painless crepitus (educate the patient that painless joint noises are safe and normal during OA strengthening). Cues: "Lift smoothly for 2 seconds, hold at the top for 2 seconds, and lower for 3 seconds" (external).
clinicalNotes: Quadriceps weakness is both a primary risk factor for Knee OA progression and the most severe impairment after TKA (where quadriceps torque drops by 50%–60% in the first month post-op). Because patients with Knee OA or TKA instinctively shift weight onto the uninvolved leg during bilateral squats, isolated open-chain knee extensions are essential to ensure the affected quadriceps receives true progressive overload.

name: Side-lying & standing hip abduction (KAM & medial compartment offloading)

description: During single-leg stance in walking, the ground reaction force vector passes medial to the knee joint center, creating an external Knee Adduction Moment (KAM) that compresses the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Strengthening the hip abductors (gluteus medius/minimus) stabilizes the pelvis in the frontal plane, prevents contralateral pelvic drop and trunk sway, and reduces medial compartment compressive load.

jointActions: Open/closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; frontal-plane moment control

execution.startingPosition: Standing Band Abduction (GLA:D® Style): Stand facing a wall or chair back for fingertip support with a resistance band looped around both ankles. Shift weight onto the affected stance leg (keeping the hip, knee, and second toe aligned vertically) and abduct the opposite leg outward 10-12 times, then switch legs so both hips work both isometrically (as the stance stabilizer) and isotonically (as the moving limb)
execution.description: During single-leg stance in walking, the ground reaction force vector passes medial to the knee joint center, creating an external Knee Adduction Moment (KAM) that compresses the medial tibiofemoral compartment. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Standing Band Abduction (GLA:D® Style): Stand facing a wall or chair back for fingertip support with a resistance band looped around both ankles. Shift weight onto the affected stance leg (keeping the hip, knee, and second toe aligned vertically) and abduct the opposite leg outward 10-12 times, then switch legs so both hips work both isometrically (as the stance stabilizer) and isotonically (as the moving limb)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Side-Lying Option: Perform straight-leg side-lying hip abduction with an ankle weight if standing balance is limited.

coachingCues: "Stand tall like a pillar on your support leg and keep your standing knee pointed straight over your middle toes while the other foot pushes the band" (external).
commonErrors: Leaning the upper body sideways each time the leg kicks out; allowing the standing knee to bow outward (varus thrust) or collapse inward (valgus).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Side-lying clamshells or supine banded hip abduction.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer resistance band; remove fingertip wall support; lateral band walks.

precautions: Leaning the upper body sideways each time the leg kicks out; allowing the standing knee to bow outward (varus thrust) or collapse inward (valgus). Cues: "Stand tall like a pillar on your support leg and keep your standing knee pointed straight over your middle toes while the other foot pushes the band" (external).
clinicalNotes: During single-leg stance in walking, the ground reaction force vector passes medial to the knee joint center, creating an external Knee Adduction Moment (KAM) that compresses the medial tibiofemoral compartment. description: Core exercise of the GLA:D® hip/trunk stability block. Builds gluteus maximus and hamstring strength with minimal tibiofemoral compressive force, supporting upright posture and propulsion during walking and stair ascent.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; hip extensor strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent at 90°, feet flat hip-width apart, and a light resistance band looped above the knees
execution.description: Core exercise of the GLA:D® hip/trunk stability block. Builds gluteus maximus and hamstring strength with minimal tibiofemoral compressive force, supporting upright posture and propulsion during walking and stair ascent.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent at 90°, feet flat hip-width apart, and a light resistance band looped above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press the knees gently outward against the band to keep the hips, knees, and feet aligned in two parallel tracks

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Drive through the heels to lift the pelvis to full hip extension over 2 seconds, hold 2-3 seconds, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight ramp from shoulders to knees" (external).
commonErrors: Cramping in the hamstrings (move feet closer to the buttocks and focus on driving through the heels while squeezing the glutes); arching the lower back.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral glute bridge without band; smaller lift height if lumbar spine is stiff.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Marching bridge (alternating 3-second single-leg lifts at the top of the bridge) -> full single-leg glute bridge.

precautions: Cramping in the hamstrings (move feet closer to the buttocks and focus on driving through the heels while squeezing the glutes); arching the lower back. Cues: "Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight ramp from shoulders to knees" (external).
clinicalNotes: Core exercise of the GLA:D® hip/trunk stability block. Builds gluteus maximus and hamstring strength with minimal tibiofemoral compressive force, supporting upright posture and propulsion during walking and stair ascent.

name: GLA:D® Neuromuscular chair sit-to-stand (strict hip-knee-foot alignment)
chineseName: GLA:D® Neuromuscular chair sit-to-stand (strict hip-knee-foot alignment)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: A signature exercise of the international GLA:D® (Good Life with osteoArthritis in Denmark) program. Rather than merely building raw force, Neuromuscular Exercise (NEMEX) trains sensorimotor alignment of the hip-knee-foot axis to eliminate dynamic varus/valgus thrust and asymmetric limb offloading during daily transfers.

jointActions: Closed chain; neuromuscular (NEMEX); functional concentric/eccentric transfer

execution.startingPosition: Sit on the front half of a standard chair with feet hip-width apart and toes pointed straight forward (or slightly outward up to 10° matching natural tibial torsion)
execution.description: A signature exercise of the international GLA:D® (Good Life with osteoArthritis in Denmark) program. Rather than merely building raw force, Neuromuscular Exercise (NEMEX) trains sensorimotor alignment of the hip-knee-foot axis to eliminate dynamic varus/valgus thrust and asymmetric limb offloading during daily transfers.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit on the front half of a standard chair with feet hip-width apart and toes pointed straight forward (or slightly outward up to 10° matching natural tibial torsion)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Cross arms over the chest (or reach forward) and position a mirror in front of you

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lean the nose over the toes and stand up smoothly over 2 seconds while keeping both knees tracking strictly over the second/third toes (zero varus bow-out or valgus cave-in) and 50/50 equal weight on both legs

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly back to the chair over 3 seconds without plopping down.

coachingCues: "Watch your knees in the mirror—keep them moving on two parallel railroad tracks right over your middle toes, and touch the chair seat as softly as a feather" (external).
commonErrors: Shifting 70% of body weight onto the unaffected leg (common for up to 1-2 years post-TKA unless explicitly retrained!); dropping onto the chair uncontrolled in the last 15 degrees.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Raise chair seat height with a firm cushion; use light armrest push-off assistance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Staggered-stance sit-to-stand (placing the uninjured foot half a foot-length forward so the OA/TKA leg bears 70%–80% of the load) -> single-leg sit-to-stand -> add dumbbell goblet weight or lower chair height.

precautions: Shifting 70% of body weight onto the unaffected leg (common for up to 1-2 years post-TKA unless explicitly retrained!); dropping onto the chair uncontrolled in the last 15 degrees. Cues: "Watch your knees in the mirror—keep them moving on two parallel railroad tracks right over your middle toes, and touch the chair seat as softly as a feather" (external).
clinicalNotes: A signature exercise of the international GLA:D® (Good Life with osteoArthritis in Denmark) program. Rather than merely building raw force, Neuromuscular Exercise (NEMEX) trains sensorimotor alignment of the hip-knee-foot axis to eliminate dynamic varus/valgus thrust and asymmetric limb offloading during daily transfers.

name: GLA:D® Neuromuscular forward & lateral step-up (pelvic-level control)
chineseName: 上階梯登階肌力訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Stair climbing is typically the first functional activity lost in Knee OA and the last recovered after TKA. Neuromuscular step-ups train concentric propulsion and eccentric lowering under single-limb load while preventing dynamic varus/valgus thrust.

jointActions: Closed chain; neuromuscular; unilateral stair ascent & descent capacity

execution.startingPosition: Stand in front of a 4-to-8-inch step with the affected foot placed flat on the step
execution.description: Stair climbing is typically the first functional activity lost in Knee OA and the last recovered after TKA. Neuromuscular step-ups train concentric propulsion and eccentric lowering under single-limb load while preventing dynamic varus/valgus thrust.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in front of a 4-to-8-inch step with the affected foot placed flat on the step

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Align the hip, kneecap, and second toe in a vertical line while keeping the belt line (pelvis) completely horizontal

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lean slightly forward from the hips and press through the whole top foot to step up to tall stance over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower the trailing leg back to the floor over 3 seconds while preventing knee wobble or hip drop.

coachingCues: "Keep a imaginary glass of water balanced on each hip bone as you step smoothly up and down" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the knee bow laterally (varus thrust in medial OA) or collapse medially (valgus in lateral/PFJ OA); pushing off with the floor leg instead of lifting with the top leg.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Use a low 2-to-3-inch aerobic step; use light fingertip balance support on a handrail.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase step height from 4 inches to 6-8 inches; hold dumbbells in both hands or carry an asymmetrical load in one hand to challenge trunk/pelvic control.

precautions: Letting the knee bow laterally (varus thrust in medial OA) or collapse medially (valgus in lateral/PFJ OA); pushing off with the floor leg instead of lifting with the top leg. Cues: "Keep a imaginary glass of water balanced on each hip bone as you step smoothly up and down" (external).
clinicalNotes: Stair climbing is typically the first functional activity lost in Knee OA and the last recovered after TKA. Neuromuscular step-ups train concentric propulsion and eccentric lowering under single-limb load while preventing dynamic varus/valgus thrust.

By keeping the affected foot planted on the ground while the opposite foot glides smoothly on a slider, the joint experiences zero impulsive ground-strike shock while the quadriceps, hamstrings, and hip stabilizers co-contract continuously to control knee alignment across changing flexion angles.

jointActions: Closed chain; neuromuscular; dynamic weight-transfer & alignment control

execution.startingPosition: Stand on a smooth floor with the affected (stance) foot planted firmly on a non-slip surface and the opposite (moving) foot resting on a furniture slider, towel, or paper plate
execution.description: Core functional progression of the GLA:D® program. By keeping the affected foot planted on the ground while the opposite foot glides smoothly on a slider, the joint experiences zero impulsive ground-strike shock while the quadriceps, hamstrings, and hip stabilizers co-contract continuously to control knee alignment across changing flexion angles.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a smooth floor with the affected (stance) foot planted firmly on a non-slip surface and the opposite (moving) foot resting on a furniture slider, towel, or paper plate

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping 80%–90% of your body weight on the planted affected leg, slowly slide the other foot backward into a reverse lunge (bending the stance knee to 45°–70° while keeping the knee aligned over the second toe)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pull through the planted heel and glute to slide the moving foot back to the starting position

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Repeat sliding sideways (lateral slider) to train frontal-plane control.

commonErrors: Transferring body weight onto the sliding back foot instead of keeping weight centered over the planted front foot; letting the front knee drift inward or outward off the toe line.

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Transferring body weight onto the sliding back foot instead of keeping weight centered over the planted front foot; letting the front knee drift inward or outward off the toe line. steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Contract the quadriceps firmly for 5-10 seconds without pushing the knee into negative hyperextension

steps.title: 步驟 3

precautions: Allowing the knee to drop into passive hyperextension (genu recurvatum) or external tibial rotation (toes falling outward toward the side of the bed); performing active hamstring heel-digs. Directly loading tibial internal rotation (first isometrically for analgesia, then with slow eccentric-concentric band resistance) isolates the popliteus tendon and actively opposes the external tibial rotation laxity seen in posterolateral corner insufficiency.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit on a chair or plinth with the knee bent at 90° and the heel resting on a smooth floor (or towel) with the hip and thigh held completely still by your hands

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stage 1 Isometric (Acute Popliteus Tendinopathy): Place a resistance band or the opposite foot against the inner border of the forefoot and push the forefoot inward (internally rotating the shin/tibia without moving the thigh) for 5 x 30-second holds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Stage 2 Isotonic (Subacute Popliteus Rehab): Anchor a resistance band laterally, loop it around the forefoot, and slowly pivot the forefoot inward on the heel through full tibial internal rotation (2s in, 2s hold, 3s slow eccentric return).

coachingCues: "Hold your thigh bone still with both hands and pivot your toes inward like a windshield wiper on your heel" (external).
commonErrors: Moving the entire thigh/femur inward (hip adduction) instead of clamping the femur with both hands and rotating purely at the shin (watch the tibial tuberosity rotate medially!); inverting the ankle (supination) instead of pivoting the whole foot horizontally on the heel.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Submaximal (40% effort) isometric tibial internal rotation against the opposite foot.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer resistance band; perform in a half-kneeling or split-squat closed-chain position with a band pulling the tibia into external rotation while the popliteus resists isometrically.

precautions: Moving the entire thigh/femur inward (hip adduction) instead of clamping the femur with both hands and rotating purely at the shin (watch the tibial tuberosity rotate medially!); inverting the ankle (supination) instead of pivoting the whole foot horizontally on the heel. Cues: "Hold your thigh bone still with both hands and pivot your toes inward like a windshield wiper on your heel" (external).
clinicalNotes: The popliteus originates on the lateral femoral condyle and inserts on the posterior-medial proximal tibia above the soleal line. In an open chain at 90° knee flexion, its primary mechanical action is internal rotation of the tibia. Directly loading tibial internal rotation (first isometrically for analgesia, then with slow eccentric-concentric band resistance) isolates the popliteus tendon and actively opposes the external tibial rotation laxity seen in posterolateral corner insufficiency.

name: Resisted ankle eversion with band (peroneal anti-varus dynamic support)
chineseName: 踝關節抗阻外翻訓練 (腓骨肌群)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Patients with LCL/PLC injuries or varus knee alignment frequently walk on the lateral border of the foot (hindfoot varus / supination), which shifts the ground reaction force vector laterally and amplifies the external Varus Moment that gaps the lateral knee compartment! Strengthening the peroneus longus and brevis everts the foot, plants the first ray (big-toe ball) firmly on the ground, shifts the center of pressure medially, and dynamically offloads the LCL.

primaryMuscles: peroneus brevis (resisting hindfoot varus and lateral knee gapping)
jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; lateral ankle-knee kinetic chain

execution.startingPosition: Sit with the leg supported and loop a resistance band around the lateral forefoot, anchored medially (or around the other foot)
execution.description: Patients with LCL/PLC injuries or varus knee alignment frequently walk on the lateral border of the foot (hindfoot varus / supination), which shifts the ground reaction force vector laterally and amplifies the external Varus Moment that gaps the lateral knee compartment! Strengthening the peroneus longus and brevis everts the foot, plants the first ray (big-toe ball) firmly on the ground, shifts the center of pressure medially, and dynamically offloads the LCL.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit with the leg supported and loop a resistance band around the lateral forefoot, anchored medially (or around the other foot)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping the knee and shin completely stationary (toes pointed up), push the outer edge of the foot outward and slightly downward (eversion) over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at end-range and return slowly over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Keep your kneecap and shin bone frozen still and lead the movement purely with your pinky toe" (external).
commonErrors: Rotating the whole leg externally at the hip/knee to pull the band (external tibial rotation is strictly avoided in early LCL/PLC injuries—isolate the movement strictly to the ankle!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Active eversion range of motion without band resistance (especially if recovering from mild common peroneal nerve neuropraxia).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing single-leg calf raises while pressing a coin or band under the first metatarsal head (big-toe ball) to maintain active peroneus longus pronation stability.

precautions: Rotating the whole leg externally at the hip/knee to pull the band (external tibial rotation is strictly avoided in early LCL/PLC injuries—isolate the movement strictly to the ankle!). Cues: "Keep your kneecap and shin bone frozen still and lead the movement purely with your pinky toe" (external).
clinicalNotes: Patients with LCL/PLC injuries or varus knee alignment frequently walk on the lateral border of the foot (hindfoot varus / supination), which shifts the ground reaction force vector laterally and amplifies the external Varus Moment that gaps the lateral knee compartment! Strengthening the peroneus longus and brevis everts the foot, plants the first ray (big-toe ball) firmly on the ground, shifts the center of pressure medially, and dynamically offloads the LCL.

name: Shallow closed-chain mini-squat (0°–60° anti-varus aligned arc)
chineseName: Shallow closed-chain mini-squat (0°–60° anti-varus aligned arc)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: In the LaPrade PLC and LCL rehabilitation guideline (once weight-bearing is cleared at Week 6 post-op, or Week 2-3 in Grade I-II non-op sprains), closed-chain mini-squats limited to 0°–60° build quadriceps and gluteal strength under stabilizing axial compression while avoiding both deep-flexion posterior shear (>70°) and terminal hyperextension (0° recurvatum).

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; axial tibiofemoral congruency

execution.startingPosition: Stand in front of a mirror with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock (or slightly inward by 5° to protect the PLC against external tibial rotation)
execution.description: In the LaPrade PLC and LCL rehabilitation guideline (once weight-bearing is cleared at Week 6 post-op, or Week 2-3 in Grade I-II non-op sprains), closed-chain mini-squats limited to 0°–60° build quadriceps and gluteal strength under stabilizing axial compression while avoiding both deep-flexion posterior shear (>70°) and terminal hyperextension (0° recurvatum).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in front of a mirror with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock (or slightly inward by 5° to protect the PLC against external tibial rotation)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Sit the hips back and bend the knees over 3 seconds to a maximum of 45°–60° flexion while preventing the knees from bowing outward (varus thrust)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press firmly through the inner ball of the foot (first metatarsal head) and heel to return to a soft 5° knee bend at the top (do NOT lock into hyperextension).

coachingCues: "Keep your big-toe ball glued to the floor, track your knees straight over your second toes, and stop with a tiny soft bend at the top" (external).
commonErrors: Bowing the knees outward into varus ("cowboy stance") or rolling onto the outside edges of the shoes; locking the knees backward at the top of the squat.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Wall slides (5°–45° flexion) with back supported; weight-shifting drills from side to side.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress depth to 70°–80° after Week 10-12; add goblet dumbbell load.

precautions: Bowing the knees outward into varus ("cowboy stance") or rolling onto the outside edges of the shoes; locking the knees backward at the top of the squat. Cues: "Keep your big-toe ball glued to the floor, track your knees straight over your second toes, and stop with a tiny soft bend at the top" (external).
clinicalNotes: In the LaPrade PLC and LCL rehabilitation guideline (once weight-bearing is cleared at Week 6 post-op, or Week 2-3 in Grade I-II non-op sprains), closed-chain mini-squats limited to 0°–60° build quadriceps and gluteal strength under stabilizing axial compression while avoiding both deep-flexion posterior shear (>70°) and terminal hyperextension (0° recurvatum).

name: Banded glute bridge (heels neutral/slightly inward to inhibit biceps femoris)
chineseName: 彈力帶 臀橋式骨盆抬高訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Because the biceps femoris (lateral hamstring) inserts directly onto the fibular head adjacent to the LCL and PFL, isolated active hamstring knee flexion is prohibited for up to 12–16 weeks after PLC injury/reconstruction. Performing a short-lever glute-biased bridge (pushing vertically through the heels with toes slightly turned in to bias the medial semitendinosus over the lateral biceps femoris) prevents gluteal atrophy safely.

primaryMuscles: medial hamstrings (minimizing lateral biceps femoris fibular pull)
jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; gluteal-dominant posterior chain

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent at ~60°–75° (feet placed slightly closer to the buttocks so the gluteus maximus dominates over the hamstrings) and feet hip-width apart with toes pointed straight ahead or 5° inward
execution.description: Because the biceps femoris (lateral hamstring) inserts directly onto the fibular head adjacent to the LCL and PFL, isolated active hamstring knee flexion is prohibited for up to 12–16 weeks after PLC injury/reconstruction. Performing a short-lever glute-biased bridge (pushing vertically through the heels with toes slightly turned in to bias the medial semitendinosus over the lateral biceps femoris) prevents gluteal atrophy safely.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent at ~60°–75° (feet placed slightly closer to the buttocks so the gluteus maximus dominates over the hamstrings) and feet hip-width apart with toes pointed straight ahead or 5° inward

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Squeeze the glutes first and push straight down through the heels (do NOT pull backward with the heels, which fires the hamstrings as knee flexors) to lift the hips over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 3 seconds at the top and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Point your toes straight ahead, push your heels straight down into the floor like elevator pistons rather than pulling them back, and lift from your glutes" (external).
commonErrors: Turning the feet outward and pulling the heels aggressively toward the buttocks (maximally recruits the biceps femoris and pulls posteriorly on the fibular head!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine isometric gluteal squeezes with zero knee flexion pull.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg glute-biased bridge; progress to hip thrusts and RDLs before re-introducing open-chain hamstring curls after Week 12-16+.

precautions: Turning the feet outward and pulling the heels aggressively toward the buttocks (maximally recruits the biceps femoris and pulls posteriorly on the fibular head!). Cues: "Point your toes straight ahead, push your heels straight down into the floor like elevator pistons rather than pulling them back, and lift from your glutes" (external).
clinicalNotes: Because the biceps femoris (lateral hamstring) inserts directly onto the fibular head adjacent to the LCL and PFL, isolated active hamstring knee flexion is prohibited for up to 12–16 weeks after PLC injury/reconstruction. Performing a short-lever glute-biased bridge (pushing vertically through the heels with toes slightly turned in to bias the medial semitendinosus over the lateral biceps femoris) prevents gluteal atrophy safely.
