name: Forward step-up with lateral-pull band cue (anti-varus thrust control)
chineseName: 上階梯登階肌力訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Chronic PLC or LCL insufficiency often leaves a persistent "varus thrust" during single-limb loading where the knee bows laterally at initial stance. A gentle lateral band pull provides Reactive Neuromuscular Training (RNT), cueing the medial dynamic stabilizers (VMO, pes anserinus, adductors) and peroneus longus to hold the knee in neutral frontal alignment.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral concentric/eccentric; frontal-plane anti-varus training

execution.startingPosition: Stand in front of a 4-to-6-inch step with the injured foot on the step and a light resistance band anchored laterally (on the outside), looped around the knee to gently pull the knee outward toward varus (for LCL/PLC neuromuscular retraining once ligament healing is solid at Week 8-10+)
execution.description: Chronic PLC or LCL insufficiency often leaves a persistent "varus thrust" during single-limb loading where the knee bows laterally at initial stance. A gentle lateral band pull provides Reactive Neuromuscular Training (RNT), cueing the medial dynamic stabilizers (VMO, pes anserinus, adductors) and peroneus longus to hold the knee in neutral frontal alignment.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in front of a 4-to-6-inch step with the injured foot on the step and a light resistance band anchored laterally (on the outside), looped around the knee to gently pull the knee outward toward varus (for LCL/PLC neuromuscular retraining once ligament healing is solid at Week 8-10+)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Actively resist the outward band pull by pressing the big-toe ball into the step and keeping the knee stacked centrally over the second toe

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step up smoothly over 2 seconds (stopping at a 5° soft knee at the top) and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Anchor your big-toe knuckle into the step and keep your kneecap tracked straight over your second toe" (external).
commonErrors: Using a heavy band too early that physically gaps the lateral joint line; rolling onto the outer edge of the shoe.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform without the resistance band first; use a 2-to-3-inch step.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase step height to 6-8 inches; hold dumbbells; remove band cue once neutral tracking is automatic.

precautions: Using a heavy band too early that physically gaps the lateral joint line; rolling onto the outer edge of the shoe. Cues: "Anchor your big-toe knuckle into the step and keep your kneecap tracked straight over your second toe" (external).
clinicalNotes: Chronic PLC or LCL insufficiency often leaves a persistent "varus thrust" during single-limb loading where the knee bows laterally at initial stance. A gentle lateral band pull provides Reactive Neuromuscular Training (RNT), cueing the medial dynamic stabilizers (VMO, pes anserinus, adductors) and peroneus longus to hold the knee in neutral frontal alignment.

name: Supported single-leg RDL (15° soft knee — anti-recurvatum & anti-rotation)
chineseName: 單腳羅馬尼亞硬舉 (平衡與後側鏈)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Trains single-leg sagittal anti-hyperextension control and transverse-plane anti-external-rotation stability simultaneously. Because the pelvis is prevented from rotating open during the hinge, the femur and tibia remain locked in neutral rotation, protecting the PLC while building strong posterior-chain hip extension.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric/concentric; rotational & sagittal posterolateral control

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg with the knee held at a fixed 15°–20° bend and the foot pointed straight ahead
execution.description: Trains single-leg sagittal anti-hyperextension control and transverse-plane anti-external-rotation stability simultaneously. Because the pelvis is prevented from rotating open during the hinge, the femur and tibia remain locked in neutral rotation, protecting the PLC while building strong posterior-chain hip extension.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with the knee held at a fixed 15°–20° bend and the foot pointed straight ahead

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge forward at the hips over 3 seconds while extending the free leg behind you, keeping both hip bones squared to the floor (preventing pelvic opening, which would cause external tibial rotation relative to the femur!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Drive the hips forward to return to standing while keeping the 15° soft knee bend.

coachingCues: "Keep your knee soft at 15 degrees, your big toe anchored, and both hip bones pointing straight down at the floor" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the pelvis twist open toward the non-stance side; straightening the knee into 0°/hyperextension at the bottom or top.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral Romanian deadlift with a 15° soft knee bend; B-stance RDL.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a dumbbell in the ipsilateral hand (holding weight on the same side challenges anti-varus stability) or contralateral hand; progress to unsupported SL RDL.

precautions: Letting the pelvis twist open toward the non-stance side; straightening the knee into 0°/hyperextension at the bottom or top. Cues: "Keep your knee soft at 15 degrees, your big toe anchored, and both hip bones pointing straight down at the floor" (external).
clinicalNotes: Trains single-leg sagittal anti-hyperextension control and transverse-plane anti-external-rotation stability simultaneously. Because the pelvis is prevented from rotating open during the hinge, the femur and tibia remain locked in neutral rotation, protecting the PLC while building strong posterior-chain hip extension.

name: Controlled forward step-down & downhill deceleration drill
chineseName: 下台階離心控制訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: During downhill running and stair descent, gravity drives the femur anteriorly over the fixed tibia while generating an external tibial rotation torque—the two exact forces that the popliteus tendon and PLC must eccentrically brake! Progressive eccentric forward step-downs and staged braking drills build the specific load capacity needed for downhill runners and field athletes to return to sport without posterolateral relapse.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric braking; femoral-on-tibial forward translation control

execution.startingPosition: Phase 1 (Eccentric Forward Step-Down on Slant/Flat Step): Stand on a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg, toes pointed straight ahead (or 5° inward to pre-activate the popliteus), and slowly lower the free heel forward to brush the floor over 4 seconds while keeping the tibia and femur strictly aligned without varus bow-out or external foot spin
execution.description: During downhill running and stair descent, gravity drives the femur anteriorly over the fixed tibia while generating an external tibial rotation torque—the two exact forces that the popliteus tendon and PLC must eccentrically brake! Progressive eccentric forward step-downs and staged braking drills build the specific load capacity needed for downhill runners and field athletes to return to sport without posterolateral relapse.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Eccentric Forward Step-Down on Slant/Flat Step): Stand on a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg, toes pointed straight ahead (or 5° inward to pre-activate the popliteus), and slowly lower the free heel forward to brush the floor over 4 seconds while keeping the tibia and femur strictly aligned without varus bow-out or external foot spin

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Linear & Downhill Deceleration): Progress to 3-step penultimate braking drills on flat ground, and finally controlled downhill walk-jog braking intervals once 100% pain-free.

coachingCues: "Keep your foot pointed at 12 o'clock, absorb the descent over 4 smooth seconds through your quad and calf, and never let your knee bow outward" (external).
commonErrors: Resuming steep downhill trail running before eccentric forward step-downs are 100% pain-free; landing with the foot externally rotated and knee in varus.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Retro (backward) step-downs or flat-ground split squats (which eliminate forward femoral-on-tibial shear).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase step height or perform on a slight 10° decline board (only in late-stage Popliteus Tendinopathy to simulate downhill running gradient); add figure-of-8 cutting drills.

precautions: Resuming steep downhill trail running before eccentric forward step-downs are 100% pain-free; landing with the foot externally rotated and knee in varus. Cues: "Keep your foot pointed at 12 o'clock, absorb the descent over 4 smooth seconds through your quad and calf, and never let your knee bow outward" (external).
clinicalNotes: During downhill running and stair descent, gravity drives the femur anteriorly over the fixed tibia while generating an external tibial rotation torque—the two exact forces that the popliteus tendon and PLC must eccentrically brake! Progressive eccentric forward step-downs and staged braking drills build the specific load capacity needed for downhill runners and field athletes to return to sport without posterolateral relapse.

name: Unresisted stationary cycling (pendulum to full revolution)
chineseName: Unresisted stationary cycling (pendulum to full revolution)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Articular hyaline cartilage and the inner two-thirds (white-white and red-white zones) of the meniscus are avascular and rely on cyclic mechanical compression and decompression to pump synovial fluid nutrients into the extracellular matrix. Unresisted cycling delivers thousands of gentle, non-shearing nutrient cycles per session while reducing intra-articular effusion.

jointActions: Cyclic mobility; closed chain; synovial diffusion & chondral nutrition

execution.startingPosition: Adjust the stationary bike seat slightly higher than standard so knee flexion at the top of the pedal stroke stays within your permitted surgical ceiling (typically <= 90°–100°)
execution.description: Articular hyaline cartilage and the inner two-thirds (white-white and red-white zones) of the meniscus are avascular and rely on cyclic mechanical compression and decompression to pump synovial fluid nutrients into the extracellular matrix. Unresisted cycling delivers thousands of gentle, non-shearing nutrient cycles per session while reducing intra-articular effusion.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Adjust the stationary bike seat slightly higher than standard so knee flexion at the top of the pedal stroke stays within your permitted surgical ceiling (typically <= 90°–100°)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Set resistance to zero or Level 1

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: If full revolution is not yet comfortable, rock the pedals gently back and forth like a pendulum between the 4 o'clock and 8 o'clock positions

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Once range allows, pedal smoothly in full circles at 60-70 RPM for 10-20 minutes.

coachingCues: "Spin the pedals effortlessly as if stirring warm water with your feet" (external); "Let the healthy leg help guide the surgical leg smoothly over the top of the circle" (internal).
commonErrors: Setting the seat too low and forcing the knee past its prescribed post-op flexion limit (e.g. >90° in early meniscal repair); standing up on the pedals or grinding high resistance early; rocking the pelvis side-to-side over the saddle.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Half-moon pendulum rocking only (bottom half of the pedal stroke); passive continuous motion (CPM) machine in early post-op cartilage repair.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Lower the saddle height by 1-2 cm as flexion range permissions increase; gradually add light aerobic resistance once joint effusion is zero.

precautions: Setting the seat too low and forcing the knee past its prescribed post-op flexion limit (e.g. >90° in early meniscal repair); standing up on the pedals or grinding high resistance early; rocking the pelvis side-to-side over the saddle.Cues: "Spin the pedals effortlessly as if stirring warm water with your feet" (external); "Let the healthy leg help guide the surgical leg smoothly over the top of the circle" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Articular hyaline cartilage and the inner two-thirds (white-white and red-white zones) of the meniscus are avascular and rely on cyclic mechanical compression and decompression to pump synovial fluid nutrients into the extracellular matrix. Unresisted cycling delivers thousands of gentle, non-shearing nutrient cycles per session while reducing intra-articular effusion.

name: Supine quad set to straight-leg raise (0° locked extension)
chineseName: 仰臥 股四頭肌等長收縮 (Quad Set)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Even small meniscal or chondral effusions (20-30 mL of intra-articular fluid) trigger profound Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) of the vastus medialis. Locking the knee in 0° extension places the menisci in their most stable, congruent anterior-to-middle horn position with zero posterior horn compression and zero tibiofemoral shear while loading the quadriceps and hip flexors.

jointActions: Isometric; open chain; AMI resolution & zero-shear hip/quad loading

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with the uninjured knee bent (foot flat on the bed) and the injured leg straight
execution.description: Even small meniscal or chondral effusions (20-30 mL of intra-articular fluid) trigger profound Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) of the vastus medialis. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with the uninjured knee bent (foot flat on the bed) and the injured leg straight

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Perform a maximal quad set first: tighten the thigh and push the back of the knee flat to lock the knee at 0° extension

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the knee locked completely straight, lift the leg to the height of the opposite bent knee (about 45° hip flexion) over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top, lower slowly over 3 seconds, and only relax the quad once the heel touches the bed.

coachingCues: "Lock the knee into a single solid beam before your heel leaves the sheet" (external); "Squeeze your kneecap tight up into your thigh the entire way up and down" (internal).
commonErrors: Lifting the leg with a 5°–10° bend in the knee ("extension lag"), which indicates unaddressed quadriceps inhibition and stresses the anterior joint capsule; arching the lower back.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine quad sets only (if an extension lag >0° is present during lifting); perform the lift with the postoperative hinged knee brace locked at 0°.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform 4-way straight-leg raises (adding side-lying hip abduction, side-lying adduction, and prone hip extension with the knee locked); add a 1-2 kg cuff weight at the proximal tibia or ankle.

precautions: Lifting the leg with a 5°–10° bend in the knee ("extension lag"), which indicates unaddressed quadriceps inhibition and stresses the anterior joint capsule; arching the lower back.Cues: "Lock the knee into a single solid beam before your heel leaves the sheet" (external); "Squeeze your kneecap tight up into your thigh the entire way up and down" (internal).

Locking the knee in 0° extension places the menisci in their most stable, congruent anterior-to-middle horn position with zero posterior horn compression and zero tibiofemoral shear while loading the quadriceps and hip flexors.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with a soft, fixed 15°–20° knee bend, resting two fingertips of the opposite hand on a wall or dowel for balance

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge at the hip to tip the torso forward while extending the free leg straight behind you

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep both hip bones pointing strictly toward the floor (zero pelvic rotation, which prevents tibiofemoral rotational shear on the meniscus)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive the hips forward to stand tall.

coachingCues: "Keep your belt buckle parallel to the floor so your knee never twists" (external); "Hinge purely from your hip crease with your knee angle frozen at 15 degrees" (internal).
commonErrors: Allowing the pelvis to rotate open toward the non-stance side (creates internal/external rotational grinding across the meniscus on the planted tibia); bending the knee deeply into a squat.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral Romanian deadlift (hip hinge); kickstand (B-stance) RDL with the rear toe resting lightly on the floor.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a dumbbell in the contralateral hand; remove fingertip balance support.

precautions: Allowing the pelvis to rotate open toward the non-stance side (creates internal/external rotational grinding across the meniscus on the planted tibia); bending the knee deeply into a squat.Cues: "Keep your belt buckle parallel to the floor so your knee never twists" (external); "Hinge purely from your hip crease with your knee angle frozen at 15 degrees" (internal).
clinicalNotes: After medial meniscal repair (especially posterior horn), high-load open-chain active knee flexion is often restricted for 6 weeks because the semimembranosus tendon inserts directly into the posterior horn of the medial meniscus and can pull on the repair. The fixed-knee SL RDL trains the hamstrings and gluteus maximus heavily as hip extensors while keeping the knee at a constant 15° angle with zero posterior horn traction and zero rotational torque.

name: Forward step-up (strict sagittal plane, zero tibial rotation)

description: Rebuilds unilateral closed-chain concentric and eccentric knee extensor strength within a controlled 0°–60° flexion arc. Emphasizes pure sagittal-plane tracking to prevent the combined compression-and-twisting mechanism that causes meniscal lesions.

execution.startingPosition: Place the entire foot of the surgical leg flat on a 4-to-6-inch step, with toes and kneecap pointing straight ahead
execution.description: Rebuilds unilateral closed-chain concentric and eccentric knee extensor strength within a controlled 0°–60° flexion arc. Emphasizes pure sagittal-plane tracking to prevent the combined compression-and-twisting mechanism that causes meniscal lesions.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place the entire foot of the surgical leg flat on a 4-to-6-inch step, with toes and kneecap pointing straight ahead

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lean the chest slightly forward over the front foot and press through the front heel to step all the way up over 2 seconds (avoid pushing off with the trailing back foot by pulling the back toes up)

steps.title: 步驟 3

precautions: Dynamic knee valgus and femoral internal rotation (twisting on a loaded meniscus); springing off the bottom trail leg; selecting a box so high that knee flexion exceeds 70°–90° prematurely.Cues: "Pull your back toes up toward your shin so your top leg does 100% of the lifting, and keep your knee on a straight laser line" (external).

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the surgical leg at the centre of the Y-grid with hands on hips
execution.description: Meniscal tears disrupt Ruffini endings and Pacinian corpuscles located in the meniscal horns and outer vascular rim, impairing joint position sense. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the surgical leg at the centre of the Y-grid with hands on hips

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Flex the stance knee smoothly within your permitted pain-free arc and reach the free foot along the anterior line, tapping lightly

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Return to tall single-leg balance

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Reach along the posteromedial and posterolateral lines while keeping the stance knee pointing strictly forward (preventing rotational twist at the tibiofemoral joint).

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Twisting the torso and pelvis aggressively during the posteromedial reach (imparts rotary shear across the meniscus); collapsing the stance knee medially.Cues: "Keep your standing kneecap locked on the 12 o'clock line even when your free foot reaches diagonally behind you" (external).

steps.instruction: Stand on a low 6-to-12-inch box on the surgical leg (progressed from double-leg drop landings)

description: Represents the core strengthening exercise of Block 2 (Weeks 5–8) in the Rathleff OSD trial. Rather than jumping straight into heavy weights, the adolescent builds structural load tolerance at the maturing tibial tuberosity by progressively adding volume (from 10 total reps up to 60 total reps per session) at a strict slow tempo, guided by the 24-hour morning pain check.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic eccentric/concentric; graded apophyseal loading (Weeks 5–8)

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your back against a smooth wall (or with a Swiss ball behind your lower back) and feet shoulder-width apart, placed 1.5 feet forward from the wall
execution.description: Represents the core strengthening exercise of Block 2 (Weeks 5–8) in the Rathleff OSD trial. Rather than jumping straight into heavy weights, the adolescent builds structural load tolerance at the maturing tibial tuberosity by progressively adding volume (from 10 total reps up to 60 total reps per session) at a strict slow tempo, guided by the 24-hour morning pain check.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with your back against a smooth wall (or with a Swiss ball behind your lower back) and feet shoulder-width apart, placed 1.5 feet forward from the wall

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly slide down over 3 seconds to the deepest pain-tolerable angle (up to 60°–90° knee flexion, keeping pain <= 2/10)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 2 seconds at the bottom, then slide back up over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Follow the Rathleff Block 2 volume ladder every other day: start with 1 set of 10 reps -> 2 sets of 10 -> 3 sets of 10 -> 3 sets of 15 -> 3 sets of 20 reps across Weeks 5–8.

coachingCues: "Slide down for 3 seconds and up for 3 seconds—if pain at your shin bump goes above 2 out of 10, stop slightly higher on the wall" (external).
commonErrors: Adding sets when next-morning pain is elevated (violates the Rathleff Traffic Light rule); placing the feet too close to the wall so the knees shoot far past the toes prematurely.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: If pain exceeds 2/10 during the squat or increases the next morning, reduce squat depth (e.g. stop at 45°–60°) or step back one set in the volume ladder for 48 hours.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Once 3 sets of 20 bilateral wall squats are completed with <= 2/10 pain and zero next-morning flare, progress to single-leg biased wall squats or hold light dumbbells.

precautions: Adding sets when next-morning pain is elevated (violates the Rathleff Traffic Light rule); placing the feet too close to the wall so the knees shoot far past the toes prematurely.Cues: "Slide down for 3 seconds and up for 3 seconds—if pain at your shin bump goes above 2 out of 10, stop slightly higher on the wall" (external).

name: Rathleff Block 2: Non-kneeling split squat / lunge (vertical shin)
chineseName: 分腿蹲 (跨步深蹲)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Complements the slow wall squat in Block 2 by building unilateral closed-chain strength and frontal-plane knee stability. Using a reverse lunge or static split squat with a vertical front shin keeps tibial tubercle traction moderate while avoiding direct floor contact on the back knee's tibial bump.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral eccentric/concentric; functional single-leg strength (Weeks 5–8)

execution.startingPosition: Stand in a long split-squat stance (or step backward into a reverse lunge) with the affected leg in front
execution.description: Complements the slow wall squat in Block 2 by building unilateral closed-chain strength and frontal-plane knee stability. Using a reverse lunge or static split squat with a vertical front shin keeps tibial tubercle traction moderate while avoiding direct floor contact on the back knee's tibial bump.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a long split-squat stance (or step backward into a reverse lunge) with the affected leg in front

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lower the body straight down over 3 seconds until both knees are at ~75°–90° flexion, hovering the back knee 2 inches above the floor (NEVER bang or kneel the back tibial tuberosity onto the floor!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep the front shin vertical (knee stacked over the ankle) and the torso inclined slightly forward (15°–20°) to co-recruit the glutes

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive through the front heel over 2 seconds to return to standing.

coachingCues: "Hover your back knee two inches off the ground—never tap the hard floor—and drive up through your front heel" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the back knee slam onto a hard floor (causes intense direct contusion pain on an OSD tibial tubercle, especially in bilateral OSD); letting the front knee cave inward into valgus.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce lowering depth to 45°–60° flexion; use hand support on a dowel or wall.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold dumbbells in both hands; progress to forward deceleration lunges as tibial tubercle tenderness resolves.

precautions: Letting the back knee slam onto a hard floor (causes intense direct contusion pain on an OSD tibial tubercle, especially in bilateral OSD); letting the front knee cave inward into valgus.Cues: "Hover your back knee two inches off the ground—never tap the hard floor—and drive up through your front heel" (external).
clinicalNotes: Complements the slow wall squat in Block 2 by building unilateral closed-chain strength and frontal-plane knee stability. Using a reverse lunge or static split squat with a vertical front shin keeps tibial tubercle traction moderate while avoiding direct floor contact on the back knee's tibial bump.

name: Rathleff Return-to-Sport Ladder: Penultimate step deceleration

Teaching the adolescent athlete to lower their centre of mass via the hips (penultimate step braking) and absorb landings across the hip, knee, and ankle prevents symptom relapse upon returning to competitive sport.

name: Supine quad set with McConnell medial-glide tape / VMO facilitation

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Following an acute lateral patellar dislocation or MPFL reconstruction, large intra-articular hemarthrosis/effusion causes profound Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI), disproportionately shutting down and delaying the firing onset of the Vastus Medialis Oblique (VMO)—the only dynamic muscular restraint whose oblique fibers (angled at 50°–55°) pull the patella medially against the lateral pull of the vastus lateralis and iliotibial band.

jointActions: Isometric; open chain; AMI resolution & active medial patellar stabilization

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting with the surgical/injured leg extended and a small rolled towel under the knee (apply medial-glide McConnell tape or a J-brace if lateral tracking apprehension is present)
execution.description: Following an acute lateral patellar dislocation or MPFL reconstruction, large intra-articular hemarthrosis/effusion causes profound Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI), disproportionately shutting down and delaying the firing onset of the Vastus Medialis Oblique (VMO)—the only dynamic muscular restraint whose oblique fibers (angled at 50°–55°) pull the patella medially against the lateral pull of the vastus lateralis and iliotibial band.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine or sit in long-sitting with the surgical/injured leg extended and a small rolled towel under the knee (apply medial-glide McConnell tape or a J-brace if lateral tracking apprehension is present)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Place two fingertips gently over the plump inner teardrop muscle above the kneecap (VMO) for tactile biofeedback

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Contract the quadriceps maximally to push the back of the knee into the towel for 5-10 seconds while feeling the VMO harden under your fingers

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Relax smoothly for 2 seconds and repeat.

coachingCues: "Tighten your thigh and make the inner muscle right under your fingertips pop up firm like a golf ball" (external/internal).
commonErrors: Allowing the leg to roll into external hip/tibial rotation while contracting; firing the hamstrings instead of the quadriceps.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform with a J-brace or medial patellar taping to eliminate apprehension during maximal contraction.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Straight-leg raises (SLR) in 0° locked extension once zero extension lag is verified; seated isometric holds at 30° and 60° flexion.

precautions: Allowing the leg to roll into external hip/tibial rotation while contracting; firing the hamstrings instead of the quadriceps. Cues: "Tighten your thigh and make the inner muscle right under your fingertips pop up firm like a golf ball" (external/internal).
clinicalNotes: Following an acute lateral patellar dislocation or MPFL reconstruction, large intra-articular hemarthrosis/effusion causes profound Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI), disproportionately shutting down and delaying the firing onset of the Vastus Medialis Oblique (VMO)—the only dynamic muscular restraint whose oblique fibers (angled at 50°–55°) pull the patella medially against the lateral pull of the vastus lateralis and iliotibial band.

name: Seated / standing banded terminal knee extension (30°–0° trochlear entry)
chineseName: 站姿 彈力帶 末端膝伸展 (TKE) 內側股肌活化
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: The 30°–0° flexion arc is the exact biomechanical zone where the patella exits and enters the bony femoral trochlear groove (and where the J-sign of lateral patellar maltracking occurs). Performing controlled closed-chain TKEs with the foot fixed on the ground trains coordinated VMO/quadriceps firing and axial joint compression through this critical 30°–0° transition without open-chain lateral shear.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; controlled trochlear engagement

execution.startingPosition: 1) Loop a resistance band around a sturdy post at knee height and step the affected leg inside so the band rests behind the knee crease
execution.description: The 30°–0° flexion arc is the exact biomechanical zone where the patella exits and enters the bony femoral trochlear groove (and where the J-sign of lateral patellar maltracking occurs). Performing controlled closed-chain TKEs with the foot fixed on the ground trains coordinated VMO/quadriceps firing and axial joint compression through this critical 30°–0° transition without open-chain lateral shear.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a resistance band around a sturdy post at knee height and step the affected leg inside so the band rests behind the knee crease

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand with the heel flat on the floor and toes pointing strictly straight ahead at 12 o'clock (zero external tibial rotation)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Allow the band to bend the knee slowly from 0° to 30° (as the patella glides into the trochlear groove), then contract the quadriceps and glutes to straighten the knee back to 0° over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at 0° without snapping into hyperextension.

coachingCues: "Keep your foot pointed dead straight at 12 o'clock and press the back of your knee into the band until your leg is straight, never locked backward" (external).
commonErrors: Turning the foot outward (external tibial rotation moves the tibial tuberosity laterally, increasing the Q-angle and pulling the patella laterally out of the groove!); snapping backward into knee hyperextension (genu recurvatum pushes the patella superiorly completely above the trochlear walls).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform wearing a patellar stabilizing J-brace; use lighter band tension.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer resistance band; single-leg stance TKE; add a 30° mini-squat at the bottom of the movement.

precautions: Turning the foot outward (external tibial rotation moves the tibial tuberosity laterally, increasing the Q-angle and pulling the patella laterally out of the groove!); snapping backward into knee hyperextension (genu recurvatum pushes the patella superiorly completely above the trochlear walls). Cues: "Keep your foot pointed dead straight at 12 o'clock and press the back of your knee into the band until your leg is straight, never locked backward" (external).
clinicalNotes: The 30°–0° flexion arc is the exact biomechanical zone where the patella exits and enters the bony femoral trochlear groove (and where the J-sign of lateral patellar maltracking occurs). Performing controlled closed-chain TKEs with the foot fixed on the ground trains coordinated VMO/quadriceps firing and axial joint compression through this critical 30°–0° transition without open-chain lateral shear.

description: Kinematic MRI studies show that "lateral patellar dislocation" is actually caused by the femur rotating internally underneath a stationary patella! Strengthening the hip external rotators and posterior gluteus medius prevents the femoral trochlear groove from rotating medially away from the kneecap.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; proximal femoral rotation control

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your unaffected side with hips at 45° and knees bent at 90°, with a resistance band looped above the knees
execution.description: Kinematic MRI studies show that "lateral patellar dislocation" is actually caused by the femur rotating internally underneath a stationary patella! Strengthening the hip external rotators and posterior gluteus medius prevents the femoral trochlear groove from rotating medially away from the kneecap.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your unaffected side with hips at 45° and knees bent at 90°, with a resistance band looped above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep your feet together and pelvis stacked vertically

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Externally rotate the top hip to lift the top knee toward the ceiling over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower slowly over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Follow immediately with 12 straight-leg side-lying hip abductions against the wall.

coachingCues: "Squeeze deep in your back pocket to open the knee without letting your belt buckle roll backward" (external).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Unresisted clamshells with back supported against a wall.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Side-plank clamshell (lifting the bottom hip off the mat while opening the top knee); heavier band resistance.

precautions: Rolling the pelvis backward; flexing the hip during abduction (which recruits the TFL—the TFL tightens the lateral iliotibial band and lateral retinaculum, pulling the patella laterally!). Cues: "Squeeze deep in your back pocket to open the knee without letting your belt buckle roll backward" (external).
clinicalNotes: Kinematic MRI studies show that "lateral patellar dislocation" is actually caused by the femur rotating internally underneath a stationary patella! Strengthening the hip external rotators and posterior gluteus medius prevents the femoral trochlear groove from rotating medially away from the kneecap.

steps.instruction: Sit the hips back and lower over 3 seconds from 0° through the 30° trochlear entry zone down to 60° flexion while keeping the patellae tracking strictly over the second toes

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Drive up over 2 seconds, stopping at 0° neutral extension (never hyperextending).

coachingCues: "Guide your kneecaps straight over your second toes and maintain an active arch in both feet" (external).
commonErrors: Allowing medial knee valgus collapse or pronation of the foot arches during the first 30° of descent; hyperextending the knees at the top.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Wall slide (0°–45° flexion) with back supported against a wall.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress depth to 75°–90° once MPFL flexion permissions allow (typically after Week 6); add goblet dumbbell load; transition to Spanish squats.

precautions: Allowing medial knee valgus collapse or pronation of the foot arches during the first 30° of descent; hyperextending the knees at the top. Cues: "Guide your kneecaps straight over your second toes and maintain an active arch in both feet" (external).
clinicalNotes: Trains smooth, congruent patellar entry into the trochlear groove (0° -> 30°) and exit out of the groove (30° -> 0°) under bilateral axial loading. Because the VMO originates partly from the adductor magnus tendon, combining neutral frontal-plane alignment with progressive squat depth restores balanced medial-lateral quadriceps force couples.

steps.title: 步驟 2

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg with a light resistance band pulling the stance knee medially

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Push the knee gently outward against the band so the patella tracks over the second toe

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly bend the stance knee over 3-4 seconds from 0° through the critical 0°–30° trochlear entry window down to 50°–60° flexion until the floating heel lightly taps the floor

progressions.name: 進階方案

jointActions: Plyometric deceleration; closed chain; high-velocity valgus & rotation resistance

execution.startingPosition: 1) Phase 1 (Single-Leg Drop Landing): Step off a 12-inch box and land softly on the affected leg, flexing rapidly past the vulnerable 0°–30° zone into a stable 45°–60° athletic pocket (where the patella is deeply seated in the trochlea) with zero medial knee collapse

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Single-Leg Drop Landing): Step off a 12-inch box and land softly on the affected leg, flexing rapidly past the vulnerable 0°–30° zone into a stable 45°–60° athletic pocket (where the patella is deeply seated in the trochlea) with zero medial knee collapse. Hold for 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Lateral Bound to Stick): Bound sideways 3-4 feet onto the affected leg and stick the landing for 3 seconds with foot, knee, and hip aligned straight ahead.

commonErrors: Landing stiff-legged at 15°–25° knee flexion (leaves the patella uncontained above the trochlear groove during peak impact!); landing with the foot turned outward and knee caved inward.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Double-leg drop landings and bilateral lateral hops.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a 90° rotational hop-and-stick (jumping and turning in mid-air to land in strict alignment without femoral-tibial twist); reactive cutting drills.

precautions: Landing stiff-legged at 15°–25° knee flexion (leaves the patella uncontained above the trochlear groove during peak impact!); landing with the foot turned outward and knee caved inward. Cues: "Drop straight past the danger zone into a deep, quiet 45-degree athletic pocket with your knee stacked over your shoelaces" (external).
clinicalNotes: Over 80% of non-contact sports patellar dislocations occur when an athlete lands or plants to cut with the knee near extension (10°–25° flexion) while the femur collapses into valgus and internal rotation. description: Serves as Stage 1 of the Cook & Rio tendon protocol. Heavy sustained mid-range isometric contractions reduce cortical motor inhibition of the quadriceps and produce immediate exercise-induced analgesia lasting several hours, without subjecting the inferior pole of the patella to repetitive shear or insertional compression.

jointActions: Open chain; heavy isometric; Stage 1 tendon analgesia & motor disinhibition

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on a seated leg extension machine with the knee positioned at 60° of flexion (or between 30° and 60°)
execution.description: Serves as Stage 1 of the Cook & Rio tendon protocol. Heavy sustained mid-range isometric contractions reduce cortical motor inhibition of the quadriceps and produce immediate exercise-induced analgesia lasting several hours, without subjecting the inferior pole of the patella to repetitive shear or insertional compression.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit upright on a seated leg extension machine with the knee positioned at 60° of flexion (or between 30° and 60°)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Set a heavy load corresponding to roughly 70%–80% of maximum voluntary isometric contraction (a load you can barely hold still without shaking)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Extend slightly to lift the weight stack 1 inch and hold completely motionless for 45 seconds using a single leg

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rest for 2 full minutes to allow metabolic recovery, then repeat for 5 total holds.

coachingCues: "Lift the weight one inch and freeze your shin like a concrete pillar for 45 seconds" (external); "Drive steady, smooth tension through the centre of your front thigh without bouncing" (internal).
commonErrors: Using a light weight or band that fails to reach the 70% MVIC threshold required for cortical disinhibition; bouncing or pulsing the weight instead of a pure static hold; extending into full 0° lockout where fat-pad impingement may occur.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce hold duration to 30 seconds; lower resistance to 50%–60% MVIC if muscle tremor or pain >4/10 occurs during the hold; perform bilaterally before single-leg.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase external load on the stack as strength improves; transition to Stage 2 Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR) isotonic knee extensions once pain irritability settles.

precautions: Using a light weight or band that fails to reach the 70% MVIC threshold required for cortical disinhibition; bouncing or pulsing the weight instead of a pure static hold; extending into full 0° lockout where fat-pad impingement may occur.Cues: "Lift the weight one inch and freeze your shin like a concrete pillar for 45 seconds" (external); "Drive steady, smooth tension through the centre of your front thigh without bouncing" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Serves as Stage 1 of the Cook & Rio tendon protocol. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Anchor a heavy, non-elastic rigid strap around a rack or pillar at knee height and step both legs inside so the strap rests behind the upper calves/proximal tibias

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Walk backward to pull the strap tight with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Sit back into a 70°–90° squat while keeping the torso completely upright

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold the static position for 45 seconds, rest 2 minutes, and repeat for 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Lean back against the strap with your chest tall as if sitting in an invisible chair" (external); "Push your shins forward into the strap to keep tension on your quads" (internal).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Position yourself on a 45° leg press sled with the affected foot placed centrally on the footplate, hip-width aligned

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Unrack the sled and lower the weight slowly over a strict 3-to-4-second count down to 90° knee flexion

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Without bouncing at the bottom, press the sled back up over a slow 3-to-4-second count (total time under tension = 6-8 seconds per rep)

steps.title: 步驟 4

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Perform 3 small, rhythmic double-leg pogo hops in place (minimal knee bend, springing off the balls of the feet)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: On the 4th contact, rapidly snap the feet into an athletic quarter-squat (about 45°–60° knee flexion), absorbing the landing quietly

steps.title: 步驟 4

commonErrors: Sinking too deeply (>75° knee flexion) during early energy-storage hops (triggers tendon flare-ups); landing with stiff, locked knees or medial valgus collapse; performing energy-storage drills on consecutive days.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Tall-to-short athletic snap-downs from tiptoes without leaving the ground (zero flight phase); bilateral low-amplitude pogo hops only.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform single-leg pogo hops (2-3 small hops) into a single-leg stick; progress to forward line hops.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place 3 to 4 low mini-hurdles (6-12 inches) spaced 2-3 feet apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand on one leg (or two legs initially), dip rapidly into a countermovement quarter-squat, and hop explosively over the first hurdle

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Initially stick each landing for 2 seconds between hurdles (Stage 3 energy storage/absorption); once tolerated with zero next-day flare, rebound continuously over all hurdles with short ground contact times (Stage 4 elastic release).

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your side with hips flexed to about 45° and knees bent to 90°, heels aligned with your spine and a resistance band looped just above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep your feet touching together and your pelvis stacked vertically

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lift the top knee upward toward the ceiling over 2 seconds by externally rotating the hip

steps.title: 步驟 4

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; posterolateral hip strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your side with your back, buttocks and top heel touching a wall behind you; bend the bottom leg slightly for stability
execution.description: Produces high electromyographic (EMG) recruitment of the gluteus medius while minimizing TFL overactivity. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your side with your back, buttocks and top heel touching a wall behind you; bend the bottom leg slightly for stability

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep the top leg completely straight with toes pointing forward or slightly downward (slight hip internal rotation) and hip in 5°–10° extension

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slide the top heel straight up the wall to about 30°–40° abduction over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the peak and lower slowly over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Keep your heel scraping gently against the wall behind you as you lift" (external); "Lead the lift with the back of your heel, keeping your toes angled slightly down" (internal).
commonErrors: Drifting the leg forward in front of the body (hip flexion substitution via TFL and hip flexors); turning the toes upward toward the ceiling; hiking the lateral waist (quadratus lumborum substitution).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Shorten the lever arm by bending the knee; perform supine slider hip abduction if side-lying causes trochanteric discomfort.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add an ankle cuff weight (1-3 kg) or loop a resistance band around the ankles; add 5-second isometric holds at top range.

precautions: Drifting the leg forward in front of the body (hip flexion substitution via TFL and hip flexors); turning the toes upward toward the ceiling; hiking the lateral waist (quadratus lumborum substitution). Cues: "Keep your heel scraping gently against the wall behind you as you lift" (external); "Lead the lift with the back of your heel, keeping your toes angled slightly down" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Produces high electromyographic (EMG) recruitment of the gluteus medius while minimizing TFL overactivity. name: Shallow-angle isometric wall sit (0°–45° safe arc)
chineseName: 靠牆等長靜蹲 (髕股關節低壓負重)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Induces exercise-induced hypoalgesia (cortical motor disinhibition and tendon/peripatellar pain relief) while building quadriceps load capacity. In closed kinetic chain exercises, patellofemoral joint stress (PFJS) increases steeply past 45°–60° of knee flexion; training at 30°–45° maximizes quadriceps recruitment while keeping compressive patellofemoral contact stress within a pain-free envelope.

jointActions: Closed chain; isometric; analgesic quadriceps loading

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall and feet shoulder-width apart, placed about 1.5 feet forward from the wall
execution.description: Induces exercise-induced hypoalgesia (cortical motor disinhibition and tendon/peripatellar pain relief) while building quadriceps load capacity. In closed kinetic chain exercises, patellofemoral joint stress (PFJS) increases steeply past 45°–60° of knee flexion; training at 30°–45° maximizes quadriceps recruitment while keeping compressive patellofemoral contact stress within a pain-free envelope.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall and feet shoulder-width apart, placed about 1.5 feet forward from the wall

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slide down into a shallow squat between 30° and 45° of knee flexion (staying above the angle where retropatellar pain begins)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep shins vertical and knees aligned over the second toes

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold the static position for 30-45 seconds, then push through the heels to slide back up.

coachingCues: "Slide down only until you hit the top of your comfort zone and press your lower back flat into the wall" (external); "Spread the floor apart with your feet and feel equal pressure across both thighs" (internal).
commonErrors: Dropping straight to 90° knee flexion when the joint is still irritable (provoking sharp retropatellar pain); allowing knees to cave inward; pushing with hands resting on the thighs.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Decrease knee flexion angle to 20°–30°; shorten hold time to 15-20 seconds.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progressively increase knee flexion angle toward 60°–75° as symptoms subside; add a resistance band above the knees to co-activate hip abductors; transition to single-leg biased wall sits.

precautions: Dropping straight to 90° knee flexion when the joint is still irritable (provoking sharp retropatellar pain); allowing knees to cave inward; pushing with hands resting on the thighs. Cues: "Slide down only until you hit the top of your comfort zone and press your lower back flat into the wall" (external); "Spread the floor apart with your feet and feel equal pressure across both thighs" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Induces exercise-induced hypoalgesia (cortical motor disinhibition and tendon/peripatellar pain relief) while building quadriceps load capacity. In closed kinetic chain exercises, patellofemoral joint stress (PFJS) increases steeply past 45°–60° of knee flexion; training at 30°–45° maximizes quadriceps recruitment while keeping compressive patellofemoral contact stress within a pain-free envelope.

name: Lateral band walk (Monster / Crab walk)

description: Transitions proximal hip abductor and external rotator strength into a functional, closed kinetic chain posture. Teaches the patient to maintain frontal-plane knee alignment against an external adduction/internal rotation band force while the trail leg works eccentrically to control step width.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; dynamic hip-knee alignment

execution.startingPosition: Place a looped resistance band just above the ankles or around the forefeet (distal placement increases lever arm and minimizes TFL dominance)
execution.description: Transitions proximal hip abductor and external rotator strength into a functional, closed kinetic chain posture. Teaches the patient to maintain frontal-plane knee alignment against an external adduction/internal rotation band force while the trail leg works eccentrically to control step width.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place a looped resistance band just above the ankles or around the forefeet (distal placement increases lever arm and minimizes TFL dominance)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Assume an athletic quarter-squat (about 30° hip and knee flexion) with feet hip-width apart and toes pointed straight ahead

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step sideways 6-8 inches with the lead foot, then slowly bring the trail foot in partway so constant band tension is maintained

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Take 10-15 steps in one direction, then return in the opposite direction.

coachingCues: "Keep your headlights (hips and toes) pointed straight ahead and glide your head at the same ceiling height" (external); "Control the trailing leg slowly so the band never snaps your foot inward" (internal).
commonErrors: Dragging the trail foot or letting the feet come all the way together (losing band tension); rocking the torso laterally like a pendulum to step; turning the lead toes outward to recruit TFL and hip flexors.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Place the band just above the knees (shorter lever arm); perform in a taller stance (15° knee bend).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Move the band from above the knees to the ankles, then around the forefeet; use a heavier resistance band; increase athletic squat depth to 45°.

precautions: Dragging the trail foot or letting the feet come all the way together (losing band tension); rocking the torso laterally like a pendulum to step; turning the lead toes outward to recruit TFL and hip flexors. Cues: "Keep your headlights (hips and toes) pointed straight ahead and glide your head at the same ceiling height" (external); "Control the trailing leg slowly so the band never snaps your foot inward" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Transitions proximal hip abductor and external rotator strength into a functional, closed kinetic chain posture. Teaches the patient to maintain frontal-plane knee alignment against an external adduction/internal rotation band force while the trail leg works eccentrically to control step width.

name: Standing pelvic hitch (hip hike on step)
chineseName: Standing pelvic hitch (hip hike on step)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Directly targets the single-limb mid-stance mechanism of PFP. When the stance-limb gluteus medius fails during walking or running, the contralateral pelvis drops (Trendelenburg sign), which forces the femur into adduction and internal rotation beneath the patella. The pelvic hitch isolates stance-hip frontal-plane torque without bending the knee or stressing the patellofemoral joint.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; frontal-plane pelvic control

execution.startingPosition: Stand sideways on the edge of a 2-to-4-inch step on the affected leg, with the unaffected leg hanging free off the side
execution.description: Directly targets the single-limb mid-stance mechanism of PFP. When the stance-limb gluteus medius fails during walking or running, the contralateral pelvis drops (Trendelenburg sign), which forces the femur into adduction and internal rotation beneath the patella. The pelvic hitch isolates stance-hip frontal-plane torque without bending the knee or stressing the patellofemoral joint.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand sideways on the edge of a 2-to-4-inch step on the affected leg, with the unaffected leg hanging free off the side

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lock the stance knee in a straight but soft (unlocked) position

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly let the free hip drop 1-2 inches below the level of the stance hip over 3 seconds (eccentric gluteus medius loading)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Contract the outer stance hip to hike the free pelvis back up slightly above level over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and repeat.

coachingCues: "Keep both knees straight and move your belt buckle like a seesaw" (external); "Pull the floor down through your standing heel and squeeze the side of your standing hip to lift the opposite pelvis" (internal).
commonErrors: Bending the stance knee to lower the foot instead of moving solely at the pelvis; leaning the shoulders laterally toward the stance side; hiking from the ribcage/waist rather than pulling through the stance glute.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Use fingertip support on a wall or dowel; reduce the pelvic drop excursion; perform isometric single-leg stance holding the pelvis level in front of a mirror.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a dumbbell in the contralateral hand (hanging side); remove fingertip balance support; combine with a small single-leg knee bend after leveling the pelvis.

precautions: Bending the stance knee to lower the foot instead of moving solely at the pelvis; leaning the shoulders laterally toward the stance side; hiking from the ribcage/waist rather than pulling through the stance glute. Cues: "Keep both knees straight and move your belt buckle like a seesaw" (external); "Pull the floor down through your standing heel and squeeze the side of your standing hip to lift the opposite pelvis" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Directly targets the single-limb mid-stance mechanism of PFP. When the stance-limb gluteus medius fails during walking or running, the contralateral pelvis drops (Trendelenburg sign), which forces the femur into adduction and internal rotation beneath the patella. The pelvic hitch isolates stance-hip frontal-plane torque without bending the knee or stressing the patellofemoral joint.

description: Develops high hip extensor and external rotator torque alongside foot-to-hip rotational stability while maintaining a constant, shallow knee flexion angle (15°–20°). This allows heavy closed-chain single-leg loading with virtually zero patellofemoral joint compression, making it ideal for strengthening the kinetic chain when deep knee flexion is still provocative.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric/concentric; posterior chain & rotational stability

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg with the knee flexed slightly at 15°–20° and hold a light support (wall or dowel) with the opposite hand if needed
execution.description: Develops high hip extensor and external rotator torque alongside foot-to-hip rotational stability while maintaining a constant, shallow knee flexion angle (15°–20°). steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with the knee flexed slightly at 15°–20° and hold a light support (wall or dowel) with the opposite hand if needed

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge backward at the hip while extending the free leg straight behind you in line with your torso

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower the torso over 3 seconds until a hamstring stretch is felt, keeping both hip bones squared toward the floor

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive the stance hip forward to return to tall standing.

coachingCues: "Push your hips straight back to close a car door with your glutes while keeping both hip headlights shining straight down at the floor" (external); "Maintain a soft, fixed knee bend and drive through your standing heel" (internal).
commonErrors: Opening the pelvis outward toward the free leg ("airplane hip opening"); rounding the lumbar spine instead of hinging at the hip; turning the exercise into a squat by bending the stance knee past 30°.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Kickstand (B-stance) RDL with the back toe resting lightly on the floor behind the heel; bilateral Romanian deadlift.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Remove hand support; hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in the contralateral hand (increases external hip adduction/internal rotation challenge); progress to B-stance or pure unsupported SL RDL.

precautions: Opening the pelvis outward toward the free leg ("airplane hip opening"); rounding the lumbar spine instead of hinging at the hip; turning the exercise into a squat by bending the stance knee past 30°. Cues: "Push your hips straight back to close a car door with your glutes while keeping both hip headlights shining straight down at the floor" (external); "Maintain a soft, fixed knee bend and drive through your standing heel" (internal).

execution.description: Systematically grades patellofemoral joint stress by controlling the exact knee flexion ceiling with a physical box target. Combines high quadriceps demand with tri-planar hip and trunk control, training the patient to avoid dynamic knee valgus and femoral internal rotation under full single-limb body weight.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on one leg directly in front of a plyo box or adjustable plinth set to a pain-free height (starting high at 18-20 inches, around 45°–60° knee flexion)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Extend the non-stance leg slightly forward and reach both arms ahead as a counterbalance

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hinge slightly at the hip and bend the knee slowly over 3 seconds to lightly tap the box with your glutes without plopping down

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive up through the midfoot and heel to return to single-leg standing.

coachingCues: "Tap the box quietly without transferring your weight and keep your kneecap aligned with your middle toes" (external); "Sit back into your hip while keeping your arch active" (internal).
commonErrors: Collapsing the knee medially inside the big toe on the descent or ascent; dropping uncontrolled onto the box in the final 10 degrees; excessive lateral trunk lean.

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Collapsing the knee medially inside the big toe on the descent or ascent; dropping uncontrolled onto the box in the final 10 degrees; excessive lateral trunk lean. Cues: "Tap the box quietly without transferring your weight and keep your kneecap aligned with your middle toes" (external); "Sit back into your hip while keeping your arch active" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Systematically grades patellofemoral joint stress by controlling the exact knee flexion ceiling with a physical box target. name: Forward (anterior) step-down

rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化

description: Descending stairs is a hallmark provocative task in PFP because the body's centre of mass moves anteriorly while the tibia translates forward, creating high eccentric quadriceps and patellofemoral compressive forces. The forward step-down directly re-educates sagittal-plane shock absorption and frontal-plane alignment (eliminating medial knee drift and pelvic drop) required for pain-free stair descent and downhill running.

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric; patellofemoral deceleration & load tolerance

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the top of a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg, facing forward toward the edge
execution.description: Descending stairs is a hallmark provocative task in PFP because the body's centre of mass moves anteriorly while the tibia translates forward, creating high eccentric quadriceps and patellofemoral compressive forces. The forward step-down directly re-educates sagittal-plane shock absorption and frontal-plane alignment (eliminating medial knee drift and pelvic drop) required for pain-free stair descent and downhill running.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the top of a 4-to-6-inch step on the affected leg, facing forward toward the edge

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step the free foot forward over the edge with the ankle dorsiflexed (toes pulled up)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly bend the stance knee over 3 seconds to lower the free heel down until it lightly brushes the floor in front of the step

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Without putting weight on the lower foot, press through the stance heel to return to the starting position.

coachingCues: "Laser-point your kneecap straight ahead into a mirror and kiss the floor with your floating heel" (external); "Control the lowering phase smoothly through your front thigh and outer hip" (internal).
commonErrors: Dynamic knee valgus collapse as the knee passes over the toes; contralateral hip drop; plantarflexing the floating foot to reach the floor early; bouncing off the floor.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce step height to 2 inches; perform a retro (backward) step-down where the free leg reaches behind the step (reduces anterior knee excursion and PFJS); use handrail support.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase step height from 4 inches to 6-8 inches; loop a resistance band around the stance knee pulling medially (reactive lateral glute feed-forward); hold light dumbbells.

precautions: Dynamic knee valgus collapse as the knee passes over the toes; contralateral hip drop; plantarflexing the floating foot to reach the floor early; bouncing off the floor. Cues: "Laser-point your kneecap straight ahead into a mirror and kiss the floor with your floating heel" (external); "Control the lowering phase smoothly through your front thigh and outer hip" (internal).
clinicalNotes: Descending stairs is a hallmark provocative task in PFP because the body's centre of mass moves anteriorly while the tibia translates forward, creating high eccentric quadriceps and patellofemoral compressive forces. The forward step-down directly re-educates sagittal-plane shock absorption and frontal-plane alignment (eliminating medial knee drift and pelvic drop) required for pain-free stair descent and downhill running.

description: Clinical studies show that Pes Anserinus Bursitis is rarely an isolated local problem—it is almost always secondary to proximal gluteus medius/maximus weakness or medial Knee OA that allows the femur to adduct and internally rotate during stance. Building strong hip abductors and external rotators takes the anti-valgus "emergency braking" burden off the small pes anserinus tendons.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; posterolateral hip strengthening

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your unaffected side with a pillow placed between your knees when resting

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Perform 12-15 side-lying clamshells (hips at 45°, knees at 90°, opening the top knee while keeping pelvis stacked)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Straighten the top leg against a wall behind you and perform 12-15 straight-leg hip abduction lifts (2s up, 2s hold, 3s down).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Unresisted clamshells and side-lying isometric abduction holds.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a resistance band above the knees (above the joint line, never below the knee over the pes anserinus!); progress to standing hip abduction.

precautions: Placing the resistance band below the knee over the tender pes anserinus insertion; letting the top knee drop across the body into adduction between sets (stretches and compresses the pes anserinus against the tibia—always rest the top leg on a pillow!).Cues: "Rest your top knee on a pillow between sets so it never hangs across your body, and lift from your back hip pocket" (external).

description: Pes planus (flat foot / excessive subtalar pronation) causes obligatory internal tibial rotation during weight acceptance, which forces a compensatory valgus torque at the knee and twists the pes anserinus insertion on the proximal tibia. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit or stand with the affected foot flat on the floor (or on a towel)

steps.title: 步驟 2

steps.title: 步驟 3

precautions: Clawing the toes tightly instead of shortening the arch from the ball of the big toe; lifting the big toe off the floor.Cues: "Keep your toes long and flat on the floor while gently suctioning your inner arch upward like a suction cup" (external).

name: Supine eccentric hamstring sliders (progressive semitendinosus remodeling)

description: Once acute bursitis has settled, the tendinopathic semitendinosus tendon requires progressive eccentric tensile loading (Stage 2 tendon remodeling) to restore collagen fiber alignment and eccentric braking strength. By sliding out with the hips bridged and resetting on the floor unloaded, the semitendinosus receives pure controlled eccentric lengthening without rapid whip-like friction over the medial tibia.

jointActions: Closed chain; slow eccentric; Stage 2 tendon matrix loading

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine on a smooth floor with both heels resting on furniture sliders, a towel, or socks, knees bent at 90°
execution.description: Once acute bursitis has settled, the tendinopathic semitendinosus tendon requires progressive eccentric tensile loading (Stage 2 tendon remodeling) to restore collagen fiber alignment and eccentric braking strength. By sliding out with the hips bridged and resetting on the floor unloaded, the semitendinosus receives pure controlled eccentric lengthening without rapid whip-like friction over the medial tibia.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine on a smooth floor with both heels resting on furniture sliders, a towel, or socks, knees bent at 90°

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Bridge the hips up off the floor

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the hips lifted and toes pointed straight up at the ceiling (neutral tibial rotation), slowly slide both heels outward over a strict 4-second eccentric count until the knees are nearly straight (~15°–20° bend)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drop the hips softly to the floor, bend the knees back to 90° on the floor (unloaded), bridge up again, and repeat.

coachingCues: "Keep your toes pointed straight at 12 o'clock and glide your heels out over a slow 4-second count" (external).
commonErrors: Externally rotating the feet/tibias during the slide-out (twists the pes anserinus); sliding out too fast (<2 seconds).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Slide out only halfway (from 90° to 45° flexion); seated slow resistance-band hamstring curls (3s concentric / 3s eccentric).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform both the eccentric slide-out AND concentric curl-in with the hips bridged; progress to single-leg eccentric sliders.

precautions: Externally rotating the feet/tibias during the slide-out (twists the pes anserinus); sliding out too fast (<2 seconds).Cues: "Keep your toes pointed straight at 12 o'clock and glide your heels out over a slow 4-second count" (external).
clinicalNotes: Once acute bursitis has settled, the tendinopathic semitendinosus tendon requires progressive eccentric tensile loading (Stage 2 tendon remodeling) to restore collagen fiber alignment and eccentric braking strength. By sliding out with the hips bridged and resetting on the floor unloaded, the semitendinosus receives pure controlled eccentric lengthening without rapid whip-like friction over the medial tibia.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a split stance (or rear-foot elevated Bulgarian split squat) with 85% of weight on the front (affected) leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lower straight down over 3 seconds to a target pad or box under the rear knee (starting at ~60°–70° front knee flexion and lowering the pad each week to reach 90° flexion)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 1 second at the bottom without bouncing, then drive through the front heel over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Kiss the foam pad lightly with your back knee on a 3-count and drive smoothly up through your front foot" (external).
commonErrors: Dropping fast into the bottom of the split squat (maximizes elastic compressive shock on the deep quadriceps tendon insertion); dynamic knee valgus.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Remove rear-knee depth pads to reach full 90° flexion; hold heavy dumbbells or barbell load.

precautions: Dropping fast into the bottom of the split squat (maximizes elastic compressive shock on the deep quadriceps tendon insertion); dynamic knee valgus.Cues: "Kiss the foam pad lightly with your back knee on a 3-count and drive smoothly up through your front foot" (external).

execution.startingPosition: Phase 3A (Box Jump with Step-Down): Stand in front of an 18-to-24-inch plyo box, perform a rapid countermovement dip to ~60°, explode onto the box, land softly at a shallow knee angle on top of the box, and step down one foot at a time

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Phase 3A (Box Jump with Step-Down): Stand in front of an 18-to-24-inch plyo box, perform a rapid countermovement dip to ~60°, explode onto the box, land softly at a shallow knee angle on top of the box, and step down one foot at a time

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 3B/4 (Depth Drop to Rebound): Once box jumps are 100% pain-free the next morning, step off a 12-to-18-inch box, absorb the landing on flat ground, and immediately rebound into a maximal vertical or broad jump.

coachingCues: "Use a box height where you can land tall in a quarter-squat on top of the box, then step down under control" (external).

progressions.name: 進階方案

description: Calms pain and restores quadriceps motor unit recruitment without pulling aggressively on the immature inferior patellar pole apophysis. By keeping the knee angle shallow (30°–45°) and the shins vertical, the patellar tendon traction force is kept within the healing tolerance of the cartilaginous ossification center.

jointActions: Closed chain; submaximal isometric; analgesic loading without excessive apophyseal traction

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall and feet shoulder-width apart, placed about 1.5 feet forward from the wall
execution.description: Calms pain and restores quadriceps motor unit recruitment without pulling aggressively on the immature inferior patellar pole apophysis. By keeping the knee angle shallow (30°–45°) and the shins vertical, the patellar tendon traction force is kept within the healing tolerance of the cartilaginous ossification center.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall and feet shoulder-width apart, placed about 1.5 feet forward from the wall

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slide down slightly to a shallow 30°–45° knee bend where pain at the bottom tip of the kneecap is 0 to 2/10 at most

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep your shins nearly vertical so your knees do not push far out over your toes

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold steady for 30-45 seconds, rest 1 minute, and repeat for 4-5 holds.

coachingCues: "Slide down just enough to wake up your thigh muscles with zero pinch at the bottom of your kneecap" (external).
commonErrors: Pushing a young athlete through >4/10 pain during a deep 90° wall sit (unlike adult tendinopathy where heavy load is desired, excessive traction in an adolescent growth plate prolongs apophysitis); letting knees cave inward.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Slide up higher on the wall (20°–30° knee bend) or shorten hold duration to 20 seconds if any discomfort >2/10 is felt at the inferior pole.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Deepen the wall sit slowly toward 60° as palpation tenderness at the inferior pole resolves; transition to slow double-leg box squats.

precautions: Pushing a young athlete through >4/10 pain during a deep 90° wall sit (unlike adult tendinopathy where heavy load is desired, excessive traction in an adolescent growth plate prolongs apophysitis); letting knees cave inward. Cues: "Slide down just enough to wake up your thigh muscles with zero pinch at the bottom of your kneecap" (external).

description: Adolescents undergoing a rapid growth spurt frequently develop a "quadriceps-dominant" movement strategy where they rely almost exclusively on the knee extensors to accelerate, decelerate, and jump, overloading the inferior patellar pole. Strengthening the gluteus maximus and hamstrings builds the "hip engine" to share propulsion and braking forces across the posterior chain.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; hip-extensor load sharing

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your back with knees bent to ~90° and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart
execution.description: Adolescents undergoing a rapid growth spurt frequently develop a "quadriceps-dominant" movement strategy where they rely almost exclusively on the knee extensors to accelerate, decelerate, and jump, overloading the inferior patellar pole. Strengthening the gluteus maximus and hamstrings builds the "hip engine" to share propulsion and braking forces across the posterior chain.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your back with knees bent to ~90° and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Squeeze your glutes and press through both heels to lift your hips until your knees, hips, and shoulders form a straight diagonal line

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold the top position for 3 seconds without overarching your lower back

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower slowly over 3 seconds and repeat.

coachingCues: "Lift your toes slightly inside your shoes and drive your heels through the floor to squeeze your glutes" (external).
commonErrors: Pushing through the toes instead of the heels (shifts load back to the quads and calves); arching the lower back instead of extending the hips.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Shorten hold time to 1 second; move feet slightly closer to the hips if hamstring cramping occurs.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Loop a resistance band above the knees; progress to marching bridges and single-leg glute bridges.

precautions: Pushing through the toes instead of the heels (shifts load back to the quads and calves); arching the lower back instead of extending the hips. Cues: "Lift your toes slightly inside your shoes and drive your heels through the floor to squeeze your glutes" (external).
clinicalNotes: Adolescents undergoing a rapid growth spurt frequently develop a "quadriceps-dominant" movement strategy where they rely almost exclusively on the knee extensors to accelerate, decelerate, and jump, overloading the inferior patellar pole. Strengthening the gluteus maximus and hamstrings builds the "hip engine" to share propulsion and braking forces across the posterior chain.

name: Side-lying clamshell & straight-leg hip abduction
chineseName: 側臥 蚌殼式臀中肌外展訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
