description: Rapid adolescent growth widens and lengthens the femur, drastically increasing the external lever arm on the hip abductors and causing temporary neuromuscular awkwardness ("adolescent motor clumsiness") with dynamic knee valgus. Strengthening the posterolateral hip stabilizes femoral tracking so the patellar tendon pulls in a straight line rather than twisting at an oblique angle on the inferior patellar pole.

jointActions: Open chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; zero-traction proximal hip strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Part 1 (Clamshell): Lie on your side with knees bent at 90° and feet together; open the top knee like a clamshell for 12-15 reps without rolling the pelvis back

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Part 1 (Clamshell): Lie on your side with knees bent at 90° and feet together; open the top knee like a clamshell for 12-15 reps without rolling the pelvis back

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Part 2 (Straight-Leg Abduction): Straighten the top leg in line with the trunk (heel sliding against a wall behind you) and lift the straight leg up to 35° for 12-15 reps.

coachingCues: "Keep your hip bones stacked one on top of the other and lift from your side hip pocket" (external).
commonErrors: Rolling the torso backward; flexing the hip forward during straight-leg lifts.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a light-to-moderate resistance band above the knees; progress to weight-bearing lateral band walks.

precautions: Rolling the torso backward; flexing the hip forward during straight-leg lifts. Cues: "Keep your hip bones stacked one on top of the other and lift from your side hip pocket" (external).

name: Mid-belly quadriceps foam roll & gentle side-lying hip flexor stretch
chineseName: Mid-belly quadriceps foam roll & gentle side-lying hip flexor stretch
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: During an adolescent growth spurt (Peak Height Velocity), longitudinal bone growth of the femur occurs faster than muscle-tendon unit elongation of the bi-articular rectus femoris. This creates high resting passive tension pulling continuously on the inferior pole of the patella. However, traditional heel-to-buttock quadriceps stretches bend the knee to 140°+, which pulls violently on the inflamed inferior patellar pole! Foam rolling the mid-belly and stretching via hip extension with the knee kept at 90° reduces rectus femoris resting tone without pulling on the apophysis.

jointActions: Myofascial release / gentle mobility; growth-spurt rectus femoris tension reduction

execution.startingPosition: Foam Rolling (60-90 seconds): Lie face down with a soft foam roller positioned under the middle third of the front thigh (strictly stays on the fleshy muscle belly, staying at least 3 inches above the kneecap). Slowly roll up and down the mid-thigh while breathing deeply

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Foam Rolling (60-90 seconds): Lie face down with a soft foam roller positioned under the middle third of the front thigh (strictly stays on the fleshy muscle belly, staying at least 3 inches above the kneecap). Slowly roll up and down the mid-thigh while breathing deeply

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Gentle Side-Lying Hip Flexor / Quad Stretch (3 x 30s): Lie on your uninjured side, hold the top ankle gently keeping the knee bent at only 90° (do NOT yank the heel all the way to the buttock!), and gently pull the thigh backward into hip extension while tucking the pelvis under until a mild stretch is felt high in the front of the hip/upper thigh.

coachingCues: "Keep your knee at a comfortable 90-degree L-shape and pull your thigh bone gently backward from the hip so you feel the stretch high in your upper thigh, with zero pull at the kneecap" (external).
commonErrors: Yanking the heel to the buttock in a standing quad stretch (compresses the patella and applies maximal traction to the SLJ growth plate, worsening pain!); rolling the foam roller directly over the bony kneecap or tendon.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Foam rolling the mid-thigh and hip flexors only if any knee flexion stretch reproduces inferior pole pain.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch on a thick cushion (back knee resting on a soft pillow, knee bent only at 90° while tucking the tailbone under).

precautions: Yanking the heel to the buttock in a standing quad stretch (compresses the patella and applies maximal traction to the SLJ growth plate, worsening pain!); rolling the foam roller directly over the bony kneecap or tendon. Cues: "Keep your knee at a comfortable 90-degree L-shape and pull your thigh bone gently backward from the hip so you feel the stretch high in your upper thigh, with zero pull at the kneecap" (external).

execution.description: Teaches the adolescent athlete to recruit the hip extensors (gluteus maximus and hamstrings) alongside the quadriceps during squatting. Keeping the shins vertical reduces the external knee flexion moment arm and cuts traction stress on the inferior patellar pole by nearly half compared to an anterior knee-dominant squat, allowing safe progressive loading.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in front of a bench or box set to ~60° knee flexion with feet shoulder-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Initiate the squat by sitting your hips far back toward the box while keeping your shins as vertical as possible (knees staying stacked over the ankles rather than translating far forward over the toes)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lightly touch the box over a 3-second descent, pause 1 second, and drive through the heels to stand up.

coachingCues: "Reach your hips back to find the box first while keeping your shins tall and your weight in your heels" (external).
commonErrors: Shooting the knees forward first with heels lifting off the floor (maximizes inferior patellar pole traction); dynamic knee valgus.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Higher box height (45° knee bend); isometric hold just above the box.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually allow normal forward knee translation over the toes as the apophysis heals and becomes non-tender to palpation; add light goblet weight; progress depth to 75°–90°.

precautions: Shooting the knees forward first with heels lifting off the floor (maximizes inferior patellar pole traction); dynamic knee valgus. Cues: "Reach your hips back to find the box first while keeping your shins tall and your weight in your heels" (external).
clinicalNotes: Teaches the adolescent athlete to recruit the hip extensors (gluteus maximus and hamstrings) alongside the quadriceps during squatting. Keeping the shins vertical reduces the external knee flexion moment arm and cuts traction stress on the inferior patellar pole by nearly half compared to an anterior knee-dominant squat, allowing safe progressive loading.

description: Progresses from bilateral squats to unilateral weight-bearing knee extensor loading within a controlled range of motion, governed by the Rathleff 0–2/10 pain-monitoring framework.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral concentric/eccentric; progressive functional knee loading

execution.startingPosition: Place the entire affected foot on a 4-to-6-inch step
execution.description: Progresses from bilateral squats to unilateral weight-bearing knee extensor loading within a controlled range of motion, governed by the Rathleff 0–2/10 pain-monitoring framework.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place the entire affected foot on a 4-to-6-inch step

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lean the torso slightly forward (20° hip hinge) to engage the glutes alongside the quads, and press through the whole foot to step up to single-leg balance over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower back down slowly over 3 seconds while keeping the kneecap tracking straight over the second toe.

coachingCues: "Lean your chest slightly over your front foot, keep your knee pointed straight ahead, and step up smoothly" (external).
commonErrors: Medial knee collapse (dynamic valgus) during step-up or lowering; springing off the bottom foot.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Lower step height to 2-3 inches; bilateral mini-squats.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase step height to 6-8 inches; progress to controlled forward and lateral step-downs once the inferior pole is pain-free on palpation.

precautions: Medial knee collapse (dynamic valgus) during step-up or lowering; springing off the bottom foot. Cues: "Lean your chest slightly over your front foot, keep your knee pointed straight ahead, and step up smoothly" (external).
clinicalNotes: Progresses from bilateral squats to unilateral weight-bearing knee extensor loading within a controlled range of motion, governed by the Rathleff 0–2/10 pain-monitoring framework.

description: Before returning to full youth sports (soccer, basketball, gymnastics), the adolescent athlete must replace stiff, upright, knee-dominant landings with a multi-joint "hip-ankle-knee" absorption strategy. Pushing the hips back on landing shifts a large share of the eccentric braking work onto the powerful gluteus maximus, protecting the matured inferior patellar pole from recurrent overload.

jointActions: Neuromuscular / plyometric; landing re-education & return-to-sport ladder

execution.startingPosition: 1) Step 1 (Bilateral Snap-Down to Stick): Rise onto tiptoes with arms overhead, then rapidly drop into an athletic landing stance by pushing the hips back (hip hinge), bending the knees to ~45°–60°, and absorbing softly through the balls of the feet to heels
execution.description: Before returning to full youth sports (soccer, basketball, gymnastics), the adolescent athlete must replace stiff, upright, knee-dominant landings with a multi-joint "hip-ankle-knee" absorption strategy. Pushing the hips back on landing shifts a large share of the eccentric braking work onto the powerful gluteus maximus, protecting the matured inferior patellar pole from recurrent overload.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Step 1 (Bilateral Snap-Down to Stick): Rise onto tiptoes with arms overhead, then rapidly drop into an athletic landing stance by pushing the hips back (hip hinge), bending the knees to ~45°–60°, and absorbing softly through the balls of the feet to heels. Hold still for 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step 2 (Low Box Drop Landing): Step off a 6-to-12-inch box and land softly on two legs (progressing to single leg) using the same hip-and-ankle shock absorption strategy.

coachingCues: "Land soft like a ninja by sitting back into your hip pockets—let your hips and ankles help your knees catch the landing" (external).
commonErrors: Landing upright with the knees shooting far forward over the toes and heels popping up (dumps 100% of impact force onto the inferior patellar pole); dynamic knee valgus ("knock-knees").

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Tall-to-short athletic snap-downs on flat ground without leaving the floor.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress through the Rathleff Return-to-Sport Activity Ladder: Straight-line jogging -> Submaximal two-leg jumps -> Single-leg hop-and-stick -> Deceleration & cutting -> Full team training.

precautions: Landing upright with the knees shooting far forward over the toes and heels popping up (dumps 100% of impact force onto the inferior patellar pole); dynamic knee valgus ("knock-knees"). Cues: "Land soft like a ninja by sitting back into your hip pockets—let your hips and ankles help your knees catch the landing" (external).

name: Supine submaximal isometric heel-dig at multiple angles (90° -> 45° -> 15°)
chineseName: Supine submaximal isometric heel-dig at multiple angles (90° -> 45° -> 15°)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Early multi-angle isometric contractions stimulate satellite cell proliferation and align regenerating myofibrils across the myotendinous tear gap, preventing disorganized scar formation and reducing cortical motor inhibition before dynamic lengthening begins.

jointActions: Closed chain; multi-angle isometric; early myofiber alignment & analgesia

execution.startingPosition: Begin in Days 2–5 post-injury. Lie supine with the affected heel resting on a low plinth or floor
execution.description: Early multi-angle isometric contractions stimulate satellite cell proliferation and align regenerating myofibrils across the myotendinous tear gap, preventing disorganized scar formation and reducing cortical motor inhibition before dynamic lengthening begins.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Begin in Days 2–5 post-injury. Lie supine with the affected heel resting on a low plinth or floor

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Start at a shortened, comfortable knee angle (90° flexion), then progress to 45° flexion and finally 15° flexion (long lever)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Gently press the heel straight down into the plinth at 40%–60% pain-free effort (0–2/10 discomfort) for 30 seconds without lifting the pelvis

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rotation Bias: Point toes slightly outward (10°) to bias the lateral Biceps Femoris, or slightly inward (10°) to bias the medial Semitendinosus/Semimembranosus.

coachingCues: "Press your heel smoothly downward into the mat until you feel a healthy muscular tension in the back of your thigh with zero sharp pinch" (external).
commonErrors: Pushing through sharp localized stabbing pain (>2/10) at the tear site; holding breath (Valsalva).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform at 90° knee flexion only with 30% effort if 45° or 15° reproduces focal tear pain.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Lift the pelvis 2 inches off the mat into a single-leg isometric bridge hold at 60°, 45°, and 20° knee angles.

precautions: Pushing through sharp localized stabbing pain (>2/10) at the tear site; holding breath (Valsalva). Cues: "Press your heel smoothly downward into the mat until you feel a healthy muscular tension in the back of your thigh with zero sharp pinch" (external).
clinicalNotes: Early multi-angle isometric contractions stimulate satellite cell proliferation and align regenerating myofibrils across the myotendinous tear gap, preventing disorganized scar formation and reducing cortical motor inhibition before dynamic lengthening begins.

name: Askling L-Protocol #1: "The Extender" (dynamic long-length flexibility)

Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Exercise #1 of Carl Askling's landmark BJSM L-Protocol (which cut hamstring return-to-sport time nearly in half compared to conventional concentric/short-range rehab: 28 days vs. 51 days!). Holding the hip at 90° places the proximal hamstring under stretch while active quadriceps extension gently glides the healing myofibers through their longest pain-free excursion via reciprocal inhibition.

jointActions: Open chain; active lengthening; dynamic fascicle excursion without scar tearing

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine on the floor or plinth and grasp behind the distal thigh of the injured leg with both hands, pulling the hip up into 90° of hip flexion (or slightly beyond 90°) and holding the thigh completely fixed there
execution.description: Exercise #1 of Carl Askling's landmark BJSM L-Protocol (which cut hamstring return-to-sport time nearly in half compared to conventional concentric/short-range rehab: 28 days vs. 51 days!). Holding the hip at 90° places the proximal hamstring under stretch while active quadriceps extension gently glides the healing myofibers through their longest pain-free excursion via reciprocal inhibition.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine on the floor or plinth and grasp behind the distal thigh of the injured leg with both hands, pulling the hip up into 90° of hip flexion (or slightly beyond 90°) and holding the thigh completely fixed there

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly and smoothly extend (straighten) the knee upward toward the ceiling only up to the point just before pain is felt

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Do NOT hold a static stretch at the top—immediately lower the lower leg back down and repeat in a smooth pendulum rhythm.

coachingCues: "Hug the back of your thigh tightly to your chest and swing your shin up smoothly just until you kiss the edge of tightness—never push into pain" (external).
commonErrors: Pulling the ankle with a strap to force a painful passive stretch at the top (Askling's rule is strictly zero pain—let your own quadriceps lift the shin only to the edge of comfort!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Hold the hip at 70°–80° flexion if 90° hip flexion is initially too tight (especially in Type II proximal Semimembranosus strains).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Naturally extend the knee 2°–5° higher each day as the pain-free ceiling moves toward full knee extension.

precautions: Pulling the ankle with a strap to force a painful passive stretch at the top (Askling's rule is strictly zero pain—let your own quadriceps lift the shin only to the edge of comfort!). Cues: "Hug the back of your thigh tightly to your chest and swing your shin up smoothly just until you kiss the edge of tightness—never push into pain" (external).
clinicalNotes: Exercise #1 of Carl Askling's landmark BJSM L-Protocol (which cut hamstring return-to-sport time nearly in half compared to conventional concentric/short-range rehab: 28 days vs. 51 days!). Holding the hip at 90° places the proximal hamstring under stretch while active quadriceps extension gently glides the healing myofibers through their longest pain-free excursion via reciprocal inhibition.

chineseName: Askling L-Protocol 膕旁肌離心三部曲
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Exercise #2 of the Askling L-Protocol. Simulates a single-leg Romanian deadlift, simultaneously training eccentric lengthening of the proximal hamstring origin across the hip joint while challenging lumbopelvic-hip neuromuscular coordination (the pelvis acts as the foundation from which the hamstrings originate—if the pelvis tilts anteriorly in fatigue, hamstring strain increases by 15%–20%!).

jointActions: Closed chain; eccentric hip-extension & balance; proximal BFLH/semimembranosus

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the injured leg with a fixed, soft 10°–20° knee bend
execution.description: Exercise #2 of the Askling L-Protocol. Simulates a single-leg Romanian deadlift, simultaneously training eccentric lengthening of the proximal hamstring origin across the hip joint while challenging lumbopelvic-hip neuromuscular coordination (the pelvis acts as the foundation from which the hamstrings originate—if the pelvis tilts anteriorly in fatigue, hamstring strain increases by 15%–20%!).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the injured leg with a fixed, soft 10°–20° knee bend

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Simultaneously hinge your torso forward like a swan-diver (reaching both arms straight out in front of you at 90° shoulder flexion) while extending your uninjured leg backward (with the uninjured knee bent at ~90°)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep your pelvis completely horizontal (zero hip opening) and lower slowly until your torso is parallel to the floor (or to your pain-free limit)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Return smoothly to upright single-leg balance.

coachingCues: "Dive your arms forward and kick your back heel toward the sky while keeping your belt buckle parallel to the floor" (external).
commonErrors: Opening the pelvis toward the ceiling on the lifted-leg side; bending the standing knee into a squat instead of hinging at the hip.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Touch a wall or dowel lightly with two fingertips for balance assistance; reduce torso dive angle to 45°.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold light dumbbells in the hands reaching forward; increase return speed while maintaining strict pelvic level.

precautions: Opening the pelvis toward the ceiling on the lifted-leg side; bending the standing knee into a squat instead of hinging at the hip. Cues: "Dive your arms forward and kick your back heel toward the sky while keeping your belt buckle parallel to the floor" (external).
clinicalNotes: Exercise #2 of the Askling L-Protocol. name: Supine bilateral-to-unilateral long-lever glute-hamstring bridge
chineseName: Supine bilateral-to-unilateral long-lever glute-hamstring bridge
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Core progression of the Aspetar Hamstring Protocol. Whereas a standard 90°-knee bridge loads primarily the gluteus maximus, walking the feet out to a 30°–45° knee angle shifts the external moment arm onto the distal and mid-belly hamstrings, building high closed-chain force capacity across the knee and hip simultaneously.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; distal-to-mid hamstring force

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with your heels resting on the floor (or on a 6-to-12-inch box) positioned further away from your buttocks so your knees are bent at a long-lever 30°–45° angle (rather than 90°)
execution.description: Core progression of the Aspetar Hamstring Protocol. Whereas a standard 90°-knee bridge loads primarily the gluteus maximus, walking the feet out to a 30°–45° knee angle shifts the external moment arm onto the distal and mid-belly hamstrings, building high closed-chain force capacity across the knee and hip simultaneously.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with your heels resting on the floor (or on a 6-to-12-inch box) positioned further away from your buttocks so your knees are bent at a long-lever 30°–45° angle (rather than 90°)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Dig the heels downward and lift the hips into full extension over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower slowly over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Progress from bilateral (2 legs up, 2 legs down) -> 2 legs up / injured leg lowers over 4 seconds -> pure single-leg long-lever bridges.

coachingCues: "Tuck your tailbone slightly under first, then dig your heel through the box to lift your hips" (external).
commonErrors: Hyperextending the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral posterior pelvic tilt (anterior pelvic tilt pulls the ischial tuberosity upward and overstretches the hamstring!); cramping due to disengaged glutes.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Standard short-lever bridge (knees at 75°–90°) if the 30°–45° long lever provokes any pain.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg long-lever bridge with heels elevated on a bench/box; add a barbell or weight plate across the pelvis.

precautions: Hyperextending the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral posterior pelvic tilt (anterior pelvic tilt pulls the ischial tuberosity upward and overstretches the hamstring!); cramping due to disengaged glutes. Cues: "Tuck your tailbone slightly under first, then dig your heel through the box to lift your hips" (external).
clinicalNotes: Core progression of the Aspetar Hamstring Protocol. Whereas a standard 90°-knee bridge loads primarily the gluteus maximus, walking the feet out to a 30°–45° knee angle shifts the external moment arm onto the distal and mid-belly hamstrings, building high closed-chain force capacity across the knee and hip simultaneously.

name: Askling L-Protocol #3: "The Glider" (supramaximal long-length eccentric slide)
chineseName: Askling L-Protocol 膕旁肌離心三部曲
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Exercise #3 of the Askling L-Protocol. Because the hamstring is injured at long muscle lengths (when the hip is flexed and the knee is extended in terminal swing), The Glider provides pure eccentric-only loading at extreme long muscle lengths while eliminating concentric fatigue via upper-body return assistance. This drives rapid longitudinal sarcomerogenesis and shifts the angle of peak torque to longer muscle lengths.

jointActions: Closed chain; long-muscle-length eccentric; sarcomerogenesis at hip-flexed angles

execution.startingPosition: Stand upright next to a wall bar, TRX anchor, or stable countertop for hand support
execution.description: Exercise #3 of the Askling L-Protocol. Because the hamstring is injured at long muscle lengths (when the hip is flexed and the knee is extended in terminal swing), The Glider provides pure eccentric-only loading at extreme long muscle lengths while eliminating concentric fatigue via upper-body return assistance. This drives rapid longitudinal sarcomerogenesis and shifts the angle of peak torque to longer muscle lengths.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand upright next to a wall bar, TRX anchor, or stable countertop for hand support

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep 90% of your body weight on the injured front leg (with the front knee held in a slight 10°–20° bend) and place your uninjured back foot on a furniture slider, towel, or slick sock

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping your weight on the front injured heel, slowly let the back foot glide backward as far as you can before any pain is felt—as you slide back, your front hip flexes deeply while your front knee stays nearly straight (stretching the injured hamstring under high eccentric load at long muscle lengths!)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Once you reach your pain-free limit, pull yourself back up using both arms on the support bar—do NOT use the injured hamstring to concentrically pull yourself back up!

coachingCues: "Keep 90% of your weight on your front injured heel as you slide back into a long stretch, then use your arms on the rail to pull yourself back to the start" (external).
commonErrors: Using the injured front leg to concentrically pull the body back up to standing (causes concentric overload soreness and violates the Askling protocol—always pull up with your arms!); putting weight on the sliding back foot instead of the stationary front heel.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Mark a tape line on the floor to restrict backward slide distance to a comfortable 30%–50% range initially.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase backward glide distance by 2–5 cm each session as pain-free excursion improves; slow the eccentric glide tempo to 5 seconds.

precautions: Using the injured front leg to concentrically pull the body back up to standing (causes concentric overload soreness and violates the Askling protocol—always pull up with your arms!); putting weight on the sliding back foot instead of the stationary front heel. Cues: "Keep 90% of your weight on your front injured heel as you slide back into a long stretch, then use your arms on the rail to pull yourself back to the start" (external).
clinicalNotes: Exercise #3 of the Askling L-Protocol. Because the hamstring is injured at long muscle lengths (when the hip is flexed and the knee is extended in terminal swing), The Glider provides pure eccentric-only loading at extreme long muscle lengths while eliminating concentric fatigue via upper-body return assistance. This drives rapid longitudinal sarcomerogenesis and shifts the angle of peak torque to longer muscle lengths.

description: Functional MRI and EMG research by Bourne et al. jointActions: Closed chain; Heavy Slow Resistance; selective Biceps Femoris Long Head hypertrophy

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the injured leg with a fixed 15° knee bend and hold a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in the opposite hand (or use a 45° Roman Chair Hip Extension bench on one leg)
execution.description: Functional MRI and EMG research by Bourne et al. (BJSM) proved that hip-extension exercises (45° Hip Extensions and Romanian Deadlifts) produce significantly greater hypertrophy of the Biceps Femoris Long Head (BFLH) and Semimembranosus than Nordic curls alone, because the BFLH has a longer moment arm at the hip than at the knee!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the injured leg with a fixed 15° knee bend and hold a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in the opposite hand (or use a 45° Roman Chair Hip Extension bench on one leg)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge slowly at the hips over a 3-to-4-second eccentric count until a deep, pain-free stretch is felt in the mid-to-upper hamstring, keeping the lumbar spine neutral and pelvis square

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 1 second at the bottom stretch, then drive the hips forward over 2 seconds to stand tall.

coachingCues: "Push your hips straight back toward the wall behind you—stop the second your hips stop moving back, and drive through your heel" (external).
commonErrors: Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the RDL to touch the weight to the floor instead of stopping when pelvic hip flexion runs out.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Kickstand (B-stance) RDL with the back toe lightly touching the floor; bilateral barbell RDL.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase dumbbell/barbell load progressively; perform single-leg 45° Roman chair hip extensions holding a weight plate at the chest.

precautions: Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the RDL to touch the weight to the floor instead of stopping when pelvic hip flexion runs out. Cues: "Push your hips straight back toward the wall behind you—stop the second your hips stop moving back, and drive through your heel" (external).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Clearance Gate: Introduce full Nordics only after supine eccentric sliders and long-lever single-leg bridges are 100% pain-free

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Kneel tall on a padded mat with ankles anchored securely

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping hips locked in 0° neutral extension (squeeze glutes, slight posterior pelvic tilt), lean forward slowly over a 4-to-5-second eccentric count, resisting gravity with the hamstrings as close to the floor as possible

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Catch yourself in a push-up position and push lightly with the hands to return to the top.

coachingCues: "Keep a straight plank from your shoulders through your hips to your knees—push equally through both shins and fight gravity all the way down" (external).

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Breaking at the hips (sticking the buttocks back) as the angle gets steep; shifting weight onto the uninjured leg during the descent. Cues: "Keep a straight plank from your shoulders through your hips to your knees—push equally through both shins and fight gravity all the way down" (external).
clinicalNotes: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses (Al Attar et al.; Van Dyk et al., BJSM) confirm that adding the Nordic Hamstring Curl to rehabilitation and prevention programs reduces primary and recurrent hamstring injuries by 51%! steps.instruction: Step 2 (Graded High-Speed Sprint Exposure): No gym exercise reaches the angular velocity (>1,000°/sec) of maximal sprinting ("sprinting is the only vaccine for sprinting"). Progress across 2-3 weeks from 60% -> 75% -> 85% -> 95% -> 100% max velocity over 30–40m build-ups

steps.title: 步驟 3

steps.instruction: Position B (0° Straight-Leg Long-Lever Squeeze — Adductor Longus & Gracilis Peak Load): Lie supine with both legs completely straight (0° extension) and place the ball between your medial malleoli (ankles). Squeeze the ankles inward for 30 seconds

description: Core exercise of Hölmich Module 2 and the Aspetar Groin Protocol. Addresses both Adductor-Related and Iliopsoas-Related groin entities while training the stance limb to prevent contralateral pelvic drop.

primaryMuscles: Moving limb: adductor longus/magnus & iliopsoas. Stance limb: gluteus medius & adductors
jointActions: Open/closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; Hölmich Module 2 pelvitrochanteric load

execution.startingPosition: Exercise A (Standing Band Adduction — Hölmich Module 2): Loop a heavy resistance band around the ankle anchored laterally. Stand tall on the uninjured leg first and pull the injured leg inward across the front of the standing leg (2s concentric, 2s hold, 4s slow eccentric return to 20° abduction—do NOT let the band yank the leg into wide end-range abduction stretch!). Then switch legs so you stand on the injured leg while pulling with the uninjured leg (standing on the injured leg trains closed-chain pelvic stabilization!)

steps.title: 步驟 2

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your side on a mat with your forearm supporting your upper body and place the knee and entire lower leg of your top (injured) leg resting on a low 12-to-16-inch bench or partner's hands (placing the support at the knee cuts the external lever arm in half compared to the ankle!)

steps.title: 步驟 1

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press the top knee downward into the bench to lift your pelvis and bottom hip up into a straight side-plank line over 2 seconds while bringing the bottom leg up to touch the bench

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top, then lower the pelvis and bottom leg slowly over 3 seconds.

description: Ice hockey skating, soccer side-tackling, and tennis wide-ball lunges require the adductors to contract eccentrically at long muscle lengths to decelerate rapid hip abduction, and then concentrically to pull the leg back under the body. Lateral sliders train this exact closed-chain lengthening-shortening cycle.

jointActions: Closed chain; slow eccentric HSR; functional outer-range adductor deceleration

execution.startingPosition: Stand with the uninjured leg on a non-slip floor and the injured foot resting on a furniture slider or towel (or reverse: stand on the injured leg and slide the uninjured leg out—both variations load the adductors in closed chain!)

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with the uninjured leg on a non-slip floor and the injured foot resting on a furniture slider or towel (or reverse: stand on the injured leg and slide the uninjured leg out—both variations load the adductors in closed chain!)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly slide the moving leg laterally outward over a strict 4-second eccentric count while sitting the hips back into a lateral lunge on the stationary leg—stop at a comfortable, pain-free outer-range adductor stretch (<= 2/10)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 1 second, then squeeze the inner thighs (adductors) to pull the sliding foot back to the starting position over 2–3 seconds!

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Use a TRX suspension strap or dowel in front of you to offload 30% of body weight and control slide distance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a goblet dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest; transition to dynamic stepping lateral lunges without the slider.

precautions: Sliding out so wide on Day 1 that the athlete cannot pull their leg back in without sharp groin pain (mark a safe tape distance on the floor and expand by 2 cm each week!). progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Letting the pelvis drop or twist during the single-leg hinge. Cues: "Keep your belt line level and drive your hips forward using both your glutes and your deep inner thigh" (external).
clinicalNotes: Prospective studies by Tyler et al. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70°, feet flat on the mat, and a soft ball or yoga block placed between the knees.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Inhale quietly through the nose into the lower ribcage; as you exhale slowly through pursed lips, gently draw the lower abdomen inward (2 cm medial to the ASIS) to tension the conjoint tendon WITHOUT bulging the abdominal wall or holding your breath.

description: Athletes with athletic pubalgia frequently exhibit anterior pelvic tilt and gluteal inhibition, which places chronic tensile stretch on the distal rectus abdominis and inguinal wall. jointActions: Closed-Chain Concentric–Eccentric + Isometric Pelvic Unloading

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with a foam yoga block squeezed between the knees and feet flat hip-width apart.
execution.description: Athletes with athletic pubalgia frequently exhibit anterior pelvic tilt and gluteal inhibition, which places chronic tensile stretch on the distal rectus abdominis and inguinal wall. Strengthening the gluteus maximus in posterior pelvic tilt dynamically unloads the anterior pubic plate (PMC11944235).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with a foam yoga block squeezed between the knees and feet flat hip-width apart.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Initiate the movement by tucking the tailbone under (posterior pelvic tilt) via gluteus maximus contraction—taking anterior-inferior traction off the pubic symphysis and inguinal ligament.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Drive through the heels to lift into a neutral 0° hip extension bridge while squeezing the block at 40% effort, hold 3 seconds at the top, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Roll your tailbone slightly toward the ceiling first, then lift your hips only until your torso and thighs form a flat line." Internal cue: "Use your glutes to hold your pelvis tucked so the front of your groin feels supported, never stretched."
commonErrors: Never hyperextend past 0° neutral hip extension at the top of the bridge, as hyperextension stretches the injured rectus abdominis–inguinal insertion.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral bridge to 50% height with reduced block squeeze force.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand tall with the affected foot on a furniture slider or towel on a smooth floor.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Bracing the lower abdomen, slowly slide the affected leg laterally over 4 seconds while sitting the stance hip backward into a single-leg squat (keeping the sliding leg straight and toes pointing straight ahead).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Stop at a controlled, pain-free abduction angle, pause 1 second, and pull the sliding foot actively back to center over 2 seconds by contracting the inner thigh and lower abs simultaneously.

commonErrors: Do not let the sliding foot externally rotate uncontrollably or slide out past the point of active muscular control.

regressions.name: 退階方案

steps.title: 步驟 1

steps.instruction: Part 1 (Ballistic Rotational RFD): Stand perpendicular to a concrete wall in an athletic stance holding a 3–5 kg medicine ball at the back hip; load into the trail hip and explosively rotate the pelvis and trunk to scoop-toss the ball into the wall, catching it on the rebound with a braced core.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Part 2 (45° Plant-and-Cut): Sprint forward 5–10 m at 75% → 100% speed, decelerate with lowered center of mass, plant the outside (affected) foot at a 45° angle, and push off explosively across the midline without trunk sway or groin pain.

coachingCues: "Drop your hips low during the final two braking steps, keep your chest over your plant knee, and punch the ground away." Internal cue: "Snap your hips and core together as one tight coil when releasing the ball or pushing out of the cut."
commonErrors: Avoid planting the cutting foot excessively wide away from the center of mass with an upright, laterally tilted trunk (which spikes adductor-inguinal shear moment).

regressions.name: 退階方案

precautions: Avoid planting the cutting foot excessively wide away from the center of mass with an upright, laterally tilted trunk (which spikes adductor-inguinal shear moment). jointActions: Zero-Pain Submaximal Isometric (Apophyseal & Bone-Protected Activation)

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70° (short lever to minimize tractional torque on the pelvic apophyses and bending torque on the femoral neck).
execution.description: Maintains corticospinal motor drive and prevents rapid disuse atrophy of the thigh and hip musculature without exceeding the mechanical failure threshold of healing trabecular bone or an inflamed adolescent growth plate.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70° (short lever to minimize tractional torque on the pelvic apophyses and bending torque on the femoral neck).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: For AIIS/ASIS: Place your palm against the distal anterior thigh at 60° hip flexion and gently press into the hand at 30–40% effort for 30 seconds with 0/10 pain.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: For Ischial Apophysitis: Press heels gently into the mat at 45° knee flexion (30–40% effort).

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: For Femoral Neck / Pediatric Hip: Press knees gently outward into a light band at 30–40% effort.

coachingCues: "Press gently into your hand like you are testing a soft sponge—keep your effort smooth and completely pain-free." Internal cue: "Wake up the muscle belly in the middle of the thigh without pulling on the bone attachment."
commonErrors: Absolute Rule: Zero pain is permitted during femoral neck BSI or acute apophyseal loading. Never perform straight-leg raises (long lever) in early femoral neck BSI or acute AIIS/ASIS avulsion, as long-lever hip flexion creates high shear across both sites.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce effort to 20% MVC or adjust joint angle further into mid-range away from any tractional stretch on the apophysis.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually lengthen the lever arm (extending the knee from 70° to 30°) and increase isometric intensity from 40% to 70% MVC over 2–3 weeks as long as palpation and contraction remain 0/10 pain.

precautions: Absolute Rule: Zero pain is permitted during femoral neck BSI or acute apophyseal loading. Never perform straight-leg raises (long lever) in early femoral neck BSI or acute AIIS/ASIS avulsion, as long-lever hip flexion creates high shear across both sites. External cue: "Press gently into your hand like you are testing a soft sponge—keep your effort smooth and completely pain-free." Internal cue: "Wake up the muscle belly in the middle of the thigh without pulling on the bone attachment."
clinicalNotes: Maintains corticospinal motor drive and prevents rapid disuse atrophy of the thigh and hip musculature without exceeding the mechanical failure threshold of healing trabecular bone or an inflamed adolescent growth plate.

jointActions: Closed-Chain Single-Leg Concentric–Eccentric Control

execution.startingPosition: Place the affected foot flat on a 15–20 cm step.
execution.description: Transitions from bilateral to unilateral weight-bearing axial loading, training the hip abductors and extensors to prevent pelvic drop and femoral adduction when the entire body weight is supported on one femoral neck.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place the affected foot flat on a 15–20 cm step.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lean the torso slightly forward (15–20° hip hinge) to engage the gluteus maximus alongside the quadriceps, press through the mid-foot/heel to step up to full single-leg extension without pushing off the trailing floor foot, hold single-leg balance with a level pelvis for 2 seconds, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Dorsiflex your bottom ankle (pull toes up) so your top hip and thigh do 100% of the lifting." Internal cue: "Keep your belt buckle level and drive the step straight down beneath your heel."

clinicalNotes: Transitions from bilateral to unilateral weight-bearing axial loading, training the hip abductors and extensors to prevent pelvic drop and femoral adduction when the entire body weight is supported on one femoral neck.

description: Bone remodeling requires brief, dynamic impact separated by rest intervals and a 48-hour monitoring window to ensure osteoblastic repair outpaces microdamage accumulation.

primaryMuscles: Proximal femur trabecular & cortical bone network
jointActions: Osteogenic Impact Resensitization & Graduated Return-to-Running Protocol

execution.startingPosition: Part 1 (Osteogenic Plyometric Primer): Perform 3–4 short bouts of 10 bilateral low-amplitude pogo hops or box drop-landings (15 cm box), taking a mandatory 60–90 second complete rest between bouts (osteocytes desensitize after ~15–20 consecutive loading cycles; long rests restore mechanosensitivity).
execution.description: Bone remodeling requires brief, dynamic impact separated by rest intervals and a 48-hour monitoring window to ensure osteoblastic repair outpaces microdamage accumulation.

steps.title: 步驟 1

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Part 2 (Alternate-Day Walk-Run): Execute on non-consecutive days (Mon/Wed/Fri, 48 h bone recovery window): Level 1 = 5 × (1 min easy jog / 4 min brisk walk); Level 2 = 5 × (2 min jog / 3 min walk); Level 3 = 5 × (3 min jog / 2 min walk); Level 4 = 5 × (4 min jog / 1 min walk); Level 5 = 20 min continuous run at +5–10% cadence.

coachingCues: "Take quick, quiet, compact steps directly underneath your hips—if you feel even a whisper of deep groin ache, switch to walking immediately." Internal cue: "Land softly through bent knees and active calves."
commonErrors: Non-negotiable: Never run on consecutive days during femoral neck BSI return-to-run, and never run with an energy deficit (RED-S).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: If any 1/10 localized ache occurs at the femoral neck or apophysis during or within 24 hours after a session, stop impact for 48–72 hours and step back 1–2 levels.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress by maximum 1 level every 2–3 successful sessions (0/10 pain); introduce multi-directional cutting and sprint accelerations for AIIS/ASIS/ischial athletes once 20 min continuous running is pain-free.

precautions: Non-negotiable: Never run on consecutive days during femoral neck BSI return-to-run, and never run with an energy deficit (RED-S). External cue: "Take quick, quiet, compact steps directly underneath your hips—if you feel even a whisper of deep groin ache, switch to walking immediately." Pause 2 seconds and rock back forward for 15 reps

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Quadruped Rock-Back for Posterior Capsule Glide): Get on hands and knees (all fours) with your knees placed slightly wider than hip-width apart (15°–20° abduction) and toes resting comfortably. Maintaining a completely flat, neutral lumbar spine (no rounding or overarching), slowly rock your hips backward toward your heels only up to the exact angle just before any anterior groin tightness or pinch is felt! Pause 2 seconds and rock back forward for 15 reps

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (High-Seat Unresisted Stationary Bike): Set the bike saddle high so the hip never flexes past 75°–80° at the top of the pedal stroke, and pedal smoothly for 10–15 minutes.

coachingCues: "Keep your knees slightly wide, keep your spine flat like a tabletop, and rock back only inside your 100% pinch-free comfort zone" (external).
commonErrors: Rocking all the way back onto the heels through a sharp front-of-hip groin pinch (crushes the torn labrum!); rounding the lower back into lumbar flexion at the bottom.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine heel slides within a safe 0°–70° hip flexion arc (especially Weeks 1–3 post-hip arthroscopy or post-THA).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a heavy resistance band looped high in the groin crease pulling laterally and inferiorly during the quadruped rock-back to provide a Mulligan lateral-inferior joint distraction glide!

precautions: Rocking all the way back onto the heels through a sharp front-of-hip groin pinch (crushes the torn labrum!); rounding the lower back into lumbar flexion at the bottom.Cues: "Keep your knees slightly wide, keep your spine flat like a tabletop, and rock back only inside your 100% pinch-free comfort zone" (external).
clinicalNotes: In FAI, Labral Tears, and Hip OA, tightness of the posterior-inferior hip capsule pushes the femoral head anteriorly into the pinched anterior labrum during hip flexion. Rocking back in quadruped with the knees slightly wide uses axial femur alignment to gently glide the femoral head posteriorly into the deeper part of the socket while nourishing the articular cartilage with zero anterior impingement!

name: Posterior-pelvic-tilt glute bridge with band (Acetabular Uncovering & Centring)
chineseName: 臀橋式骨盆抬高訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Why does the Gluteus Maximus protect the anterior labrum? When the hamstrings extend the hip without the gluteus maximus, the distal femur is pulled backward while the proximal femoral head levers forward (anteriorly) into the anterior labrum and capsule (Sahrmann's Anterior Femoral Glide)! In contrast, the Gluteus Maximus attaches directly to the proximal femur and pulls the femoral head posteriorly into the center of the socket while Posterior Pelvic Tilt rotates the anterior acetabular rim upward out of the way of the cam lesion!

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; preventing anterior femoral glide

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent at 90°, feet flat shoulder-width apart, and a resistance band looped above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent at 90°, feet flat shoulder-width apart, and a resistance band looped above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step 1 (Posterior Pelvic Tilt — "Uncovering the Rim"): Exhale, draw the lower ribs down, and gently tuck your tailbone under to flatten your lower back before lifting

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step 2 (Glute-First Drive): Place your fingers on your glutes to ensure the gluteus maximus fires BEFORE the hamstrings, then drive through the heels while pressing the knees gently outward against the band to lift the hips over 2 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold 3 seconds at the top (without overarching the lower back) and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Tuck your belt buckle slightly toward your chin, squeeze your glutes first, and lift to a flat ramp without arching your lower back" (external).
commonErrors: Hyperextending the lumbar spine and tilting the pelvis anteriorly at the top of the bridge; pushing the hips past 0° into hip hyperextension (which stresses the anterior capsule and labral repair!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine isometric gluteal squeezes with posterior pelvic tilt at 0° lift.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Offset (staggered) glute bridge -> single-leg glute bridge -> barbell hip thrust (stopping at 0° neutral extension with a tucked pelvis).

precautions: Hyperextending the lumbar spine and tilting the pelvis anteriorly at the top of the bridge; pushing the hips past 0° into hip hyperextension (which stresses the anterior capsule and labral repair!).Cues: "Tuck your belt buckle slightly toward your chin, squeeze your glutes first, and lift to a flat ramp without arching your lower back" (external).

name: Prone / side-lying deep hip external rotator & abductor series ("Hip Cuff")
chineseName: Prone / side-lying deep hip external rotator & abductor series ("Hip Cuff")
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: The deep external rotators (obturator internus, superior/inferior gemelli, quadratus femoris) run horizontally across the posterior neck of the femur just like the infraspinatus and teres minor at the shoulder! Strengthening this "Hip Rotator Cuff" in neutral/extended hip angles compresses and centers the femoral head deep inside the acetabulum, preventing anterior labral shear and preventing dynamic femoral internal rotation during weight-bearing.

jointActions: Open chain; isometric to isotonic; dynamic femoral head stabilization

execution.startingPosition: Exercise A (Prone Isometric/Isotonic Internal-Rotation-of-Shins = Hip External Rotation at 0° Hip Angle): Lie face down (prone) with knees bent at 90° and a resistance band looped around the ankles. Keeping the knees hip-width apart on the mat, pull the ankles gently inward toward each other against a band or ball (which externally rotates the hips at 0° hip flexion—completely outside the FADIR impingement zone!) for 5 x 30s holds or 3 x 12 slow reps
execution.description: The deep external rotators (obturator internus, superior/inferior gemelli, quadratus femoris) run horizontally across the posterior neck of the femur just like the infraspinatus and teres minor at the shoulder! Strengthening this "Hip Rotator Cuff" in neutral/extended hip angles compresses and centers the femoral head deep inside the acetabulum, preventing anterior labral shear and preventing dynamic femoral internal rotation during weight-bearing.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Prone Isometric/Isotonic Internal-Rotation-of-Shins = Hip External Rotation at 0° Hip Angle): Lie face down (prone) with knees bent at 90° and a resistance band looped around the ankles. Keeping the knees hip-width apart on the mat, pull the ankles gently inward toward each other against a band or ball (which externally rotates the hips at 0° hip flexion—completely outside the FADIR impingement zone!) for 5 x 30s holds or 3 x 12 slow reps

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (Side-Lying Clamshell & Wall-Slide Hip Abduction): Perform 3 sets of 12–15 banded clamshells (at a shallow 30°–45° hip angle, not 90°!) and straight-leg hip abductions.

coachingCues: "Keep your hips open at a shallow angle and rotate smoothly from deep inside your back hip pocket" (external).
commonErrors: Flexing the hips up to 90° during clamshells in an FAI patient (90° flexion brings the cam bump right to the acetabular rim—keep the hip angle shallow at 30°–45° during clamshells!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Prone isometric gluteal and external rotator squeezes at 30%–50% effort.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Seated 60°-hip-angle banded external rotation -> standing single-leg "Airplane / Pelvic Rotation" drills (stopping before internal rotation pinch).

precautions: Flexing the hips up to 90° during clamshells in an FAI patient (90° flexion brings the cam bump right to the acetabular rim—keep the hip angle shallow at 30°–45° during clamshells!).Cues: "Keep your hips open at a shallow angle and rotate smoothly from deep inside your back hip pocket" (external).
clinicalNotes: The deep external rotators (obturator internus, superior/inferior gemelli, quadratus femoris) run horizontally across the posterior neck of the femur just like the infraspinatus and teres minor at the shoulder! Strengthening this "Hip Rotator Cuff" in neutral/extended hip angles compresses and centers the femoral head deep inside the acetabulum, preventing anterior labral shear and preventing dynamic femoral internal rotation during weight-bearing.

name: Supine / standing banded Iliopsoas march with Posterior Pelvic Tilt lock
chineseName: Supine / standing banded Iliopsoas march with Posterior Pelvic Tilt lock
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Anatomical and biomechanical studies (Casartelli et al.; King et al.) prove that patients with FAI and Labral Tears have significant weakness of the Iliopsoas—and because the iliacus and psoas major pass directly across the anterior femoral head, a strong, well-controlled iliopsoas acts as an active dynamic buttress that prevents anterior femoral head subluxation! Furthermore, locking the pelvis in posterior tilt prevents the psoas from pulling the lumbar spine into lordosis and anterior pelvic tilt.

jointActions: Open/closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; anterior femoral head stabilizer

execution.startingPosition: 1) Precaution Note: In Post-Op Hip Arthroscopy, wait until Week 4–6 clearance before resisted open-chain hip flexor loading to avoid post-op iliopsoas tendinitis; in Non-Op FAI / Labral Tear / Hip OA, start early!2) Lie supine (or stand against a wall) with a mini-band looped around both feet

Furthermore, locking the pelvis in posterior tilt prevents the psoas from pulling the lumbar spine into lordosis and anterior pelvic tilt.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Precaution Note: In Post-Op Hip Arthroscopy, wait until Week 4–6 clearance before resisted open-chain hip flexor loading to avoid post-op iliopsoas tendinitis; in Non-Op FAI / Labral Tear / Hip OA, start early

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lie supine (or stand against a wall) with a mini-band looped around both feet

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press the lower back flat into the mat/wall (posterior pelvic tilt) and squeeze the standing glute

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: March the affected knee upward only to 70°–80° hip flexion (stopping 10° below the 90° anterior impingement pinch!) over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower slowly over 3 seconds without letting the lower back arch off the mat!

coachingCues: "Glue your lower back to the mat, march your knee up to just below a right angle with zero front pinch, and control the 3-second lowering phase" (external).
commonErrors: Pulling the knee past 90° into the chest until the front of the hip pinches; letting the pelvis tilt anteriorly and the lower back arch as the leg lowers.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine heel-slide marches with the foot sliding on the mat (short lever arm).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer mini-band; standing single-leg cable/band hip flexion marches while holding a kettlebell overhead or in rack position.

precautions: Pulling the knee past 90° into the chest until the front of the hip pinches; letting the pelvis tilt anteriorly and the lower back arch as the leg lowers.Cues: "Glue your lower back to the mat, march your knee up to just below a right angle with zero front pinch, and control the 3-second lowering phase" (external).
clinicalNotes: Anatomical and biomechanical studies (Casartelli et al.; King et al.) prove that patients with FAI and Labral Tears have significant weakness of the Iliopsoas—and because the iliacus and psoas major pass directly across the anterior femoral head, a strong, well-controlled iliopsoas acts as an active dynamic buttress that prevents anterior femoral head subluxation! Furthermore, locking the pelvis in posterior tilt prevents the psoas from pulling the lumbar spine into lordosis and anterior pelvic tilt.

chineseName: 彈力帶怪獸步橫向行走 (臀中肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Because the FADIR impingement position consists of Flexion + Adduction + Internal Rotation, strengthening the gluteus medius and maximus in a closed-chain athletic stance trains the athlete to dynamically maintain slight Abduction + External Rotation, keeping the femoral cam lesion away from the anterosuperior labrum during cutting and squatting!

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; keeping femur out of FADIR vector

execution.startingPosition: 1) Loop a resistance band around the ankles or above the knees
execution.description: Because the FADIR impingement position consists of Flexion + Adduction + Internal Rotation, strengthening the gluteus medius and maximus in a closed-chain athletic stance trains the athlete to dynamically maintain slight Abduction + External Rotation, keeping the femoral cam lesion away from the anterosuperior labrum during cutting and squatting!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a resistance band around the ankles or above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand in a shallow 25°–35° athletic squat with your pelvis tucked into neutral (eliminating anterior pelvic tilt / "butt wink" arch!) and feet hip-to-shoulder width apart

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step sideways 6–8 inches while keeping both knees pushed wide over the middle/outer toes, then control the trail foot in slowly—stopping at hip-width apart (12–15 steps each direction).

coachingCues: "Keep your ribs stacked over your belt buckle with a neutral tailbone, and push your knees wide from your back pockets" (external).
commonErrors: Sticking the buttocks out in deep anterior pelvic tilt ("Donald Duck posture") while doing band walks—anterior pelvic tilt rotates the acetabular rim down onto the femoral neck!

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Place the band above the knees and reduce athletic stance depth to 15°.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Diagonal forward/backward Monster walks; add upper-body medicine ball perturbations.

precautions: Sticking the buttocks out in deep anterior pelvic tilt ("Donald Duck posture") while doing band walks—anterior pelvic tilt rotates the acetabular rim down onto the femoral neck!Cues: "Keep your ribs stacked over your belt buckle with a neutral tailbone, and push your knees wide from your back pockets" (external).
clinicalNotes: Because the FADIR impingement position consists of Flexion + Adduction + Internal Rotation, strengthening the gluteus medius and maximus in a closed-chain athletic stance trains the athlete to dynamically maintain slight Abduction + External Rotation, keeping the femoral cam lesion away from the anterosuperior labrum during cutting and squatting!

name: Wide-stance / Sumo-biased box squat (stopping above the 80°–90° pinch ceiling)
chineseName: Wide-stance / Sumo-biased box squat (stopping above the 80°–90° pinch ceiling)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: A narrow, toes-straight-ahead deep squat places the hip straight into Flexion + Internal Rotation/Adduction, causing the cam bump on the anterosuperior femoral neck to collide with the acetabular rim at ~85° flexion. By widening the stance and externally rotating the hips 15°–30° while using a box to cap depth above the pinch ceiling, the anterosuperior cam bump rotates inferiorly and laterally away from the rim, allowing heavy, 100% pain-free lower-limb hypertrophy!

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic HSR; functional quad & glute loading with cam clearance

execution.startingPosition: 1) Set a plyo box or bench behind you at a height that stops your hip flexion 10°–15° above your personal anterior pinch angle (typically a 16-to-18-inch box, ~70°–80° hip flexion)
execution.description: A narrow, toes-straight-ahead deep squat places the hip straight into Flexion + Internal Rotation/Adduction, causing the cam bump on the anterosuperior femoral neck to collide with the acetabular rim at ~85° flexion. By widening the stance and externally rotating the hips 15°–30° while using a box to cap depth above the pinch ceiling, the anterosuperior cam bump rotates inferiorly and laterally away from the rim, allowing heavy, 100% pain-free lower-limb hypertrophy!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Set a plyo box or bench behind you at a height that stops your hip flexion 10°–15° above your personal anterior pinch angle (typically a 16-to-18-inch box, ~70°–80° hip flexion)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and turn your toes outward 15°–30° while tracking your knees outward directly in line with your toes

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Maintain a neutral spine (no anterior pelvic tilt arch and no bottom "butt wink") and lower over 3 seconds to lightly tap the box

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Drive through your heels and glutes over 2 seconds to stand tall.

coachingCues: "Widen your stance, turn your toes out 20 degrees, push your knees out over your toes, and tap the box cleanly with zero front groin pinch" (external).
commonErrors: Squatting deep past 90° ("ass-to-grass") with a narrow stance in an athlete with bony Cam/Pincer FAI (bony morphology does not "stretch out"—forcing past the bony block tears the labrum and delaminates cartilage!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Higher box (18–20 inches); TRX-assisted wide-stance squats.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a heavy goblet dumbbell/kettlebell at the chest (front-loaded goblet weights naturally encourage an upright torso and posterior pelvic tilt, reducing hip flexion angle by 10°!); gradually test slightly lower box heights only if 100% pinch-free.

precautions: Squatting deep past 90° ("ass-to-grass") with a narrow stance in an athlete with bony Cam/Pincer FAI (bony morphology does not "stretch out"—forcing past the bony block tears the labrum and delaminates cartilage!).Cues: "Widen your stance, turn your toes out 20 degrees, push your knees out over your toes, and tap the box cleanly with zero front groin pinch" (external).
clinicalNotes: A narrow, toes-straight-ahead deep squat places the hip straight into Flexion + Internal Rotation/Adduction, causing the cam bump on the anterosuperior femoral neck to collide with the acetabular rim at ~85° flexion. By widening the stance and externally rotating the hips 15°–30° while using a box to cap depth above the pinch ceiling, the anterosuperior cam bump rotates inferiorly and laterally away from the rim, allowing heavy, 100% pain-free lower-limb hypertrophy!

name: Supported single-leg Romanian deadlift & GLA:D® step-up (pelvic-level HSR)
chineseName: 單腳 上階梯登階肌力訓練 (HSR高負荷)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Builds unilateral gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, and hamstring strength while respecting the hip-flexion impingement ceiling. In Hip Osteoarthritis and Post-THA (Koc et al., 2025 JOSPT Hip OA CPG), progressive unilateral step-ups and hip hinges restore symmetric gait propulsion and stair-climbing capacity.

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral HSR; posterior-chain power & KAM/joint offloading

execution.startingPosition: Exercise A (Capped-Range Single-Leg RDL): Stand on the affected leg with a 15°–20° knee bend and slight 5°–10° toe-out. Hinge backward at the hips over 3 seconds stopping at 60°–70° hip flexion (before any anterior groin pinch), keeping the pelvis horizontal; drive the hips forward with the glutes to stand tall
execution.description: Builds unilateral gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, and hamstring strength while respecting the hip-flexion impingement ceiling. In Hip Osteoarthritis and Post-THA (Koc et al., 2025 JOSPT Hip OA CPG), progressive unilateral step-ups and hip hinges restore symmetric gait propulsion and stair-climbing capacity.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Capped-Range Single-Leg RDL): Stand on the affected leg with a 15°–20° knee bend and slight 5°–10° toe-out. Hinge backward at the hips over 3 seconds stopping at 60°–70° hip flexion (before any anterior groin pinch), keeping the pelvis horizontal; drive the hips forward with the glutes to stand tall

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (GLA:D® Forward & Lateral Step-Up on 4-to-6-inch Box): Step up on the affected leg (choosing a moderate 4-to-6-inch box rather than a high 12-inch box so hip flexion stays <65°!) while keeping the kneecap over the second/third toe and the belt line level.

coachingCues: "Use a moderate step height, keep your pelvis slightly open rather than twisted inward, and drive through your heel and glute" (external).
commonErrors: Using a very high 12-to-16-inch plyo box for step-ups (forces the hip into >95° flexion + adduction at the start of the step-up, pinching the anterior labrum!); letting the pelvis rotate inward toward the standing leg during the RDL (creates relative internal rotation = FADIR!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Kickstand (B-stance) RDL; 3-to-4-inch low step-ups with handrail balance support.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase dumbbell/kettlebell load; progress to Rear-Foot Elevated Split Squats with an upright torso and front knee tracking slightly outward.

precautions: Using a very high 12-to-16-inch plyo box for step-ups (forces the hip into >95° flexion + adduction at the start of the step-up, pinching the anterior labrum!); letting the pelvis rotate inward toward the standing leg during the RDL (creates relative internal rotation = FADIR!).Cues: "Use a moderate step height, keep your pelvis slightly open rather than twisted inward, and drive through your heel and glute" (external).
clinicalNotes: Builds unilateral gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, and hamstring strength while respecting the hip-flexion impingement ceiling. In Hip Osteoarthritis and Post-THA (Koc et al., 2025 JOSPT Hip OA CPG), progressive unilateral step-ups and hip hinges restore symmetric gait propulsion and stair-climbing capacity.

name: Multi-directional lunging sliders & open-hip deceleration cuts (Late RTS)
chineseName: 衝刺減速著地緩衝控制
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
Phase 4: 增強式與重返運動
description: Validated in the UK FASHIoN Personalised Hip Therapy (PHT) trial (Griffin et al., Lancet) and Aspetar Return-to-Sport Hip protocols: teaching athletes to absorb multi-planar cutting and deceleration forces in an "open-hip" (abducted + externally rotated + neutral pelvis) posture allows return to high-level pivot sports without chondrolabral impingement.

jointActions: Neuromuscular / functional; closed chain; sport-specific agility without FADIR

execution.startingPosition: Exercise A (GLA:D® / FAI Backward & 45°-Open Lateral Sliders): Stand on the affected leg with the opposite foot on a slider. Slide backward into a reverse lunge (keeping the front hip flexion <75° and front knee tracked over the 3rd toe), then slide laterally at a 45° angle while keeping the stance hip slightly externally rotated
execution.description: Validated in the UK FASHIoN Personalised Hip Therapy (PHT) trial (Griffin et al., Lancet) and Aspetar Return-to-Sport Hip protocols: teaching athletes to absorb multi-planar cutting and deceleration forces in an "open-hip" (abducted + externally rotated + neutral pelvis) posture allows return to high-level pivot sports without chondrolabral impingement.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (GLA:D® / FAI Backward & 45°-Open Lateral Sliders): Stand on the affected leg with the opposite foot on a slider. Slide backward into a reverse lunge (keeping the front hip flexion <75° and front knee tracked over the 3rd toe), then slide laterally at a 45° angle while keeping the stance hip slightly externally rotated

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B ("Open-Hip" Deceleration & Cutting Mechanics): When decelerating to cut in field/court sports (or skating in ice hockey), train a wider plant with 15° external foot/hip rotation and a neutral pelvis—eliminating the narrow, internally rotated valgus collapse that rams the femoral neck into the labrum at high velocity!

coachingCues: "Plant outside your shoulder line with your knee pushed wide over your middle toes and your chest proud—never cut across a caved-in knee" (external).
commonErrors: Planting across the midline ("crossover cut") with the knee caving inward and trunk pitching forward (places the hip into violent high-speed FADIR impingement!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Controlled static reverse lunges and lateral weight-shifts in front of a mirror.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add medicine ball catches at peak lunge/cut; progress to reactive figure-of-8 runs, skating strides, and full sport participation (passing the Copenhagen Hip and Groin Outcome Score [HAGOS] and \ge 90% single-leg hop LSI).

precautions: Planting across the midline ("crossover cut") with the knee caving inward and trunk pitching forward (places the hip into violent high-speed FADIR impingement!).Cues: "Plant outside your shoulder line with your knee pushed wide over your middle toes and your chest proud—never cut across a caved-in knee" (external).
clinicalNotes: Validated in the UK FASHIoN Personalised Hip Therapy (PHT) trial (Griffin et al., Lancet) and Aspetar Return-to-Sport Hip protocols: teaching athletes to absorb multi-planar cutting and deceleration forces in an "open-hip" (abducted + externally rotated + neutral pelvis) posture allows return to high-level pivot sports without chondrolabral impingement.

name: Supine slight-abduction isometric belt press (LEAP Stage 1 — Zero Compression)
chineseName: Supine slight-abduction isometric belt press (LEAP Stage 1 — Zero Compression)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Foundational exercise of the 2018 BMJ LEAP Trial. Why is this superior to Clamshells in acute GTPS? In side-lying Clamshells, the patient lies on their side with the top knee dropped downward in adduction across the midline, compressing the gluteal tendons! In contrast, lying supine in 10°–15° of hip abduction completely lifts the iliotibial band off the greater trochanter (0 N compression!) while applying pure tensile load to the deep gluteus minimus and medius insertions.

jointActions: Open/closed chain; submaximal isometric in 10° abduction; tendon analgesia

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine on a bed or mat with a pillow under your knees (knees bent at ~30°) and position your feet and knees slightly wider than hip-width apart (~10°–15° of hip abduction)
execution.description: Foundational exercise of the 2018 BMJ LEAP Trial. Why is this superior to Clamshells in acute GTPS? In side-lying Clamshells, the patient lies on their side with the top knee dropped downward in adduction across the midline, compressing the gluteal tendons! In contrast, lying supine in 10°–15° of hip abduction completely lifts the iliotibial band off the greater trochanter (0 N compression!) while applying pure tensile load to the deep gluteus minimus and medius insertions.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine on a bed or mat with a pillow under your knees (knees bent at ~30°) and position your feet and knees slightly wider than hip-width apart (~10°–15° of hip abduction)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a non-elastic belt or heavy resistance band around your distal thighs so it holds your legs in that 10°–15° abducted position

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Gently push both thighs outward against the belt at 30%–50% pain-free effort ("slow ramp-up and slow ramp-down" over 3 seconds so you recruit the deep gluteus minimus and medius rather than snapping on the superficial TFL!)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Hold static for 30-45 seconds, rest 1 minute, and complete 5 sets.

coachingCues: "With your knees resting slightly wider than your hips, gently swell your outer hip muscles outward into the belt like inflating a balloon" (external).
commonErrors: Pushing out violently at 100% effort (over-recruits the TFL, which tensions the ITB—Grimaldi emphasizes a smooth "slow ramp" to 40%–50% effort to target the deep postural gluteus minimus!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Place a thick pillow between the knees/ankles while lying supine or on the unaffected side and perform gentle 20% effort outward presses.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase push intensity to 70% MVIC; combine the outward belt push with a supine glute bridge.

precautions: Pushing out violently at 100% effort (over-recruits the TFL, which tensions the ITB—Grimaldi emphasizes a smooth "slow ramp" to 40%–50% effort to target the deep postural gluteus minimus!). Cues: "With your knees resting slightly wider than your hips, gently swell your outer hip muscles outward into the belt like inflating a balloon" (external).

description: Trains the primary functional role of the gluteus medius—holding the pelvis level during single-leg weight-bearing—while ensuring the stance hip remains in 5°–10° abduction where ITB compressive force over the greater trochanter is zero.

jointActions: Closed chain; isometric; weight-bearing stance-hip gluteus medius activation

execution.startingPosition: Stand parallel to a wall with your uninjured leg closest to the wall and your affected (GTPS) leg on the outside as the standing stance leg
execution.description: Trains the primary functional role of the gluteus medius—holding the pelvis level during single-leg weight-bearing—while ensuring the stance hip remains in 5°–10° abduction where ITB compressive force over the greater trochanter is zero.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand parallel to a wall with your uninjured leg closest to the wall and your affected (GTPS) leg on the outside as the standing stance leg

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Place your affected stance foot slightly out to the side so your affected hip is in 5°–10° of abduction (strictly avoiding standing with the pelvis shifted outward in hip adduction!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Bend the inside (uninjured) knee to 90° and press it firmly into the wall for 30-45 seconds—this forces your outside (affected) gluteus medius to fire isometrically in a weight-bearing, compression-free posture!

coachingCues: "Keep your outside hip tucked directly over your ankle—never let your hip pop out to the side—and press your inside knee into the wall" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the outside (affected) hip jut outward toward the side (hip adduction / Trendelenburg hang—this is the #1 posture that causes GTPS!).

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Letting the outside (affected) hip jut outward toward the side (hip adduction / Trendelenburg hang—this is the #1 posture that causes GTPS!). Cues: "Keep your outside hip tucked directly over your ankle—never let your hip pop out to the side—and press your inside knee into the wall" (external).
