description: Core progression of the LEAP Trial. The Offset (Staggered) Bridge is a brilliant clinical bridge between two-legged and one-legged loading because it allows the clinician to dial up the vertical load on the affected hip from 50% to 75% to 100% without ever allowing the opposite pelvis to drop into Trendelenburg adduction!

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic concentric/eccentric; posterior-lateral hip synergy

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent at 90° and feet placed slightly wider than hip-width apart (10° hip abduction) with a resistance band looped above the knees
execution.description: Core progression of the LEAP Trial. The Offset (Staggered) Bridge is a brilliant clinical bridge between two-legged and one-legged loading because it allows the clinician to dial up the vertical load on the affected hip from 50% to 75% to 100% without ever allowing the opposite pelvis to drop into Trendelenburg adduction!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent at 90° and feet placed slightly wider than hip-width apart (10° hip abduction) with a resistance band looped above the knees

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain gentle outward pressure against the band to keep the thighs in 10° abduction

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Drive through the heels to lift the pelvis to full extension over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds at the top, and lower over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: LEAP Progression: Progress from Bilateral Bridge -> Offset Bridge (slide the uninjured foot 6 inches forward so the affected leg carries 75% of the weight) -> Pure Single-Leg Bridge (keeping the pelvis 100% horizontal!).

coachingCues: "Keep two headlights on your hip bones shining straight up at the ceiling—if one hip drops, slide your other heel down for an offset bridge" (external).
commonErrors: Attempting a full single-leg bridge too early when the unsupported side of the pelvis drops toward the floor (pelvic drop places the stance hip into adduction and twists the greater trochanter!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral bridge without band resistance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Bilateral Bridge -> Offset Bridge -> Marching Bridge (3s single-leg holds at the top) -> Single-Leg Bridge with weight plate.

precautions: Attempting a full single-leg bridge too early when the unsupported side of the pelvis drops toward the floor (pelvic drop places the stance hip into adduction and twists the greater trochanter!). Cues: "Keep two headlights on your hip bones shining straight up at the ceiling—if one hip drops, slide your other heel down for an offset bridge" (external).
clinicalNotes: Core progression of the LEAP Trial. name: Pillow-supported side-lying hip abduction (strictly stopping at 0° neutral)
chineseName: 側臥 髖關節外展肌力強化 (臀中肌/臀小肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Standard side-lying leg lifts start and finish with the top foot touching the bottom foot on the floor—which puts the top hip into 15°–20° of adduction at the bottom of every single rep, pinching the gluteus medius tendon against the greater trochanter 15 times per set! Stacking two thick pillows under the top leg creates a physical floor at 0° neutral so the tendon is loaded purely in its non-compressive tensile zone.

primaryMuscles: gluteus minimus (zero adduction drop across midline)
jointActions: Open chain; isotonic HSR; isolated gluteus medius hypertrophy without ITB pinch

execution.startingPosition: Clearance Gate: Begin side-lying exercises only once lying on the unaffected side for 5 minutes is comfortable
execution.description: Standard side-lying leg lifts start and finish with the top foot touching the bottom foot on the floor—which puts the top hip into 15°–20° of adduction at the bottom of every single rep, pinching the gluteus medius tendon against the greater trochanter 15 times per set! Stacking two thick pillows under the top leg creates a physical floor at 0° neutral so the tendon is loaded purely in its non-compressive tensile zone.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Clearance Gate: Begin side-lying exercises only once lying on the unaffected side for 5 minutes is comfortable

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lie on your unaffected side with your back against a wall AND place two thick pillows between your knees/shins so that at the bottom of the movement, your top (affected) leg rests completely horizontal (at 0° neutral to 5° abduction—NEVER dropping downward toward the floor across the midline!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: From the pillow support, lift the straight top leg (heel sliding along the wall in slight hip extension) up to 30°–35° abduction over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower slowly over 3 seconds back onto the pillows!

coachingCues: "Always start and finish on the thick pillow platform so your top leg never dips below horizontal" (external).
commonErrors: Removing the pillows and letting the top leg drop down to the mattress between reps (immediately compresses the greater trochanter!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform standing banded hip abduction if side-lying position still causes lateral hip ache.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a 1-3 kg ankle cuff weight or resistance band above the knees while keeping the pillow stop in place.

precautions: Removing the pillows and letting the top leg drop down to the mattress between reps (immediately compresses the greater trochanter!). Cues: "Always start and finish on the thick pillow platform so your top leg never dips below horizontal" (external).
clinicalNotes: Standard side-lying leg lifts start and finish with the top foot touching the bottom foot on the floor—which puts the top hip into 15°–20° of adduction at the bottom of every single rep, pinching the gluteus medius tendon against the greater trochanter 15 times per set! Stacking two thick pillows under the top leg creates a physical floor at 0° neutral so the tendon is loaded purely in its non-compressive tensile zone.

execution.description: Key functional progression in the LEAP Trial. Keeping the minimum step width at hip-width guarantees that both the leading and trailing hips remain in >= 5°–10° abduction throughout the entire set, building high-load abductor endurance without trochanteric compression.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a resistance band around the ankles or forefeet

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Stand in an athletic quarter-squat (20°–30° hip and knee bend) with feet hip-width apart

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Step sideways 6-8 inches, then bring the trailing foot in slowly—stopping at hip-width apart (never letting the feet come close together into hip adduction!)

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Take 10-15 steps in each direction while keeping the torso tall and pelvis level.

coachingCues: "Never let your feet come closer than hip-width apart—imagine holding a wide beach ball between your shins as you step" (external).
commonErrors: Bringing the trailing foot all the way in to touch the lead foot (puts the hips into adduction and loses band tension); waddling the shoulders side to side.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform side-steps without a band first, focusing on landing quietly with a level pelvis.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Stiffer forefoot band resistance; add slow 3-second single-leg balance pauses on each side-step.

precautions: Bringing the trailing foot all the way in to touch the lead foot (puts the hips into adduction and loses band tension); waddling the shoulders side to side. Cues: "Never let your feet come closer than hip-width apart—imagine holding a wide beach ball between your shins as you step" (external).
clinicalNotes: Key functional progression in the LEAP Trial. Keeping the minimum step width at hip-width guarantees that both the leading and trailing hips remain in >= 5°–10° abduction throughout the entire set, building high-load abductor endurance without trochanteric compression.

description: Notice the critical modification for GTPS compared to standard PFP or ITBS: in acute/subacute GTPS, dropping the free hip below horizontal places the stance hip into adduction under full body weight, which crushes the gluteus medius tendon against the greater trochanter! Therefore, Phase 1 trains from Horizontal (0°) UP to Abduction (+10°) before introducing eccentric drops in Phase 2!

jointActions: Closed chain; concentric/isometric (progressing to eccentric); mid-stance control

execution.startingPosition: Phase 1 (Neutral-to-High Pelvic Hitch — Weeks 3–6): Stand sideways on a low step on the affected leg, starting with your pelvis completely horizontal (0° neutral)—do NOT let the free hip drop below level in Phase 1! From horizontal, contract your standing outer hip to hike the free pelvis 1-2 inches upward (into slight stance-hip abduction), hold for 3 seconds, and lower slowly back to horizontal only
execution.description: Notice the critical modification for GTPS compared to standard PFP or ITBS: in acute/subacute GTPS, dropping the free hip below horizontal places the stance hip into adduction under full body weight, which crushes the gluteus medius tendon against the greater trochanter! From horizontal, contract your standing outer hip to hike the free pelvis 1-2 inches upward (into slight stance-hip abduction), hold for 3 seconds, and lower slowly back to horizontal only

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Controlled Eccentric Pelvic Drop — Weeks 7–12+): Only once lateral trochanteric tenderness has resolved, slowly introduce a 1-inch eccentric drop below horizontal to build outer-range compressive tolerance.

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Letting the unsupported hip sag below level at the bottom of the rep during Phase 1–2 GTPS (recreates the exact Trendelenburg compression mechanism!). Cues: "Treat the horizontal belt line as a solid floor—hike your opposite hip up from level and stop right back at level" (external).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Exercise A (Level-Pelvis Step-Up — LEAP Phase 3): Place the affected foot on a 4-to-8-inch step. steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Exercise B (Gait & Running Retraining — Eliminating "Tightrope Crossover" & Overstriding): When walking, climbing stairs, or returning to running, increase cadence by 5%–10% and keep feet tracking on two parallel hip-width rails (eliminating midline "crossover gait," which forces the hip into adduction on every footstrike!).

precautions: Walking or running along a single line like a tightrope walker (crossover gait increases hip adduction angle by 5°–8° and doubles ITB compression over the greater trochanter!). execution.description: In athletes (especially soccer players, skaters, and runners), the obturator nerve becomes tethered in thickened fascia over the adductor brevis as it exits the obturator foramen, causing deep exercise-induced medial thigh pain that mimics an adductor strain. Reciprocal head-and-hip sliding restores free longitudinal gliding without stretching the irritated nerve (Flossing Exercises for Obturator Nerve Entrapment — Performance Place).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand holding a wall or lie on the unaffected side.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Distal Slide): Gently slide or swing the affected leg out into comfortable hip abduction + slight extension (10–15°) while simultaneously flexing the neck/upper back forward (looking down) to slacken the lumbar spinal cord and L2–L4 nerve roots.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Proximal Slide): Bring the leg back across toward midline (adduction + slight flexion) while simultaneously lifting the head/chest upright (looking up) to draw the nerve proximally.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Oscillate smoothly for 12–15 reps.

coachingCues: "When your leg glides out to the side, nod your chin down; when your leg comes back to the middle, lift your eyes up—like a single piece of dental floss sliding back and forth." Internal cue: "Keep the movement silky and stop well before any deep groin tug."
commonErrors: Critical distinction: Do NOT look up while swinging the leg outward in Early Rehab—that pulls both ends of the nerve simultaneously (a tensioner) and can flare up an entrapped obturator nerve.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce the hip abduction arc by 50% and keep the hip in 0° neutral extension (avoiding extension component) if acutely sensitive.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Transition to a gentle Obturator Tensioner in Late Rehab: slowly look up while abducting/extending the hip to a mild 2/10 tension barrier, then immediately release.

precautions: Critical distinction: Do NOT look up while swinging the leg outward in Early Rehab—that pulls both ends of the nerve simultaneously (a tensioner) and can flare up an entrapped obturator nerve. name: Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Nerve (LFCN) Inguinal Tunnel Decompression & Slider (Meralgia Paresthetica)
chineseName: Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Nerve (LFCN) Inguinal Tunnel Decompression & Slider (Meralgia Paresthetica)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: The LFCN passes directly beneath or through a split in the lateral inguinal ligament just medial to the ASIS. Anterior pelvic tilt, hip hyperextension, and hip adduction ("hanging on one hip") compress and stretch the nerve against the ASIS, causing Meralgia Paresthetica (burning, tingling, or numbness over the anterolateral thigh). Decompressing the inguinal tunnel and gliding the LFCN resolves symptoms without aggravating the sensory fibers (Meralgia Paresthetica Exercises — Paul Marquis PT).

description: Chronic obturator or femoral nerve compression causes focal denervation inhibition and motor-unit drop-out in the adductors or quadriceps. Loading these muscles in a neuro-slackened joint angle (flexed hip) restores maximal efferent motor recruitment without compressing the nerve tunnel.

secondaryMuscles: Femoral motor path: Quadriceps (vastus medialis/lateralis/rectus femoris)
jointActions: Isometric-to-Concentric Neuromuscular Re-Education (Restoring Efferent Drive)

execution.description: Chronic obturator or femoral nerve compression causes focal denervation inhibition and motor-unit drop-out in the adductors or quadriceps. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Perform in a slackened, decompressed posture (seated or hook-lying at 60–70° hip flexion where neither the obturator nor femoral nerve is under longitudinal tension): 4A) For Obturator Entrapment: Squeeze a foam roller or ball between the knees at 50–70% effort for 10 seconds × 8 reps, focusing on symmetric medial thigh recruitment.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: 4B) For Femoral Entrapment: Perform seated short-arc terminal knee extensions (45° to 0°) with an ankle weight or band, holding full quadriceps lockout for 5 seconds × 10 reps while sitting upright (avoiding reclining backward).

coachingCues: "Sit tall with your hips bent so the nerve tunnel stays wide open while you squeeze the muscle belly hard." Internal cue: "Focus on waking up a crisp, symmetric contraction in the inner or front thigh."
commonErrors: Do not perform long-lever supine straight-leg adduction or hyperextended hip exercises while motor weakness is still recovering.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase external load (heavy medicine ball squeeze or seated leg extension machine at 60–90° hip flexion).

precautions: Do not perform long-lever supine straight-leg adduction or hyperextended hip exercises while motor weakness is still recovering. description: In frozen hip and capsular fibrosis, loss of posterior-inferior capsular glide causes the femoral head to impinge anteriorly during hip flexion. Lateral-inferior band distraction restores arthrokinematic accessory glide while flexing the femur (PMC4808257).

primaryMuscles: Posterior-inferior hip capsule (ischiofemoral ligament & zona orbicularis)
jointActions: Mobilization with Movement (MWM) — Inferior-Lateral & Posterior Capsular Glide

execution.startingPosition: Anchor a heavy monster resistance band low to a squat rack and loop it high into the proximal groin crease of the affected hip (right against the proximal medial femur)
execution.description: In frozen hip and capsular fibrosis, loss of posterior-inferior capsular glide causes the femoral head to impinge anteriorly during hip flexion. Lateral-inferior band distraction restores arthrokinematic accessory glide while flexing the femur (PMC4808257).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Anchor a heavy monster resistance band low to a squat rack and loop it high into the proximal groin crease of the affected hip (right against the proximal medial femur).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Step out laterally on all fours (quadruped) so the band pulls the proximal femur laterally and slightly inferiorly.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the spine flat in neutral, slowly rock the pelvis backward toward the heels over 4 seconds into comfortable hip flexion (90–110°), hold for 3 seconds while the band clears the anterior joint space, then return forward.

coachingCues: "Let the band tug the very top of your thigh bone outward to create space in the socket as you sit your hips back with a flat back." Internal cue: "Feel the front of the hip crease open up instead of jamming as you fold back."
commonErrors: Ensure the band is positioned as high up in the groin crease as possible (acting on the femoral neck/proximal shaft, not pulling down near the knee).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce band tension and limit rock-back flexion to 80–90° if capsule irritability is moderate.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Internally rotate the affected hip slightly (moving the shin outward by 10–15°) during the quadruped rock-back to bias the tight posterior-superior ischiofemoral capsule.

precautions: Ensure the band is positioned as high up in the groin crease as possible (acting on the femoral neck/proximal shaft, not pulling down near the knee). External cue: "Let the band tug the very top of your thigh bone outward to create space in the socket as you sit your hips back with a flat back." Internal cue: "Feel the front of the hip crease open up instead of jamming as you fold back."
clinicalNotes: In frozen hip and capsular fibrosis, loss of posterior-inferior capsular glide causes the femoral head to impinge anteriorly during hip flexion. Lateral-inferior band distraction restores arthrokinematic accessory glide while flexing the femur (PMC4808257).

description: Targets contracture of the thick anterior iliofemoral ligament (which restricts hip extension and external rotation in frozen hip) by combining Grade III anterior-lateral capsular traction with reciprocal inhibition of the hip flexors via gluteus maximus contraction (PMC12417861).

jointActions: Capsular Distraction + Active Antagonist Contraction (Iliofemoral Remodeling)

execution.startingPosition: Anchor a heavy band in front of or at a 45° anterolateral angle to you, looping it high around the proximal posterior-medial thigh of the affected (down-kneeling) leg.
execution.description: Targets contracture of the thick anterior iliofemoral ligament (which restricts hip extension and external rotation in frozen hip) by combining Grade III anterior-lateral capsular traction with reciprocal inhibition of the hip flexors via gluteus maximus contraction (PMC12417861).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Anchor a heavy band in front of or at a 45° anterolateral angle to you, looping it high around the proximal posterior-medial thigh of the affected (down-kneeling) leg.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Assume a half-kneeling posture with the affected knee on a pad.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Perform a firm posterior pelvic tilt (tucking the tailbone under) and squeeze the affected glute for 5 seconds while gently shifting the pelvis 3–5 cm forward, then relax for 5 seconds without losing the pelvic tuck.

coachingCues: "Lock your belt buckle tilted upward toward your chest before you let the band draw your hip gently forward." Internal cue: "Squeeze your back pocket firmly to open the tight capsule in the front of your hip."
commonErrors: Do not let the band pull the lumbar spine into hyperextension—if the lower back arches, the iliofemoral capsule is not being stretched.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform in a standing split stance (without kneeling on the floor) with the band pulling the rear proximal thigh forward/laterally.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Add a gentle thoracic rotation toward the lead leg or reach the ipsilateral arm overhead to lengthen the entire anterior fascial chain.

precautions: Do not let the band pull the lumbar spine into hyperextension—if the lower back arches, the iliofemoral capsule is not being stretched. External cue: "Lock your belt buckle tilted upward toward your chest before you let the band draw your hip gently forward." Internal cue: "Squeeze your back pocket firmly to open the tight capsule in the front of your hip."
clinicalNotes: Targets contracture of the thick anterior iliofemoral ligament (which restricts hip extension and external rotation in frozen hip) by combining Grade III anterior-lateral capsular traction with reciprocal inhibition of the hip flexors via gluteus maximus contraction (PMC12417861).

name: Supine Figure-4 & Adductor Low-Load Long-Duration (LLLD) Viscoelastic Creep Hold
chineseName: Supine Figure-4 & Adductor Low-Load Long-Duration (LLLD) Viscoelastic Creep Hold
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Fibrotic joint capsules respond best to Total End-Range Time (TERT) under low, sustained mechanical tension (viscoelastic creep) rather than short, high-force ballistic stretching, which triggers reflex muscle guarding (PMC9560891).

jointActions: Low-Load Long-Duration (LLLD) Viscoelastic Capsular Creep + Submaximal Contract-Relax

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine facing a wall with the unaffected foot resting flat on the wall (knee bent 70–90°) and cross the affected ankle over the opposite distal thigh (supine wall-supported Figure-4), OR place both heels up on the wall in a wide V-straddle for pure abduction creep.
execution.description: Fibrotic joint capsules respond best to Total End-Range Time (TERT) under low, sustained mechanical tension (viscoelastic creep) rather than short, high-force ballistic stretching, which triggers reflex muscle guarding (PMC9560891).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine facing a wall with the unaffected foot resting flat on the wall (knee bent 70–90°) and cross the affected ankle over the opposite distal thigh (supine wall-supported Figure-4), OR place both heels up on the wall in a wide V-straddle for pure abduction creep.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Position yourself at a distance from the wall that produces a mild, completely tolerable 2–3/10 capsular stretch.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold completely supported for 90–120 seconds while breathing slowly, applying a gentle 5-second 20% isometric press of the knee every 30 seconds.

coachingCues: "Let the wall hold your legs so your muscles can turn off completely for two full minutes." Internal cue: "Every time you exhale, let the tight hip capsule soften by one millimeter."
commonErrors: Stop immediately if you feel a sharp lateral or anterior impingement pinch rather than a broad deep stretch.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform supine hook-lying butterfly (soles of feet together) with thick yoga blocks or pillows propped underneath both outer thighs to support the hips at their comfortable limit.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Scoot the hips 3–5 cm closer to the wall over successive weeks as external rotation and abduction range improve.

precautions: Stop immediately if you feel a sharp lateral or anterior impingement pinch rather than a broad deep stretch. External cue: "Let the wall hold your legs so your muscles can turn off completely for two full minutes." Internal cue: "Every time you exhale, let the tight hip capsule soften by one millimeter."
clinicalNotes: Fibrotic joint capsules respond best to Total End-Range Time (TERT) under low, sustained mechanical tension (viscoelastic creep) rather than short, high-force ballistic stretching, which triggers reflex muscle guarding (PMC9560891).

name: 90–90 Seated Hip Internal Rotation PAILs & RAILs (Ischiofemoral Capsule Remodeling)
chineseName: 坐姿 髖關節內旋控制與活動度
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Internal rotation is the #1 most restricted motion in the hip capsular pattern (PMC12417861). PAILs/RAILs induces sarcomereogenesis and longitudinal collagen reorganization at the exact end-range barrier while teaching the nervous system active control over the new degrees of freedom.

jointActions: End-Range Isometric Conditioning — Progressive & Regressive Angular Isometric Loading (PAILs/RAILs)

execution.startingPosition: Sit in a modified 90–90 posture on the floor (elevating the pelvis on 1–2 yoga blocks if internal rotation is severely limited so the lumbar spine stays upright without lateral leaning)
execution.description: Internal rotation is the #1 most restricted motion in the hip capsular pattern (PMC12417861). PAILs/RAILs induces sarcomereogenesis and longitudinal collagen reorganization at the exact end-range barrier while teaching the nervous system active control over the new degrees of freedom.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Passive Hold: Hold the stretch for 60–90 seconds.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: PAILs: Progressively drive the trail ankle/shin Down into the floor (attempting external rotation from the internally rotated position) ramping from 20% to 60–70% effort over 15 seconds.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: RAILs: Immediately reverse and attempt to lift the trail ankle slightly off the floor (driving deeper into internal rotation) for 10–15 seconds. Relax into the newly gained range for 30 seconds.

coachingCues: "Sit tall on the yoga block, press your back shin down into the floor like a gas pedal for 15 seconds, then try to make your back ankle light on the floor for 15 seconds." Internal cue: "Rotate purely from the deep hip socket without twisting your knee or arching your lower back."
commonErrors: Always elevate the hips on yoga blocks if the patient cannot sit in 90–90 without rounding or cranking the knee joint.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Seated on a chair with a foam block between the knees: bring the affected foot outward into end-range internal rotation against a wall or band and perform gentle 40% PAILs/RAILs presses without floor-sitting strain.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Remove the yoga blocks under the sitting bone and lean the torso slightly toward the trail hip to increase internal rotation torque.

precautions: Always elevate the hips on yoga blocks if the patient cannot sit in 90–90 without rounding or cranking the knee joint. External cue: "Sit tall on the yoga block, press your back shin down into the floor like a gas pedal for 15 seconds, then try to make your back ankle light on the floor for 15 seconds." Internal cue: "Rotate purely from the deep hip socket without twisting your knee or arching your lower back."
clinicalNotes: Internal rotation is the #1 most restricted motion in the hip capsular pattern (PMC12417861). PAILs/RAILs induces sarcomereogenesis and longitudinal collagen reorganization at the exact end-range barrier while teaching the nervous system active control over the new degrees of freedom.

jointActions: End-Range Isometric Conditioning (PAILs/RAILs)

execution.startingPosition: Sit in the 90–90 position (hips elevated on a block if needed) with the affected leg as the lead (front) leg in external rotation and 90° flexion
execution.description: Restores combined hip flexion + external rotation + abduction capacity (required for putting on shoes/socks, sitting cross-legged, and squatting) by remodeling the inferior-posterior capsule and deep rotator fascia.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Hold: 60–90 s passive creep

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: PAILs: Drive the front ankle and knee Down into the floor for 15 seconds at 50–70% effort

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: RAILs: Actively pull the front shin/chest closer together (attempting to lift the front ankle toward the torso) for 15 seconds, then hold the deeper hinge for 30 seconds.

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Elevated Pigeon (front shin resting on a 40–50 cm box/plinth) PAILs/RAILs for precise height customization.

precautions: Do not round the thoracic/lumbar spine forward to touch the head to the floor—hinge strictly at the hip joint with a flat back. External cue: "Lead with your breastbone forward over your front shin—never round your spine—and push your front shin through the floor." Internal cue: "Feel the work deep in the back pocket of the front hip, with zero pinching in the front groin crease."
clinicalNotes: Restores combined hip flexion + external rotation + abduction capacity (required for putting on shoes/socks, sitting cross-legged, and squatting) by remodeling the inferior-posterior capsule and deep rotator fascia.

name: Standing & Quadruped Hip Controlled Articular Rotations (CARs — Active Capsule Expansion)
chineseName: Standing & Quadruped Hip Controlled Articular Rotations (CARs — Active Capsule Expansion)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: After passive and isometric mobilization opens new capsular range, Controlled Articular Rotations (CARs) train active neuromuscular ownership along the entire outer perimeter of the acetabular rim, preventing re-adhesion of the synovial folds (PMC12417861).

jointActions: Active End-Range Circumduction & Articular Capsule Control

execution.startingPosition: Stand tall holding a wall or squat rack for firm stability (or perform in quadruped).
execution.description: After passive and isometric mobilization opens new capsular range, Controlled Articular Rotations (CARs) train active neuromuscular ownership along the entire outer perimeter of the acetabular rim, preventing re-adhesion of the synovial folds (PMC12417861).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand tall holding a wall or squat rack for firm stability (or perform in quadruped).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Brace the core and stance glute to lock the pelvis completely stationary.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lift the affected knee into maximal active flexion + external rotation, transition smoothly out into maximal abduction, internally rotate the hip (lifting the heel toward the ceiling while the knee stays out) as you sweep the thigh behind you into maximal hip extension, and lower to neutral.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Reverse the circle from extension back to flexion.

steps.title: 步驟 5
steps.instruction: Each circle should take a full 10–12 seconds.

coachingCues: "Imagine your kneecap is a paintbrush tracing the largest slow-motion circle possible without your belt buckle moving a millimeter." Internal cue: "Move through thick honey—feel every degree of rotation inside the hip socket."
commonErrors: Do not hike the pelvis, lean the trunk sideways, or twist the lower back to fake a bigger circle—trace the true boundary of the ball-and-socket joint.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Side-lying Hip CARs (eliminating single-leg balance demand while supporting the pelvis against a wall).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing Hip CARs stepping over a 40–50 cm hurdle with a 1–2 kg ankle weight.

precautions: Do not hike the pelvis, lean the trunk sideways, or twist the lower back to fake a bigger circle—trace the true boundary of the ball-and-socket joint. External cue: "Imagine your kneecap is a paintbrush tracing the largest slow-motion circle possible without your belt buckle moving a millimeter." Internal cue: "Move through thick honey—feel every degree of rotation inside the hip socket."
clinicalNotes: After passive and isometric mobilization opens new capsular range, Controlled Articular Rotations (CARs) train active neuromuscular ownership along the entire outer perimeter of the acetabular rim, preventing re-adhesion of the synovial folds (PMC12417861).

rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化

description: Consolidates newly restored flexion, abduction, and rotational capsular mobility into functional, multi-joint weight-bearing strength so the capsule retains its extensibility under daily and athletic loads.

jointActions: Full-Excursion Eccentric–Concentric Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR)

execution.startingPosition: Loop a heavy distraction band around the proximal groin crease of the affected hip (pulling laterally) and hold a 8–16 kg kettlebell or dumbbell in the Goblet position at the chest, with heels slightly elevated on a 2–3 cm slant board if needed.
execution.description: Consolidates newly restored flexion, abduction, and rotational capsular mobility into functional, multi-joint weight-bearing strength so the capsule retains its extensibility under daily and athletic loads.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Loop a heavy distraction band around the proximal groin crease of the affected hip (pulling laterally) and hold a 8–16 kg kettlebell or dumbbell in the Goblet position at the chest, with heels slightly elevated on a 2–3 cm slant board if needed.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slowly descend over 4 seconds into your deepest comfortable, pinch-free squat stance, hold the bottom position for 3 seconds while gently shifting weight 2–3 cm left and right to load the capsule under eccentric tension, then drive smoothly to standing.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pair with controlled Cossack lateral squats to load end-range abduction.

coachingCues: "Hold the kettlebell close to your chest, spread your knees wide over your toes, and pause calmly at the bottom for three seconds." Internal cue: "Use the weight of the kettlebell to gently sink your hips into a strong, open bottom position before driving the floor away."
commonErrors: Avoid "butt wink" (lumbar flexion collapse at the bottom of the squat); stop just above the depth where pelvic neutrality is lost.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: TRX/Suspension-Assisted Deep Squat Hold with a 5-second pause at the bottom of the comfortable range.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Unbanded full-depth Goblet Squat, Front-Foot Elevated Split Squat (loaded end-range hip flexion + contralateral hip extension), and full return to running/sport.

precautions: Avoid "butt wink" (lumbar flexion collapse at the bottom of the squat); stop just above the depth where pelvic neutrality is lost. External cue: "Hold the kettlebell close to your chest, spread your knees wide over your toes, and pause calmly at the bottom for three seconds." Internal cue: "Use the weight of the kettlebell to gently sink your hips into a strong, open bottom position before driving the floor away."
clinicalNotes: Consolidates newly restored flexion, abduction, and rotational capsular mobility into functional, multi-joint weight-bearing strength so the capsule retains its extensibility under daily and athletic loads.

description: Activates the deep posterior-lateral hip rotator cuff ("rotator cuff of the hip") to draw the femoral head posteriorly and medially into the shallow acetabulum, unloading the anterior-superior labrum and iliofemoral capsule without provoking shear.

jointActions: Isometric Co-Contraction (Joint Centration & Analgesia)

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70°, feet flat hip-width apart, and a firm mini-band looped just above the knees.
execution.description: Activates the deep posterior-lateral hip rotator cuff ("rotator cuff of the hip") to draw the femoral head posteriorly and medially into the shallow acetabulum, unloading the anterior-superior labrum and iliofemoral capsule without provoking shear.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70°, feet flat hip-width apart, and a firm mini-band looped just above the knees.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Gently flatten the lower back into a neutral pelvis without gripping the superficial hip flexors.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press both knees outward into the band by 2–3 cm to create firm isometric tension, hold for 30–45 seconds while breathing diaphragmatically, then slowly release.

coachingCues: "Press the outside of your knees gently against the band while keeping your big toes planted." Internal cue: "Feel a deep, warm tightening deep inside the back pocket of your hip, with zero pinching in the front crease."

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Avoid overarching the lumbar spine or rolling onto the lateral borders of the feet. External cue: "Press the outside of your knees gently against the band while keeping your big toes planted." Internal cue: "Feel a deep, warm tightening deep inside the back pocket of your hip, with zero pinching in the front crease."
clinicalNotes: Activates the deep posterior-lateral hip rotator cuff ("rotator cuff of the hip") to draw the femoral head posteriorly and medially into the shallow acetabulum, unloading the anterior-superior labrum and iliofemoral capsule without provoking shear.

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with a mini-band above the knees and feet flat 15–20 cm from the buttocks.
execution.description: Strengthens the gluteus maximus—the primary posterior vector that pulls the femoral head backward during terminal stance—Preventing the anterior femoral head glide characteristic of hip micro-instability.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with a mini-band above the knees and feet flat 15–20 cm from the buttocks.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Initiate a slight posterior pelvic tilt, press the knees slightly outward into the band, and drive through the heels to lift the hips until the torso and thighs form a straight line (0° neutral hip extension—do NOT hyperextend).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold the top position for 3 seconds before lowering over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Stop lifting as soon as your knees, hips, and ribs form a flat ramp—do not arch your back or push your hips to the ceiling." Internal cue: "Squeeze your glutes to pull the thigh bone back into the socket at the top."
commonErrors: Critical: Never push the hips past 0° into hyperextension, which drives the femoral head anteriorly against the dysplastic labrum and iliofemoral ligament.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Two-leg isometric bridge hover lifting only 5–8 cm off the floor if full neutral extension triggers anterior capsule stretch discomfort.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: B-Stance (kickstand) glute bridge (80% weight on affected leg, 20% on contralateral heel) → Single-leg glute bridge to neutral 0° extension.

precautions: Critical: Never push the hips past 0° into hyperextension, which drives the femoral head anteriorly against the dysplastic labrum and iliofemoral ligament. External cue: "Stop lifting as soon as your knees, hips, and ribs form a flat ramp—do not arch your back or push your hips to the ceiling." Internal cue: "Squeeze your glutes to pull the thigh bone back into the socket at the top."
clinicalNotes: Strengthens the gluteus maximus—the primary posterior vector that pulls the femoral head backward during terminal stance—Preventing the anterior femoral head glide characteristic of hip micro-instability.

primaryMuscles: Stance-leg gluteus medius/minimus & deep rotators (centration under load)
moving-leg posterior gluteus medius & external rotators
jointActions: Isometric / Motor Control (Closed-Chain Stance Leg + Open-Chain Moving Leg)

execution.startingPosition: Start in quadruped with hands under shoulders, knees under hips, and spine neutral.
execution.description: Dual-purpose drill: when the affected hip is the weight-bearing support leg, it trains tri-planar acetabular centration over a fixed femur; when moving, it builds posterior-lateral cuff endurance.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Start in quadruped with hands under shoulders, knees under hips, and spine neutral.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Shift weight onto the stance hip without letting the pelvis drop laterally, then lift the opposite knee outward to 30–40° abduction/external rotation while keeping the lower back completely flat.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 5 seconds at the peak, then return slowly.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Perform on both sides (when the dysplastic hip is the stance leg, it trains weight-bearing socket centration).

coachingCues: "Balance a cup of water across your lower back as your knee lifts just a few inches." Internal cue: "Push the floor away through your supporting knee so your hip socket stays tall and centered."

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Prevent trunk twist or lumbar side-bending to fake extra hip abduction range. External cue: "Balance a cup of water across your lower back as your knee lifts just a few inches." Internal cue: "Push the floor away through your supporting knee so your hip socket stays tall and centered."
clinicalNotes: Dual-purpose drill: when the affected hip is the weight-bearing support leg, it trains tri-planar acetabular centration over a fixed femur; when moving, it builds posterior-lateral cuff endurance.

execution.description: Forward trunk inclination (20–30° hip hinge) shifts mechanical leverage away from the tensor fasciae latae (which can anteriorly translate the femoral head) toward the gluteus medius, minimus, and deep external rotators that compress and stabilize the dysplastic hip joint.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place a loop band around the ankles or just above the knees.

steps.title: 步驟 2

steps.title: 步驟 3

description: Builds heavy eccentric and concentric strength across the posterior kinetic chain and deep hip rotators while maintaining a level pelvis, directly countering Trendelenburg overload on the shallow lateral acetabular rim (Delphi Consensus, IJSPT).

jointActions: Eccentric–Concentric Closed-Chain Hypertrophy (Heavy Slow Resistance)

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg with the knee unlocked at 15–20° flexion, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in the contralateral hand and keeping fingertips lightly touching a wall or rack for balance (or rear toes lightly on the floor in a B-stance).
execution.description: Builds heavy eccentric and concentric strength across the posterior kinetic chain and deep hip rotators while maintaining a level pelvis, directly countering Trendelenburg overload on the shallow lateral acetabular rim (Delphi Consensus, IJSPT).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg with the knee unlocked at 15–20° flexion, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in the contralateral hand and keeping fingertips lightly touching a wall or rack for balance (or rear toes lightly on the floor in a B-stance).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge at the hip by gliding the pelvis straight back while keeping the pelvis level in the frontal plane.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Stop at ~60–70° hip flexion (mid-shin level), then drive the heel into the floor to return to neutral 0° hip extension.

External cue: "Keep both headlights on the front of your pelvis pointing straight toward the floor as you hinge back." Internal cue: "Push the floor away with your mid-foot and squeeze your back pocket to stand tall, stopping right at vertical."
clinicalNotes: Builds heavy eccentric and concentric strength across the posterior kinetic chain and deep hip rotators while maintaining a level pelvis, directly countering Trendelenburg overload on the shallow lateral acetabular rim (Delphi Consensus, IJSPT).

name: Standing Single-Leg Hip Airplane in Mid-Range Safe Arc (Controlled Pelvic Rotation)
chineseName: Standing Single-Leg Hip Airplane in Mid-Range Safe Arc (Controlled Pelvic Rotation)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Specifically trains the ligamentum teres' secondary muscular backups—the deep external rotators and gluteus minimus/medius—to control transverse-plane rotation of the acetabulum over a fixed femoral head without allowing subluxation.

jointActions: Closed-Chain Tri-Planar Neuromuscular Control

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg in a 30–45° hip hinge with light fingertip support on a dowel or squat rack.
execution.description: Specifically trains the ligamentum teres' secondary muscular backups—the deep external rotators and gluteus minimus/medius—to control transverse-plane rotation of the acetabulum over a fixed femoral head without allowing subluxation.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg in a 30–45° hip hinge with light fingertip support on a dowel or squat rack.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping the stance knee stable over the second toe, slowly rotate the pelvis 10–15° internally (closing the pelvis toward the stance thigh) over 3 seconds, return to neutral, and rotate 10–15° externally (opening the pelvis slightly) over 3 seconds.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keep the rotational arc strictly within a pain-free, apprehension-free mid-range zone.

coachingCues: "Swivel your belt buckle smoothly just a few degrees left and right while your stance knee stays frozen like a statue." Internal cue: "Feel the muscles deep around the hip socket gripping and guiding the socket smoothly around the ball."
commonErrors: Vital for Ligamentum Teres & Dysplasia: Never force end-range internal or external rotation where the hip feels unstable or clicks; stay strictly inside the middle 50% of rotational range.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Isometric Single-Leg Hip Hinge Hold (0° pelvic rotation) with a horizontal Pallof band pull from the side.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Unassisted Hip Airplane holding a light kettlebell (4–8 kg) at the chest, or adding an elastic band pulling the pelvis horizontally.

precautions: Vital for Ligamentum Teres & Dysplasia: Never force end-range internal or external rotation where the hip feels unstable or clicks; stay strictly inside the middle 50% of rotational range. External cue: "Swivel your belt buckle smoothly just a few degrees left and right while your stance knee stays frozen like a statue." Internal cue: "Feel the muscles deep around the hip socket gripping and guiding the socket smoothly around the ball."
clinicalNotes: Specifically trains the ligamentum teres' secondary muscular backups—the deep external rotators and gluteus minimus/medius—to control transverse-plane rotation of the acetabulum over a fixed femoral head without allowing subluxation.

rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化

description: Prepares the hypermobile or dysplastic hip for unpredictable sport forces by training reflexive pre-activation of the periacetabular cuff prior to foot contact and during single-leg deceleration.

jointActions: Reactive Neuromuscular Stabilization & Eccentric Deceleration

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg on a low 10–15 cm step in a slight athletic hip hinge while holding a resistance band anchored at chest height (Pallof position).
execution.description: Prepares the hypermobile or dysplastic hip for unpredictable sport forces by training reflexive pre-activation of the periacetabular cuff prior to foot contact and during single-leg deceleration.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg on a low 10–15 cm step in a slight athletic hip hinge while holding a resistance band anchored at chest height (Pallof position).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Perform rapid 5-second oscillatory band pulses or partner perturbations while maintaining a level pelvis and aligned knee, followed immediately by a controlled 3-second lateral step-down tap of the opposite heel to the floor and an explosive return to single-leg stance.

coachingCues: "Land softly with your chest slightly over your knee and freeze your belt buckle level as you punch the band forward." Internal cue: "Pre-tense your glutes and deep hip muscles before your foot hits the ground."
commonErrors: Stop immediately if the pelvis drops into Trendelenburg or if the athlete lands upright with a stiff knee and anterior pelvic shift.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Floor-level single-leg athletic stance with rhythmic Pallof band presses (no step-down).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg hop-and-stick onto a floor target with immediate Pallof band punch, or multi-directional 45° reactive bound and stabilization (sticking the landing in a 25° hip hinge for 3 seconds).

precautions: Stop immediately if the pelvis drops into Trendelenburg or if the athlete lands upright with a stiff knee and anterior pelvic shift. External cue: "Land softly with your chest slightly over your knee and freeze your belt buckle level as you punch the band forward." Internal cue: "Pre-tense your glutes and deep hip muscles before your foot hits the ground."
clinicalNotes: Prepares the hypermobile or dysplastic hip for unpredictable sport forces by training reflexive pre-activation of the periacetabular cuff prior to foot contact and during single-leg deceleration.

name: Supine & Standing Neutral-Spine Oblique–Abductor Isometric Co-Contraction (Hip Pointer Phase 1–2)
chineseName: Supine & Standing Neutral-Spine Oblique–Abductor Isometric Co-Contraction (Hip Pointer Phase 1–2)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Because the iliac crest is the shared bony anchor between the lateral abdominal muscles pulling upward and the gluteus medius/TFL pulling downward, gentle neutral-angle isometric co-contraction re-establishes tensile alignment across the healing periosteum without tearing fragile blood clots (PhysioWorks).

secondaryMuscles: transversus abdominis (superior iliac crest attachment) + Gluteus medius & TFL (inferior iliac crest origin)
jointActions: Subperiosteal Protective Isometric (Zero-Shear Enthesis Activation)

execution.startingPosition: Once acute 48–72 hour hematoma bleeding has stabilized (or in early TFL enthesopathy): Lie supine in hook-lying with a light mini-band around the knees, or stand tall in neutral alignment (0° lateral trunk bend—never stretching the bruised crest).
execution.description: Because the iliac crest is the shared bony anchor between the lateral abdominal muscles pulling upward and the gluteus medius/TFL pulling downward, gentle neutral-angle isometric co-contraction re-establishes tensile alignment across the healing periosteum without tearing fragile blood clots (PhysioWorks).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Once acute 48–72 hour hematoma bleeding has stabilized (or in early TFL enthesopathy): Lie supine in hook-lying with a light mini-band around the knees, or stand tall in neutral alignment (0° lateral trunk bend—never stretching the bruised crest).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Gently exhale to engage the lateral abdominal wall at 30% effort while simultaneously pressing the knees outward into the band at 30% effort for 20–30 seconds.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Progress to standing sideways next to a wall and pressing the forearm and lateral thigh gently into the wall simultaneously with a straight spine.

coachingCues: "Keep your ribs stacked straight above your pelvis—no side-bending—and gently tighten your side waist and outer hip against the wall." Internal cue: "Wake up the muscles above and below your hip bone with smooth, gentle tension."
commonErrors: Critical for Hip Pointer: Never stretch the trunk into contralateral side-flexion or massage directly over a fresh iliac crest hematoma, as this causes myositis ossificans (heterotopic bone formation inside the muscle).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Pure diaphragmatic breathing with gentle transversus abdominis setting in supine hook-lying (15–20% effort) during days 2–4 post-contusion.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase isometric intensity to 60–70% MVC in standing unilateral wall-press posture.

precautions: Critical for Hip Pointer: Never stretch the trunk into contralateral side-flexion or massage directly over a fresh iliac crest hematoma, as this causes myositis ossificans (heterotopic bone formation inside the muscle). External cue: "Keep your ribs stacked straight above your pelvis—no side-bending—and gently tighten your side waist and outer hip against the wall." Internal cue: "Wake up the muscles above and below your hip bone with smooth, gentle tension."
clinicalNotes: Because the iliac crest is the shared bony anchor between the lateral abdominal muscles pulling upward and the gluteus medius/TFL pulling downward, gentle neutral-angle isometric co-contraction re-establishes tensile alignment across the healing periosteum without tearing fragile blood clots (PhysioWorks).

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction with Slight External Rotation & Extension against Wall (Posterior Glute Med Bias / TFL Unloader)
chineseName: 側臥 髖關節外展肌力強化 (臀中肌/臀小肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Fine-wire EMG studies show that standard side-lying hip abduction with the hip slightly flexed or internally rotated heavily recruits the TFL. Adding slight hip extension + external rotation mechanically disadvantages the TFL (an internal rotator/flexor) and maximally isolates the posterior gluteus medius, breaking the cycle of TFL overload (4 Tensor Fascia Latae Exercises; Performance Place TFL Guide).

secondaryMuscles: deep external rotators (minimizing TFL EMG activity)
jointActions: Selective Synergist Isolation (Reciprocal Inhibition / Unloading of TFL)

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your unaffected side with your back, buttocks, and shoulders flush against a wall.
execution.description: Fine-wire EMG studies show that standard side-lying hip abduction with the hip slightly flexed or internally rotated heavily recruits the TFL. Adding slight hip extension + external rotation mechanically disadvantages the TFL (an internal rotator/flexor) and maximally isolates the posterior gluteus medius, breaking the cycle of TFL overload (4 Tensor Fascia Latae Exercises; Performance Place TFL Guide).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on your unaffected side with your back, buttocks, and shoulders flush against a wall.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Slide the heel of the top (affected) leg backward until it touches the wall (putting the hip in 5–10° extension), then turn the top foot/toes slightly upward toward the ceiling by 10–15° (external hip rotation).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the heel lightly touching the wall behind you, lift the leg to 25–30° abduction over 2 seconds, hold 3 seconds at the top while feeling the work purely in the upper-back glute pocket, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Keep your heel grazing the wall behind you and turn your toes slightly toward the ceiling as you lift." Internal cue: "Feel the burn strictly in your back jeans pocket, leaving the front-side hip muscle completely quiet."
commonErrors: If you feel the front-side pocket of the hip (TFL) cramping or taking over, your leg has drifted forward away from the wall or rolled into internal rotation.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Clamshell with the pelvis braced vertically against the wall (which exhibits one of the highest gluteus medius-to-TFL EMG ratios).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Side-lying wall-slide abduction with a mini-band above the knees AND around the ankles.

precautions: If you feel the front-side pocket of the hip (TFL) cramping or taking over, your leg has drifted forward away from the wall or rolled into internal rotation. External cue: "Keep your heel grazing the wall behind you and turn your toes slightly toward the ceiling as you lift." Internal cue: "Feel the burn strictly in your back jeans pocket, leaving the front-side hip muscle completely quiet."
clinicalNotes: Fine-wire EMG studies show that standard side-lying hip abduction with the hip slightly flexed or internally rotated heavily recruits the TFL. Adding slight hip extension + external rotation mechanically disadvantages the TFL (an internal rotator/flexor) and maximally isolates the posterior gluteus medius, breaking the cycle of TFL overload (4 Tensor Fascia Latae Exercises; Performance Place TFL Guide).

name: Supine-to-Standing Multi-Angle Sartorius ("Hacky-Sack" FABER) Isometric & Cable Arc

description: The sartorius originates on the ASIS and inserts on the proximal medial tibia (pes anserinus), acting simultaneously to flex, abduct, and externally rotate the hip while flexing and internally rotating the knee. Direct diagonal loading along this exact vector remodels proximal ASIS or mid-belly sartorius strains.

primaryMuscles: Sartorius (the longest muscle in the human body
crossing the hip anteriorly and knee posteromedially)
jointActions: Diagonal Bi-Articular Isometric-to-Isotonic Conditioning

execution.startingPosition: Phase 1 (Isometric): Lie supine or sit tall; bring the affected leg into a partial "hacky-sack" or figure-4 motion (simultaneous hip flexion + abduction + external rotation + knee flexion), sliding the heel up along the opposite shin.
execution.description: The sartorius originates on the ASIS and inserts on the proximal medial tibia (pes anserinus), acting simultaneously to flex, abduct, and externally rotate the hip while flexing and internally rotating the knee. Direct diagonal loading along this exact vector remodels proximal ASIS or mid-belly sartorius strains.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Isometric): Lie supine or sit tall; bring the affected leg into a partial "hacky-sack" or figure-4 motion (simultaneous hip flexion + abduction + external rotation + knee flexion), sliding the heel up along the opposite shin.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Apply manual resistance with your hand against the medial calcaneus/ankle and lateral knee for 20–30 seconds at 40–60% effort.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Isotonic Cable/Band): Stand with a low cable strap or band attached to the ankle; draw the heel diagonally up and across the front of the opposite shin (inside-of-the-foot soccer volley motion) over 2 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Slide your heel smoothly up the front of your opposite shin as if passing a soccer ball with the inside of your foot." Internal cue: "Feel the diagonal strap muscle running from the front point of your hip down to your inner knee working smoothly."
commonErrors: Avoid lumbar flexion (tucking the lower back) to bring the foot higher; keep the pelvis level and upright.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine heel-slide up the opposite shin (supported on the treatment table) to reduce gravity torque on the ASIS origin.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing cable hacky-sack lift starting from a lengthened position (10° hip extension + adduction + internal rotation behind the stance leg).

precautions: Avoid lumbar flexion (tucking the lower back) to bring the foot higher; keep the pelvis level and upright. External cue: "Slide your heel smoothly up the front of your opposite shin as if passing a soccer ball with the inside of your foot." Internal cue: "Feel the diagonal strap muscle running from the front point of your hip down to your inner knee working smoothly."
clinicalNotes: The sartorius originates on the ASIS and inserts on the proximal medial tibia (pes anserinus), acting simultaneously to flex, abduct, and externally rotate the hip while flexing and internally rotating the knee. name: Seated / Standing Psoas March Above 90° Flexion (Unloading TFL & Sartorius Compensation)
chineseName: Seated / Standing Psoas March Above 90° Flexion (Unloading TFL & Sartorius Compensation)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: When the deep iliopsoas is weak, athletes recruit the superficial TFL and sartorius to flex the hip during sprinting and stair climbing, leading to chronic TFL tendinopathy or sartorius strain (Southgate Physio). Above 90° hip flexion, the TFL and rectus femoris are mechanically slackened (active insufficiency), forcing the psoas major to do the work and curing secondary TFL overactivity.

jointActions: Deep Synergist Isolation (Active Insufficiency of TFL & Rectus Femoris)

execution.startingPosition: Sit tall on the edge of a box or stand facing a wall with the affected foot resting on a 30–40 cm box so the hip starts at 90° flexion.
execution.description: When the deep iliopsoas is weak, athletes recruit the superficial TFL and sartorius to flex the hip during sprinting and stair climbing, leading to chronic TFL tendinopathy or sartorius strain (Southgate Physio). Above 90° hip flexion, the TFL and rectus femoris are mechanically slackened (active insufficiency), forcing the psoas major to do the work and curing secondary TFL overactivity.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit tall on the edge of a box or stand facing a wall with the affected foot resting on a 30–40 cm box so the hip starts at 90° flexion.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Loop a mini-band around both feet or place a light kettlebell on the forefoot.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Keeping the torso vertical and pelvis neutral (0° hip internal rotation or abduction), lift the knee 5–10 cm higher (to 100–110° hip flexion), hold isometrically for 5 seconds, and lower slowly back to the box.

coachingCues: "Keep your kneecap and toes pointing straight ahead like train tracks as you lift your knee above hip height." Internal cue: "Lift from deep inside your lower spine and front hip crease without the outer hip cramping."
commonErrors: Watch for the thigh drifting outward into abduction/internal rotation (TFL cheat) or the foot turning inward into FABER (sartorius cheat)—keep the femur tracking dead straight in the sagittal plane.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Supine 90–90 psoas march pressing the distal thigh into manual or band resistance at 95° flexion.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Free-standing single-leg kettlebell psoas march holding 95–100° hip flexion for 5 seconds while balancing on the extended contralateral leg.

precautions: Watch for the thigh drifting outward into abduction/internal rotation (TFL cheat) or the foot turning inward into FABER (sartorius cheat)—keep the femur tracking dead straight in the sagittal plane. External cue: "Keep your kneecap and toes pointing straight ahead like train tracks as you lift your knee above hip height." Internal cue: "Lift from deep inside your lower spine and front hip crease without the outer hip cramping."
clinicalNotes: When the deep iliopsoas is weak, athletes recruit the superficial TFL and sartorius to flex the hip during sprinting and stair climbing, leading to chronic TFL tendinopathy or sartorius strain (Southgate Physio). Above 90° hip flexion, the TFL and rectus femoris are mechanically slackened (active insufficiency), forcing the psoas major to do the work and curing secondary TFL overactivity.

execution.description: Tendons and bi-articular muscles require direct, progressive tensile loading along their anatomical lines of pull in late rehabilitation so they do not fail when exposed to high-speed diagonal forces on the field.

steps.title: 步驟 1

name: Lateral Step-Down & Hip-Hinge Monster Walk with Trunk-Lean Bias (Functional TFL-to-Glute Load Sharing)
chineseName: 下台階離心控制訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Teaches the athlete to decelerate single-leg vertical and frontal-plane loads using the large gluteal prime movers rather than hanging passively on the TFL/ITB complex (OrthoInfo Hip Conditioning).

jointActions: Closed-Chain Multi-Planar Eccentric Control & Load Redistribution

execution.startingPosition: Stand on the affected leg on a 15–20 cm box with a loop band around the distal thighs and dumbbells in hand.
execution.description: Teaches the athlete to decelerate single-leg vertical and frontal-plane loads using the large gluteal prime movers rather than hanging passively on the TFL/ITB complex (OrthoInfo Hip Conditioning).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand on the affected leg on a 15–20 cm box with a loop band around the distal thighs and dumbbells in hand.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge the hips backward to create a 20–25° forward trunk lean (which biomechanically shifts frontal-plane single-leg support torque toward the gluteus maximus and posterior gluteus medius so the TFL shares rather than monopolizes the load).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lower the opposite heel to tap the floor over 4 seconds while keeping the pelvis level and knee aligned over the 2nd toe, then drive back up over 2 seconds.

coachingCues: "Send your hips back slightly as you lower your opposite heel so your nose, knee, and toes stay stacked in one line." Internal cue: "Absorb the landing in your big back-pocket glute muscle."
commonErrors: Never descend with a vertical, arched-back torso and knee pushed far forward with internal rotation, which transfers peak load back onto the TFL and anterior knee.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce step height to 10 cm or perform a B-Stance (kickstand) Dumbbell RDL.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg drop-jump from a 15 cm box, sticking the landing in a 25° hip-hinged athletic posture for 3 seconds.

precautions: Never descend with a vertical, arched-back torso and knee pushed far forward with internal rotation, which transfers peak load back onto the TFL and anterior knee. External cue: "Send your hips back slightly as you lower your opposite heel so your nose, knee, and toes stay stacked in one line." Internal cue: "Absorb the landing in your big back-pocket glute muscle."
clinicalNotes: Teaches the athlete to decelerate single-leg vertical and frontal-plane loads using the large gluteal prime movers rather than hanging passively on the TFL/ITB complex (OrthoInfo Hip Conditioning).

description: Delivers heavy isometric mechanical tension to the iliopsoas and proximal rectus femoris tendons in a safe mid-range angle without compressing the iliopsoas bursa in deep (>100°) flexion or snapping the tendon in full extension.

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with a resistance band looped around both feet.
execution.description: Delivers heavy isometric mechanical tension to the iliopsoas and proximal rectus femoris tendons in a safe mid-range angle without compressing the iliopsoas bursa in deep (>100°) flexion or snapping the tendon in full extension.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with a resistance band looped around both feet.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep one knee bent at 90° (anchored foot) and extend the opposite leg slightly to a 45–60° hip angle (staying completely above any snapping threshold).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Gently flatten the lumbar spine into the mat, pull the affected knee up to 75–80° hip flexion against the band, and hold isometrically for 30–45 seconds before slowly returning to the starting angle.

coachingCues: "Keep your lower ribs gently pressed into the mat as you freeze your knee against the band's pull." Internal cue: "Feel a steady, deep muscular work in the front of your hip without any clicking or sharp pinching."
commonErrors: Do not allow the lower back to arch off the floor as the band pulls on the foot.

regressions.name: 退階方案

Internal cue: "Feel a steady, deep muscular work in the front of your hip without any clicking or sharp pinching."
clinicalNotes: Delivers heavy isometric mechanical tension to the iliopsoas and proximal rectus femoris tendons in a safe mid-range angle without compressing the iliopsoas bursa in deep (>100°) flexion or snapping the tendon in full extension.

name: Posterior-Pelvic-Tilt Eccentric Leg Lowering (Snap-Free Arc Control)
chineseName: Posterior-Pelvic-Tilt Eccentric Leg Lowering (Snap-Free Arc Control)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Internal snapping hip occurs when anterior pelvic tilt increases the prominence of the iliopectineal eminence while the psoas tendon translates medially (PMC4961351). Active posterior pelvic tilt rotates the pelvic brim out of the tendon's path, allowing gradually deeper snap-free extension week by week.

jointActions: Eccentric Motor Control & Lumbopelvic Dissociation

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with hips flexed to 90° and a blood-pressure cuff or folded towel under the lumbar spine.
execution.description: Internal snapping hip occurs when anterior pelvic tilt increases the prominence of the iliopectineal eminence while the psoas tendon translates medially (PMC4961351). Active posterior pelvic tilt rotates the pelvic brim out of the tendon's path, allowing gradually deeper snap-free extension week by week.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with hips flexed to 90° and a blood-pressure cuff or folded towel under the lumbar spine.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Engage the anterior core to maintain steady pressure on the towel (slight posterior pelvic tilt).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lower the affected heel toward the floor over 4 seconds while keeping the hip centered in neutral rotation (avoiding external rotation + abduction).

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Stop 5–10° before the angle where the hip normally snaps, pause 2 seconds, and return to 90°.

coachingCues: "Keep crushing the towel under your lower back and stop lowering your leg just above the spot where it wants to click." Internal cue: "Pull your belt buckle toward your sternum so your pelvis doesn't tip forward as your leg lengthens."
commonErrors: Golden Rule: Never push through an audible or palpable snap; every snap reinforces bursal irritation.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bend the knee to 90° (short-lever heel tap) to reduce the external flexion moment arm on the psoas and anterior core.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase the lowering arc by 5–10° each week as long as the movement remains 100% snap-free; progress to lowering off the edge of a treatment plinth into 10° hip extension.

precautions: Golden Rule: Never push through an audible or palpable snap; every snap reinforces bursal irritation. External cue: "Keep crushing the towel under your lower back and stop lowering your leg just above the spot where it wants to click." Internal cue: "Pull your belt buckle toward your sternum so your pelvis doesn't tip forward as your leg lengthens."
clinicalNotes: Internal snapping hip occurs when anterior pelvic tilt increases the prominence of the iliopectineal eminence while the psoas tendon translates medially (PMC4961351). Active posterior pelvic tilt rotates the pelvic brim out of the tendon's path, allowing gradually deeper snap-free extension week by week.

Strengthening the gluteus medius and posterior gluteus maximus controls pelvic drop and anchors the ITB smoothly over the trochanter.

primaryMuscles: superior/posterior gluteus maximus (which tenses the posterior ITB)
jointActions: Eccentric–Concentric Frontal & Transverse Plane Control

execution.startingPosition: Stand with the affected foot on a 10–15 cm step and the opposite leg hanging off the side, or lie on the unaffected side with the top leg aligned in 5° hip extension and neutral rotation.
execution.description: In External Snapping Hip (Coxa Saltans Externa), the thickened posterior iliotibial band or anterior border of the gluteus maximus snaps forward over the greater trochanter during flexion/adduction/internal rotation (Physiopedia). steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with the affected foot on a 10–15 cm step and the opposite leg hanging off the side, or lie on the unaffected side with the top leg aligned in 5° hip extension and neutral rotation.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: In standing: slowly lower the non-stance pelvis 3–4 cm over 4 seconds (controlled eccentric adduction without internal rotation collapse), then drive through the stance glute to level the pelvis.

steps.title: 步驟 3

progressions.rationale: Banded lateral step-down with an anti-internal-rotation band pulling the knee medially.

precautions: Avoid crossing the top leg below midline in side-lying if it triggers trochanteric snapping or bursal compression. Internal cue: "Use the upper back part of your glute to hold the side of your hip steady."
clinicalNotes: In External Snapping Hip (Coxa Saltans Externa), the thickened posterior iliotibial band or anterior border of the gluteus maximus snaps forward over the greater trochanter during flexion/adduction/internal rotation (Physiopedia). name: Seated & Standing Cable/Band Hip Flexor March above 90° (Active End-Range Control)
chineseName: Seated & Standing Cable/Band Hip Flexor March above 90° (Active End-Range Control)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Above 90° of hip flexion, the rectus femoris and TFL become mechanically disadvantaged due to active insufficiency, isolating the psoas major and iliacus. Training this zone eliminates compensatory TFL cramping and builds true psoas strength.

primaryMuscles: Psoas major (primary hip flexor above 90° hip flexion)
jointActions: Concentric–Eccentric End-Range Isotonic Strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Sit tall at the edge of a bench (or stand facing a wall/rack) with a mini-band around the feet or a kettlebell hooked over the forefoot.
execution.description: Above 90° of hip flexion, the rectus femoris and TFL become mechanically disadvantaged due to active insufficiency, isolating the psoas major and iliacus. Training this zone eliminates compensatory TFL cramping and builds true psoas strength.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Sit tall at the edge of a bench (or stand facing a wall/rack) with a mini-band around the feet or a kettlebell hooked over the forefoot.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping the torso completely vertical and ribs stacked over the pelvis, lift the knee from 85° up to 105–110° hip flexion (provided there is no FAI pinch), hold for 3 seconds at the top without leaning backward, and lower over 3 seconds.

coachingCues: "Stay tall as if your back is glued to a wall and lift your knee straight toward your shoulder." Internal cue: "Lift purely from the deep crease of the hip without tilting your waist backward."
commonErrors: Watch for trunk lean backward, pelvic tucking (lumbar flexion), or external rotation of the foot (sartorius cheat).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Limit top flexion angle to 85–90° if >95° flexion causes anterior acetabular pinching.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing unassisted kettlebell hip flexor lift with the stance leg fully extended (0° hip/knee extension) on a low step.

precautions: Watch for trunk lean backward, pelvic tucking (lumbar flexion), or external rotation of the foot (sartorius cheat). External cue: "Stay tall as if your back is glued to a wall and lift your knee straight toward your shoulder." Internal cue: "Lift purely from the deep crease of the hip without tilting your waist backward."
clinicalNotes: Above 90° of hip flexion, the rectus femoris and TFL become mechanically disadvantaged due to active insufficiency, isolating the psoas major and iliacus. Training this zone eliminates compensatory TFL cramping and builds true psoas strength.

name: Rear-Foot Elevated Split Squat (RFESS) with Upright Controlled Torso (Bi-Articular Lengthened Load)
chineseName: 分腿蹲 (跨步深蹲)
rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Simultaneous hip extension and knee flexion on the rear leg places the bi-articular rectus femoris (AIIS direct head and reflected acetabular head) under high tensile load in its lengthened position—essential for remodeling proximal musculotendinous scar tissue and preventing re-injury during kicking or sprinting.

primaryMuscles: Trail leg (target): Rectus femoris & iliopsoas under eccentric lengthened tension
jointActions: Eccentric–Concentric Closed-Chain Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR)

execution.startingPosition: Place the forefoot of the affected (rectus femoris / iliopsoas) leg on a low 25–35 cm bench behind you and step the front foot forward.
execution.description: Simultaneous hip extension and knee flexion on the rear leg places the bi-articular rectus femoris (AIIS direct head and reflected acetabular head) under high tensile load in its lengthened position—essential for remodeling proximal musculotendinous scar tissue and preventing re-injury during kicking or sprinting.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Place the forefoot of the affected (rectus femoris / iliopsoas) leg on a low 25–35 cm bench behind you and step the front foot forward.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Maintain a slight posterior pelvic tilt and upright torso.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower slowly over 4 seconds until the trail knee hovers 3–5 cm above the floor, creating a controlled eccentric stretch-load across the trail-leg hip flexors and rectus femoris, then push through both the rear forefoot and front leg to return to the top.

coachingCues: "Keep your belt buckle tucked under and lower your back knee straight toward the floor." Internal cue: "Press the top of your back foot gently into the bench as you rise so the front of your rear thigh works actively."
commonErrors: Avoid hyperextending the lumbar spine as the rear knee drops—if the lower back arches, the stretch is absorbed by the spine rather than the hip flexor.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Standard floor Split Squat (both feet on the floor, lessening rear knee flexion angle) to reduce bi-articular rectus femoris strain.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Front-foot + rear-foot elevated split squat with a cable or band pulling the rear thigh backward, or driving the rear foot actively down into the pad (isometric rectus femoris contraction at bottom stretch).

precautions: Avoid hyperextending the lumbar spine as the rear knee drops—if the lower back arches, the stretch is absorbed by the spine rather than the hip flexor. External cue: "Keep your belt buckle tucked under and lower your back knee straight toward the floor." Internal cue: "Press the top of your back foot gently into the bench as you rise so the front of your rear thigh works actively."
clinicalNotes: Simultaneous hip extension and knee flexion on the rear leg places the bi-articular rectus femoris (AIIS direct head and reflected acetabular head) under high tensile load in its lengthened position—essential for remodeling proximal musculotendinous scar tissue and preventing re-injury during kicking or sprinting.
