execution.description: The Reverse Nordic is the anterior-chain counterpart to the Nordic hamstring curl: it selectively increases rectus femoris fascicle length and eccentric peak torque at long muscle lengths, directly addressing the mechanism of kicking and sprint-deceleration rectus femoris tears.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Kneel tall on a padded mat with knees hip-width apart, ankles plantarflexed (or toes tucked), and a resistance band anchored in front of you at chest height for assistance.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lock the hips in 0° neutral extension by squeezing the glutes and bracing the core so the thighs, pelvis, and trunk form one rigid plank.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lean backward from the knees over 4 seconds as far as tolerable without breaking at the hips or overarching the lumbar spine, pause 1 second, and pull through the quads to return upright.

coachingCues: "Keep a straight steel rod from your knees through your hips to your shoulders as you hinge backward from the knee joints only." Internal cue: "Squeeze your glutes throughout the lean so the front of your thighs controls the descent."
commonErrors: Do not allow the hips to flex ("sitting back onto the heels") on the way up, which unloads the rectus femoris.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Short-arc Reverse Nordic (leaning back only 20–25°) with heavy band assistance anchored in front, or prone cable/band knee extension with the hip in 0° extension.

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Do not allow the hips to flex ("sitting back onto the heels") on the way up, which unloads the rectus femoris. Internal cue: "Squeeze your glutes throughout the lean so the front of your thighs controls the descent."
clinicalNotes: The Reverse Nordic is the anterior-chain counterpart to the Nordic hamstring curl: it selectively increases rectus femoris fascicle length and eccentric peak torque at long muscle lengths, directly addressing the mechanism of kicking and sprint-deceleration rectus femoris tears.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand facing away from a low cable pulley or band anchor with an ankle strap attached to the affected leg, holding a rack in front for stability.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Begin with the working leg extended 10–15° behind the body (lengthened hip extension while keeping the pelvis tucked) and drive the knee forward and upward to 90° hip flexion over 2 seconds.

steps.title: 步驟 3

regressions.name: 退階方案

execution.startingPosition: Stand at a 45° forward lean with hands bracing against a wall and a light-to-medium resistance band looped around both feet (or ankles tethered to a rear anchor).
execution.description: Restores the stretch-shortening cycle (SSC) and rapid reflexive stiffness of the iliopsoas and rectus femoris required for maximal sprint acceleration (toe-off to knee drive) and soccer ball striking.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand at a 45° forward lean with hands bracing against a wall and a light-to-medium resistance band looped around both feet (or ankles tethered to a rear anchor).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Start with one knee driven up to 90° hip flexion (dorsiflexed ankle) and the stance leg extended in triple extension.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: On command, rapidly switch the legs in mid-air ("A-Switch") with maximal piston-like velocity, sticking the opposite knee at 90° hip flexion and neutral pelvis for 2 seconds without lumbar arch or hip snap.

coachingCues: "Punch your knee toward the wall and drive your opposite foot straight through the floor like a piston." Internal cue: "Snap the thigh up fast from a rigid core while keeping your ribs locked down."

regressions.name: 退階方案

progressions.name: 進階方案

clinicalNotes: Restores the stretch-shortening cycle (SSC) and rapid reflexive stiffness of the iliopsoas and rectus femoris required for maximal sprint acceleration (toe-off to knee drive) and soccer ball striking.

description: Hip abduction and neutral-to-slight internal rotation physically pull the lesser trochanter laterally and anteriorly away from the ischial tuberosity, maximally widening the ischiofemoral space while building gluteus medius force capacity (PMC12019084).

primaryMuscles: gluteus minimus — while unloading the compressed quadratus femoris
jointActions: Decompressive Isometric (Symptom Modulation & Abductor Recruitment)

execution.startingPosition: Lie on the unaffected side with two firm pillows stacked between the knees so the top (affected) leg rests in at least 10–15° of hip abduction, 0° neutral extension (do NOT push into hyperextension), and 0° neutral rotation (kneecap and toes pointing straight ahead, or 5° internal rotation—never external rotation).
execution.description: Hip abduction and neutral-to-slight internal rotation physically pull the lesser trochanter laterally and anteriorly away from the ischial tuberosity, maximally widening the ischiofemoral space while building gluteus medius force capacity (PMC12019084).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie on the unaffected side with two firm pillows stacked between the knees so the top (affected) leg rests in at least 10–15° of hip abduction, 0° neutral extension (do NOT push into hyperextension), and 0° neutral rotation (kneecap and toes pointing straight ahead, or 5° internal rotation—never external rotation).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Lift the top leg 5 cm above the pillows to ~25° abduction and hold isometrically for 30–45 seconds against gravity or manual resistance at the distal thigh.

coachingCues: "Keep your kneecap and toes pointing straight forward—even slightly downward—and never let your top knee sink below hip height." Internal cue: "Feel the burn high on the side of your hip, with deep space and relief in the lower buttock."

progressions.name: 進階方案

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Tightness in the iliopsoas and rectus femoris forces patients to compensate during walking with pelvic rotation and abnormal lumbar/hip coupling. Lengthening the anterior hip in a widened (abducted + slightly internally rotated) posture restores stride mechanics without impinging the posterior ischiofemoral space (World J Clin Cases).

jointActions: Active Mobility & Reciprocal Inhibition

execution.startingPosition: Kneel on a pad with the affected hip as the rear kneeling leg, placing the rear knee slightly wider than hip-width (10° abduction) and the lower leg angled slightly outward (creating 5–10° of internal hip rotation to keep the lesser trochanter clear of the ischium).
execution.description: Tightness in the iliopsoas and rectus femoris forces patients to compensate during walking with pelvic rotation and abnormal lumbar/hip coupling. Lengthening the anterior hip in a widened (abducted + slightly internally rotated) posture restores stride mechanics without impinging the posterior ischiofemoral space (World J Clin Cases).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Kneel on a pad with the affected hip as the rear kneeling leg, placing the rear knee slightly wider than hip-width (10° abduction) and the lower leg angled slightly outward (creating 5–10° of internal hip rotation to keep the lesser trochanter clear of the ischium).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Strongly tuck the tailbone under (posterior pelvic tilt) by squeezing the rear glute and bracing the lower abs—do NOT lunge far forward into deep hip hyperextension.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold for 30 seconds while feeling a stretch solely in the front of the hip/thigh.

coachingCues: "Widen your back knee slightly, point your back foot slightly outward, and tuck your belt buckle up toward your ribs." Internal cue: "Feel the stretch exclusively down the front of the thigh, never a pinch in the back pocket."
commonErrors: Never allow a deep buttock pinch during the stretch—if felt in the back of the hip, widen the rear knee further outward and reduce forward translation.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Standing staggered-stance posterior pelvic tilt with a short stride and wide foot placement.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Raise the ipsilateral arm overhead and side-bend gently away from the kneeling side (while keeping the knee wide so the hip does not adduct).

precautions: Never allow a deep buttock pinch during the stretch—if felt in the back of the hip, widen the rear knee further outward and reduce forward translation. External cue: "Widen your back knee slightly, point your back foot slightly outward, and tuck your belt buckle up toward your ribs." Internal cue: "Feel the stretch exclusively down the front of the thigh, never a pinch in the back pocket."
clinicalNotes: Tightness in the iliopsoas and rectus femoris forces patients to compensate during walking with pelvic rotation and abnormal lumbar/hip coupling. description: Standard single-leg wall presses often place the stance leg too close to the wall, forcing the stance hip into adduction and compressing the quadratus femoris. Widening the base by 15–20 cm loads the stance gluteus medius at high intensity while maintaining an open ischiofemoral corridor.

jointActions: Closed-Chain Multi-Joint Isometric

execution.startingPosition: Stand sideways next to a wall with the affected leg as the outside (stance) leg, positioned 15–20 cm away from the wall so the stance hip rests in 10° of abduction (never adducted beneath the torso) and 15° knee flexion.
execution.description: Standard single-leg wall presses often place the stance leg too close to the wall, forcing the stance hip into adduction and compressing the quadratus femoris. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand sideways next to a wall with the affected leg as the outside (stance) leg, positioned 15–20 cm away from the wall so the stance hip rests in 10° of abduction (never adducted beneath the torso) and 15° knee flexion.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Flex the inside (unaffected) knee to 60° with a foam roller between the lateral knee and the wall.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Press the inside knee into the wall for 20–30 seconds, forcing the stance-leg abductors to fire intensely while keeping the stance hip in a decompressed, slightly abducted alignment.

precautions: Do not let the stance pelvis drift laterally toward the outside (hip hanging/adduction) or let the stance foot turn outward into external rotation. execution.description: Because external rotation brings the lesser trochanter posteriorly into direct contact with the ischial tuberosity, training controlled internal/neutral rotation strength via the anterior gluteus medius and minimus actively keeps the lesser trochanter clear during stance phase (PMC12019084).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Start in quadruped or prone with the knees placed slightly wider than hip-width (15° hip abduction).

name: Standing Step Pelvic Drop-to-Hike (Stopping at Neutral 0° Adduction — Anti-Trendelenburg)

rehabPhase: Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Classic pelvic drops let the pelvis sag below horizontal into hip adduction, which compresses the ischiofemoral space in IFI patients. jointActions: Eccentric–Concentric Frontal-Plane Closed-Chain Strengthening

execution.startingPosition: Stand with the affected foot on a 10 cm step, toes pointing straight ahead (0° external rotation) and knee unlocked at 10° flexion.
execution.description: Classic pelvic drops let the pelvis sag below horizontal into hip adduction, which compresses the ischiofemoral space in IFI patients. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand with the affected foot on a 10 cm step, toes pointing straight ahead (0° external rotation) and knee unlocked at 10° flexion.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Start with the non-stance pelvis slightly elevated (5° hip abduction on the stance hip).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Slowly lower the non-stance pelvis over 4 seconds only to horizontal neutral (0° pelvic drop—do NOT drop below level into adduction), hold at neutral for 2 seconds, and drive through the stance lateral hip to hike the opposite pelvis back up by 5°.

coachingCues: "Lower your free foot until your belt line is perfectly flat—treat flat level as a brick wall you never sink past—then hike it slightly higher." Internal cue: "Press your standing heel through the step to lift the pelvis from the outer hip."

progressions.name: 進階方案

precautions: Critical modification for IFI: Never let the free hip sag below the level of the standing hip. External cue: "Lower your free foot until your belt line is perfectly flat—treat flat level as a brick wall you never sink past—then hike it slightly higher." Internal cue: "Press your standing heel through the step to lift the pelvis from the outer hip."
clinicalNotes: Classic pelvic drops let the pelvis sag below horizontal into hip adduction, which compresses the ischiofemoral space in IFI patients. execution.startingPosition: Stand alongside a 15–20 cm box with the affected foot placed on the box, slightly wider than directly beneath the hip (5–10° abduction), and a loop band anchored laterally pulling the stance knee inward.
execution.description: Builds high eccentric single-leg capacity in the frontal plane to prevent dynamic hip adduction (medial femoral collapse and pelvic drop) during stair negotiation, cutting, and running stance phase.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand alongside a 15–20 cm box with the affected foot placed on the box, slightly wider than directly beneath the hip (5–10° abduction), and a loop band anchored laterally pulling the stance knee inward.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hinge the trunk forward 20°, press the stance knee slightly outward against the band so it tracks over the 2nd–3rd toe (without externally rotating the foot), and drive up to full single-leg stance.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Lower the non-stance heel to the floor over 4 seconds while keeping the pelvis level.

coachingCues: "Keep your belt line horizontal and guide your kneecap straight over your middle toes as your opposite heel kisses the floor." Internal cue: "Push the box away through your whole foot using the side and back of your hip."
commonErrors: Do not let the stance knee dive inward inside the big toe or the opposite pelvis drop during the final 10 cm of descent.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce box height to 10 cm or perform a lateral mini-squat weight shift on the floor.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Increase box height to 25 cm or add a reactive catch with a medicine ball at the bottom of the step-down tap.

precautions: Do not let the stance knee dive inward inside the big toe or the opposite pelvis drop during the final 10 cm of descent. External cue: "Keep your belt line horizontal and guide your kneecap straight over your middle toes as your opposite heel kisses the floor." Internal cue: "Push the box away through your whole foot using the side and back of your hip."

execution.description: Directly reverses the Long-Stride Walking (LSW) impingement mechanism: increasing cadence by 7.5–10% reduces peak terminal hip extension by ~3–5° and reduces peak hip adduction angle during mid-to-late stance by ~2–4°, keeping the ischiofemoral space open across thousands of gait cycles (PMC12019084).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Using a smartphone or watch metronome during brisk walking or treadmill running, increase baseline step rate (cadence) by +5% to +10% (e.g., from 160 to 172 steps/min for running, or 115 to 125 steps/min for brisk walking) while maintaining the same speed.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Concurrently cue a 2–3 cm wider step width (feet landing on either side of a center line on the treadmill rather than crossing over midline) and foot strike closer to the center of mass.

coachingCues: "Match the faster metronome beat with quicker, lighter steps—land with your feet on two separate ski tracks and push off quickly behind you." Internal cue: "Keep your hips tall and level at push-off instead of letting your leg trail far behind your body."
commonErrors: Avoid running with a duck-footed (externally rotated) toe-out posture or scissoring feet across a single line.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Brisk flat walking at +10% cadence with visual mirror or floor-line feedback to eliminate cross-over gait.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Fade metronome audio feedback (5 min on / 5 min off) and progress to outdoor hills and tempo running while maintaining compact stride length behind the pelvis.

precautions: Avoid running with a duck-footed (externally rotated) toe-out posture or scissoring feet across a single line. External cue: "Match the faster metronome beat with quicker, lighter steps—land with your feet on two separate ski tracks and push off quickly behind you." clinicalNotes: Directly reverses the Long-Stride Walking (LSW) impingement mechanism: increasing cadence by 7.5–10% reduces peak terminal hip extension by ~3–5° and reduces peak hip adduction angle during mid-to-late stance by ~2–4°, keeping the ischiofemoral space open across thousands of gait cycles (PMC12019084).

name: Constructive Rest & Happy-Baby Diaphragmatic "Pelvic Drop" (Alcock's Canal & Levator Ani Down-Training)
chineseName: Constructive Rest & Happy-Baby Diaphragmatic "Pelvic Drop" (Alcock's Canal & Levator Ani Down-Training)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: During normal respiration, downward excursion of the diaphragm on inhalation increases intra-abdominal pressure smoothly to eccentrically lengthen the pelvic floor and obturator internus fascia. Athletes with Pudendal Neuralgia, Obturator Internus Syndrome, or Coccygodynia exhibit chronic resting hypertonicity ("pelvic gripping") that strangles Alcock's canal; down-training restores fascial slack and microvascular perfusion (Dr. Bri's Vibrant Pelvic Health).

jointActions: Neuromuscular Down-Training & Respiratory-Pelvic Piston Restoration

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with lower legs resting comfortably on a chair/ottoman or in a gentle, supported Happy Baby / Deep Squat on the Back position (holding behind the thighs—never pulling into a sharp groin pinch) with the sacrum and tailbone heavy on the mat.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with lower legs resting comfortably on a chair/ottoman or in a gentle, supported Happy Baby / Deep Squat on the Back position (holding behind the thighs—never pulling into a sharp groin pinch) with the sacrum and tailbone heavy on the mat.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Place one hand on the lower ribs and one on the lower belly.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Inhale slowly for 4 seconds through the nose, expanding the lower ribcage 360° while visualizing the two sitting bones (ischial tuberosities) widening apart and the perineum/tailbone gently dropping and lengthening downward ("Reverse Kegel").

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Exhale passively for 6 seconds without clenching or lifting the pelvic floor.

coachingCues: "As you breathe in into your side ribs, imagine your two sitting bones gently melting wider apart on the mat."Internal cue: "Let your tailbone and deep hip muscles drop heavy and completely unclench."
commonErrors: Critical: Do NOT forcefully bear down (Valsalva push like straining on a toilet) during the Reverse Kegel—allow the breath pressure alone to gently blossom and soften the pelvic outlet.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Side-lying fetal position with a thick pillow between the knees and ankles if supine Happy Baby places too much tension on the pudendal nerve.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform the 360° inhale pelvic drop in quadruped (Child's Pose / Puppy Pose with knees comfortably apart and tailbone untucked).

precautions: Critical: Do NOT forcefully bear down (Valsalva push like straining on a toilet) during the Reverse Kegel—allow the breath pressure alone to gently blossom and soften the pelvic outlet.External cue: "As you breathe in into your side ribs, imagine your two sitting bones gently melting wider apart on the mat."Internal cue: "Let your tailbone and deep hip muscles drop heavy and completely unclench."

name: Supine Hook-Lying Knee-Inward Drop ("Reverse Clam" — Passive/Active Obturator Internus Lengthening)
chineseName: Supine Hook-Lying Knee-Inward Drop ("Reverse Clam" — Passive/Active Obturator Internus Lengthening)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: At <60–70° of hip flexion, the obturator internus is a primary external rotator of the hip; therefore, gently rotating the hip into internal rotation directly lengthens the contracted obturator internus muscle belly and decompresses its fascial investment around Alcock's canal, while anterior hip internal rotators reciprocally inhibit OI spasm (Journal of Parker University OI Contracture; How to Release Your Obturator Internus).

primaryMuscles: superior/inferior gemelli (lengthening via internal hip rotation)
secondaryMuscles: gluteus minimus & TFL (gentle internal rotator agonists creating reciprocal inhibition)
jointActions: Reciprocal Inhibition & Myofascial Lengthening of the Obturator Internus

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70° and feet placed wider than shoulder-width apart on the mat.
execution.description: At <60–70° of hip flexion, the obturator internus is a primary external rotator of the hip; therefore, gently rotating the hip into internal rotation directly lengthens the contracted obturator internus muscle belly and decompresses its fascial investment around Alcock's canal, while anterior hip internal rotators reciprocally inhibit OI spasm (Journal of Parker University OI Contracture; How to Release Your Obturator Internus).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent to 60–70° and feet placed wider than shoulder-width apart on the mat.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping the pelvis completely flat on the floor, slowly allow the affected knee to drop inward toward the midline (hip internal rotation) over 4 seconds while inhaling to lengthen the deep posterior hip and pelvic wall.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold the gentle end-range internal rotation stretch for 5–10 seconds (resting the inner knee against a yoga block or the opposite knee for support), then return to neutral on the exhale.

coachingCues: "Walk your feet wide on the mat and let your knee gently knock inward toward a yoga block as you breathe in."Internal cue: "Feel the deep muscle next to your sitting bone lengthen and let go."
commonErrors: Never force internal rotation past a bony block or anterior groin pinch.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce knee flexion to 30–40° (legs more extended) and gently roll the whole thigh inward if 70° flexion + internal rotation causes anterior hip impingement.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Side-lying "Reverse Clamshell" (lying on the unaffected side with a pillow between the knees, keeping the knees together and lifting the top ankle upward into internal rotation for 5 seconds).

precautions: Never force internal rotation past a bony block or anterior groin pinch.External cue: "Walk your feet wide on the mat and let your knee gently knock inward toward a yoga block as you breathe in."Internal cue: "Feel the deep muscle next to your sitting bone lengthen and let go."

name: Side-Lying & Quadruped Obturator / Pudendal Neurodynamic Slider (S2–S4 & L2–L4 Canal Decompression)
chineseName: Side-Lying & Quadruped Obturator / Pudendal Neurodynamic Slider (S2–S4 & L2–L4 Canal Decompression)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: The pudendal nerve passes between the piriformis and coccygeus, wraps around the ischial spine (between the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments), and enters Alcock's canal along the obturator internus (PHRC). Gentle reciprocal spinal-and-pelvic sliding restores free microvascular glide without compressing the nerve in deep >90° hip flexion.

primaryMuscles: Neural targets: Pudendal nerve (S2–S4) & Obturator nerve (L2–L4)
jointActions: Neurodynamic Slider (Perineural Gliding across Alcock's Canal & Sacrospinous/Sacrotuberous Interface)

execution.startingPosition: Start in quadruped on hands and knees with a wide knee base.
execution.description: The pudendal nerve passes between the piriformis and coccygeus, wraps around the ischial spine (between the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments), and enters Alcock's canal along the obturator internus (PHRC). Gentle reciprocal spinal-and-pelvic sliding restores free microvascular glide without compressing the nerve in deep >90° hip flexion.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Start in quadruped on hands and knees with a wide knee base.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Phase 1 (Caudal/Distal Slide): Slowly rock the hips halfway back toward the heels while gently untucking the tailbone (slight anterior pelvic tilt to widen the ischial tuberosities) AND lifting the chin/eyes slightly forward (slackening the spinal cord cranially).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Phase 2 (Cranial/Proximal Slide): Rock the hips forward back over the knees while gently tucking the tailbone and nodding the chin toward the chest.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Perform 10–12 smooth, small-amplitude cycles.

coachingCues: "Rock your hips back just halfway while keeping your sitting bones wide, moving your head and pelvis together like a smooth wave."Internal cue: "Keep the movement effortless and completely free of any saddle-area tingling."
commonErrors: Vital for Pudendal Neuralgia: Do not rock all the way back onto the heels (>110° hip flexion) during acute pudendal neuralgia, as extreme hip flexion stretches the pudendal nerve over the sacrospinous ligament.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Limit quadruped rock-back to only 10–15 cm of excursion if deeper hip flexion irritates Alcock's canal.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Combine with side-lying straight-leg abduction/extension to adduction/flexion nerve gliding (How to Floss the Obturator Nerve for Pelvic Floor Dysfunction).

precautions: Vital for Pudendal Neuralgia: Do not rock all the way back onto the heels (>110° hip flexion) during acute pudendal neuralgia, as extreme hip flexion stretches the pudendal nerve over the sacrospinous ligament.External cue: "Rock your hips back just halfway while keeping your sitting bones wide, moving your head and pelvis together like a smooth wave."Internal cue: "Keep the movement effortless and completely free of any saddle-area tingling."
clinicalNotes: The pudendal nerve passes between the piriformis and coccygeus, wraps around the ischial spine (between the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments), and enters Alcock's canal along the obturator internus (PHRC). description: Research demonstrates that when the large superficial gluteus maximus and gluteus medius are weak, the brain recruits the tiny obturator internus and pelvic floor as substitute hip stabilizers (Herman & Wallace Hip–Pelvic Floor Review). Training the superficial glutes to generate hip extension torque without "butt-wink clenching" relieves chronic OI overload.

secondaryMuscles: hamstrings (while keeping obturator internus & levator ani relaxed)

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with knees bent to 90° and feet hip-width apart pointing straight ahead (0° external rotation—do NOT use a heavy abduction band around the knees early on if it triggers deep obturator internus/piriformis spasm).
execution.description: Research demonstrates that when the large superficial gluteus maximus and gluteus medius are weak, the brain recruits the tiny obturator internus and pelvic floor as substitute hip stabilizers (Herman & Wallace Hip–Pelvic Floor Review). Training the superficial glutes to generate hip extension torque without "butt-wink clenching" relieves chronic OI overload.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent to 90° and feet hip-width apart pointing straight ahead (0° external rotation—do NOT use a heavy abduction band around the knees early on if it triggers deep obturator internus/piriformis spasm).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Inhale to soften the pelvic floor; on a gentle pursed-lip exhale, drive straight down through both heels to lift the hips to a neutral bridge without clenching the sphincter or deep tailbone muscles.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 3 seconds, then lower over 3 seconds while inhaling to let the sitting bones widen.

coachingCues: "Push the floor downward through your heels to float your hips—do not pinch your tailbone inward at the top."Internal cue: "Let the big outer glute muscles do the heavy lifting while your tailbone and pelvic floor stay relaxed."
commonErrors: Avoid squeezing the buttocks together like "cracking a walnut" at the top of the bridge, which pulls on the coccyx (gluteus maximus coccygeal fibers) and spasms the obturator internus.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral heel-drive isometric bridge hover (lifting hips only 5 cm off the mat) if full extension causes coccygeal or perineal pulling.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: B-Stance (kickstand) Glute Bridge → Single-Leg Glute Bridge with feet straight ahead.

precautions: Avoid squeezing the buttocks together like "cracking a walnut" at the top of the bridge, which pulls on the coccyx (gluteus maximus coccygeal fibers) and spasms the obturator internus.External cue: "Push the floor downward through your heels to float your hips—do not pinch your tailbone inward at the top."Internal cue: "Let the big outer glute muscles do the heavy lifting while your tailbone and pelvic floor stay relaxed."

description: Combines closed-chain hip flexion with internal rotation and diaphragmatic inhalation to train the obturator internus and posterior pelvic floor to eccentrically yield and widen under load—a prerequisite for pain-free squatting, sitting, and running shock absorption (Hinge Health Obturator Internus Guide).

jointActions: Eccentric Closed-Chain Myofascial Lengthening

execution.startingPosition: Assume a quadruped position with knees hip-width apart and walk both lower legs/feet outward by 15–20° so both hips are positioned in gentle internal rotation.
execution.description: Combines closed-chain hip flexion with internal rotation and diaphragmatic inhalation to train the obturator internus and posterior pelvic floor to eccentrically yield and widen under load—a prerequisite for pain-free squatting, sitting, and running shock absorption (Hinge Health Obturator Internus Guide).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Assume a quadruped position with knees hip-width apart and walk both lower legs/feet outward by 15–20° so both hips are positioned in gentle internal rotation.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keeping the lumbar spine in neutral (do not round the lower back), inhale slowly for 4 seconds as you shift your hips backward toward your heels—actively allowing the sitting bones to spread apart and the obturator internus/posterior pelvic floor to lengthen eccentrically.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Pause 2 seconds at the comfortable limit, then exhale and pull forward through the hips to return to the start.

coachingCues: "Angle your shins slightly outward, keep a tiny natural curve in your lower back, and let your sitting bones flare wide like headlights as you sit back."Internal cue: "Inhale down into your back pockets to stretch the deep hip wall open."

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce the outward shin angle to neutral (0° rotation) if internal rotation is still mildly restricted.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Single-leg biased quadruped rock-back (shifting 70% of weight onto the affected hip while keeping the shin angled slightly outward).

precautions: Do not tuck the tailbone under (posterior pelvic tilt) as you rock back—tucking narrows the pelvic outlet and shortens the coccygeus/levator ani.External cue: "Angle your shins slightly outward, keep a tiny natural curve in your lower back, and let your sitting bones flare wide like headlights as you sit back."Internal cue: "Inhale down into your back pockets to stretch the deep hip wall open."

jointActions: Eccentric-Biased Isotonic Tendon & Muscle Remodeling

execution.startingPosition: Once resting spasm has resolved, directly restore the obturator internus's eccentric load capacity so it no longer fatigues into trigger-point contracture: Sit on a high bench (or stand on the unaffected leg) with a cable or resistance band attached to the affected ankle, pulling the lower leg outward (creating an internal hip rotation torque).
execution.description: A weak, deconditioned obturator internus develops myofascial trigger points whenever it is exposed to eccentric internal rotation torques during single-leg stance (Journal of Parker University). Eccentric training from neutral into internal rotation increases sarcomere length and tensile resilience without compressing Alcock's canal in shortened external rotation.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Once resting spasm has resolved, directly restore the obturator internus's eccentric load capacity so it no longer fatigues into trigger-point contracture: Sit on a high bench (or stand on the unaffected leg) with a cable or resistance band attached to the affected ankle, pulling the lower leg outward (creating an internal hip rotation torque).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Start in neutral rotation and slowly allow the band to pull the foot outward into 15–20° of hip internal rotation over 4 full seconds (lengthening the obturator internus under eccentric control), pause 1 second, and smoothly pull the foot back to neutral (0°—do not push into hard end-range external rotation) over 2 seconds.

coachingCues: "Let the band slowly draw your foot outward for four seconds to lengthen the deep hip muscle, then bring your shin right back to vertical neutral."Internal cue: "Control the lengthening phase smoothly without clenching your pelvic floor."
commonErrors: Critical modification: Stop the concentric return at 0° neutral rotation—do not pull all the way into full shortened external rotation, where the obturator internus can cramp and pinch Alcock's canal.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Submaximal isometric holds at 10° hip internal rotation (pressing the medial ankle gently against a band for 20 seconds).

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Standing Single-Leg Hip Airplane from 0° neutral into 15° controlled pelvic closure (closed-chain eccentric internal rotation) and back to neutral.

precautions: Critical modification: Stop the concentric return at 0° neutral rotation—do not pull all the way into full shortened external rotation, where the obturator internus can cramp and pinch Alcock's canal.External cue: "Let the band slowly draw your foot outward for four seconds to lengthen the deep hip muscle, then bring your shin right back to vertical neutral."Internal cue: "Control the lengthening phase smoothly without clenching your pelvic floor."
clinicalNotes: A weak, deconditioned obturator internus develops myofascial trigger points whenever it is exposed to eccentric internal rotation torques during single-leg stance (Journal of Parker University). Eccentric training from neutral into internal rotation increases sarcomere length and tensile resilience without compressing Alcock's canal in shortened external rotation.

steps.instruction: On the 4-second descent/hinge: Inhale through the nose and consciously allow the sitting bones to widen and the pelvic floor to lengthen eccentrically.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: On the 2-second ascent: Exhale smoothly through pursed lips (never holding your breath in a Valsalva maneuver) while driving through the mid-foot to stand tall, stopping at 0° neutral extension without butt-clenching.

coachingCues: "Breathe in and spread your sitting bones apart as you sit back toward the box; blow air out smoothly as you push the floor away to stand."Internal cue: "Let your pelvic floor act like a flexible trampoline that stretches on the way down and rebounds naturally on the way up."
commonErrors: Never perform a heavy Valsalva breath-hold or tuck the tailbone aggressively at lockout.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Higher box height (50 cm, ~60° hip flexion) with bodyweight only.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Staggered B-Stance RDL and Split Squat with the same inhale-widen / exhale-rise breathing cadence.

precautions: Never perform a heavy Valsalva breath-hold or tuck the tailbone aggressively at lockout.External cue: "Breathe in and spread your sitting bones apart as you sit back toward the box; blow air out smoothly as you push the floor away to stand."Internal cue: "Let your pelvic floor act like a flexible trampoline that stretches on the way down and rebounds naturally on the way up."
clinicalNotes: Retrains the automatic eccentric-on-descent / concentric-on-ascent coordination between the hip prime movers and the pelvic diaphragm under heavy external load, ensuring the athlete can lift and absorb ground reaction forces without reflex pelvic floor spasm (Foundational Concepts).

description: Prolonged seated cycling on a narrow saddle reduces perineal/pudendal oxygen tension by up to 70–80%, while repetitive >95° hip flexion at top dead center compresses the pudendal nerve inside Alcock's canal (PHRC). Biomechanical bike fitting plus periodic standing intervals and gluteal shock absorption allow safe return to endurance training.

jointActions: Sport-Specific Biomechanical Return-to-Sport (RTS) Conditioning

execution.startingPosition: For Cyclists & Rowers (Alcock's Canal / Coccygodynia RTS): Fit a wide ischial-supported, center-cut-out (or split-nose) saddle tilted 1–2° downward with raised handlebars to reduce anterior perineal compression and hip flexion angle (<90° at top dead center)

Biomechanical bike fitting plus periodic standing intervals and gluteal shock absorption allow safe return to endurance training.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: For Cyclists & Rowers (Alcock's Canal / Coccygodynia RTS): Fit a wide ischial-supported, center-cut-out (or split-nose) saddle tilted 1–2° downward with raised handlebars to reduce anterior perineal compression and hip flexion angle (<90° at top dead center).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Start with 20–30 min rides incorporating a mandatory 30-second out-of-the-saddle standing pedal interval every 5 minutes to restore pudendal blood flow.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: For Runners: Execute an alternate-day walk-to-run progression at +5–7.5% cadence with a gentle forward trunk lean from the ankles (avoiding stiff upright impact or gluteal clenching).

coachingCues: "Support your weight on your bony sitting bones—never on the soft tissue in front—and stand up on the pedals for 30 seconds every five minutes."Internal cue: "Power the pedals from your big glutes and quads while keeping your pelvic floor relaxed."
commonErrors: Immediate stop rule: Numbness in the saddle/perineal region during cycling is never normal—if any numbness occurs, stand up off the saddle immediately and adjust saddle width/cut-out/tilt.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Elliptical trainer or standing indoor bike drills if seated saddle contact still provokes >1/10 discomfort.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Gradually increase ride/run duration by 10–15% per week and introduce out-of-saddle hill climbs and sprint intervals.

name: Supine long-lever isometric bridge hold (Stage 1 — 0° hip flexion analgesia)
chineseName: Supine long-lever isometric bridge hold (Stage 1 — 0° hip flexion analgesia)
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Forms Stage 1 of the Goom & Malliaras (2016 JOSPT) PHT protocol. Delivers high tensile mechanotransduction to the proximal hamstring tendon and induces immediate exercise-induced hypoalgesia (reducing sitting pain!) without compressing the inflamed enthesis against the ischial tuberosity.

jointActions: Closed chain; heavy isometric at 0° hip angle; pure tension with zero ischial compression

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with your heels resting on the floor (or on a low 6-inch step) with your knees bent at a long-lever 30°–45° angle
execution.description: Forms Stage 1 of the Goom & Malliaras (2016 JOSPT) PHT protocol. Delivers high tensile mechanotransduction to the proximal hamstring tendon and induces immediate exercise-induced hypoalgesia (reducing sitting pain!) without compressing the inflamed enthesis against the ischial tuberosity.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with your heels resting on the floor (or on a low 6-inch step) with your knees bent at a long-lever 30°–45° angle

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Press through both heels (or single leg once tolerable at <= 2-3/10 pain) to lift your hips so your trunk and thighs are in a straight line (0° hip flexion)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold the static bridge for 45 seconds—because the hip is at 0° extension, the proximal hamstring tendon pulls straight away from the ischial tuberosity with zero bony wrap-around compression

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes and complete 5 sets.

coachingCues: "Tuck your tailbone slightly under and lift your hips all the way up to a straight plank so your sit-bone is completely free of pinch" (external).
commonErrors: Letting the hips sag downward into 30°–40° of hip flexion during the bridge hold (introduces ischial compression); arching the lumbar spine into anterior pelvic tilt (anterior pelvic tilt rotates the ischial tuberosity superiorly and increases compressive wrap!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Shorten the lever arm by bending the knees to 75°–90° (shifts load slightly toward the gluteus maximus if 30° long-lever is initially >3/10 painful); or perform prone isometric knee flexion against a band at 0° hip extension.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Shift from bilateral (50/50) -> staggered stance (75% on affected leg) -> pure single-leg long-lever isometric bridge hold -> hold a weight plate on the pelvis.

precautions: Letting the hips sag downward into 30°–40° of hip flexion during the bridge hold (introduces ischial compression); arching the lumbar spine into anterior pelvic tilt (anterior pelvic tilt rotates the ischial tuberosity superiorly and increases compressive wrap!). Cues: "Tuck your tailbone slightly under and lift your hips all the way up to a straight plank so your sit-bone is completely free of pinch" (external).
clinicalNotes: Forms Stage 1 of the Goom & Malliaras (2016 JOSPT) PHT protocol. Delivers high tensile mechanotransduction to the proximal hamstring tendon and induces immediate exercise-induced hypoalgesia (reducing sitting pain!) without compressing the inflamed enthesis against the ischial tuberosity.

name: Supine Sciatic Nerve Slider & Deep Gluteal External Rotator Isometric
chineseName: Supine Sciatic Nerve Slider & Deep Gluteal External Rotator Isometric
rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: In Deep Gluteal Syndrome and chronic PHT, peritendinous oedema around the ischial tuberosity or hypertonicity of the piriformis/obturator internus irritates the adjacent sciatic nerve. Gentle sliders at a safe 45°–60° hip angle mobilize the sciatic nerve past the ischial tunnel without compressing the tendon enthesis, while isometric external rotation loads the deep hip rotators (avoiding the provocative FAIR stretch [Flexion-Adduction-Internal Rotation] which crushes the piriformis against the sciatic nerve!).

jointActions: Neurodynamic slider + isometric; open/closed chain; deep gluteal space decompression

execution.startingPosition: Part A (Non-Pinching Sciatic Nerve Slider): Lie supine and hold behind the thigh with the hip flexed to only 45°–60° (staying below the 90° angle that compresses the ischial tuberosity and piriformis!). Slowly extend the knee while pointing the foot down (plantarflexion), then bend the knee while pulling the foot up (dorsiflexion) for 10-12 smooth, zero-tingling oscillations
execution.description: In Deep Gluteal Syndrome and chronic PHT, peritendinous oedema around the ischial tuberosity or hypertonicity of the piriformis/obturator internus irritates the adjacent sciatic nerve. Gentle sliders at a safe 45°–60° hip angle mobilize the sciatic nerve past the ischial tunnel without compressing the tendon enthesis, while isometric external rotation loads the deep hip rotators (avoiding the provocative FAIR stretch [Flexion-Adduction-Internal Rotation] which crushes the piriformis against the sciatic nerve!).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Part A (Non-Pinching Sciatic Nerve Slider): Lie supine and hold behind the thigh with the hip flexed to only 45°–60° (staying below the 90° angle that compresses the ischial tuberosity and piriformis!). Slowly extend the knee while pointing the foot down (plantarflexion), then bend the knee while pulling the foot up (dorsiflexion) for 10-12 smooth, zero-tingling oscillations

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Part B (Neutral-Hip External Rotation Isometric for Deep Gluteal Syndrome): Lie supine with knees bent at 60° and a resistance band looped above the knees; gently press the knees outward into abduction/external rotation for 5 x 30s holds (0/10 deep buttock pain).

coachingCues: "Keep your thigh at a gentle 45-degree angle and glide the nerve smoothly without ever feeling a stretch or pinch in your sit-bone" (external).
commonErrors: Aggressively stretching the buttock with a deep Figure-4 / Pigeon stretch when Deep Gluteal Syndrome or PHT is acutely inflamed (compresses the sciatic nerve and proximal hamstring tendons against the ischium!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Perform sliders at 30° hip flexion if 60° produces any buttock pulling.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress to side-lying clamshells and standing banded hip external rotations.

precautions: Aggressively stretching the buttock with a deep Figure-4 / Pigeon stretch when Deep Gluteal Syndrome or PHT is acutely inflamed (compresses the sciatic nerve and proximal hamstring tendons against the ischium!). Cues: "Keep your thigh at a gentle 45-degree angle and glide the nerve smoothly without ever feeling a stretch or pinch in your sit-bone" (external).
clinicalNotes: In Deep Gluteal Syndrome and chronic PHT, peritendinous oedema around the ischial tuberosity or hypertonicity of the piriformis/obturator internus irritates the adjacent sciatic nerve. name: Single-leg long-lever isotonic bridge & supine slider (Stage 2A — 0° hip HSR)

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: Initiates Stage 2A isotonic Heavy Slow Resistance. By keeping the hip between 0° and 30° of flexion throughout the bridge (or during supine eccentric heel sliders), the proximal hamstring tendon undergoes heavy slow tensile remodeling with zero bony compression against the ischial tuberosity.

jointActions: Closed chain; isotonic HSR (3s up / 3s down); high-load remodeling without hip flexion

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine with the affected heel elevated on a 12-inch box or bench (knee bent at ~30°–45°)
execution.description: Initiates Stage 2A isotonic Heavy Slow Resistance. By keeping the hip between 0° and 30° of flexion throughout the bridge (or during supine eccentric heel sliders), the proximal hamstring tendon undergoes heavy slow tensile remodeling with zero bony compression against the ischial tuberosity.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with the affected heel elevated on a 12-inch box or bench (knee bent at ~30°–45°)

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Tuck the pelvis slightly posteriorly and drive through the heel to lift the hips to 0° full extension over 3 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Hold 2 seconds at the top

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Lower the hips only halfway down (stopping at ~20°–30° hip flexion so the pelvis hovers above the floor, keeping the exercise in the non-compressive arc) over 3 seconds, then press back up!

coachingCues: "Drive through your heel to a straight plank at the top and control the 3-second lowering phase" (external).
commonErrors: Dropping the buttocks all the way into a deep hip-flexed fold at the bottom if the ischial tuberosity is still compression-sensitive.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral long-lever bridges with single-leg eccentric lowering.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold a heavy dumbbell or barbell across the hips; combine with supine eccentric hamstring sliders (bridging up at 0° hip extension and sliding the heels out over 4 seconds).

precautions: Dropping the buttocks all the way into a deep hip-flexed fold at the bottom if the ischial tuberosity is still compression-sensitive. Cues: "Drive through your heel to a straight plank at the top and control the 3-second lowering phase" (external).
clinicalNotes: Initiates Stage 2A isotonic Heavy Slow Resistance. name: Prone / standing resisted hamstring curl & Nordic curl (Stage 2A — 0° hip lock)
chineseName: Prone / standing resisted hamstring curl & Nordic curl (Stage 2A — 0° hip lock)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
description: A crucial clinical pearl from Goom et al. (JOSPT): Seated leg curls are highly provocative in early PHT because sitting flexes the hip to 90° and compresses the tendon against the chair and ischium; in contrast, Prone leg curls and Nordic curls keep the hip at 0° extension, allowing massive isolated hamstring hypertrophy with zero ischial compression!

jointActions: Open/closed chain; eccentric/HSR at 0° hip extension; isolated tensile hypertrophy

execution.startingPosition: Option A (Prone Hamstring Curl HSR): Lie face down (prone) on a hamstring curl machine or plinth with a resistance band/ankle weight—place a flat pillow under your pelvis only, keeping your hips at 0°–15° flexion (avoid seated hamstring curl machines in Stage 2A, because seated machines lock the hip at 90° flexion and crush the ischial tuberosity!). Curl up over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower over 3-4 seconds
execution.description: A crucial clinical pearl from Goom et al. (JOSPT): Seated leg curls are highly provocative in early PHT because sitting flexes the hip to 90° and compresses the tendon against the chair and ischium; in contrast, Prone leg curls and Nordic curls keep the hip at 0° extension, allowing massive isolated hamstring hypertrophy with zero ischial compression!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Option A (Prone Hamstring Curl HSR): Lie face down (prone) on a hamstring curl machine or plinth with a resistance band/ankle weight—place a flat pillow under your pelvis only, keeping your hips at 0°–15° flexion (avoid seated hamstring curl machines in Stage 2A, because seated machines lock the hip at 90° flexion and crush the ischial tuberosity!). Curl up over 3 seconds, hold 2 seconds, and lower over 3-4 seconds

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Option B (Nordic Hamstring Curl at 0° Hip Extension): Kneel tall with hips locked at 0° extension and lower slowly over 4 seconds—because the hips stay at 0°, Nordics place zero wrap-around compression on the ischial tuberosity!

coachingCues: "Keep your hips locked straight at zero degrees—let your knee do 100% of the bending so your sit-bone never gets pinched" (external).
commonErrors: Using a Seated Leg Curl machine in Stage 1 or 2A PHT; breaking at the hips (bending into hip flexion) during a Nordic curl!

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Prone band curls with light-to-moderate resistance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: 2-up / 1-down heavy eccentric prone curls; unassisted deeper Nordic curls.

precautions: Using a Seated Leg Curl machine in Stage 1 or 2A PHT; breaking at the hips (bending into hip flexion) during a Nordic curl! Cues: "Keep your hips locked straight at zero degrees—let your knee do 100% of the bending so your sit-bone never gets pinched" (external).
clinicalNotes: A crucial clinical pearl from Goom et al. Strengthening the gluteal complex offloads both the deep gluteal space and the ischial origin.

jointActions: Open/closed chain; isotonic HSR; stabilizing the deep hip rotator cuff

execution.startingPosition: Perform 3 sets of 12-15 side-lying straight-leg hip abductions (sliding the heel along a wall in slight hip extension) and side-plank clamshells
execution.description: In both Deep Gluteal Syndrome and PHT, weak gluteus medius and maximus muscles force the small deep external rotators (piriformis, obturator internus) and biceps femoris to work overtime to prevent femoral internal rotation and pelvic drop during running mid-stance. steps.title: 步驟 1

name: Graded-depth Romanian Deadlift (Stage 2B — 30° -> 60° -> 90° hip-flexion exposure)
chineseName: 羅馬尼亞硬舉 (RDL 膕旁肌與臀肌)
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷

description: Because daily life (sitting, bending) and sports (running uphill, lunging, sprinting) require the hip to flex under load, a PHT athlete can never fully recover if they avoid hip flexion forever! Stage 2B of the Goom & Malliaras protocol gradually re-introduces hip-flexion compression in 15°–20° increments under slow heavy load, stimulating the fibrocartilaginous enthesis at the ischial tuberosity to adapt to combined compressive + tensile strain!

jointActions: Closed chain; graded compressive-tensile HSR; enthesis wrap-around adaptation

execution.startingPosition: Clearance Gate: Begin Stage 2B only once Stage 2A (0° hip bridges and prone curls) is strong and sitting pain has improved
execution.description: Because daily life (sitting, bending) and sports (running uphill, lunging, sprinting) require the hip to flex under load, a PHT athlete can never fully recover if they avoid hip flexion forever! Stage 2B of the Goom & Malliaras protocol gradually re-introduces hip-flexion compression in 15°–20° increments under slow heavy load, stimulating the fibrocartilaginous enthesis at the ischial tuberosity to adapt to combined compressive + tensile strain!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Clearance Gate: Begin Stage 2B only once Stage 2A (0° hip bridges and prone curls) is strong and sitting pain has improved

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Set a barbell on rack pins or elevate kettlebells on blocks to control exact hip-flexion depth: Weeks 1–2 of Stage 2B: Hinge to 30°–45° hip flexion (hands stopping above the knees, 3s down / 3s up) -> Weeks 3–4: Lower the blocks to hinge to 60° hip flexion (hands at mid-shin) -> Weeks 5–8: Full 75°–90° hip flexion RDL and Single-Leg RDL.

coachingCues: "Lower slowly for 3 seconds only until the bar kisses the rack pins at your prescribed angle, then drive your hips forward through your glutes" (external).
commonErrors: Jumping straight from supine bridges into full-depth floor-touching RDLs on Day 1 of Stage 2B (causes an immediate compressive flare-up at the sit-bone!).

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Step the rack pins up 15° higher if next-morning sitting pain increases by >1-2 points on the 0-10 scale.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Progress from bilateral rack-pin RDL (30° -> 60° -> 90°) to Single-Leg RDL across the same angle ladder.

precautions: Jumping straight from supine bridges into full-depth floor-touching RDLs on Day 1 of Stage 2B (causes an immediate compressive flare-up at the sit-bone!). Cues: "Lower slowly for 3 seconds only until the bar kisses the rack pins at your prescribed angle, then drive your hips forward through your glutes" (external).

Stage 2B of the Goom & Malliaras protocol gradually re-introduces hip-flexion compression in 15°–20° increments under slow heavy load, stimulating the fibrocartilaginous enthesis at the ischial tuberosity to adapt to combined compressive + tensile strain!

name: Graded-depth Bulgarian split squat & high step-up (Stage 2B unilateral compression)
chineseName: 單腳 上階梯登階肌力訓練
rehabPhase: Phase 2: 次急性控制負荷
Phase 3: 後期肌力與肥大強化
description: Teaches the athlete to control trunk inclination (the primary modifier of ischial tuberosity compression during squatting and lunging): an upright torso biases the quadriceps and keeps hip flexion shallow, whereas a forward-inclined torso increases hip flexion and loads the proximal hamstring enthesis!

jointActions: Closed chain; unilateral HSR; functional single-leg hip-flexion load tolerance

execution.startingPosition: Stand in a split-squat stance (or in front of a 6-to-8-inch step for Forward Step-Ups) with the affected leg in front
execution.description: Teaches the athlete to control trunk inclination (the primary modifier of ischial tuberosity compression during squatting and lunging): an upright torso biases the quadriceps and keeps hip flexion shallow, whereas a forward-inclined torso increases hip flexion and loads the proximal hamstring enthesis!

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a split-squat stance (or in front of a 6-to-8-inch step for Forward Step-Ups) with the affected leg in front

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Keep the torso relatively upright in Weeks 1–2 of Stage 2B (an upright torso reduces the hip flexion angle to ~45°–60° even when the knee bends to 75°!)

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: In Weeks 3–6, gradually incline the torso forward 15°–25° over the front thigh and deepen the split squat to 90° to progressively load the gluteus maximus and proximal hamstring origin in deeper hip flexion.

coachingCues: "Start with a tall chest to protect your sit-bone, and only lean forward into your hip in later weeks as your tendon gets stronger" (external).
commonErrors: Pitching the chest far forward over the front knee in early split squats before the ischial enthesis tolerates >70° hip flexion compression.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Keep the torso completely vertical and limit split-squat depth with a foam pad under the rear knee.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Hold heavy dumbbells; deepen squat depth and increase forward trunk lean angle sequentially.

precautions: Pitching the chest far forward over the front knee in early split squats before the ischial enthesis tolerates >70° hip flexion compression. steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine with both hips and knees flexed to 90°.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Place one palm against the front of the anteriorly rotated (or painful anterior-tilt) thigh to resist hip flexion, and place the other hand behind the opposite distal thigh to resist hip extension.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Simultaneously push the first thigh Up into your palm and the opposite thigh Down into your other hand at 30–40% effort for 6–8 seconds while breathing evenly.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Relax for 5 seconds, then alternate sides for 4–5 cycles each.

coachingCues: "Push one knee gently into your top hand and the other thigh into your bottom hand with equal, gentle pressure—like turning a steering wheel smoothly."Internal cue: "Feel both sides of your pelvis settling evenly onto the mat as you exhale."
commonErrors: Do not push at 100% maximal effort or hold your breath (Valsalva), which increases intrathecal and pelvic floor pressure.

regressions.name: 退階方案

rehabPhase: Phase 1: 急性保護/神經肌肉活化
description: Co-contracting the bilateral adductors (anterior pubic symphysis tether) followed by the bilateral abductors/external rotators (posterior SIJ tether) together with the transversus abdominis and pelvic floor creates a 360° muscular corset that compresses and stabilizes both the pubic symphysis and sacroiliac joints (PMC7041669).

jointActions: Bilateral Isometric Co-Contraction (Local & Global Pelvic Ring Closure)

execution.startingPosition: Lie supine in hook-lying (knees bent 70°, feet flat hip-width apart).
execution.description: Co-contracting the bilateral adductors (anterior pubic symphysis tether) followed by the bilateral abductors/external rotators (posterior SIJ tether) together with the transversus abdominis and pelvic floor creates a 360° muscular corset that compresses and stabilizes both the pubic symphysis and sacroiliac joints (PMC7041669).

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Lie supine in hook-lying (knees bent 70°, feet flat hip-width apart).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: First, draw the lower abdomen gently inward (transversus abdominis + pelvic floor zip-up) and squeeze a yoga block or small ball between the knees at 40–50% effort for 10 seconds (5 reps).

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Immediately switch to looping a firm mini-band around the knees and pressing both knees outward at 40–50% effort for 10 seconds (5 reps).

coachingCues: "Exhale gently, zip up your lower abs, and squeeze the block with both knees using the exact same force on left and right."Internal cue: "Imagine drawing the two halves of your pelvis snugly together toward the midline."
commonErrors: Do not tilt the pelvis violently or allow one leg to push harder than the other.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Reduce effort to 25–30% MVC and focus on coordinating diaphragmatic exhalation with transversus abdominis drawing-in.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Perform the alternating adductor squeeze and abductor band press while holding a low bilateral glute bridge hover (hips 10 cm off the mat).

precautions: Do not tilt the pelvis violently or allow one leg to push harder than the other.External cue: "Exhale gently, zip up your lower abs, and squeeze the block with both knees using the exact same force on left and right."Internal cue: "Imagine drawing the two halves of your pelvis snugly together toward the midline."

steps.title: 步驟 2

steps.title: 步驟 3

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Assume a quadruped position facing a low resistance band anchor.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Hold the band in one hand while keeping the spine in neutral and lower abdominals braced.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Simultaneously pull the band straight back toward your hip with a straight arm (engaging the latissimus dorsi) while extending the opposite leg straight back to hip height (engaging the contralateral gluteus maximus).

execution.startingPosition: Stand in a compact athletic stance (or wide-base half-kneeling with a foam roller squeezed lightly between the inner thighs) next to a cable machine.
execution.description: Trains the Anterior Oblique Sling (AOS)—linking the external/internal obliques across the anterior abdominal aponeurosis to the contralateral adductors—which provides anterior force closure across the pubic symphysis and prevents rotational shear at the SIJ during trunk rotation.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a compact athletic stance (or wide-base half-kneeling with a foam roller squeezed lightly between the inner thighs) next to a cable machine.

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Pull the cable diagonally across the torso from high-to-low (Chop) or low-to-high (Lift) over 2 seconds while keeping the pelvis and knees completely still and squeezing the inner thighs inward by 30% to co-activate the adductors.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Stand in a B-Stance (kickstand: 80% weight on affected leg, 20% on rear toes for pelvic symmetry) facing a cable pulley or band anchor at waist height, holding the handle in the contralateral hand.

execution.description: Trains the Lateral Myofascial Sling (gluteus medius/minimus coupled with the contralateral quadratus lumborum and obliques) to dynamically compress and stabilize the SIJ during every single-leg stance phase of walking, stair climbing, and running—directly normalizing the Active Straight Leg Raise (ASLR) load transfer mechanism.

steps.title: 步驟 1
steps.instruction: Hold a heavy kettlebell or dumbbell in one hand at your side (Suitcase Carry) or one kettlebell in the front-rack position and one at the side (Mixed-Rack Carry).

steps.title: 步驟 2
steps.instruction: Pre-engage the pelvic floor, lower abs, and glutes.

steps.title: 步驟 3
steps.instruction: Walk slowly with short, deliberate, slightly wide-track steps for 25–30 meters (including stepping over 15 cm hurdles or onto a 15 cm step) without allowing the ribcage to tilt or the pelvis to drop on the unweighted side.

steps.title: 步驟 4
steps.instruction: Switch hands and repeat.

coachingCues: "Take short, crisp steps as if walking on thin ice with a full bucket of water in one hand—keep your shoulders and belt line dead level."Internal cue: "Pre-tense your outer hip before each foot touches the ground."
commonErrors: Avoid taking long, lazy strides or letting the hip swing out laterally on weight acceptance.

regressions.name: 退階方案
regressions.rationale: Bilateral Farmer's Carry (equal weights in both hands) to eliminate frontal-plane asymmetry while building axial compression tolerance.

progressions.name: 進階方案
progressions.rationale: Overhead Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry + Single-Leg Step-Up Hold, or alternate-day return-to-running progression with +5–10% cadence.

precautions: Avoid taking long, lazy strides or letting the hip swing out laterally on weight acceptance.External cue: "Take short, crisp steps as if walking on thin ice with a full bucket of water in one hand—keep your shoulders and belt line dead level."Internal cue: "Pre-tense your outer hip before each foot touches the ground."
clinicalNotes: Trains the Lateral Myofascial Sling (gluteus medius/minimus coupled with the contralateral quadratus lumborum and obliques) to dynamically compress and stabilize the SIJ during every single-leg stance phase of walking, stair climbing, and running—directly normalizing the Active Straight Leg Raise (ASLR) load transfer mechanism.
